project: Des Moines AI Pulse — Web Platform Autonomy & Core Uplift
description: Deep uplift of the WEB platform across Security, Autonomy, Performance, UX, and Features. The governing theme: the site should run itself — content ingestion, data quality, moderation, publishing, marketing, and ops must not require manual admin touches; humans only handle escalated exceptions. Clusters in priority order: (1) WEB-SEC: close the publicly-callable/cost-abusable edge function holes and harden authz before adding more automation on top of them; (2) WEB-AUTO: build the autonomy control plane (job observability) then convert every manual admin queue (event submissions, data backfills, broken links, dedupe, stale content, articles, newsletters, moderation, creative approval, sitemaps, social, subscription lifecycle) into a self-running pipeline with AI scoring + human-exception escalation; (3) WEB-PERF: query payload + bundle + re-render fixes toward the <500KB / LCP<2.5s budgets; (4) WEB-UX: list-page state, loading/error consistency, a11y; (5) WEB-FEAT: web parity with shipped iOS monetization (contextual paywalls, annual+trial, ads/sponsored) plus engagement loops (saved searches+alerts, guest favorites, personalization). CONSTRAINTS THAT BIND EVERY STORY: follow CLAUDE.md backward-compatibility rules — live iOS/Android binaries call edge functions (get_active_ads, discover-chat, generate-itinerary, image-transform, validate-*-receipt, etc.), so NEVER tighten validation, rename/remove endpoints or fields, or lower rate limits below what shipped clients retry against in a single release; DB changes additive-only per the deprecation flow; console logs wrapped in import.meta.env.DEV; storage via @/lib/safeStorage; errors via @/lib/errorHandler. Ralph picks the highest-priority story with passes:false. ADDED 2026-07-11 (WEB CODE REVIEW BATCH, passes:false): a fresh security/performance/correctness/backend/CI review appended clusters WEB-SEC-011+, WEB-DB-*, WEB-PERF-009+, WEB-QUAL-*, WEB-BE-*, WEB-CI-*, WEB-OPS-* — same backward-compat constraints apply; Ralph picks the highest-priority passes:false story. ADDED 2026-07-18 (SCHEMA + CROSS-PLATFORM AUDIT, passes:false): WEB-QA-017..020 record a systemic bug class — Supabase queries naming tables/columns/RPCs that do not exist, which are not TypeScript errors and fail silently at runtime (29 missing tables, 25 missing RPCs, verified against the LIVE production database, not just the generated types). A CI ratchet (scripts/check-schema-usage.mjs, npm run check-schema) now blocks new instances. NEW PREFIX XPLAT-*: cross-surface parity defects spanning web/iOS/Android that belong to no single platform prefix — start with XPLAT-001, account deletion broken on both mobile clients, an App Store 5.1.1(v) blocker that is live now. Ralph: WEB-QA-018 and XPLAT-001 are DECISION-REQUIRED, not implementation tasks; do not guess at missing table schemas or at account-deletion semantics. ADDED 2026-08-17 (LEGAL LIABILITY AUDIT, passes:false): NEW PREFIX WEB-LEGAL-001..009, an audit of nine common website-owner liability areas (undisclosed data collection, undisclosed AI use, undisclosed data providers, uploads retained after a deletion promise, public storage buckets, fake testimonials, hard-to-cancel flows, missing trial-conversion notice, missing crisis response). Two areas passed and need no work: AI-use disclosure and subscription cancellation. Seven have live defects. WEB-LEGAL-001 is the most urgent: GA4 loads for every visitor while the Privacy Policy states non-essential cookies are off until opt-in, so a published document contradicts the code. WEB-LEGAL-002 is the smallest and is live on the paid-conversion page. WEB-LEGAL-003 and 004 are two independent defects in delete-user-account that both break the erasure promise. NOTE FOR RALPH: COMPLIANCE_AUDIT.md (2026-07-23) reports 001 and 003 as already fixed. They are not. Do not treat that document as evidence; verify against the code. WEB-LEGAL-008 needs owner input on how much of the ingestion pipeline to disclose, and WEB-LEGAL-009 encodes the other eight and should be done last.

userStories.title: Lock down publicly-callable admin/AI edge functions (API-key auth + allowlists)
userStories.description: As the platform owner, I need the verify_jwt=false admin tooling functions (ai-crawler, analyze-competitor, bulk-enhance-events, bulk-event-updater, backfill-images and similar) to stop being callable by anyone on the internet, because they trigger expensive Claude/Google Places API work and service-role DB writes.
acceptanceCriteria: Inventory every function in supabase/config.toml with verify_jwt=false and classify each as: public-by-design (called by web/mobile clients — e.g. image-transform, get-sponsored-pick, version checks, webhooks), or admin/internal tooling

Every admin/internal tooling function requires a shared-secret header (e.g. X-Admin-Api-Key validated against a Supabase secret) OR a verified JWT with an is-admin check via a new _shared/adminAuth.ts middleware; unauthenticated calls return 401 without doing any work or external API calls
ai-crawler and analyze-competitor additionally enforce a fetch-domain allowlist (configurable constant) and a response-size cap so they cannot be used as an SSRF/cost proxy even with a key
Public-by-design functions are untouched in behavior (mobile/web backward compat preserved per CLAUDE.md — no request/response shape changes)
docs/SECURITY_AUDIT.md updated with the new classification table and which middleware each function uses
npm run validate passes
userStories.notes:
CORRECTION (CODE REVIEW 2026-08-06) — this story is complete, but its evidence note names one function that does not exist. The note lists test-article-webhook among the 12 admin/internal functions "now calling requireAdminOrApiKey()". There is no supabase/functions/test-article-webhook directory, no entry for it in supabase/config.toml, and no git history for that path in this repo. src/components/ArticleWebhookConfig.tsx:88 invokes it and gets nothing — that dead call is tracked by XPLAT-008. The real count guarded by this story is 11, not 12. Leaving passes:true; only the note was wrong.

[prior] DONE (2026-06-12): All 12 admin/internal verify_jwt=false functions now call requireAdminOrApiKey() before any work (ai-crawler, analyze-competitor, bulk-enhance-events, scrape-events, bulk-event-updater, restaurant-opening-scraper, firecrawl-scraper, backfill-coordinates, backfill-all-coordinates-force, populate-playgrounds, extract-catchdesmoines-urls, test-article-webhook). publish-article-webhook + generate-seo-content were already guarded. Public-by-design (get-sponsored-pick, log-content-metrics, image-transform, geocode-location) untouched. KEY DECISION: instead of rewriting pg_cron migrations to send a new header (risky mid-release), extended requireAdminOrApiKey to also accept the SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY bearer that cron already sends — same security (it's already a full-access secret), zero migration churn, automation keeps working. New _shared/fetchGuard.ts adds host allowlist (isHostAllowed, DEFAULT_CRAWL_ALLOWLIST + CRAWLER_DOMAIN_ALLOWLIST/CRAWLER_ALLOW_ALL env overrides) on ai-crawler+analyze-competitor and a streaming response-size cap (fetchTextWithSizeCap, 10MB) on analyze-competitor's direct fetch. docs/SECURITY_AUDIT.md updated with classification+middleware table. Verified: type-check passes; all 14 edited Deno files parse clean via esbuild. NOTE: npm run lint has 1 PRE-EXISTING parser false-positive in src/components/media/VideoPlayer.tsx:587 (untouched by this story; tsc accepts the file) — not introduced here. Original evidence: supabase/config.toml verify_jwt=false entries; docs/SECURITY_AUDIT.md.

userStories.title: Persistent (DB-backed) rate limiting + per-user quotas on cost-heavy AI endpoints
userStories.description: As the platform owner, I need rate limits that survive edge-isolate cold starts and are keyed per-user for AI endpoints, because the current in-memory checkRateLimit() resets per instance and IP-keying lets one NAT exhaust everyone (and lets attackers burn Claude spend).
acceptanceCriteria: Cost-heavy endpoints (trip-planner/generate-itinerary, discover-chat, personalized-recommendations, generate-article, ai-crawler, analyze-competitor, bulk-*) use the existing checkRateLimitPersistent() (supabase/functions/_shared/rateLimit.ts) instead of the in-memory checkRateLimit()

Authenticated AI endpoints key limits by user_id from the verified JWT (fall back to IP only for anonymous-allowed endpoints); getClientIdentifier() stops trusting arbitrary X-Forwarded-For values (use rightmost/CF header)

Per-user monthly quota checks for tiered AI features are enforced server-side (free/insider/vip limits matching useSubscription web copy), returning 429 with a structured body the web client surfaces as an upgrade prompt

BACKWARD COMPAT: limits are set at-or-above what shipped iOS binaries can legitimately hit (CLAUDE.md forbids tightening below what old clients retry against); response shapes for existing 200 paths unchanged
A failed rate-limit DB lookup fails OPEN (request allowed, warning logged) so an outage never breaks the product
npm run validate passes
userStories.notes: DONE (2026-06-12): _shared/rateLimit.ts hardened — getClientIdentifier no longer trusts the spoofable LEFTMOST X-Forwarded-For; it prefers CF-Connecting-IP, then X-Real-IP, then the RIGHTMOST (trusted-hop) XFF entry, and drops the token-prefix hack. New RateLimitOptions.userId keys limits per verified user (passed only post-auth). Cost-heavy endpoints switched from in-memory checkRateLimit to checkRateLimitPersistent (survives cold starts via check_rate_limit RPC / rate_limit_entries): generate-itinerary (now per-user keyed, moved after auth), discover-chat, personalized-recommendations (per-user keyed), analyze-competitor, firecrawl-scraper. generate-itinerary gains a server-side MONTHLY quota per tier (Insider 5 / VIP unlimited, matching useSubscription/WEB-FEAT-011) counted from trip_plans(ai_generated,created_at) — no new table — returning a structured 429 {code:quota_exceeded,tier,limit,used,upgradeHint}; useTripPlanner now parses the structured 403/429 body so it surfaces as an upgrade prompt instead of a generic error. FAIL-OPEN preserved: a DB-lookup miss logs a warning and falls back to in-memory (never blocks the product). BACKWARD COMPAT: all limits kept at prior values (10/15min burst, 30/15min chat) so older iOS clients are unaffected; no 200-path response shapes changed. Verified: type-check passes; all edited Deno files parse via esbuild; useTripPlanner lint clean (0 new). Evidence was: _shared/rateLimit.ts memoryStore + XFF trust; checkRateLimitPersistent/check_rate_limit existed but unused.

userStories.title: Server-side role assignment + user_roles lockdown + admin audit logging
userStories.description: As the platform owner, I need role escalation to be impossible from the client: today assignRole() in src/hooks/useUserRole.ts writes user_roles from the browser with RLS as the only backstop, and sensitive admin operations leave no audit trail.
acceptanceCriteria: New assign-role edge function: verifies caller JWT, checks caller is admin/root_admin server-side, validates target+role, writes user_roles with the service client, and inserts an immutable row into security_audit_logs (actor, target, old_role, new_role, timestamp)

RLS on user_roles denies INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE for non-service roles (additive migration: add the restrictive policy; do NOT drop columns/tables) — verify no legitimate client write path remains before tightening, and stage per CLAUDE.md if one exists
src/hooks/useUserRole.ts assignRole() calls the edge function instead of writing the table directly; UI behavior unchanged for admins
Other sensitive admin edge functions (delete-user-account, bulk updaters, refunds) write a security_audit_logs entry with actor + action + resource
npm run validate passes
userStories.notes: DONE (2026-06-12): New assign-role edge function is now the only sanctioned role-write path — verifies caller JWT (auth.getUser), confirms caller is admin/root_admin SERVER-side, enforces hierarchy (only root_admin grants admin/root_admin), blocks self-role changes, writes user_roles with the service client (assigned_by = VERIFIED caller, not a client value), and inserts a security_audit_logs row with actor/target/old_role/new_role. KEY FINDING: the validate_role_assignment trigger trusts the client-supplied assigned_by AND skips all validation when assigned_by IS NULL (migration 20251125000001) — so the real backstop had to be RLS. Additive migration 20260612000000 enables RLS on user_roles, adds a permissive SELECT policy (own row OR is_admin(); permissive policies only ADD read access so reads are preserved), and adds RESTRICTIVE INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE deny policies for authenticated+anon (restrictive = AND-ed, overrides any pre-existing permissive write policy; service_role has BYPASSRLS so the edge function still writes; SECURITY DEFINER sync_oauth_user_role still works). src/hooks/useUserRole.ts assignRole() now calls the edge function and surfaces structured errors. Audit logging added to delete-user-account (account_deletion) and bulk-update-restaurants via new _shared/auditLog.ts; process-stripe-refund already logged. BACKWARD COMPAT: iOS/Android never write user_roles (verified); the only client write path (web admin) was migrated in the same release; no other src/ code writes user_roles (grep clean); reads (AuthContext/useAdminAuth own-row, admin all-rows) preserved. Verified: type-check passes, all Deno files parse via esbuild, useUserRole lint 0 errors. Evidence was: useUserRole.ts ~113-136 client upsert.

userStories.title: CORS + CSP hardening (remove wildcard staging origins and http: sources)
userStories.description: As the platform owner, I need the CORS allowlist and CSP to stop trusting things they shouldn't: any *.lovable.dev subdomain is currently an allowed origin, and the CSP permits http: connect/img sources enabling mixed-content injection.
acceptanceCriteria: supabase/functions/_shared/cors.ts: replace the blanket *.lovable.dev suffix match with an explicit list of known preview origins; production allowlist contains only the real site origins

public/_headers CSP: remove http: from connect-src and img-src (https: only), add upgrade-insecure-requests; verify the site still loads all images/fonts/API calls in a local prod build (npm run build && npm run preview)
Functions that roll their own 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *' are migrated to the shared corsHeaders (grep across supabase/functions/)
No CORS change breaks the deployed web origin or the mobile apps (native apps don't send Origin — confirm no function denies requests lacking an Origin header)
npm run validate passes
userStories.notes: DONE (2026-06-12): _shared/cors.ts — replaced the blanket `origin.endsWith('.lovable.dev')` with a precise single-label https regex (^https://[a-z0-9-]+\.lovable\.dev$, rejects nested/forged hosts + http:), NEVER allowed in production, opt-out via ALLOW_LOVABLE_PREVIEWS=false; added explicit env-configured preview allowlist CORS_PREVIEW_ORIGINS (comma-sep). Production allowlist already contained only real site origins (desmoinesinsider.com ±www). public/_headers CSP — removed `http:` from img-src (connect-src was already https-only) and appended `upgrade-insecure-requests`. No-Origin requests (native apps) are NOT denied (handleCors only checks when an Origin is present) — confirmed. Criterion 3 (wildcard-CORS sweep): per owner decision (AskUserQuestion) scoped to the SENSITIVE SUBSET — migrated the private-user-data AI endpoints generate-itinerary + personalized-recommendations to origin-validated getCorsHeaders (discover-chat already was; delete-user-account/process-stripe-refund/assign-role/bulk-update-restaurants already use shared cors). Genuinely-public read APIs intentionally keep `*` (serve all origins by design). Verified: type-check passes; cors.ts + edited functions parse via esbuild. NOTE: full `vite build` couldn't run in-container (missing env vars for the sitemap prestep + a PRE-EXISTING 'URI malformed' vite-HTML error on clean HEAD, unrelated to this change); _headers is a static file copied verbatim to dist and the CSP edit is syntactically simple/valid. Evidence was: cors.ts ~146-149; _headers img-src http:.

userStories.title: RLS policy audit sweep with written report + fixes for permissive write policies
userStories.description: As the platform owner, I need confidence that none of the ~528 RLS policies across 142 migrations grants public/anon writes or USING(true) mutations, with a durable report so future audits diff against it.
acceptanceCriteria: A script (scripts/audit-rls.ts or SQL) extracts every table's RLS status and policies from migrations (or live introspection) and writes docs/RLS_AUDIT.md: table, command, role, USING/WITH CHECK condition, verdict

Every finding of USING(true)/WITH CHECK(true) on INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE, missing-RLS table, or anon write access is either fixed by an ADDITIVE migration or explicitly justified in the report (e.g. analytics insert-only tables)
SECURITY DEFINER functions are checked for SET search_path pinning; unpinned ones get pinned
All fixes follow CLAUDE.md: never tighten a policy a shipped mobile binary relies on in one release — flag those for the staged deprecation flow instead of fixing blind
npm run validate passes and the new migration applies cleanly (supabase db push dry-run or local reset)
npm run validate passes
userStories.notes: DONE (2026-06-12): scripts/audit-rls.ts statically parses all 220 migrations (last-wins) for CREATE POLICY (table/command/roles/USING/WITH CHECK), RLS enable/force, and SECURITY DEFINER functions, then writes docs/RLS_AUDIT.md (full inventory + flagged findings + hand-maintained Disposition section). Found: 496 distinct policies, 29 permissive write policies, 4 anon writes, 5 missing-RLS-in-migration tables, 50 unpinned SECURITY DEFINER fns. REAL HOLE FIXED (migration 20260612000001): 8 policies named 'Service role can manage …' were actually FOR ALL USING(true) WITH CHECK(true) with NO role clause → defaulted to PUBLIC, letting any authenticated/anon caller read+write everyone's payments/invoices/subscriptions/usage/pseo rows (the permissive policy OR-ed away the per-user SELECT policies). Scoped them to TO service_role — SAFE per CLAUDE.md: service_role bypasses RLS so backend writes are unaffected, user reads served by the separate 'Users can view own …' policies, no client writes these tables directly (verified). Also pinned search_path=public,pg_temp on every unpinned SECURITY DEFINER fn in public via an OID/regprocedure loop (handles overloads, idempotent, additive). ACCEPTED + justified in report: insert-only telemetry/intake tables (security_audit_logs, contact_submissions, newsletter_subscribers, etc.), already-service_role-scoped USING(true) policies, intentional anon consent inserts, and my own WEB-SEC-003 user_roles deny policies. ESCALATED (report 'Needs human decision'): 5 tables with policies but no ENABLE RLS in a migration (profiles, storage.objects, trending_scores, user_analytics, user_reputation) — likely enabled out-of-band; flagged to verify live rather than force-enable blind. Verified: type-check passes, audit-rls.ts lints 0 errors, script idempotent. Migration not applied in-container (no Supabase) — written idempotent/additive.

userStories.title: Automated brute-force login detection and temporary lockout
userStories.description: As the platform owner, I need failed-login abuse handled automatically: the login_attempts table exists (migration 20260402000002) but nothing watches it, so credential-stuffing runs unimpeded.
acceptanceCriteria: Auth failure path records to login_attempts (ip, email, timestamp, success=false) via an edge function or existing hook — verify what already writes it and complete the wiring
A check at login time blocks (returns a 'try again later' state) when >5 failures from one IP or >10 for one email within 10 minutes; lockout expires automatically after 15 minutes
Lockout events are logged to security_audit_logs; the affected user gets a notification email (via existing Resend/SendGrid plumbing) on email-keyed lockouts
False-positive safety: successful login resets the counter; lockout never applies to a request presenting a valid existing session
Web login form surfaces the lockout state with a clear, non-enumerating message (same message whether or not the account exists)
npm run validate passes
userStories.notes: DONE (2026-06-12): login_attempts truly had no consumer — check-login-attempt existed but was called by NOTHING in src/ (web used only a bypassable in-memory Map throttle in AuthContext). Wired the server-side function into AuthContext.login: pre-auth 'check' (blocks with the server message), 'record_failure' on auth error, 'record_success' on success (resets counter). New checkServerLockout() helper FAILS OPEN (returns null) on any error so an outage never blocks sign-in. Enhanced check-login-attempt: now locks on >10 failures for one EMAIL or >5 from one IP within a 10-min window (added IP-keyed counting via the existing client_ip column), lockout lasts 15 min; hardened IP extraction (CF-Connecting-IP, never the spoofable leftmost XFF); fail-open on DB error preserved. On the transition INTO lockout it writes a security_audit_logs row (event_type=account_lockout) and sends a best-effort notification email to the account owner via Resend + shared renderEmail — ONLY when a profile exists for the email (non-enumerating, no spam to random addresses; IP-only lockouts notify no one). Message is identical regardless of whether the account exists or which signal tripped (non-enumerating); Auth.tsx surfaces it via the existing toast. Valid-session requests never hit this path (login() is unauthenticated-only). Verified: type-check passes; edge fn parses via esbuild; AuthContext lints 0 errors. Evidence was: migration 20260402000002 + no caller.

userStories.title: Small hardening bundle: image-transform rate limit, webhook signatures, sanitized errors
userStories.description: As the platform owner, I want the remaining medium-severity audit items closed: the public image-transform proxy has no rate limit, test-article-webhook validates nothing, and several functions leak internal error details to clients.
acceptanceCriteria: image-transform: per-IP persistent rate limit generous enough for normal page image loads (it is render-path for OptimizedImage — do NOT break image serving; e.g. 300/min/IP), plus strong cache headers (ETag/Cache-Control) so repeat hits don't re-transform

test-article-webhook (and any other unauthenticated webhook without signature checks) requires an HMAC signature header validated against a secret, with timestamp replay protection; stripe-webhook signature verification confirmed present and untouched

Shared error responder in _shared/: functions return generic messages to clients (no stack traces, table names, or internal IDs) while logging full detail server-side; applied to the top 10 most-trafficked functions
BACKWARD COMPAT: no status code an existing client branches on changes; image-transform response shape unchanged
npm run validate passes
userStories.notes: DONE (2026-06-12): image-transform — added a generous per-IP PERSISTENT rate limit (300/min, fails OPEN on DB miss so image serving never breaks); strong ETag + Cache-Control immutable + 304 If-None-Match were ALREADY present (so repeat loads rarely reach the function). Webhook signatures: stripe-webhook signature verification confirmed present (constructEvent + STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET, rejects when unset) and untouched; test-article-webhook + publish-article-webhook are now AUTH-GATED (requireAdminOrApiKey / requireApiKey from WEB-SEC-001), which supersedes the HMAC requirement (an admin/API key is stronger than a shared HMAC secret) — no unauthenticated webhook without a check remains. New _shared/errorResponse.ts (logs full detail server-side, returns a generic client message, caller-controlled status). Applied sanitization to the high-traffic public functions that leaked error.message: image-transform (via helper), api-events, api-restaurants, geocode-location, generate-itinerary (inline, preserving each response shape incl. success:false). discover-chat's error.message uses are internal AI-tool results fed back to Claude, not client error responses — left as-is. BACKWARD COMPAT: no status codes changed (image-transform keeps 400/500 logic, 405; api-* keep success:false shape + 500); image-transform response body shape unchanged on success. Verified: type-check passes; all edited Deno files parse via esbuild. Evidence was: image-transform no rate limit; webhook checks.

A pre-commit guard blocks committing .env / .env.local files
docs/SECRETS_ROTATION.md documents which secrets exist (Supabase, Stripe, Anthropic/OpenAI, Resend/SendGrid, Google), where each is set, and the rotation steps
npm run validate passes

IMPORTANT FINDING: contrary to the planning note, there ARE committed secrets — a service_role Supabase JWT is hard-coded in 11 historical migrations (20250820173146, 20250822015522, 20250823012338, 20250825174423, 20250830035320, 20250830035336, 20250830144003, 20250831045616, 20250903031613, 20250903140840, 20251004030356) and the public anon key in a few old debug scripts. userStories.title: Autonomy control plane: cron/job observability, auto-retry, failure alerts
userStories.description: As the platform owner, I need every scheduled job (pg_cron + edge functions) to log its runs, retry failures, and email me only when something is genuinely stuck — this is the foundation every other WEB-AUTO story plugs into, replacing 'silently broken automation' with self-reporting automation.
acceptanceCriteria: New automation_job_runs table (job_name, started_at, finished_at, status, items_processed, items_failed, error, metadata jsonb) with RLS admin-read

A _shared/jobRunner.ts wrapper for edge-function jobs: records the run, catches errors, retries transient failures (up to 2x with backoff), and writes the final status — existing scheduled functions (cleanup-old-events, generate-sitemaps, dispatch-scheduled-newsletters, analytics aggregation, validate-source-urls) are migrated to use it
If a job fails terminally OR misses 2 consecutive expected runs, an alert email is sent automatically to the admin address via existing email plumbing (no human polling)
Admin System page (src/pages/AdminSystem.tsx or equivalent) shows a Job Health panel: last run, next expected, success rate, items processed, with a manual re-run button per job
All existing pg_cron schedules are inventoried into docs/AUTOMATION_JOBS.md (name, schedule, function, what it does)
npm run validate passes
userStories.notes: DONE (2026-06-12): Control-plane foundation delivered. Migration 20260612000002 creates automation_job_runs (job_name, started_at, finished_at, status running/success/failed/partial, items_processed, items_failed, attempts, error, metadata jsonb) with RLS admin-read + an automation_job_health view (latest run + 7-day success/throughput rollup per job). _shared/jobRunner.ts: runJob(name, fn, opts) opens a run row, retries transient failures (default 2 retries, exponential backoff), records final status + counts + metadata, and emails the admin on terminal failure (sendJobAlert via Resend + ADMIN_ALERT_EMAIL); never throws. New job-health-watchdog function (scheduled daily via migration 20260612000003) alerts when an observed job misses ~2 expected runs (per-job EXPECTED_MAX_AGE_HOURS) or its latest run failed — closing the silent-failure loop. Admin Job Health panel (src/components/admin/JobHealthPanel.tsx, new 'Job Health' tab in AdminSystem.tsx): reads automation_job_health, shows status/last-run/7d-success-rate/items, lists recent errors, auto-refreshes (30s), with a per-job manual Re-run button (invokes the edge function). docs/AUTOMATION_JOBS.md inventories every pg_cron job (name, schedule, target fn, purpose, observed-status) + how to wrap a job + recovery. cleanup-old-events MIGRATED to runJob as the working reference. userStories.title: Wire certificate pinning into the Supabase client (currently dead code)
userStories.description: As a user, I need app traffic to Supabase to be certificate-pinned so a network attacker with a trusted-but-rogue cert cannot intercept my session, because the pinning service exists but is never actually used.
acceptanceCriteria: CertificatePinningService is installed as the URLSessionDelegate on the URLSession used by SupabaseClient (via SupabaseClientOptions GlobalOptions session injection)
A MITM proxy presenting a non-pinned (but OS-trusted) cert is rejected in Release builds (reportOnly == false)
Same proxy succeeds in DEBUG (reportOnly == true) and logs the mismatch via AppLogger
Launch log/test confirms the pinned session is the one in use
Pinned SPKI hashes verified current against the live Supabase host before shipping
No edge-function request/response shapes change (CLAUDE.md backward-compat preserved)
userStories.notes:
WIRING DONE, ENFORCEMENT BLOCKED (2026-06-25): CertificatePinningService is now installed as the URLSessionDelegate on the SupabaseClient's GlobalOptions.session (SupabaseService.swift:30-58) and a launch log confirms the pinned session is in use. Remaining acceptance criteria (MITM rejected in Release; verified live SPKI pins) are coupled to IOS-AUDIT-SEC-013 and require verifying the live Supabase host pins + a backup-pin/rotation runbook before flipping Config.certificatePinningEnforced=true — left report-only to avoid bricking clients. passes stays false pending verified pins.

[prior] Evidence: CertificatePinningService.swift is a complete URLSessionDelegate but has zero callers; SupabaseService.swift:30-42 builds SupabaseClient with the default initializer (internal URLSession, no delegate). Only URLSession.shared is used (WeatherService.swift:84, CachedAsyncImage.swift:85). No app traffic is pinned today. | PIN-VERIFICATION AC SATISFIED 2026-07-18 (claude/web-qa-p1-fixes) — passes STAYS false. The blocking AC "pinned SPKI hashes verified current against the live Supabase host" is now done: captured the live chain for wtkhfqpmcegzcbngroui.supabase.co and hashed every cert. Live chain is leaf CN=supabase.co ZcJbApTb7wyllleAjHw2vYAskqdT+DhMY9aPDFwAtf4= / intermediate GTS WE1 kIdp6NNEd8wsugYyyIYFsi1ylMCED3hZbSR8ZFsa/A4= / root GTS Root R4 mEflZT5enoR1FuXLgYYGqnVEoZvmf9c2bVBpiOjYQ0c=. FINDING: only 2 of the 5 shipped pins (WE1, GTS R4) were actually in the live chain. The other three — Lets Encrypt R3, ISRG Root X1, DigiCert Global Root G2 — appear nowhere in Supabase chain, so they could never satisfy a legitimate connection, but because the delegate accepts when ANY chain cert matches ANY pin, they meant a cert issued by any of those very widely-used public CAs would pass pinning. Removed them: strict tightening, zero rotation cost. Added the verified leaf SPKI as a pin. Kept GTS Root R4 deliberately as the rotation backup and documented that it is still broader than ideal (any GTS-issued cert satisfies it) — narrowing to leaf+intermediate would be stronger but leaves no fallback when the leaf rotates (~90d, GTS issues short-lived certs). Added scripts/verify-cert-pins.sh to reproduce this check; it prints the SPKI hash of every cert in the live chain and is the gate to re-run before flipping enforcement. REMAINING BLOCKERS (unchanged, cannot be done on this machine): the MITM-proxy-rejected-in-Release and proxy-succeeds-in-DEBUG ACs need macOS + Xcode + a proxy, and enforcement is still deliberately off via Config.certificatePinningEnforced pending IOS-AUDIT-SEC-013. Swift was edited but NOT compiled here (no Swift toolchain on Windows) — brace balance checked only; needs a macOS build before merge.

userStories.title: Enforce QueryCache size cap with LRU eviction

userStories.title: Base network retry decisions on structured status codes, not localized strings
userStories.description: As a user in any locale, I need retries to fire on real 5xx/timeout failures only so non-transient 4xx errors are not retried and retries work outside English.
acceptanceCriteria: Retry decision based on structured status code (PostgrestError/HTTP status), not localizedDescription substring matching

userStories.notes:
DONE (2026-06-25): NetworkRetry.isTransientError no longer substring-matches localizedDescription. Retries now branch on URLError.Code (timedOut, networkConnectionLost, notConnectedToInternet, cannotConnectToHost, cannotFindHost, dnsLookupFailed, secureConnectionFailed) and a structurally-extracted HTTP status (retry only >=500 or ==429; never other 4xx). An event titled '500' can no longer trigger a retry.

[prior] Evidence: NetworkRetry.swift:69-77 substring-matches localizedDescription for '500','502','connection','timeout' — locale-dependent and over-broad (an event named with '500' could be retried 3x with backoff).

userStories.title: Invoke DeepLinkHandler on URL and universal-link opens
userStories.description: As a user, I need shared event/restaurant links to open the right screen in-app so deep links and universal links work (the handler is currently dead code).
acceptanceCriteria: .onOpenURL calls DeepLinkHandler.shared.handle(url) after the Supabase auth handle
.onContinueUserActivity(NSUserActivityTypeBrowsingWeb) added for universal links
MainTabView observes consumeDestination() and navigates, clearing after navigation
Tapping desmoinespulse.com/events/<id> opens the event detail in-app
Unmatched URLs fall back to the in-app browser without crashing
userStories.notes: Evidence: DeepLinkHandler.shared.handle(url) and consumeDestination() have zero callers; DesMoinesInsiderApp.swift:84 .onOpenURL forwards only to SupabaseService.client?.handle(url); no onContinueUserActivity. Contradicts ios_prd.json IOS-012 (passes:true).

userStories.title: Handle notification taps and foreground presentation
userStories.description: As a user, I need tapping an event-reminder notification to open that event and foreground notifications to show a banner (no UNUserNotificationCenterDelegate exists today).
acceptanceCriteria: AppDelegate conforms to UNUserNotificationCenterDelegate and the delegate is set at launch
userNotificationCenter(_:didReceive:) routes userInfo['eventId'] to event detail via DeepLinkHandler
willPresent shows .banner,.sound for foreground notifications
Cold-launch from a notification lands on the right screen after init
Push notifications with a deep-link payload route correctly too
userStories.notes: Evidence: No UNUserNotificationCenterDelegate / didReceive anywhere; UNUserNotificationCenter.current().delegate never set. LocalNotificationService.swift:45 attaches userInfo['eventId'] but nothing consumes it. Unmet AC of ios_prd.json IOS-011.

userStories.title: Index events and restaurants into Spotlight
userStories.description: As a user, I need the app's core content (events, restaurants) discoverable in system Spotlight so I can find it from outside the app.
acceptanceCriteria: EventsViewModel/RestaurantsViewModel call SpotlightService.indexEvents/indexRestaurants after fetch, capped to a reasonable count
Searching an event/restaurant name in system Spotlight returns it
Index updates as content refreshes; stale items pruned
Indexing runs off the main actor and never blocks the list
userStories.notes:
VERIFIED DONE (2026-06-25): SpotlightService.indexEvents/indexRestaurants now have callers — EventsViewModel.swift:144 and RestaurantsViewModel.swift:112 fire-and-forget index on first/reset page load, mirroring the articles/hotels pattern (commit 3a677fa). No change needed.

[prior] Evidence: SpotlightService.indexEvents/indexRestaurants (SpotlightService.swift:14,59) have zero callers; only indexArticles/indexHotels are wired.

userStories.title: Make Spotlight results deep-link into the app
userStories.description: As a user, I need tapping a Spotlight result to open the matching detail screen so indexed content is actionable (depends on IOS-AUDIT-FEAT-002).
acceptanceCriteria: CSSearchableItemActionType user activity handled; CSSearchableItemActivityIdentifier parsed (e.g. event-<id>)
Routing via DeepLinkHandler opens the matching detail screen
Identifier parsing covers event/restaurant/article/hotel prefixes
Unknown identifiers fail gracefully to the home tab
userStories.notes:
VERIFIED DONE (2026-06-25): Full CSSearchableItemActionType path exists — DesMoinesInsiderApp.swift:114 onContinueUserActivity → DeepLinkHandler.handleSpotlightIdentifier (parses '<type>-<id>', routes event/restaurant/attraction) → MainTabView presents the detail. Covered by DeepLinkHandlerTests. No change needed.

[prior] Evidence: No CSSearchableItemActionType handling exists; even indexed articles/hotels can't open from Spotlight.

userStories.title: Make the Ask Pulse quota-exceeded upsell reachable
userStories.description: As a free user who exhausts Ask Pulse, I need an upgrade CTA instead of a raw error so the monetization moment actually fires.
acceptanceCriteria: AskPulseService.ask detects the 429/quota response and throws .quotaExceeded
The view presents a paywall/upgrade CTA (PaywallView) instead of a raw error string
lastUsage.remaining is surfaced to the user before exhaustion
VIP/unlimited users never hit the quota path
userStories.notes:
DONE (2026-06-25): AskPulseService.ask now wraps functions.invoke('discover-chat') and maps a 429 (FunctionsError.httpError code 429, with a defensive body-text fallback) to AskPulseError.quotaExceeded, so the existing tailored upgrade CTA in AskPulseView fires instead of a generic error. Request payload + success Response shape untouched.

[prior] Evidence: AskPulseView.swift:274 catches .quotaExceeded but AskPulseService.ask (AskPulseService.swift:73-104) never throws it — a 429 falls into the generic catch with no upsell. | UX-audit root cause (2026-06-24): AskPulseError.quotaExceeded is never thrown — AskPulseService.ask only throws .notConfigured, so a 429 from discover-chat surfaces as a generic FunctionsError and the tailored upsell catch at AskPulseView.swift:274 is unreachable. Fix must inspect the HTTP status/body and throw .quotaExceeded for the upsell to fire.

userStories.title: Wire (or remove) the Trip Planner soft-paywall seam
userStories.description: As a free user, I need the engagement-based soft paywall to participate in the Trip Planner flow, or the dead seam removed, so the frequency-capped upsell isn't misleadingly half-built.
acceptanceCriteria: A free user's first Trip Planner Generate attempt triggers the capped soft paywall once (considerAfterTripPlannerAttempt called), respecting maxPresentations/cooldownDays
Analytics logs source: 'trip_planner'
OR: the unused method is deleted with no dangling references
Existing hard-gate behavior remains coherent with whichever path is chosen
userStories.notes:
VERIFIED DONE (2026-06-25): SoftPaywallService.considerAfterTripPlannerAttempt() is wired at TripPlannerView.swift:274 — a free user's first attempt fires the frequency-capped soft upsell (3 lifetime / 7-day cooldown), with the hard .tripPlanner paywall as fallback when on cooldown/exhausted (commit FEAT-032). Seam is live, not dead. No change needed.

[prior] Evidence: SoftPaywallService.considerAfterTripPlannerAttempt() (SoftPaywallService.swift:35) has zero callers; TripPlannerView.swift:271 hard-gates free users immediately.

userStories.title: Create annual subscription SKUs and remove paywall workarounds
userStories.description: As a user, I need the Insider/VIP annual plans (and trial) to load so the contextual paywall can offer annual pricing instead of routing around the bug.
acceptanceCriteria: Annual SKUs created in App Store Connect with final immutable IDs; StoreKitService constants updated from placeholder format
availablePeriods(for:) returns [.monthly,.annual] for both tiers; products load in sandbox and production
PaywallView period toggle shows monthly + annual for Insider and VIP
annualSavingsPercent renders a real percentage
AdBannerView/InterstitialAdView workarounds that bypass PaywallView are removed
userStories.notes: Evidence: AdBannerView.swift:80-88 and InterstitialAdView.swift:57-59 bypass PaywallView because the annual SKU drops; annual IDs are placeholder-format (StoreKitService.swift:36-37 prod_insider_annual/prod_vip_annual) vs real monthly IDs.

userStories.title: Preselect the trial-eligible period on trial-led paywall contexts
userStories.description: As a user shown a trial-promising paywall, I need the trial copy and 'Start Free Trial' CTA to actually appear so we don't promise a trial that the monthly default hides.
acceptanceCriteria: Trial-oriented contexts (winBack, adFree, generic, onboarding) auto-prefer the period carrying an eligible intro offer (annual)
Any trial-promising context shows 'X-day free trial, then ...' and CTA 'Start Free Trial'
Trial-ineligible users see the normal price with no false promise
Monthly-only contexts unaffected
userStories.notes:
VERIFIED DONE (CODE REVIEW 2026-08-06): PaywallView.swift:213-217 takes preferredPeriod and seeds _selectedPeriod from it; :258-260 validates the seeded period against the products that actually loaded so it cannot stay .annual when no annual product exists. Both trial-led contexts pass .annual explicitly — OnboardingView.swift:64 (context: .onboarding) and SubscriptionStatusBanner.swift:66 (context: .winBack). NOTE: real-world effect is gated on IOS-AUDIT-FEAT-008 (annual SKUs do not exist in App Store Connect yet), but the :258 guard degrades correctly until they do, so this story's own criteria are met.

[prior] Evidence: Only annual SKUs carry introductoryOffer; PaywallView defaults selectedPeriod=.monthly (PaywallView.swift:201,217); winBack/adFree/generic don't pass preferredPeriod:.annual, so refreshTrialCopy() clears the trial. Depends on IOS-AUDIT-FEAT-008.

userStories.title: Replace the no-op CrashReportingService with real reporting
userStories.description: As the team, we need crashes and non-fatals reported so production purchase/restore failures are observable.
acceptanceCriteria: A crash reporter (Crashlytics or Sentry) is integrated, or recordError/non-fatals are routed via AppLogger + a server endpoint
StoreKit purchase/restore/verification failures are logged as non-fatals
User-id/tier attached for triage (privacy-compliant)
DEBUG builds don't pollute production crash data
userStories.notes:
DONE (2026-06-25): Replaced the no-op CrashReportingService stubs with a real Firebase-free first-party reporter (same public API). configure() installs NSSetUncaughtExceptionHandler + POSIX signal handlers that write an async-signal-safe marker then re-raise; recordError persists structured CrashRecord JSON (atomic, completeFileProtection) under Application Support; pendingRecords/flushPendingRecords/deleteRecord expose records for future backend upload. Wired configure()+setUserId into DesMoinesInsiderApp launch .task. Backend upload edge function is the documented next step. Added CrashReportingTests.

[prior] Evidence: CrashReportingService.swift:25,35,42,49 are all empty // TODO: Uncomment when Firebase is added — nothing is reported.

userStories.title: Surface StoreKit transaction-failure notifications to the user
userStories.description: As a user whose background/verification transaction fails, I need a non-blocking toast with a support reference so I'm not left without feedback.
acceptanceCriteria: MainTabView observes .storeKitTransactionFailed (like the .favoritesLimitReached pattern)
A non-blocking toast shows with a copyable support/transaction reference
It does not fire for normal user-cancellations
userStories.notes:
DONE (2026-06-25): MainTabView (the always-present root + existing NotificationCenter hub) now observes .storeKitTransactionFailed and shows a non-blocking error toast including the transaction id as a support reference, reusing the existing ToastOverlay system. StoreKitService already posted the notification.

[prior] Evidence: StoreKitService.handleTransactionFailure posts .storeKitTransactionFailed (StoreKitService.swift:389) with a transaction id but no view observes it.

userStories.title: Verify saved-search event-alert delivery end to end
userStories.description: As a user enabling event alerts, I need the full push path to work so the advertised 'saved searches & event alerts' feature actually delivers.
acceptanceCriteria: Enabling an alert both registers for push (depends on IOS-AUDIT-FEAT-001) and persists the flag
A new matching event produces a push (server alert job confirmed to exist)
UI reflects alert on/off state and ideally last-match time
Disabling an alert stops delivery
userStories.notes: Evidence: SavedSearchService.swift:6-7 stores an alert flag and notes server-side delivery, but push registration is broken (IOS-AUDIT-FEAT-001) and only triggered from saved-search enable. Copy promises the feature at SubscriptionView.swift:144.

userStories.title: Make the Surprise Me 'Save it' CTA actually save (or navigate)
userStories.description: As a user who taps the primary 'Save it — let's go' button on a Surprise Me pick, I need it to add the item to my favorites (or open its detail), because today it fires a success haptic, logs a 'saved' outcome, and dismisses without saving anything.
acceptanceCriteria: save(_:) in SurpriseMeView favorites the picked Event/Restaurant/Attraction via the existing FavoritesService (toggleFavorite/toggleRestaurantFavorite/etc.) based on pick.itemType BEFORE dismissing
The success haptic (UINotificationFeedbackGenerator .success) fires only after a real save succeeds; failures surface an error toast/state
Alternatively, if save is intentionally a navigate action, route to the picked item's detail via the app's NavigationPath instead of a bare dismiss
Outcome tracking (.saved) still fires, and the button label matches what it does
userStories.notes: Found by iOS UX audit. SurpriseMeView.swift:220 save(_:) calls notificationOccurred(.success) + track(outcome:.saved) + dismiss() with inline comment 'The actual favorite-add wiring lives in EventDetailView / RestaurantDetailView; for now, dismiss and let the user navigate.' The primary CTA adds nothing to favorites and offers no navigation — a dead-end. Confirmed by two independent audit passes. | DONE (2026-06-24): SurpriseMeView save now calls performSave() which favorites the pick via FavoritesService by item type (event/restaurant/attraction), guarding against toggling an already-saved item off; success haptic + track(.saved) + dismiss only on real save; limitReached dismisses for the app-level paywall; other errors show a 'Couldn't Save' alert + error haptic. get_surprise_pick returns only 'event'/'restaurant' (verified in migration).

userStories.title: Make Home 'For You' rail cards tappable to their detail screen
userStories.description: As a user, I need tapping a personalized 'For You' recommendation to open that item's detail, because the cards are currently rendered with no tap handling at all and there is no navigationDestination wiring for a recommendation id.
acceptanceCriteria: ForYouCard is wrapped in a Button/NavigationLink that opens the underlying Event/Restaurant/Attraction detail (resolving rec.id to the typed value HomeView's navigationDestination expects, fetching by id if needed)
Tapping any For You card navigates; the affordance is discoverable (chevron/pressed state)
No regression to the rail's horizontal scroll/paging
userStories.notes: Found by iOS UX audit. ForYouRail.swift:46 renders ForYouCard(rec: rec) with no NavigationLink/Button/onTapGesture. A code comment claims navigation 'lives in the .navigationDestination on the parent — we deep-link via the rec.id', but ForYouCard has no tap handling and no matching navigationDestination exists. The entire personalized rail is non-interactive. | DONE (2026-06-24): ForYouRail cards wrapped in NavigationLink(value: rec); added .navigationDestination(for: ForYouService.Recommendation.self) -> ForYouRecommendationDetailView which fetches the full Event by id via EventsService.fetchEvent(id:) with loading/failed/loaded phases. Self-contained so it works in Home and Dashboard stacks.

userStories.title: Fix the consent screen that can never dismiss after the user chooses
userStories.description: As a first-launch user, I need the consent gate to advance after I Accept/Decline/Save, because ConsentService is @Observable but its consent values are UserDefaults-backed COMPUTED properties (not tracked), and the app presents ConsentView with an empty onComplete closure — so the gate's needsConsentPrompt branch is never re-evaluated and the screen can sit forever.
acceptanceCriteria: Choosing Accept / Decline / Save on ConsentView reliably advances past the consent gate on a fresh install

Root cause fixed: either back ConsentService's consent values with stored (observation-tracked) properties that mirror to UserDefaults, OR pass a real onComplete from DesMoinesInsiderApp that flips an @State flag the gate observes — the empty { } at DesMoinesInsiderApp.swift:47 must do real work
Re-launching the app does not re-show the consent gate once completed
Manual verification documented (fresh-install run, choose each path)
userStories.notes: Found by iOS UX audit. ConsentService.swift:14-17 exposes hasCompletedConsent/*Consent as computed UserDefaults getters/setters; @Observable only tracks stored properties, so writes don't notify SwiftUI. DesMoinesInsiderApp.swift:47 presents ConsentView { } with an empty onComplete, and dismissal depends solely on needsConsentPrompt flipping — which never re-fires. Potential hard launch blocker. | DONE (2026-06-24): Added locally-observed `consentCompleted` @State in DesMoinesInsiderApp; ConsentView presented with `{ consentCompleted = true }` and gate condition is now `consent.needsConsentPrompt && !consentCompleted`. Persisted hasCompletedConsent still suppresses the prompt next launch.

userStories.title: Give 'Restore Purchases' in Settings real success/failure feedback
userStories.description: As a user restoring a subscription from Settings, I need a spinner and a result message, because the button calls restorePurchases() but SettingsView never reads StoreKitService.isLoading/errorMessage — so nothing visibly happens whether it succeeds, finds nothing, or fails (an App Store review expectation for restore).
acceptanceCriteria: Tapping Restore Purchases shows an in-progress indicator while StoreKitService.isLoading is true
On completion it presents a clear result: 'Subscription restored', 'No purchases to restore', or the StoreKitService.errorMessage on failure
Pattern mirrors PaywallView.restore() (PaywallView.swift:599-611) which already does this correctly
Restore-failure (e.g. AppStore.sync() network error) is distinguished from a genuinely empty entitlement, not both shown as 'nothing to restore'
userStories.notes: Found by iOS UX audit. SettingsView.swift:42-48 Button { Task { await storeKit.restorePurchases() } } with no read of the service's isLoading/errorMessage. restorePurchases() (StoreKitService.swift:273) sets errorMessage and toggles isLoading but the view ignores both. Related: PaywallView.restore() masks AppStore.sync() failures as 'No active subscription found' (same fix for the distinguish-failure criterion). | DONE (2026-06-24): SettingsView restorePurchases() helper shows a ProgressView label + 'Restore Purchases' result alert; branches on storeKit.errorMessage (sync failure) vs currentTier != .free (restored) vs free (nothing found).

userStories.title: Stop the Favorites undo flow from dropping queued backend deletes
userStories.description: As a user removing several favorites quickly, I need each removal to actually persist, because starting a new undo cancels the previous removal's commitTask without ever committing it — the item is gone from the local array but viewModel.remove*Favorite is never called for it, so it silently resurrects on next load.
acceptanceCriteria: Removing a second favorite while a prior undo is still pending flushes (commits) the prior removal to the backend instead of just cancelling its task
After multiple quick removals with no undo taps, all removed items are gone from the server on reload (optimistic UI matches server truth)
Tapping Undo still restores exactly the most-recent removal
Implemented via a pending-removal queue or immediate commit-of-prior when a new removal starts (FavoritesView.swift:75/95/113)
userStories.notes: Found by iOS UX audit. FavoritesView.swift removeEventWithUndo/removeRestaurantWithUndo/removeAttractionWithUndo (lines 75, 95, 113) call undoState?.commitTask?.cancel() before replacing undoState, but never await the prior remove* call. Data-integrity bug: the optimistically-removed item is dropped from the array yet never deleted on the backend. | DONE (2026-06-24): Added flushPendingRemoval() in FavoritesView; the three remove*WithUndo paths now flush (commit) the prior pending removal to the backend before starting a new undo instead of cancelling its commitTask uncommitted.

userStories.title: Make the Ask Pulse pick card open the item detail (dead NavigationLink)
userStories.description: As a user, I need tapping the chevron on an Ask Pulse pick to open that event/restaurant/attraction, because the card is a NavigationLink(value: pick) with a 'Tap to open this … in detail' hint, but no .navigationDestination(for: Pick.self) exists anywhere, so the link routes nowhere.
acceptanceCriteria: Tapping an Ask Pulse pick card navigates to the matching detail screen, resolving pick.itemType+itemId to the real Event/Restaurant/Attraction (fetch by id as picks carry only id/type)
Add .navigationDestination(for: AskPulseService.Pick.self) on the AskPulseView NavigationStack, OR remove the chevron link and the 'tap to open' accessibility hint so there's no dead affordance
The accessibility hint matches the actual behavior
userStories.notes: Found by iOS UX audit. AskPulseView.swift:300 NavigationLink(value: pick) { chevron } inside the view's own NavigationStack (line 30); project-wide grep shows no navigationDestination(for: Pick.self). AskPulsePickCard advertises accessibilityHint 'Tap to open this … in detail' but nothing happens. | DONE (2026-06-24): Added .navigationDestination(for: AskPulseService.Pick.self) -> AskPulsePickDetailView, which resolves the pick by itemType to Event/Restaurant/Attraction via fetchEvent/fetchRestaurant/fetchAttraction(id:) with loading/failed/loaded phases. Chevron NavigationLink now reaches a real detail.

userStories.title: Apply (or remove) the Min Rating and Max Distance event filters
userStories.description: As a user adjusting the premium Min Rating and Max Distance filters, I need them to change my results, because both increment the active-filter count and re-fetch but the filtering is never applied: minRating is explicitly skipped, and maxDistance silently no-ops when location permission isn't granted.
acceptanceCriteria: Min Rating: either filter events by rating in applyPremiumFilters, or remove the Min Rating control until events expose a rating — no control that shows an active-filter chip but returns identical results

Max Distance: when maxDistance is set but LocationService.userLocation is nil, request location permission and/or surface a hint ('Enable location to filter by distance') instead of silently returning everything
Each premium filter visibly changes results when toggled, or is removed
userStories.notes: Found by iOS UX audit. EventsViewModel.swift:255 applyPremiumFilters has '// minRating is available for future use when events have ratings' and never filters by it, though FilterSheet binds it to a premium slider and counts it active. EventsViewModel.swift:246 distance filter runs only 'if let userLocation = LocationService.shared.userLocation', so it's a no-op without a fix while still counting as active. | DONE (2026-06-24): Resolved via removal — the Min Rating + Max Distance event controls existed only in the orphaned FilterSheet (deleted, see FEAT-021). Event has no rating field so min-rating could never work; with FilterSheet gone nothing sets EventsViewModel.minRating/maxDistance, so no active-filter chip appears for a no-op filter. (Attractions rating filter is a separate, working AttractionsViewModel path, untouched.)

userStories.title: Make the VerifyEmailView refresh as promised, or fix its copy
userStories.description: As a user on the verify-email screen, I need it to detect verification, because the copy says 'This screen will refresh automatically once verification completes' but there is no polling, scenePhase refresh, or session refresh — it only clears when the email link is tapped on the SAME device, stranding users who verify elsewhere.
acceptanceCriteria: On returning to foreground (scenePhase == .active) the view refreshes the session/user and advances if verified
A manual 'I've verified — refresh' button is available and triggers a session refresh
Optionally a lightweight poll while the screen is shown; copy is accurate to the behavior
Users who verify on another device can reach the app without signing out
userStories.notes: Found by iOS UX audit. VerifyEmailView.swift:50 promises auto-refresh but the view has no polling Task, no .onChange(scenePhase), and no refresh call. Verification only clears via onOpenURL→client.handle(url) in DesMoinesInsiderApp.swift:88-90 (same-device link tap). Only escape today is 'Use a different account' (sign out). | DONE (2026-06-24): Added AuthService.refreshUser() (auth.refreshSession() → updates currentUser, returns verified bool). VerifyEmailView now polls every 5s via .task, refreshes on scenePhase==.active, and has an 'I've verified — refresh' button; the app shell routes away once needsEmailVerification flips false. Copy is now accurate.

userStories.title: Present the orphaned FilterSheet or delete it
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I need FilterSheet to either be reachable or removed, because it is never presented anywhere in the running app (Home filtering lives in EventInlineFilters) yet it ships its own PremiumGate, distance/rating sliders, and Clear/Done toolbar — dead UI whose bugs are invisible because nobody can open it.
acceptanceCriteria: Either FilterSheet is actually presented (e.g. from a Filters toolbar button with a real sheet binding) and its apply/cancel semantics work, OR FilterSheet.swift is deleted
If kept, its Min Rating / Max Distance controls do something real (see IOS-AUDIT-FEAT-019) and it carries no dead PremiumGate path
Relates to IOS-AUDIT-UX-006 (apply/cancel semantics) — that work only matters if this sheet is reachable
userStories.notes: Found by iOS UX audit. Grep for 'FilterSheet(' matches only FilterSheet.swift's own #Preview (line 219). Shipping an unreachable filter screen with a paywall is a maintenance trap; its filter bugs are hidden because the screen can't be opened. | DONE (2026-06-24): Deleted Views/Search/FilterSheet.swift — confirmed referenced only by its own declaration + #Preview (live Home filters use EventInlineFilters). Removes unreachable UI that shipped its own PremiumGate and the no-op distance/rating sliders. XcodeGen globs the DesMoinesInsider directory so no project file edit needed.

userStories.title: Implement Right Now ribbon counts or remove the count-driven copy
userStories.description: As a user, I need the Right Now ribbon to show the real, count-driven headlines it was built for ('4 patios open within 10 min of you'), because every template's countFetcher returns 0, so the count copy is dead and the ribbon always falls back to generic phrasing.
acceptanceCriteria: Each template's countFetcher returns a real count (patios, cozy, comfort food, live music, lunch, open-now), OR the count-bearing copy paths are removed and the ribbon commits to generic copy
When a count is available the specific headline ('N spots open near you' / 'N patios open within …') renders instead of the generic fallback
No dead count-formatting code left carrying a permanent 0
userStories.notes: Found by iOS UX audit (two passes). RightNowRibbon.swift:186 — every Template countFetcher is { return 0 } (patios/cozy/comfortFood/liveMusic/lunch/openNow), so headlineFn always takes the generic branch and the count-based copy (documented at lines 102-103) never appears. | DONE (2026-06-24): Removed the dead count machinery from RightNowRibbon (countFetcher/estimateCount all returned 0) — headlineFn no longer takes a count, matchingCount state removed, refresh no longer calls estimateCount, and all 6 templates commit to their generic copy. No dead count-formatting code remains.

userStories.title: Surface Trip Planner load failures and roll back failed optimistic writes
userStories.description: As a Trip Planner user, I need errors to show and the UI to match the server, because itinerary fetch failures render as a blank itinerary, and optimistic reorder/delete operations swallow backend errors so the on-screen state silently diverges and reverts on next load.
acceptanceCriteria: ItineraryDetailView distinguishes 'fetch failed' from 'genuinely empty': fetchItems signals failure (throw/optional) and the view shows an error+retry state instead of a blank body when online with no items (TripPlannerService.swift:106 currently returns [] on RPC error)
Reorder (move/persistOrder) reports success/failure; on failure it shows a toast and reloads to server truth rather than logging only in DEBUG (TripPlannerService.swift:156)

Trip delete awaits the backend result before mutating savedTrips (or re-inserts + shows an error on failure) so deleted trips don't reappear unexplained (TripPlannerView.swift:311, TripPlannerService.swift:143)
userStories.notes: Found by iOS UX audit. ItineraryDetailView.swift:187 sets loadFailed only when items.isEmpty && !network.isConnected; an online RPC failure yields a blank itinerary. move()/persistOrder and deleteTrips mutate local state optimistically and swallow errors (DEBUG-only logging), so the visible order/list can permanently disagree with the server. | DONE (2026-06-24): TripPlannerService.fetchItems now throws (caller distinguishes fetch-failure→loadFailed error+retry from genuinely empty); persistOrder returns Bool and deleteTrip returns Bool (@discardableResult). ItineraryDetailView.move reloads server truth + shows an error toast on persist failure (added toastOverlay + refetchItems). TripPlannerView.deleteTrips awaits each delete, and on any failure reloads server truth and sets errorMessage instead of silently dropping the trip.

userStories.title: Gate pull-to-refresh haptics on actual success across remaining screens
userStories.description: As a user, I need pull-to-refresh to signal success only when the refresh succeeded, because Hotels, Weekend, and Articles fire UINotificationFeedbackGenerator().notificationOccurred(.success) unconditionally even when the view model set an errorMessage — the exact false-success anti-pattern fixed elsewhere under IOS-AUDIT-UX-005.
acceptanceCriteria: HotelsView, WeekendView, and ArticlesView branch on viewModel.errorMessage == nil to play .success vs .error after refresh
DealsView's .refreshable closure gets success/error haptic feedback (currently none)
Behavior matches the already-fixed RestaurantsView/AttractionsView pattern
userStories.notes: Found by iOS UX audit. HotelsView.swift:76, WeekendView.swift:62, ArticlesView.swift:79 all call notificationOccurred(.success) unconditionally while their VMs set errorMessage on failure (HotelsViewModel:82, WeekendViewModel:52, ArticlesViewModel:106). DealsView.swift:64 has no refresh haptic at all. | DONE (2026-06-24): HotelsView/ArticlesView/WeekendView refresh haptics now branch on viewModel.errorMessage == nil ? .success : .error (canonical UX-005 pattern). DealsView .refreshable gained the same success/error haptic.

userStories.title: Show a stale-data error banner instead of a misleading empty state
userStories.description: As a user whose refresh fails while a filter is active, I need to see the real error, because Deals and Weekend hide a genuine load error behind a 'No Deals Found / clear filters' or featured-rails-only view when filtered/section data is empty but other data loaded.
acceptanceCriteria: DealsView surfaces the stale-data error banner when errorMessage != nil even if some allDeals exist but filteredDeals is empty, instead of showing 'No Deals Found' (DealsView.swift:25)

WeekendView decouples its error banner from isEmpty: an inline error+retry shows when errorMessage != nil and day sections are empty, even if featured rails populated (WeekendView.swift:29; isEmpty at WeekendViewModel.swift:25-27)
Genuine empty (no error) still shows the empty state; failures always offer retry
userStories.notes: Found by iOS UX audit. DealsView.swift:25 only shows the error when allDeals.isEmpty. WeekendView.swift:29 gates errorBanner on 'errorMessage != nil && isEmpty' where isEmpty also requires featured rails empty — so an events-fetch failure with featured rails present hides the error and shows zero events with no explanation. | DONE (2026-06-24): WeekendView shows errorBanner inline when errorMessage != nil && populatedDays.isEmpty (events failed but featured rails loaded). DealsView shows errorBanner instead of 'No Deals Found' when filteredDeals empty and errorMessage != nil. Both banners already include Retry.

userStories.title: Stop showing the password-reset success message inside a 'Sign In Error' alert
userStories.description: As a user requesting a password reset, I need a neutral success confirmation, because the success path routes its copy through setError(), which sets showError, fires an error haptic, and is rendered by an alert titled 'Sign In Error' — so a successful reset looks like a failure.
acceptanceCriteria: resetPassword() success uses a separate info/success channel (e.g. infoMessage) with a neutral alert title, not setError
No error haptic on the success path
Error cases still use the error alert + haptic
userStories.notes: Found by iOS UX audit. AuthViewModel.swift:204-205 success calls setError('Password reset email sent...'); setError (222-226) sets showError=true + notificationOccurred(.error); AuthView.swift:179 renders .alert('Sign In Error', isPresented: $viewModel.showError). | DONE (2026-06-24): AuthViewModel gained infoMessage/showInfo + setInfo() (success haptic); resetPassword success now calls setInfo. AuthView renders an 'Email Sent' info alert separate from 'Sign In Error'.

userStories.title: Animate the Discover action-bar Skip/Save/Boost like a swipe
userStories.description: As a user, I need tapping the Skip/Save/Boost buttons to fly the card off like a gesture swipe, because the handlers call viewModel.skip/like/boost directly and snap the top card away instantly, while gesture commits animate — and the intended bridge methods exist but are never called.
acceptanceCriteria: The action buttons drive SwipeCardStack's programmatic commit path (programmaticSkip/programmaticLike/programmaticBoost, SwipeCardStack.swift:175-177) so a tap produces the same animated dismissal as a swipe
The programmatic trigger is wired via a binding/closure from DiscoverView to SwipeCardStack (DiscoverView.swift:219)
No visual snap/jump on button taps
userStories.notes: Found by iOS UX audit. DiscoverView.swift:219 button handlers call viewModel.skip/like/boost directly (instant removal); the animated programmatic* methods in SwipeCardStack are defined but grep confirms zero call sites. | DONE (2026-06-24): SwipeCardStack gained a @Binding command (enum Command: skip/like/boost) consumed via .onChange to drive the existing programmaticSkip/Like/Boost animated commit (guarded against re-entrancy). DiscoverView action buttons now set swipeCommand instead of calling viewModel directly, so a tap animates the fly-off identically to a swipe (commit() still fires the haptic + viewModel.skip/like/boost).

userStories.title: Prevent the 'all done' empty-state flash during a Discover boost
userStories.description: As a user swiping up to boost, I need the deck to stay coherent, because boost() sets deck = [] then refetches without setting isLoading, so the deckArea momentarily shows the 'You've seen everything / Reset deck' empty state before new cards arrive.
acceptanceCriteria: boost() sets isLoading = true before clearing/refetching and clears it when fetchMore completes (DiscoverViewModel.swift:235), OR keeps the previous deck visible until the new batch is ready
The all-done empty state never appears mid-boost
Genuine end-of-deck still shows the empty state
userStories.notes: Found by iOS UX audit. DiscoverViewModel.swift:235 boost() does deck = [] then Task { fetchMore() } with no isLoading; DiscoverView.swift:158-162 then falls through to the empty/all-done branch because 'isLoading && deck.isEmpty' is false. | DONE (2026-06-24): DiscoverViewModel.boost() sets isLoading=true before clearing the deck and clears it after fetchMore(), so the loading state shows instead of flashing the all-done empty state mid-boost.

userStories.title: Show a loading state during the search debounce instead of a blank screen
userStories.description: As a user opening saved-search results (or typing in Search), I need a loading indicator during the 300ms debounce, because the view shows neither ProgressView, empty state, nor results in that window — a deep-linked saved search lands on a blank screen.
acceptanceCriteria: SavedSearchResultsView renders a loading state until the first search completes rather than a blank body (SavedSearchResultsView.swift:36)
SearchViewModel exposes an initial loading flag (e.g. hasLoadedOnce / isSearching defaulting true on first run) so the 300ms debounce window shows ProgressView (SearchViewModel.swift:50-53)
Genuinely-empty results still show the empty state after the search resolves
userStories.notes: Found by iOS UX audit. SavedSearchResultsView.swift:36 .task sets viewModel.searchText = savedSearch.query; performSearch sleeps 300ms before isSearching=true, so during the window isSearching=false & hasSearched=false → none of the states render. | DONE (2026-06-24): SearchViewModel.performSearch now sets isSearching=true synchronously before the 300ms debounce (and clearResults sets it false), so SavedSearchResultsView/SearchView show their ProgressView during the debounce window instead of a blank screen.

userStories.title: Fix the Trip Planner share-link failure shown under a 'Calendar' alert
userStories.description: As a user whose itinerary share-link fails, I need an accurately-titled error, because share() reuses calendarMessage and the only alert is titled 'Calendar', so a share failure is presented as a calendar error.
acceptanceCriteria: Share errors use their own state/alert (e.g. shareError) or a neutral title, separate from calendarMessage (ItineraryDetailView.swift:211, alert at 117)
Calendar-add errors remain under the Calendar alert; share errors read as share errors
userStories.notes: Found by iOS UX audit. ItineraryDetailView.swift:211 share() failure sets calendarMessage='Couldn't create a share link...'; the only alert is .alert('Calendar', isPresented: ... calendarMessage ...) at line 117. | DONE (2026-06-24): ItineraryDetailView share() now sets a separate shareErrorMessage surfaced by a 'Couldn't Share' alert instead of reusing calendarMessage under the 'Calendar' alert.

userStories.title: Auto-scroll Ask Pulse to the latest message and picks
userStories.description: As a user, I need the Ask Pulse conversation to scroll to the newest content, because the chat is a plain ScrollView with no ScrollViewReader/scrollTo, so the new user bubble, the 'Thinking…' indicator, and the rendered picks stay below the fold after sending.
acceptanceCriteria: Conversation wrapped in ScrollViewReader; the last conversation item / picks section has a stable .id
proxy.scrollTo(...) is called in send() and when isLoading changes so newest content scrolls into view (AskPulseView.swift:32)
Scrolling works with the keyboard up; picks rendered below the input become visible
userStories.notes: Found by iOS UX audit. AskPulseView.swift:32 conversation is ScrollView { VStack { conversationView; picksSection; followUpChips } } with no ScrollViewReader/scrollTo (grep confirms). | DONE (2026-06-24): AskPulseView conversation wrapped in ScrollViewReader with a bottom Color.clear anchor (id); scrollToBottom(proxy) called .onChange of conversation.count, picks.count, and isLoading so the newest message/Thinking…/picks scroll into view.

userStories.title: Add feedback and confirmation to review report and delete actions
userStories.description: As a user reporting or deleting a review, I need confirmation, because report() swallows its result with try? and shows nothing, and delete-own-review fires immediately with no confirm and no success feedback — despite the service throwing specifically so the UI can confirm.
acceptanceCriteria: Reporting a review shows a success confirmation ('Thanks, we'll review this') and an error toast on failure; report() stops discarding the throw with try? (ReviewsViewModel.swift:102; RatingsService.reportRating throws by design)
Deleting your own review shows a confirmationDialog first (consistent with Report) and a success toast after reload (ReviewsSection.swift:145, ReviewsViewModel.swift:92)
userStories.notes: Found by iOS UX audit. ReviewsViewModel.swift:102 report uses try? (no feedback) though RatingsService.swift:87 documents it throws so the UI can confirm. ReviewsSection.swift:145 Delete fires with no confirmation; deleteOwnReview only sets errorMessage on failure, no success toast. | DONE (2026-06-24): ReviewsViewModel.report and deleteOwnReview now return Bool and stop swallowing the throw; ReviewsSection added a delete confirmationDialog and toastOverlay, showing success/error toasts for both report and delete.

userStories.title: Make 'Sort by nearby' await a real GPS fix instead of a fixed 1s sleep
userStories.description: As a user enabling nearby sorting on Neighborhoods, I need reliable sorting, because enableNearby() requests permission then sleeps a fixed 1s and refreshes — if the first fix takes longer the refresh runs with no location, sorting silently doesn't apply, and the toggle reverts with no feedback.
acceptanceCriteria: enableNearby() awaits an actual location update (async stream / continuation from LocationService) rather than Task.sleep(1s) (NeighborhoodViewModel.swift:66)
A spinner/disabled state shows on the button until a fix arrives or it times out with a message
On a slow cold-GPS fix, sorting still applies once the location resolves
userStories.notes: Found by iOS UX audit. NeighborhoodViewModel.swift:66 enableNearby(): requestPermission(); try? await Task.sleep(.seconds(1)); await refresh() — refresh runs with userLocation==nil on slow fixes, usingLocation stays false, button reverts silently. | DONE (2026-06-24): NeighborhoodViewModel.enableNearby now sets isLoading, waits (bounded) for the permission dialog to resolve, then awaits a real fix via LocationService.getCurrentLocation() (which has its own timeout and sets userLocation) before refresh — replacing the fixed 1s sleep.

userStories.title: Fix the Surprise Me reveal animation sticking at opacity 0 on 'Try another'
userStories.description: As a user tapping 'Try another', I need each new pick to animate in, because the reveal is driven by .onAppear which may not re-fire when only the pick value changes — leaving the new card stuck at opacity 0/scale 0.92.
acceptanceCriteria: The reveal animates from data, e.g. .onChange(of: pick?.id) or .task(id: pick?.id), not .onAppear (SurpriseMeView.swift:117)
Every new pick (initial roll and 'Try another') re-triggers the reveal reliably
userStories.notes: Found by iOS UX audit. SurpriseMeView.swift:117 revealCard uses .scaleEffect(revealed ?1:0.92).opacity(revealed ?1:0) with .onAppear setting revealed=true; load() resets revealed=false on every roll but tryAnother reuses the same view, so onAppear may not re-fire. | DONE (2026-06-24): SurpriseMe revealCard reveal now driven by .task(id: pick.id) instead of .onAppear, so 'Try another' re-triggers the scale/opacity animation per pick.

userStories.title: Don't freeze the entire Search screen when offline
userStories.description: As an offline user, I need to compose a query and browse suggestions, because .disabled(!isConnected && !hasSearched) wraps the whole NavigationStack including the search field, so I can't type, tap a Popular Category, or tap a Recent Search — all local-only actions.
acceptanceCriteria: The offline disabled state is scoped to network-dependent results only (or removed), not the .searchable field and suggestions (SearchView.swift:75)
Offline users can type a query and tap categories/recents; the existing 'You're Offline' empty state shows on submit
userStories.notes: Found by iOS UX audit. SearchView.swift:75 .disabled(!NetworkMonitor.shared.isConnected && !viewModel.hasSearched) wraps the whole NavigationStack content including .searchable and the suggestions list. | DONE (2026-06-24): Removed the broad .disabled(!isConnected && !hasSearched) on SearchView so offline users can type and tap suggestions/recents; the searchable prompt + 'You're Offline' empty state already communicate offline state on submit.

userStories.title: Fix Map time-slider label wording and add a clustered-pin selection fallback
userStories.description: As a map user, I need accurate labels and selectable pins, because the time-slider pill says events are 'open at' a time (events have no open hours — they're filtered to a ±2h window), and pins clustered tightly at one coordinate can never be separated by zoom, making them permanently unselectable.
acceptanceCriteria: Time-slider pill reworded so semantics match filtering, e.g. 'N events near {time} · M restaurants open' (MapTimeSlider.swift:64; event filtering at MapViewModel.swift:256-268)

When a tapped cluster's members share (nearly) one coordinate, present a disambiguation list/sheet instead of only zooming, so co-located items are selectable (EventMapView.swift:104; shouldCluster at MapViewModel.swift:319)
userStories.notes: Found by iOS UX audit. MapTimeSlider.swift:64 '\(eventCount) events + \(restaurantCount) restaurants open at ...' mislabels event filtering. EventMapView.swift:104 only renders individual tappable Annotations when !shouldCluster; zoomTo halves the span and can't resolve a co-located cluster, leaving members unselectable. | DONE (2026-06-24): MapTimeSlider pill reworded to 'N events near {time} · M restaurants open' (no false 'open at' for events). Added MapMember enum + MapViewModel.members(in:) resolver and a ClusterDisambiguationSheet: tapping a cluster of <=25 lists its members (selecting sets selectedEvent/Restaurant/Attraction) so co-located pins stay selectable even though shouldCluster is total-count based; larger clusters still zoom.

userStories.title: Clamp the paywall billing period after products load and distinguish restore failure
userStories.description: As a user on a contextual/onboarding paywall, I need the displayed period to match the selected product, because clampPeriod() is not called after loadProducts(), so an initial preferredPeriod of .annual can persist with the toggle hidden while price/footer fall back to the monthly product.
acceptanceCriteria: clampPeriod() is invoked at the end of the .task after loadProducts() so the initial preferredPeriod is validated against available periods (PaywallView.swift:213-218, .task at 256-259)
