Root cause was NOT one bug but a class of four missing/renamed named exports that resolve to `undefined` once bundled (React #130): (a) src/hooks/useAuth.ts re-exported `useAuthStatus`, renamed to `useAuthFlags` by WEB-PERF-005 — this poisoned the barrel for all 56 importers and is what actually took down /advertise; (b) SearchSection imported `fetchRestaurantFilterFacets`, never exported from useRestaurants.ts — crashed the HOMEPAGE into the route error boundary; (c) AdminAutonomy imported { SEOHead } as named from a default-only module — this broke `npm run build` outright, i.e. main did not build; (d) Advertise ICON_MAP was missing the `sidebar` PlacementType key, so Object.values(PLACEMENT_SPECS) yielded icon:undefined. Added scripts/check-import-exports.mjs (wired into `npm run validate`) to statically catch this whole class, since tsc does not flag it and esbuild strips types without checking. Verified against a production build: /advertise and /business-partnership both render full content, no error boundary, no console errors.

userStories.title: Fix event listing→detail mismatch (listed events 404 as 'Event Not Found')
userStories.description: As a visitor, I need every event that appears in a listing to open a working detail page, because at least one event surfaced by filters ('Ringling Bros...') links to an 'Event Not Found' page, turning the primary events happy-path into a dead end.
acceptanceCriteria: Reproduce: /events?category=Family surfaces the Ringling Bros. card, whose detail URL (/events/ringling-bros-and-barnum-bailey-presents-the-greatest-show-on-earth-des-moines-2026-10-01) renders 'Event Not Found'

Determine whether the listing query and the detail query disagree (slug generation mismatch, detail lookup filtering on a stricter condition e.g. status/visibility/date the list does not apply, or a stale/orphaned row) and fix so a listed event always resolves
Add a data-integrity guard: an event that cannot resolve a detail page must not be rendered as a clickable card (or the detail lookup must use the same predicate as the list)
Backward-compat per CLAUDE.md: additive-only DB changes; no edge-function request/response shape changes; no tightened validation that could break shipped iOS/Android event fetches
Add a test that asserts every card in a listing response resolves to a 200 detail render for a representative sample
npm run validate passes
userStories.notes: FOUND 2026-07-13 (5-PERSONA QA PASS — production live; persona: Marcus / weekend dad). SEVERITY: HIGH — breaks the core events flow and torches trust. Evidence: Family filter returns 1 result; clicking it navigates to the slug above and shows the 'Event Not Found — This event may have ended or been removed' state. Likely related to WEB-QA-003 (events querying is unhealthy). Note the surfaced event is also dated 2026-10-01 (~3 months out) which is a separate content-freshness concern, not the bug here. | RESOLVED 2026-07-18 (claude/web-qa-p1-fixes). Root cause: EventDetails had no detail query at all — it called useEvents() (unbounded, extra visibility filters) and did a client-side Array.find over a slug computed from each row, so any row the list showed but that hook did not return 404d. Two independent failure modes: (1) predicate asymmetry — the list applied neither is_merged nor is_hidden while useEvents applied both; (2) the unbounded fetch was silently truncated at PostgREST max-rows, so far-future events were never in the array. Fix: new src/hooks/useEventBySlug.ts does a bounded server-side lookup, parsing the -YYYY-MM-DD off the slug and querying only that date window with the SAME visibility predicates as the list; EventsPage list now also applies .neq(is_merged)/.neq(is_hidden). NOTE for future work: events.date is a timestamptz, not a DATE — an inclusive `.lte(date, YYYY-MM-DD)` bound resolves to midnight and drops same-day evening events (an evening-Central event stores as the next day in UTC). Uses an exclusive `.lt` upper bound one day past the window. Covered by tests/route-smoke.spec.ts, which caught exactly that timestamptz case on a real row.

userStories.title: Fix homepage events + active-ad fetch errors on load (useEvents / useActiveAds)
userStories.description: As a visitor, I need the homepage to load real event and ad data without errors, because on every homepage load the console logs database query failures ('useEvents: Database query error', 'Error fetching events', 'useActiveAds:fetchActiveAd Error fetching active ad'), which correlates with a suspiciously thin surface ('2 Events Today' against a marketed '500+ events weekly').
acceptanceCriteria: Reproduce and capture the actual error payload behind the logged 'Object' for useEvents and useActiveAds (log the message/code/details, not just the object, wrapped in import.meta.env.DEV per CLAUDE.md)

Root-cause the homepage events query failure — note the featured restaurants/attractions/playgrounds REST calls succeed (200) while the events request does not even appear as a completed network request, suggesting the query errors before/at fetch (malformed select, RLS denial, or bad column/filter)
Homepage loads with zero error-level console messages from useEvents and useActiveAds; events widgets populate; the 'Events Today' / 'New This Week' counters reflect real data
useActiveAds fetch failure must degrade gracefully (it currently still shows a fallback house/partner ad) but should stop logging an error on the happy path
Reconcile the '500+ events weekly' homepage claim with actual inventory once the query is fixed (adjust copy or ingestion), so the trust stats are defensible
Backward-compat per CLAUDE.md: additive-only DB changes; no tightening of get_active_ads / events shapes that shipped mobile binaries read
npm run validate passes
userStories.notes:
CLOSED 2026-08-22 (claude/prd-p1-loop). All seven ACs verified with evidence, not inference.

AC1 - payload captured: get_active_ads returned 42702 'column reference "campaign_id" is ambiguous / It could refer to either a PL/pgSQL variable or a table column.' Not the PGRST203 this story recorded; that overload was already resolved and its removal is what exposed this.
AC2 - root-caused, and the events half was a false lead: the events projection returns 206 through the anon key. Only the ads RPC was failing. Fixed by 20260822000001, applied to production.
AC3 - both halves. First: tests/route-smoke.spec.ts:59, the test named for this story, asserts zero console errors matching /useEvents|useActiveAds|PGRST/ on / and it PASSES on the merged commit (it was the single failing assertion in an otherwise 79/79 suite). Second: the trust-strip count queried through the anon key with the same is_merged/is_hidden predicate returns Content-Range 0-0/19, matching a direct database count of 19 events today. Real data, not a confident zero.
AC4 - useActiveAds now degrades without logging: log.error fires only on an RPC error, and an empty result returns null cleanly. All four placements return [] instead of erroring.
AC5 - reconciled against measured inventory (341 upcoming events, 48 in the next 7 days, 480 restaurants, 22 attractions, 69 playgrounds). Three overstated claims corrected; the important one was SEOTools.tsx, which GENERATES public/llms.txt and would have silently reverted the WEB-SEO-015 fix on the next regenerate.
AC6 - CREATE OR REPLACE with a byte-identical signature and the same seven returned columns. Shipped mobile binaries went from receiving an error to receiving rows or an empty set.
AC7 - npm run validate exits 0 (0 errors, 5121 warnings).

AC5 DONE 2026-08-22 - the last open AC on this story. Measured against the production database rather than estimated: 341 upcoming events, 48 in the next 7 days, 140 in the next 30, 188 added in the last 30, 1246 rows total; 480 restaurants, 22 attractions, 69 playgrounds.

The literal '500+ events weekly' string was already removed from EnhancedHero and SocialProof by earlier work (48 in the next 7 days - it was off by more than 10x). But the audit had never been carried past those two files, and three overstated claims were still rendering:
  - SEOTools.tsx GENERATES public/llms.txt and still emitted '500+ monthly events tracked' (188), '50+ attractions documented' (22) and '100+ playgrounds mapped' (69). public/llms.txt itself was corrected under WEB-SEO-015, so regenerating and publishing would have SILENTLY REVERTED that fix. This is the important one - a corrected artifact with an uncorrected generator behind it.
  - GEOContent.tsx renders on the homepage (src/pages/Index.tsx), aimed at AI crawlers, claiming '500+ venues' against 480. Now 450+. Its '1,000+ events' claim is TRUE (1246) and was left alone.
  - RealTimePage.tsx claimed '500+ Businesses Tracked' against 480 restaurants + 22 attractions = 502. True by two rows and false the moment one is deleted, which is not a defensible trust stat. Now 450+.

All figures now match public/llms.txt exactly (250+/450+/20+/65+) so the generator reproduces the corrected file rather than a third set of numbers, and the provenance is in a code comment above generateLLMsTxt. VERIFIED: public/llms.txt's own counts check out against the database independently of the sitemaps WEB-SEO-015 used - 341 vs '250+', 480 vs '450+', 22 vs '20+', 69 vs '65+'.

WEB-SEO-015 already names the permanent fix: generate llms.txt from the database alongside the sitemaps. Until then this drifts again.

ADS HALF FIXED 2026-08-22 (claude/prd-p1-loop). This story's 2026-08-11 measurement is now out of date in both directions.

1. supabase/migrations/20260718000001_resolve_get_active_ads_overload.sql IS applied to production - confirmed by diffing supabase_migrations.schema_migrations against disk. The PGRST203 overload ambiguity this story recorded is gone.
2. Applying it exposed a DIFFERENT bug in the same RPC: 42702, ambiguous campaign_id between the RETURNS TABLE OUT parameter and ad_impressions.campaign_id in the two frequency-cap subqueries. That is what has actually been erroring on every page load since. Fixed by 20260822000001 and applied to production; all four placements now return [] through PostgREST rather than an error. See WEB-CI-026 for the full trace - the same bug was the single failing assertion in the required smoke gate.

AC4 SATISFIED: useActiveAds now degrades to the house/partner ad WITHOUT logging an error, because log.error fires only on an RPC error and an empty result returns null cleanly.

PREMISE CORRECTION for this and every story that repeats it: '.this environment has no production DB access' is FALSE. .env carries SUPABASE_DB_URL and psql is installed. Read access and, with the owner's approval, migration application both work from here.

STILL OPEN: AC5, reconcile the '500+ events weekly' homepage claim against real inventory.

RE-CONFIRMED LIVE 2026-08-11 (claude/prd-p1-loop), still blocked, unchanged since July. Captured from the browser console on a production build against the real backend, on BOTH / and /events:
  [useActiveAds:fetchActiveAd] Error fetching active ad {placementType: top_banner, message: Could not choose the best candidate function between ... p_placement_type, p_session_id => ...}
  [useActiveAds:fetchActiveAd] Error fetching active ad {placementType: below_fold, ...}
That is the PGRST203 get_active_ads overload ambiguity this story already documents. supabase/migrations/20260718000001_resolve_get_active_ads_overload.sql is written and still not applied, so the ads half remains blocked exactly as recorded — the hub is disarmed and this environment has no production DB access.

The EVENTS half is confirmed healthy in the same measurement: /events issues 9 REST requests for 40 cards with a 200/206 on the events projection, and the homepage events queries return 200. AC3's counter half is also now satisfied by the WEB-QA-024 rewrite — the trust-strip counts carry the same is_merged/is_hidden predicate as /events and surface an error state instead of rendering 0.

[prior] FOUND 2026-07-13 (5-PERSONA QA PASS — production live; personas: all, first seen by Marcus/Gary). SEVERITY: HIGH — core content path is erroring. Evidence: on https://desmoinesinsider.com load, console errors from vendor-three-*.js: '[useEvents] Database query error: Object', 'Error fetching events: Object', '[useActiveAds:fetchActiveAd] Error fetching active ad Object' (ad error recurs on /events too). Network capture shows featured restaurants/attractions/playgrounds at 200 but NO completed events REST request. Homepage shows only '2 Events Today' vs the '500+ events weekly' trust claim. | PARTIALLY RESOLVED 2026-07-18 (claude/web-qa-p1-fixes) — LEFT passes:false DELIBERATELY. (A) EVENTS HALF: FIXED AND VERIFIED. Root cause was `archived_at` in EVENT_LIST_COLUMNS (src/lib/listColumns.ts) — that column lives on archived_events/event_archive and has never existed on public.events, so PostgREST rejected the whole projection with 42703. That is also why restaurants/attractions/playgrounds returned 200 while events did not: only the events projection carried the bad column. All /rest/v1/events requests now return 200/206. Introduced by WEB-PERF-001 (commit 6c2c1a94) when select(*) was replaced with explicit projections. (B) ADS HALF: code fixed, BLOCKED ON DEPLOY. Confirmed live as HTTP 300 / PGRST203: two get_active_ads overloads coexist — get_active_ads(TEXT) from migration 20260227000000 and the canonical get_active_ads(placement_type, text, uuid) — so every single-arg call is ambiguous. CREATE OR REPLACE did not replace the original because the param type differs. Wrote supabase/migrations/20260718000001_resolve_get_active_ads_overload.sql to drop the superseded TEXT overload (restorative, not destructive — the call currently fails for web AND every shipped mobile binary; passes scripts/check-migration-safety.mjs). THIS STORY CANNOT CLOSE UNTIL THAT MIGRATION IS APPLIED. Also fixed in code: `sidebar` is a front-end-only placement never added to the placement_type enum, so useActiveAds now skips the RPC for it rather than erroring on every render; both hooks now log message/code/details/hint instead of a bare object (the collapsed `Object` is why 42703/PGRST203 went undiagnosed). (C) NEWLY FOUND, NOT YET FILED: homepage also logs `column search_analytics.query does not exist` (42703) — same bug class, separate table, still open. (D) The 500+ events weekly copy reconciliation AC is untouched.

userStories.title: Restaurants list: blank result count + 'Most Popular' sort surfaces only 'Opening Soon' venues
userStories.description: As a visitor browsing restaurants, I need an accurate result count and a sort that leads with places I can actually visit, because the results header renders a blank count ('___ found') and the default 'Most Popular' sort puts three 'Opening Soon' venues at the top.
acceptanceCriteria: The restaurants results header shows the real count (e.g. 'N found') — the number currently renders blank while the equivalent events page correctly shows 'N results'; align the two

Default 'Most Popular' sort deprioritizes or clearly separates 'Opening Soon' (not-yet-open) venues so currently-operating restaurants lead, OR the sort semantics are made explicit; a first-time visitor should see places they can eat at now
Per-card date chips (e.g. '3/30/2026', '4/28/2026') are labeled so their meaning (opening date vs added date) is unambiguous, or removed if not user-facing
npm run validate passes
userStories.notes: FOUND 2026-07-13 (5-PERSONA QA PASS — production live; personas: Priya / newcomer, Zoe). SEVERITY: MED. Evidence: /restaurants results bar reads 'Most Popular ▾   found' with no number rendered before 'found'; top 3 cards (Le's Chinese Bar-B-Que, Marv's Mainstreet Dive, Bonchon) all carry an 'Opening Soon' badge under the 'Most Popular' sort; cards show unlabeled dates 3/30/2026 & 4/28/2026. Contrast: /events correctly renders '1 results' (though see WEB-QA-006 for the plural bug). | RESOLVED 2026-07-18 (claude/web-qa-p1-fixes). (1) BLANK COUNT: useRestaurants selected with { count: "planned" } — a pure planner row-estimate that PostgREST returns as NULL whenever it has no usable statistic for the filtered query, hence "___ found". Switched to "estimated" (exact under PostgREST threshold, planner estimate only for large sets) which keeps the WEB-PERF-009 intent of not forcing a full-table exact count on every filter/sort, and the header now falls back to restaurants.length so a null count can never render blank again. Verified live: header reads "434 found". (2) SORT: the root cause was NOT null popularity_score ordering (checked: zero NULL scores in the table, and the direct query already leads with open venues). The default sort routes through the get_rotated_restaurants RPC, which shuffles by a rotation seed so the top varies per visit and ignores status entirely — so "Most Popular" was neither popularity-ordered nor open-first. Two changes: added deprioritizeUnvisitable(), a STABLE partition sinking opening_soon/closed below visitable venues while preserving rotation variety within each group (verified live: 2 unvisitable in the raw first 10 -> 0 after, 24 of 434 sunk); and relabeled the option from "Most Popular" to "Recommended", since calling a seeded shuffle "Most Popular" told visitors the top three were the city most popular when the order was largely arbitrary. "Highest Rated" remains the deterministic quality sort. (3) DATE CHIPS: RestaurantOpenings rendered a bare "3/30/2026" next to a calendar glyph, ambiguous against the "Added <date>" footer directly below; now reads "Opens <date>" / "Opens <timeframe>" and the icon is aria-hidden. Verified live: zero bare-date chips remain. NEWLY FOUND, NOT FIXED: get_rotated_restaurants returns an inconsistent total_count — 480 when called with limit_count 8 but 434 with limit_count 1000, i.e. the count is entangled with the limit. The page shows 434, which does match rows actually returned, but the RPC total_count is unreliable and fixing it needs a migration.

userStories.title: Resolve AI-planning expectation gap (marketed as free, hard-paywalled)
userStories.description: As a first-time visitor, I need the homepage's prominent AI promises to match what I can actually do, because 'AI Plan My Night', 'Let AI build your itinerary', and '24/7 AI Assistant' are front-and-center free-looking CTAs, but clicking through to the Trip Planner hits an immediate Insider-only paywall ('Upgrade to Unlock') with no free taste.
acceptanceCriteria: Decide and implement the intended funnel: either (a) give anonymous/free users a limited free itinerary (e.g. 1 trip) before the paywall, or (b) label the homepage AI CTAs as a premium feature up front so the paywall is not a surprise
The gold 'AI Plan My Night' homepage CTA and the '24/7 AI Assistant' stat set accurate expectations for a logged-out visitor
Preserve the existing good AI-accuracy disclaimer on the Trip Planner ('AI output may be inaccurate... confirm hours/prices... nothing here is a paid endorsement unless labeled')
Backward-compat per CLAUDE.md: no tightening of generate-itinerary quota/shape below what shipped iOS/Android binaries rely on (see WEB-SEC-002 tier quotas)
npm run validate passes
userStories.notes:
RE-VERIFIED LIVE 2026-08-22 (claude/prd-p1-loop). The gap is unchanged and every element of it is still true in production. Recording the current state so AC1's decision can be made without re-deriving it; NOT deciding the funnel, because AC1 is explicitly a product call.

MARKETING SIDE - all four claims confirmed present in the HTML a LOGGED-OUT visitor receives on desmoinesinsider.com:
  'First AI-Powered Conversational City Guide'
  'AI Plan My Night' / 'Let AI build your itinerary'  (the gold homepage CTA)
  '24/7 AI Assistant'  (trust-strip stat)

PRODUCT SIDE - src/pages/TripPlanner.tsx:92-93 reads hasFeature('trip_planner') and wraps the planner in <PremiumGate requiredTier="insider"> at :333. useSubscription.ts:231 puts 'trip_planner' in the isInsiderOrHigher group, so FREE AND ANONYMOUS USERS GET ZERO ITINERARIES - not a reduced quota, none. That matches the documented tier design (Free: no trip planner; Insider: 5/month; VIP: unlimited), so this is a marketing/product mismatch rather than a bug in the gate.

WHAT THE DECISION ACTUALLY IS, framed from the code: AC1 offers (a) a limited free itinerary before the paywall or (b) accurate logged-out copy. Option (a) is a one-line change to the feature map plus a quota - 'trip_planner' would move out of the isInsiderOrHigher group and gain a free allowance, and the existing quota machinery already exists for the Insider 5/month case. Option (b) touches EnhancedHero copy only and ships today. They are not equivalent in cost, and (b) does not require abandoning (a) later.

AC3 - the AI-accuracy disclaimer on the Trip Planner is still present and should survive either option.
AC4 - neither option touches generate-itinerary's quota or response shape, so the shipped iOS/Android binaries are unaffected either way.

FOUND 2026-07-13 (5-PERSONA QA PASS — production live; personas: Priya / newcomer, Gary / skeptic). SEVERITY: MED — conversion friction / expectation mismatch, not a defect. Evidence: homepage headlines 'First AI-Powered Conversational City Guide', gold CTA 'AI Plan My Night / Let AI build your itinerary', stat '24/7 AI Assistant'; /trip-planner immediately shows an Insider-gated card 'AI Trip Planner — Insider members get 5 trips/month, VIP unlimited' with 'Upgrade to Unlock' and no free path. Product decision, flagged for triage.

userStories.notes: FOUND 2026-07-13 (5-PERSONA QA PASS — production live; personas: Marcus, Zoe). SEVERITY: LOW (cosmetic/polish). Evidence: /events?category=Family header 'Family Events / 1 events in Des Moines'; that event card shows a placeholder calendar glyph instead of an image; banner ad slot renders 'AD' badge overlapping the ad headline ('...scover your path less traveled'); selecting Light in the theme dropdown turns the top nav white while the hero section remains dark navy. | RESOLVED 2026-07-18 (claude/web-qa-p1-fixes). (1) PLURALS: added src/lib/pluralize.ts (pluralize/formatCount, handles -es/-ies suffixes and a small irregulars map; deliberately not i18n — swap for Intl.PluralRules if a second locale ever ships) and applied it at 8 user-facing count sites across EventsPage (x2), Attractions, EventsNearMe, MonthlyEventsPage, EventsThisWeekend, EventsToday, NeighborhoodsPage and EnhancedGroupPlanner, including the FAQ answer strings that read "We have 1 events happening today". userStories.title: QA coverage follow-up: verify mobile-device rendering and logged-in / uncovered flows
userStories.description: As the platform owner, I need the surfaces the 5-persona pass could not reach to be verified, because that walkthrough ran at desktop viewport width and logged-out, leaving true mobile rendering and authenticated features unconfirmed.
acceptanceCriteria: Verify true mobile rendering (real device or DevTools device emulation at iPhone/Pixel widths) for the homepage, events list/detail, restaurants, pricing, and auth — the persona pass could not force a sub-400px viewport (browser reported ~1544px), so responsive layout, the mobile nav/hamburger, and touch targets are unverified
Verify logged-in flows: Free-tier limits (3 favorites, 0 alerts/saved searches per subscription config), saved searches, review submission + AI auto-moderation (WEB-AUTO-009), and social sharing
Verify B2B/contact surfaces not reached: contact form submission, Business Partnership page, and reviews moderation UI
Verify SEO landing pages and secondary sections not reached: /events/today, /restaurants/open-now and similar, Attractions/Explore, and Articles/blog
File any new defects found as their own WEB-QA-* stories with severity and evidence
This is a verification/testing story — no product code change required unless a defect is found
userStories.notes: FOUND 2026-07-13 (5-PERSONA QA PASS — production live). SEVERITY: N/A (coverage gap). The persona pass (Marcus/mobile dad, Priya/newcomer, Gary/skeptic, Zoe/power user, Diana/business owner) covered homepage, events list+detail+filters, trip-planner, restaurants, pricing, auth, and theme toggle, but could not verify: true mobile viewport rendering (window stayed desktop-width), any authenticated feature (no account created — signup is out of scope for automated QA), contact/reviews submission, Stripe checkout, and SEO landing/attractions/articles pages. | RESOLVED 2026-07-18 (claude/web-qa-p1-fixes) — with one AC explicitly NOT covered; see below. MOBILE RENDERING (AC1) VERIFIED: swept 14 routes x 3 viewports (320x568, 375x667 iPhone SE, 393x851 Pixel 5) with isMobile/hasTouch, measuring document overflow, error boundaries and HTTP status. Found real horizontal overflow on SIX routes at EVERY phone width - /events, /restaurants, /attractions, /articles, /playgrounds, /neighborhoods - up to 215px at 320px wide. Root-caused and FIXED as WEB-QA-008 (FAQ accordion questions could not wrap because the shadcn Button base sets whitespace-nowrap). The sweep went from 18 problematic combinations to 1 after the fix, the survivor being a 1px rounding artifact. Mobile nav verified: bottom nav present on every sampled route, labelled hamburger present everywhere except /auth (appears intentional). Touch targets measured and filed as WEB-QA-009. SEO LANDING + SECONDARY SECTIONS (AC4) VERIFIED: /events/today, /restaurants/open-now, /attractions, /articles, /playgrounds, /neighborhoods all return 2xx and mount without an error boundary at all three phone widths. B2B/CONTACT SURFACES (AC3) PARTIALLY VERIFIED: /advertise, /business-partnership and /contact all mount cleanly at phone widths (/advertise only because WEB-QA-001 fixed its React #130 crash earlier in this same branch). NOT verified: actual contact-form SUBMISSION and the reviews moderation UI - both require either sending real data to production or an authenticated admin session. LOGGED-IN FLOWS (AC2) NOT VERIFIED AT ALL. This is the significant coverage gap and it is unchanged from the original persona pass. Free-tier limits (3 favorites, 0 alerts/saved searches), saved searches, review submission with AI auto-moderation (WEB-AUTO-009) and social sharing all require an authenticated account. The story notes state signup is out of scope for automated QA, and creating an account against the production database is not something to do unilaterally. Everything behind auth therefore remains unconfirmed and needs a human pass or a seeded test account. STATIC ANALYSIS FOUND SOMETHING THE SWEEP ALONE WOULD NOT HAVE: while verifying the favorites surface, the regenerated types showed the favorites write path and read path target different tables (filed as WEB-QA-010) - so even a manual logged-in pass of AC2 would likely find restaurant/attraction favorites silently broken. DEFECTS FILED PER AC5: WEB-QA-008 (mobile overflow, MED, fixed), WEB-QA-009 (touch targets, LOW-MED), WEB-QA-010 (favorites read/write mismatch, MED), WEB-QA-011 (get_rotated_restaurants inconsistent total_count, LOW), WEB-QA-012 (search_analytics 42703, LOW), WEB-SEC-020 (unmapped ownership resource types, MED latent). METHOD NOTE: naive overflow detection is misleading and cost two wrong diagnoses before the real one. Carousel children inside an overflow-x:auto container legitimately extend past the viewport, and position:fixed elements with inset-x-0 size to the EXPANDED layout viewport, so they report widths of exactly viewport + overflow and look like the biggest offenders while actually being symptoms. Any future overflow hunt must exclude clipped ancestors and fixed subtrees before ranking candidates.

userStories.notes: FOUND 2026-07-18 during WEB-QA-007 mobile verification (claude/web-qa-p1-fixes). SEVERITY: LOW-MED. Measured at 375x667 with isMobile/hasTouch: 9-22 sub-44px interactive elements per page (/ 11, /events 22, /restaurants 21, /pricing 9, /auth 11). NOTE ON STANDARD: WCAG 2.1 AA (2.5.8) requires only 24x24, which these mostly meet, so this is NOT an AA failure - 44x44 is WCAG AAA (2.5.5) and the Apple/Google platform guidance. CLAUDE.md states a mobile-first, touch-targets-first standard, which is why this is filed. A repo .touch-target utility (min-h-[44px] min-w-[44px]) already exists and is the intended fix. Mobile nav verified working: bottom nav present on all sampled routes and a labelled hamburger present everywhere except /auth, which appears intentional. | PARTIAL 2026-07-18 (claude/web-qa-p1-fixes) — LEFT passes:false ON PURPOSE. The AC asks for a 44x44 minimum across mobile controls; what landed covers the highest-traffic ones, not all of them, so claiming this story is done would be false. WHAT WAS FIXED. Added a .tap-area-44 utility that overlays a centred, invisible 44x44 hit region via ::after instead of growing the element. That distinction matters: the pre-existing .touch-target utility works by enlarging the control itself, which is wrong for icon-sized controls — a 24px close button or 36px social icon would visibly change size and reflow the surrounding layout. The overlay is scoped to (pointer: coarse) so a mouse never gets an expanded region that could overlap adjacent controls. Applied to the header logo (32x32), the cookie banner close button (24x24) and the three footer social links (36x36). VERIFIED: each still RENDERS at its original size while its effective tap area measures 44x44. Separately bumped min-h-[44px] on the event date-preset chips (were 92x38), the restaurant quick chips, and the Event/Restaurant inline category filters (were 122x38) — verified live, "Today" now measures 92x44. WHAT IS NOT FIXED, AND WHY THE STORY STAYS OPEN. Dozens of controls remain under 44px, spread across many components — pagination links, sort/select triggers, "Load More" buttons, newsletter inputs (mostly 36-42px tall with adequate width) and a long tail of icon buttons. Fixing them all is a broad sweep across shared components with real desktop-regression risk, and it was not attempted here. ONE CATEGORY SHOULD BE CLOSED AS A DOCUMENTED EXCEPTION RATHER THAN FIXED: roughly 21 per page are inline text links inside running copy (Privacy Policy 65x15, footer nav links 89x19, the contact email 155x16, "Forgot password?" 110x20, breadcrumb "Home" 38x20). WCAG 2.5.8 explicitly exempts inline links in a block of text, and enlarging them would break line flow; applying the overlay to them would be actively harmful, since it would collide with neighbouring text and steal its clicks. That reasoning is recorded in the utility comment in index.css so nobody applies it there later. ALSO STILL OPEN from this story AC: the residual 1px horizontal overflow on /attractions at 320px is unchanged (the 42-combination sweep still reports exactly that one item, down from 18 before WEB-QA-008). | COMPLETED 2026-07-18 (claude/web-qa-p1-fixes), second pass. Measured inventory of distinct sub-44px-height controls across /, /events, /restaurants, /attractions, /pricing and /auth went 15 -> 5, and all 5 survivors are the documented-exception category (below). THE LEVERAGE WAS IN THE SHARED PRIMITIVES, not in individual pages. Added a `coarse:` Tailwind variant (@media (pointer: coarse)) and applied `coarse:min-h-[44px]` to the shadcn Button default/sm sizes, Input, and the Select trigger. That one change fixed 8 of the 15 at once. The variant matters: a blanket min-height would have visibly loosened dense admin and toolbar layouts on desktop, which is presumably why nobody wanted to touch these primitives before. Verified both directions — on desktop (pointer: fine) the overlay computes to display:none and control heights are unchanged; on mobile the select trigger measures 44 and the overlay is active. FOR CONTROLS THAT CANNOT GROW, used the .tap-area-44 overlay from the first pass (invisible centred 44x44 ::after, coarse-pointer only): the pricing Switch (24px tall by design — a taller switch would look wrong beside its label) and the card FavoriteButton (36x36, sits on card imagery in a fixed corner, so growing it would cover the photo and shift the badges). FOLLOWED THE EXISTING CONVENTION RATHER THAN ADDING A SECOND ONE: the Restaurants view-mode toggles were 32x32, and I first applied the overlay — then found EventsPage already solves the identical widget with `h-11 w-11 sm:h-8 sm:w-8` (44px on mobile, compact on desktop). Reverted to match that pattern, since two different solutions for the same widget is worse than either one. THE 5 REMAINING ARE A DELIBERATE, DOCUMENTED EXCEPTION — four are text links styled as text ("Events" in the footer, "View All Featured", the "Home" breadcrumb, and "Forgot password?"), all 20px tall. WCAG 2.5.8 AA explicitly exempts inline links in a block of text, these already meet the 24x24 AA floor in the axis that matters, and enlarging them would break line flow. Applying the overlay to them would be actively harmful — it would collide with adjacent text and steal its clicks, which is warned about in the utility comment in index.css. The fifth is a whole-card <a> at 42px, 2px short, where the entire card is already the tap area. ALSO CLOSED FROM THIS STORY AC: nothing changed for the residual 1px overflow on /attractions at 320px — the 42-combination sweep still reports exactly that one item and it remains a sub-pixel rounding artifact, not a layout defect. Build clean, validate clean, strict ratchet holding at the 88-error baseline.

userStories.title: Favorites write path and read path target different tables, so restaurant/attraction favorites never appear
userStories.description: As a signed-in user, I need my saved favorites to show up in My Favorites, because the button that saves them writes to a different table than the view that lists them.
acceptanceCriteria: Identify the canonical favorites table (content_favorites appears to be the intended destination) and migrate reads and writes onto it
useFavorites (used by every FavoriteButton) currently writes ONLY to user_event_interactions
FavoritesView reads user_restaurant_interactions and user_attraction_interactions; the latter does not exist in the schema at all
Restaurant and attraction favorites round-trip end to end after the fix
Backward-compat per CLAUDE.md: additive-only DB changes, dual-write across releases if the storage table changes
userStories.notes: FOUND 2026-07-18 during WEB-DB-003 types regeneration (claude/web-qa-p1-fixes). SEVERITY: MED - a shipped feature that silently does nothing for two of three content types. Evidence: src/hooks/useFavorites.ts queries only user_event_interactions (lines 23, 42, 86). src/components/FavoritesView.tsx reads user_restaurant_interactions (line ~55) and user_attraction_interactions (line ~82). The regenerated types.ts confirms user_attraction_interactions does not exist, so that query always errors; the code swallows it via a debug log and returns [], which is why this never surfaced as a visible error. A generic content_favorites table exists and looks like the intended destination. The one remaining .from(... as any) cast in the codebase is on this line and is deliberately retained with an explanatory comment - do not remove it without fixing the write path first. | RESOLVED 2026-07-18 (claude/web-qa-p1-fixes). CORRECTION TO MY OWN ROOT CAUSE ABOVE — the diagnosis I filed this story with was partly WRONG and the note is left in place rather than rewritten so the error is visible. I claimed useFavorites (used by every FavoriteButton) writes only to user_event_interactions, so neither read path could ever match. That is not right: FavoriteButton has TWO paths. EventFavoriteButton uses useFavorites -> user_event_interactions, but non-event content goes through a separate hook, useContentFavorites, which correctly writes to content_favorites with (user_id, content_type, content_id). So the WRITE side was never broken. THE ACTUAL DEFECT WAS READ-SIDE ONLY: FavoritesView queried user_restaurant_interactions (a table nothing writes to) and user_attraction_interactions (a table that does not exist at all), instead of content_favorites where the writes actually land. Both queries then swallowed their errors via a debug log and returned [], which is why saved restaurants and attractions silently never appeared and no error was ever visible. FIX: both queries now read content_favorites filtered by content_type. Implemented as a TWO-STEP fetch (collect content_ids, then select the content rows by .in("id", ids)) rather than an embedded join, because content_favorites.content_id is polymorphic — it points at whichever table content_type names — so there is no foreign key for PostgREST to traverse. Verified live: the embedded form `restaurants:content_id(*)` fails with PGRST200 "Could not find a relationship", while the two-step form returns OK against both restaurants and attractions. Errors are now logged with message/code/details/hint instead of being swallowed. This also removed the last `.from(... as any)` table cast in the codebase — it only existed to reference a table that does not exist, so WEB-DB-003 is now fully clean at 0 such casts. VERIFICATION LIMIT, STATED PLAINLY: the query shapes are verified against the live database and both steps return OK, but the full round-trip (favorite a restaurant, see it in My Favorites) needs an authenticated session with stored favorites. content_favorites currently returns 0 rows to an anonymous client, both because there is no seeded data and because RLS would hide other users rows regardless. That is the same authenticated-coverage gap tracked in WEB-QA-007 AC2 and it is NOT closed by this story.

userStories.title: Default rating filter silently hides every unrated restaurant (46 of 480)
userStories.description: As a visitor, I need the restaurants result count to be trustworthy, because the RPC backing the default sort reports a different total depending on the page size requested.
acceptanceCriteria: get_rotated_restaurants returns a total_count representing all matching rows, independent of limit_count/offset_count
Reproduce: same filters with limit_count 8 returns total_count 480, while limit_count 1000 returns 434 rows and total_count 434
Reconcile against the direct query count (480 non-merged restaurants) and determine which filter accounts for the 46-row difference
Backward-compat per CLAUDE.md: the RPC is called by shipped clients - behavioural fix only, no signature change
userStories.notes: FOUND 2026-07-18 during WEB-QA-004 (claude/web-qa-p1-fixes). SEVERITY: LOW - the number currently rendered (434) does match the rows actually returned, so the UI is self-consistent; the defect is that total_count is entangled with the limit and so cannot be trusted as a real total. Fixing it needs a migration to the RPC, which is why it was not folded into WEB-QA-004. | RESOLVED 2026-07-18 (claude/web-qa-p1-fixes) — AND THE PREMISE I FILED THIS STORY WITH WAS WRONG. The original note is left above rather than rewritten, so the mistake stays visible. This is the second story I filed with an incorrect root cause (see also WEB-QA-010). THE RPC IS FINE. get_rotated_restaurants uses COUNT(*) OVER () on the filtered set, which is limit-independent by construction. Called with identical filters at limit_count 8, 30, 500 and 1000 it returns total_count = 480 every single time. My original 480-vs-434 observation compared two different contexts — a node script against the browser — and I wrongly attributed the difference to limit_count. There was never a total_count bug. THE REAL DEFECT, which that wrong measurement happened to expose: the app ALWAYS sent min_rating and max_rating, because filters.rating defaults to [0, 5] and the code only checked `rating.length === 2` before forwarding it. The RPC predicate is `(min_rating IS NULL OR r.rating >= min_rating)`, and for a restaurant with a NULL rating that comparison evaluates to NULL, so the row is dropped. The "no filter" default therefore silently excluded every unrated restaurant. Exactly 46 of 480 — verified three ways: rating IS NULL count = 46, 480 - 434 = 46, and calling the RPC with min/max NULL returns 480 while min=0/max=5 returns 434. Those 46 are disproportionately the newest listings, so roughly 10% of inventory — including the freshest — was invisible on the default restaurants page. FIX IS CLIENT-SIDE, NO MIGRATION NEEDED (unlike what this story assumed): a hasRatingFilter() guard treats the full [0, 5] range as "not filtered" and sends NULL, on BOTH the RPC path and the direct-query fallback, which had the same bug via .gte/.lte. VERIFIED IN THE RUNNING APP: /restaurants now returns 480 rows with total_count 480 and the header reads "480 found" (was 434), and all 46 previously-hidden unrated restaurants are present in the payload. WORTH RECORDING: the strict-mode ratchet added in WEB-CI-007 immediately caught a regression in MY OWN fix — useRestaurants went 1 -> 5 errors because hasRatingFilter returned a plain boolean, which does not narrow `number[] | undefined` under strictNullChecks, so the `rating[0]` accesses right after it were unsafe. Converting it to a type predicate (`rating is [number, number]`) brought it back to the 88-error baseline. That is the ratchet doing exactly the job it was built for, on real work rather than an injected probe.

userStories.title: Homepage logs 42703: column search_analytics.query does not exist
userStories.description: As the platform owner, I need the homepage free of database errors, because a search-analytics query references a column that does not exist and errors on every load.
acceptanceCriteria: Identify the caller issuing the search_analytics query and reconcile it with the actual table columns
Homepage loads with no 42703 error from search_analytics
Same bug class as WEB-QA-003 (a projection naming a nonexistent column) - check sibling analytics queries for the same drift
npm run validate passes
userStories.notes: FOUND 2026-07-18 while verifying WEB-QA-003 (claude/web-qa-p1-fixes). SEVERITY: LOW - degrades silently, no visible breakage. Evidence: browser console on / logs "Error fetching search data: {code: 42703, message: column search_analytics.query does not exist}". This is the same defect class as the archived_at bug fixed in WEB-QA-003: a query naming a column the table does not have, which PostgREST rejects wholesale. Now that types.ts is regenerated (WEB-DB-003), the real column set is available to check against. | RESOLVED 2026-07-18 (claude/web-qa-p1-fixes). MUCH WIDER THAN THE REPORTED SINGLE COLUMN. The real search_analytics schema is (clicked_event_id, clicked_position, created_at, id, results_count, search_filters Json, search_query, user_id). The code referenced query, category, location, price_filter, date_filter, session_id and clicked_result_id — of everything it touched, only results_count and user_id actually existed. Four call sites were wrong: the INSERT in useAnalytics.trackSearch plus SELECTs in useSearchInsights, useSimplePersonalization and usePersonalizedRecommendations. THE INSERT NEVER WORKED, so no search analytics has ever been recorded — confirmed against the live database, where the table returns 0 rows. It was silenced by an `as never` cast on the insert payload, which is exactly the escape hatch that let the drift ship. FIX: search_query for the query text; the facet values (category/location/dateFilter/priceRange) and the session id now go into the search_filters JSON column, and readers derive them back out of it. clickedResultId is deliberately NOT written to clicked_event_id — that column is a foreign key to events, and a search result can be a restaurant or attraction, which would violate the constraint; it stays in search_filters until a content-type-agnostic column exists. VERIFIED AGAINST THE LIVE DATABASE, not just type-check: the new query shapes return OK, the old shape still reproduces the exact reported error (42703 column search_analytics.query does not exist), and the homepage now logs zero search_analytics errors. ADJACENT FINDING while verifying: the homepage console went from 323 errors to 15, because most of them were a "Maximum update depth exceeded" render loop in SmartEventNavigation that I INTRODUCED in the WEB-PERF-013 TanStack migration — returning `data?.events ?? []` handed consumers a new array identity on every render, re-firing their dependent effects forever. Fixed with module-level stable empty constants in useEvents and useAdvancedSearch (useTrending already had one). The remaining 15 are the known unapplied-migration ad errors plus a fetchPriority React warning. A separate page-view tracking defect found at the same time is filed as WEB-QA-013.

userStories.title: Resolve the three unmapped resource types in the security ownership map before wiring it up
userStories.description: As the platform owner, I need every ownable resource type to resolve to a real table, because three of them currently map to null and their ownership checks can only deny.
acceptanceCriteria: advertisement, trip_plan and event_alert map to real tables carrying the owner column OWNERSHIP_COLUMNS expects, or the resource types are removed from OwnableResource
Verify the chosen owner column identifies the same principal the check assumes - a table whose user_id refers to a different entity would make the check fail OPEN
useResourceOwnership currently has zero consumers; resolve this BEFORE wiring the module into any surface
type-check passes with the map still typed against keyof Database public Tables
userStories.notes: FOUND 2026-07-18 during WEB-QUAL-004 (claude/web-qa-p1-fixes). SEVERITY: MED (latent). Retyping getTableName from Record<OwnableResource, string> to the generated table-name union made the compiler reveal six entries pointing at nonexistent tables. Three were renames and are now fixed after verifying each carries user_id: review -> event_reviews, rating -> user_ratings, favorite -> content_favorites. The remaining three (advertisement, whose owner column is campaign_id; trip_plan; event_alert) have no identified equivalent - curated_itineraries and advertising_packages exist but are editorial/pricing tables, not per-user records - so they are mapped to null deliberately rather than guessed. null makes isResourceOwner log an explicit error and deny (fails closed, safe). Guessing a wrong table is the dangerous direction and could fail OPEN. The module is dead code today, which is the only reason this is not urgent. | RESOLVED 2026-07-18 (claude/web-qa-p1-fixes) via the AC second option ("or the resource types are removed from OwnableResource"), and the module turned out to be considerably more broken than this story described. THE STORY SAID 3 OF 15 WERE BROKEN. Verifying every remaining pair against the LIVE schema — not just the generated types — found 7 of 15 were. Beyond the three with no table (advertisement, trip_plan, event_alert), four more had owner columns that do not exist: events.created_by, restaurants.claimed_by, attractions.created_by and discussion_replies.user_id all returned 42703. isResourceOwner would have errored and denied for those too, so the module could only ever have worked for 8 of the 15 types it advertised. EVENTS, RESTAURANTS AND ATTRACTIONS ARE NOT OWNABLE AT ALL. Dumped the full column list for each: there is no created_by, claimed_by, user_id or any equivalent. They are crawler-ingested editorial content that nobody owns in the database, so an ownership check on them cannot be expressed, never mind pass. Removed from OwnableResource rather than papered over. If a "claim your business" feature is wanted, it needs a schema change first — there is no claims table either. discussion_reply was a real fix rather than a removal: the column is created_by, not user_id. FINAL STATE: OwnableResource is down to 9 types, and ALL 9 are verified end to end against the live database — table exists AND owner column exists (review->event_reviews.user_id, rating->user_ratings.user_id, favorite->content_favorites.user_id, discussion->event_discussions.user_id, discussion_reply->discussion_replies.created_by, photo->event_photos.user_id, campaign->campaigns.user_id, profile->profiles.id, saved_search->saved_searches.user_id). The table map is typed Record<OwnableResource, TableName> with NO `| null`, so the compiler now rejects both a nonexistent table name and a null placeholder. IMPORTANT DISCOVERY FOR WHOEVER WIRES THIS UP — a server-side RPC already exists that does this job properly: user_owns_resource(p_table_name, p_resource_id, p_user_id, p_owner_column) returns boolean. Delegating isResourceOwner to it would be strictly better than maintaining a client-side table map: it is authoritative, it cannot drift out of sync with the schema the way this map did, and a client-side ownership check is advisory anyway since RLS is the real gate. That rewrite is a design change beyond this story AC, so it was not done here, but it is the recommended direction and useResourceOwnership still has zero consumers, so nothing is blocked by leaving it. METHOD NOTE: an early check that parsed types.ts with a regex reported ALL 12 owner columns missing, which was a false alarm from a broken pattern. Querying each column against the live database instead gave the true 8/12, then 9/9 after the fixes. Where a claim is checkable against the real system, check it there.

userStories.title: Page views have never been recorded — user_analytics.content_id is a NOT NULL uuid receiving a pathname
userStories.description: As the platform owner, I need page views to actually be recorded, because every page-view insert fails on a type error and the failure is invisible in production.
acceptanceCriteria: Page views are persisted for every route navigation
Apply migration 20260718000002 (drops NOT NULL on user_analytics.content_id) — the code fix does not work without it
Any consumer reading user_analytics must tolerate a null content_id on page_view rows (filter content_type <> 'page' or content_id IS NOT NULL)
Homepage loads with no 22P02/23502 error from usePageTracking
userStories.notes:
FIXED 2026-08-11 (claude/prd-p1-loop). This story was recorded as "blocked SOLELY on migration 20260718000002" with "the CODE half is already fixed". BOTH halves of that were wrong, and page views were still being dropped on every load.

MEASURED AGAINST PRODUCTION, before the fix, with analytics consent granted:
  POST /rest/v1/user_analytics
  400 {"code":"23502","message":"null value in column \"content_id\" of relation \"user_analytics\" violates not-null constraint"}
usePageTracking wrote content_id: null into a uuid NOT NULL column. The earlier "fix" swapped 22P02 (pathname into a uuid) for 23502 (null into NOT NULL) — a different rejection, the same outcome. Page views have never been recorded, through two failure codes.

FIXED WITHOUT THE MIGRATION. content_id now takes crypto.randomUUID(). A page is not a content row, so the value is filler and page_url carries the real identity — but a filler that persists the row beats a semantically-pure null that discards it. This matches useAnalytics.ts:229, which already mints one for page views for exactly this reason, and the three writers fixed under WEB-QA-026 the same day.

AC1 + AC4 VERIFIED after the change, same probe: page_view insert returns 201, and all five user_analytics writes on / are 201 with zero 22P02/23502.

AC2 IS NO LONGER A BLOCKER. Migration 20260718000002 (drop NOT NULL) is still unapplied and still tracked in WEB-QA-020, but this story no longer waits on it. If it lands, null becomes available again; there was no reason to keep discarding every page view until then.

AC3 IS MOOT: no consumer has to tolerate a null content_id, because none is written.

TWO THINGS THAT MADE THIS INVISIBLE, both worth carrying forward:
 1. The error was reported with console.error behind an import.meta.env.DEV guard. vite.config.ts strips console.* from production via esbuild.drop, so a rejected insert produced NO signal in the only environment that mattered. Now routed through handleError. That is the fourth writer this session hiding a failure the same way — see WEB-QA-026 for the other three.
 2. The insert is consent-gated on hasConsent('analytics'), so a probe in a fresh browser context sees NO page_view request at all. My first measurement showed zero writes and could easily have been read as "not firing" rather than "failing". Seed a cookie-consent record in localStorage before first paint to observe it. Absence of a request is not absence of a bug.

VERIFIED: npm run lint 0 errors, npx vitest run 193/193, check-imports clean, check-schema no new findings, build green at 35/35.

[prior] RE-VERIFIED (CODE REVIEW 2026-08-06): the CODE half is already fixed — src/hooks/usePageTracking.ts:48-52 now writes content_id: null with a comment explaining the uuid/pathname mismatch. This story is now blocked SOLELY on migration 20260718000002 (drop NOT NULL on user_analytics.content_id), which is in the unapplied batch tracked by WEB-QA-020. Nothing further to implement here; it ships when WEB-QA-020 ships.

[prior] FOUND 2026-07-18 while verifying WEB-QA-012 (claude/web-qa-p1-fixes). SEVERITY: LOW-MED — no user-visible breakage, but page analytics has been silently empty for the life of the feature. CODE FIX APPLIED, BLOCKED ON DEPLOY. usePageTracking inserted the pathname into user_analytics.content_id, which is a uuid, so every insert failed with 22P02 "invalid input syntax for type uuid: '/'". Verified live. Simply writing null instead is NOT sufficient: the column is NOT NULL, so that fails with 23502 — also verified live. Migration 20260718000002 drops the NOT NULL, which is a loosening and therefore safe in a single release per CLAUDE.md (existing writers always send a content_id for content interactions, so nothing they do starts failing; only readers must tolerate null). traffic_metrics is not an alternative destination — it holds provider-aggregated daily totals, not individual views. THIS STORY CANNOT CLOSE UNTIL THAT MIGRATION IS APPLIED; the code change is already committed and is inert until then (page views fail today either way, so there is no regression in the meantime). NOTE: session_id on this table is also a uuid, but the app generates it with crypto.randomUUID(), so it is fine — an early diagnosis briefly blamed it because the probe passed a non-uuid string.

userStories.title: Pagination controls on /restaurants and /attractions silently did nothing
userStories.description: As a visitor browsing past the first page, I need Load More / Next / Previous to work, because all three passed an updater function into a setter that only accepts a number, so the page never changed.
acceptanceCriteria: Load More, Next and Previous change the page on /restaurants and /attractions
The ?page= URL param carries a real number
npm run validate passes
userStories.notes: FOUND AND FIXED 2026-07-18 (claude/web-qa-p1-fixes) while working down the WEB-CI-007 strict-mode backlog — this is a user-facing bug that the strict type-check surfaced and that nothing else had caught. SEVERITY: MED. ROOT CAUSE: `const setPage = (v: number) => setParam("page", v, { def: 1 })`, but six call sites across Attractions.tsx (L732, L745, L787) and Restaurants.tsx (L723, L736, L778) passed a React-style updater, e.g. setPage((p) => p + 1). setParam serialises with String(value), so the function SOURCE went into the URL — String((p)=>p+1) is literally "(p)=>p+1". getNum then parsed NaN and fell back to 1, so Load More, Next and Previous were all silent no-ops on both pages. The strict project reported it as TS2345 "Argument of type (p: any) => any is not assignable to parameter of type number"; the default tsconfig has the checks that would catch this turned off, which is why it shipped. FIX: setPage now accepts `number | ((prev: number) => number)` and resolves the updater against the current page, in Attractions, Restaurants and EventsPage (the last for consistency — it had the same signature but no updater call sites yet, so it was one edit away from the same bug). VERIFIED IN THE BROWSER: /restaurants Next now navigates to ?page=2 and Previous returns to page 1.

userStories.title: User preferences are local-only — the sync target table never existed

acceptanceCriteria: Decide the storage shape for user-set preferences (the existing user_preference_profiles table is inferred behavioural data, not user-set settings — it is not the same thing)
Add the table via an additive migration and restore read + write in useUserPreferences

userStories.notes: FOUND 2026-07-18 (claude/web-qa-p1-fixes) while working down the WEB-CI-007 strict backlog. SEVERITY: LOW-MED — no visible breakage, but a feature that reads as cross-device has never been. useUserPreferences read from and upserted to a `user_preferences` table that does not exist in the schema and never has. Both calls failed on every invocation; the read failure fell through to the localStorage path and the write failure was swallowed as `log.debug(... "Not critical - localStorage backup exists")`, so preferences have always been local-only for every user. The dead calls have been REMOVED rather than left in place: they guaranteed an error on each load and made the strict type-check unresolvable, since an unknown table name forces Supabase to consider all 245 table overloads (TS2589 "type instantiation is excessively deep"). useUserPreferences went 7 -> 0 strict errors. The hook now documents that it is deliberately local-only and points here. NOTE the shape mismatch that makes this a real decision rather than a rename: UserPreferences is a nested app-level object (interests / cuisine / location / time / notifications), while user_preference_profiles holds inferred signals (preferred_cuisines, interaction_patterns, preference_confidence). Reusing that table would conflate user-stated settings with machine-inferred ones.

userStories.title: Burn down the schema-usage baseline (84 remaining silently-dead queries)
userStories.description: As the platform owner, I need every Supabase query in src/ to name a table, column, and RPC that actually exists, because a query naming something absent is not a TypeScript error — it 400s at runtime, the hook catches it, and the UI renders its empty state, so the feature silently does nothing and nothing reports it.
acceptanceCriteria: scripts/check-schema-usage.mjs reports zero findings with --all (baseline file removed entirely)
Each burn-down commit re-runs `npm run check-schema:update` so schema-baseline.json only ever shrinks
Any finding that cannot be fixed without a product decision is split into its own story rather than left silently baselined
npm run validate passes
userStories.notes:
BASELINE SHRUNK 179 -> 164 on 2026-08-22 (claude/prd-p1-loop), and the interesting half is WHY.

THE CHECKER COULD NOT SEE OVERLOADED FUNCTIONS. scripts/check-schema-usage.mjs parsed entity names with /^ {6}(\w+): \{/, which requires the opening brace on the SAME line. The Supabase codegen emits an overloaded function as a union instead:
      get_active_ads:
        | { Args: ...; Returns: ... }
        | { Args: ...; Returns: ... }
so every overloaded function was invisible to the parser and reported as 'no such function in the generated schema'. Regex is now /^ {6}(\w+):(?: \{| *?$)/, which matches both shapes; parsed function count went 329 -> 362. Verified as a strict SUPERSET before shipping - 597 old matches, 638 new, zero lines the old regex caught that the new one does not.
  The four affected findings were get_active_ads, fuzzy_search_events, fuzzy_search_restaurants and calculate_campaign_pricing. All four exist in production - the first has 1 overload now, the two fuzzy searches have 2 each. So the baseline was carrying FALSE POSITIVES, which contradicts this story's own note that the baseline was verified with 'ZERO FALSE POSITIVES'. That verification probed PostgREST, which is a different question from what this checker asks: the checker compares against the GENERATED TYPES, not the database. 'Absent from types.ts' and 'absent from the database' are different claims and the baseline conflates them.

ELEVEN MORE ENTRIES WERE SIMPLY STALE: profiles.role / full_name / username across eleven edge functions. Those call sites no longer reference the columns at all - stripe-webhook and admin-home-stats now have zero 'role' references - so the code was fixed and nobody re-ran check-schema:update. Checked with the HEAD version of the script too, which also reports zero, confirming my parser change did not cause the removal.
  Note the columns themselves genuinely do NOT exist in production (profiles has no role, full_name or username). There is simply nothing left querying them.

AC1 IS UNREACHABLE AS WRITTEN, and worth restating in the story: it asks for zero findings and the baseline file removed entirely. But the project convention recorded in scripts/ralph/progress.txt is that new DB tables/views/RPCs are deliberately NOT added to the generated types - they are accessed with `as never` casts. So every deliberately-untyped object will always appear as a finding. apple_notification_log and play_rtdn_log, which I created earlier today, are exactly this case: they exist in production and are absent from types.ts, so they stay baselined and correctly so. Reaching zero requires either regenerating types.ts to cover everything or teaching the checker the difference between untyped and missing.

AC2 SATISFIED for this pass: the baseline only shrank, and every removal was verified to correspond to something that genuinely resolves. npm run validate exits 0.

BASELINE INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED AGAINST PRODUCTION 2026-08-11 (claude/prd-p1-loop). Not burned down — but nobody needs to re-verify it, which was the expensive part.

Probed every distinct table and column in schema-baseline.json through PostgREST with the anon key. PostgREST is the arbiter here: 42P01 = no such table, 42703 = no such column, 200/[] = exists (RLS hiding rows is fine and does not confuse the signal). The generated types can be stale, so absence there is not proof — this is the same technique that settled WEB-SEC-023's profiles.role ambiguity.

RESULT: 179 findings across 56 tables and 29 rpcs.
  45 of 56 tables CONFIRMED MISSING
  32 columns CONFIRMED MISSING
  0 columns that actually exist
ZERO FALSE POSITIVES. The baseline is accurate; there is no stale-types noise in it to write off, and the burn-down is real work rather than a cleanup of bad findings.

Missing tables, grouped — this is what the burn-down actually is, and most of these are whole subsystems rather than stray queries:
  CRM (12): crm_contacts, crm_deals, crm_notes, crm_tasks, crm_segments, crm_activities* (table exists, 6 columns missing), crm_communications, crm_pipeline_stages, crm_deal_stage_history, crm_lead_score_history, crm_lead_score_rules, crm_contact_segments
  SEO monitoring (10): seo_alerts, seo_alert_rules, seo_audit_history, seo_core_web_vitals, seo_crawl_results, seo_image_analysis, seo_monitoring_log, seo_monitoring_schedules, seo_notification_preferences, seo_settings
  Media (4): media, videos, thumbnails, event_analytics
  Billing/mobile (6): payments, invoices, usage_events, device_tokens, apple_notification_log, play_rtdn_log
  Trip planner (2): trip_plans, trip_plan_items — the AI Trip Planner is a headline feature in CLAUDE.md and persists NOTHING
  Content/social (7): favorites, reviews, article_categories, article_tags, author_profiles, event_submissions, content_queue_comments
  Other (4): api_keys, api_key_usage, user_sessions, restaurant_analytics, dummy

CLAUDE.md WAS WRONG AND IS NOW FIXED. Its "Core tables" line named favorites, ratings, reviews and advertisements. All four return 42P01. That is the file every contributor and assistant reads first, so the error propagates into new code — which is plausibly how some of these 179 references got written in the first place. The line now lists only what exists, and carries the curl one-liner for checking a table before writing against it.

AC1 (zero findings) NOT DONE and should not be done as one change. AC3 is the operative one: most of what remains is not a broken query, it is a subsystem that was built client-side against tables that were never created. Deciding whether the CRM, SEO-monitoring, media and trip-planner backends get built or their code gets deleted is a product call per subsystem, and each deserves its own story with its own evidence. Filing four stories speculatively without that decision would just move the pile.

AC2 and AC4 unaffected: schema-baseline.json is untouched, npm run check-schema still reports no NEW findings, npm run validate passes.

[prior] RE-VERIFIED (CODE REVIEW 2026-08-06): the count is exactly right. npm run check-schema:all reports 293 unresolvable references, of which schema-baseline.json holds 179 findings: 84 in src/ (matching this story's number precisely), 93 in supabase/functions/. Split by kind: 84 table, 59 column, 36 rpc. Notable inclusion: src/hooks/useTripPlanner.ts -> trip_plans + trip_plan_items, i.e. the AI Trip Planner (a headline feature in CLAUDE.md) persists nothing.

[prior] FOUND 2026-07-18 (claude/prd-loop-schema-gaps). Every claim below was verified against the LIVE production database via the REST API, not inferred from src/integrations/supabase/types.ts — generated types can be stale, so absence there was treated as a hypothesis and confirmed by probing prod. | GUARD SHIPPED, BURN-DOWN INCOMPLETE. scripts/check-schema-usage.mjs parses the generated types (266 tables/views, 329 functions) and validates every .from()/.select()/.rpc()/filter/order call in src/. Wired into `npm run validate` and pr-checks.yml. Runs as a RATCHET matching the strictNullChecks convention already in this repo: known findings frozen in schema-baseline.json, only NEW ones fail the build. Regression-tested in both directions (planted a bad column, confirmed exit 1 and correct line number). Three false-positive classes were found and fixed during development: embedded resources (`author:profiles(name)`) parsed as columns once splitSelect consumed the parens; comment-stripping that deleted newlines and shifted every reported line number (pointing reviewers at interface declarations ~60 lines from the real query); and PostgREST aggregates (`select=count`, which is valid and returns a row count). Baseline went 93 -> 84 via the fixes in WEB-QA-018-adjacent work (four content routes, campaign notifications). THE REMAINING 84 ARE ALMOST ENTIRELY WEB-QA-018 AND WEB-QA-019 — they are blocked on a product decision, not on effort.

userStories.notes:
INVENTORY RE-VERIFIED AND ONE ITEM FIXED 2026-08-22 (claude/prd-p1-loop), this time by direct database query rather than REST probing.

All 26 named tables confirmed absent via to_regclass over public: the 11 CRM tables, payments, invoices, usage_events, user_sessions, api_keys, api_key_usage, author_profiles, article_categories, article_tags, content_queue_comments, trip_plans, trip_plan_items, device_tokens, event_analytics, restaurant_analytics. The inventory in this story is ACCURATE. The decision it asks for is still the owner's - inventing eleven CRM schemas on a guess remains the wrong move.

THE SHARPEST CASE IS FIXED, because it was a defect and not a decision. Confirmed that public.events has NO description, start_time, end_time or address column (it has date, location, title, venue and the enhanced/original_description pair), so useReviewEvent's insert failed with PGRST204 on every approved submission. Worse than recorded: the error was only console.error'd and console.* is stripped from production builds, so in production there was NO signal - EventReviewSystem.tsx:76 fired toast.success and the admin saw success. Nothing has ever published.

Remapped onto columns that exist, following the crawler's convention (catchdesmoines_crawler.py:372-389): description -> original_description + enhanced_description, date -> date + event_start_utc, event_start_local DERIVED from date via formatInCentralTime (it is `timestamp without time zone`, local wall-clock - an earlier draft sent the user's free-text '7:00 PM' and Postgres rejected it, which is why this was tested rather than reasoned about), address folded into location. start_time/end_time are not published - events has no text time columns and end_date is used by 0 of 1246 rows - and both stay on the submission row, so nothing is lost. Null date is guarded against the NOT NULL. Publish failures now THROW so the admin sees an error toast instead of a false success.

VERIFIED against production in a transaction: old column set errors with 'column "description" of relation "events" does not exist', new column set returns INSERT 0 1. Rolled back.

STILL A DECISION: the 26 tables. Note trip_plans/trip_plan_items gates the flagship marketed AI feature, and device_tokens ties to IOS-AUDIT-FEAT-029.

FOUND 2026-07-18 (claude/prd-loop-schema-gaps). Every claim below was verified against the LIVE production database via the REST API, not inferred from src/integrations/supabase/types.ts — generated types can be stale, so absence there was treated as a hypothesis and confirmed by probing prod. | SEVERITY: HIGH — but this is a DECISION, not a defect to fix blind. Confirmed 42P01 "relation does not exist" from the live REST API for all 14 probed directly (crm_contacts, crm_deals, crm_tasks, crm_notes, user_sessions, api_keys, payments, invoices, usage_events, device_tokens, author_profiles, article_categories, trip_plans, event_analytics); the remaining 15 are absent from the generated schema by the same check. BLAST RADIUS: seven CRM hooks with ~60 call sites (useCrmContacts/Deals/Tasks/Notes/Segments/Communications/Dashboard) are 100% non-functional; AdminRefunds.tsx cannot work; SessionManagementDashboard and API-key issuance are dead UI. SHARPEST CASE — useUserSubmittedEvents.ts:220 inserts description/start_time/end_time/address into public.events. None of those four columns exist, so the insert fails with PGRST204 and the error is only console.error'd. ADMINS BELIEVE THEY ARE PUBLISHING USER-SUBMITTED EVENTS. NOTHING PUBLISHES. Deliberately NOT fixed autonomously: inventing eleven CRM table schemas on a guess is worse than leaving the finding recorded.

userStories.title: 25 RPC functions the web app calls do not exist (PGRST202)
userStories.description: As the platform owner, I need every .rpc() call to resolve, because a missing function returns PGRST202 and the calling hook falls back silently — so view counts, fuzzy search, and the session/password-policy suite have never worked.
acceptanceCriteria: Decide per function: implement it, or remove the call and its fallback path
View tracking: increment_event_view, increment_restaurant_view, batch_increment_views — ALL view counting is silently dead
Search: fuzzy_search_events, fuzzy_search_restaurants — both fall back silently, so search quality is degraded with no signal

Session/security: get_user_session_policy, update_session_with_timeout, revoke_session, revoke_all_other_sessions, get_user_login_activity, log_login_activity, get_active_password_policy, validate_password_policy
CRM (blocked on WEB-QA-018): add_crm_activity, evaluate_segment_rules, update_lead_score
Billing: get_user_payment_summary, get_current_usage, record_usage_event, create_api_key, revoke_api_key, calculate_campaign_pricing, increment_deal_redemption
Trip planner: get_trip_itinerary
Any new function is additive per CLAUDE.md (adds optional params / returned columns only)
userStories.notes:
THE THREE BROKEN-BUT-PRESENT RPCs ARE REPAIRED 2026-08-22, migration 20260822000004. AC3 is done; the 24 genuinely-missing functions remain the decision this story is really about.

fuzzy_search_events had TWO defects, the second hidden behind the first because Postgres reports only the first failure - the same trap WEB-BE-033's AC2 warns about:
  (a) the body selected and searched e.description, which does not exist on public.events. The declared output column `description` is preserved so callers see an unchanged shape, now fed by COALESCE(enhanced_description, original_description). Matching and relevance consider BOTH columns, so a query matching only the raw crawler text still finds the row.
  (b) it declared latitude/longitude as numeric while events.latitude/.longitude are real - a 42804 queued up behind the 42703.
fuzzy_search_restaurants declared latitude/longitude numeric against real columns. latitude IS column 6, exactly what the 42804 named. restaurants.description exists and rating really is numeric, so those were fine.
calculate_campaign_pricing had two overloads taking the SAME parameter names and differing only in type, so named arguments could not disambiguate and every call was PGRST203. The superseded TEXT overload is dropped, on the same reasoning and with the same overload-count guard as 20260718000001 used for get_active_ads.

VERIFIED in a rolled-back transaction against production: fuzzy_search_events('jazz',5) -> 5 rows, fuzzy_search_restaurants('pizza',5) -> 5 rows, calculate_campaign_pricing -> 1 overload remaining and returns daily_price 10.00 / total_price 70.00 for 7 days. All three errored before. check-migration-safety.mjs passes.

Both fuzzy functions keep their unused (text, real, integer) overload. Nothing calls it and its parameter names differ from the 2-arg form, so it cannot cause the PGRST203 that affected calculate_campaign_pricing.

GROUND TRUTH ESTABLISHED 2026-08-22 (claude/prd-p1-loop) by querying pg_proc directly, which is the method the story's own correction note said was needed and which was unavailable until DB access was confirmed this session. The premise is wrong in a way that changes what the work IS.

IT IS 24 MISSING, NOT 25. Five of the 29 baselined RPCs EXIST in public:
  calculate_campaign_pricing, fuzzy_search_events, fuzzy_search_restaurants, get_active_ads, reclaim_stuck_newsletter_campaigns

AND FOUR OF THOSE FIVE ARE BROKEN, each in a DIFFERENT way, every one failing silently:
  get_active_ads             42702 ambiguous campaign_id  -> FIXED today, migration 20260822000001
  fuzzy_search_events        42703 'column e.description does not exist'
  fuzzy_search_restaurants   42804 'Returned type real does not match expected type numeric in column 6'
  calculate_campaign_pricing PGRST203 overload ambiguity - TWO overloads exist, (placement_type,integer) and (text,integer)
  reclaim_stuck_newsletter_campaigns  WORKS, returns 0
Measured by calling each with the EXACT argument shape its caller uses (useEvents.ts:134, useRestaurants.ts:312, useCampaigns.ts:142).

SO AC1's FRAMING - 'implement it, or remove the call' - DOES NOT FIT FOUR OF THEM. They are neither absent nor working; they are present and defective, and each needs a different repair:
  - fuzzy_search_events references events.description, a column that DOES NOT EXIST (events has original_description / enhanced_description). Same missing column that broke user-submission publishing in WEB-QA-018.
  - fuzzy_search_restaurants has a RETURNS TABLE signature mismatch, the identical class as WEB-BE-033 and detectable only when a row is produced.
  - calculate_campaign_pricing has duplicate overloads, the identical class that 20260718000001 fixed for get_active_ads and ONLY for get_active_ads.

AC3 CONFIRMED WITH A CAUSE: both fuzzy searches do fall back silently. useEvents.ts:139 is `if (!fuzzyError && fuzzyData)`, so a 42703 is indistinguishable from no results and search quietly degrades to the non-fuzzy path. That is the story's claim, now with the reason attached.

METHOD NOTE, extending the story's own correction: pg_proc is the ONLY reliable existence check. Argumentless POSTs return PGRST202 whether or not the function exists, AND - as these five show - existence is not health. A function can exist, resolve, and still fail with 42702 / 42703 / 42804 / PGRST203. Any future audit needs to call each RPC with its caller's real arguments, not probe for presence.

THE 24 GENUINELY MISSING remain a decision, unchanged: view tracking (increment_event_view, increment_restaurant_view, batch_increment_views - ALL view counting is dead), session/security (7), billing (7), CRM (3, blocked on WEB-QA-018), trip planner (get_trip_itinerary), plus exec_sql, generate_invoice_number, generate_trip_share_code, get_active_password_policy, validate_password_policy.

METHOD CORRECTION 2026-08-11 (claude/prd-p1-loop). No AC advanced. Recording this because I tried to re-verify the list, got a clean-looking answer, and the answer was wrong — and the same trap is sitting in front of whoever picks this up.

WHAT I DID: POSTed {} to each of the 29 RPCs in schema-baseline.json. All 29 returned PGRST202, which reads as "all 29 confirmed absent".

WHY THAT IS INVALID. The full PostgREST message is "Searched for the function public.X WITHOUT PARAMETERS OR WITH A SINGLE UNNAMED json/jsonb PARAMETER, but no matches were found in the schema cache". PGRST202 from an argumentless call means there is no ZERO-ARGUMENT overload. It does not mean the function is absent. Every function here takes parameters, so an argumentless probe returns PGRST202 for all of them regardless of whether they exist.

PROOF, from this same session: get_active_ads is in that list and returned PGRST202 to my probe — but it demonstrably EXISTS. The homepage measurement for WEB-PERF-025 caught it returning HTTP 300 / PGRST203, "could not choose the best candidate function between two candidates", which is only possible if two overloads of it exist. WEB-QA-003 documents exactly that, and migration 20260718000001 exists to drop the superseded one.

SO THE BASELINE HAS AT LEAST ONE FALSE RPC ENTRY. That is a genuine correction to something I recorded earlier today under WEB-QA-017: I verified the TABLE and COLUMN halves of schema-baseline.json against production and found zero false positives, and that finding stands. I did NOT verify the rpc half, and it now has a known-bad entry. The 25/29 count in this story's title should be treated as unverified rather than as established.

HOW TO ACTUALLY VERIFY, and why I stopped rather than doing it: each function must be called with its real argument names, taken from the call site in src/. That is per-function work, and 16 of the 29 are side-effecting — exec_sql, revoke_session, revoke_all_other_sessions, revoke_api_key, create_api_key, log_login_activity, record_usage_event, increment_event_view, increment_restaurant_view, increment_deal_redemption, add_crm_activity, update_lead_score, update_session_with_timeout, reclaim_stuck_newsletter_campaigns, generate_invoice_number, generate_trip_share_code. Probing those with plausible arguments against PRODUCTION could revoke a real session, mint an API key or corrupt a counter. Do it against a branch database, or read pg_proc directly with a service-role key, not by calling them.

The 13 read-only-ish ones (get_active_ads, get_trip_itinerary, get_current_usage, fuzzy_search_*, get_user_*, validate_password_policy, calculate_campaign_pricing, evaluate_segment_rules, batch_increment_views) are safe to probe with real arguments and would settle most of the list cheaply.

RELATED, ALREADY FILED: WEB-BE-033 is the mirror image of this — get_trending_events EXISTS, is not in the baseline, and fails at execution with 42804 because its declared RETURNS TABLE disagrees with its own body. Between that and get_active_ads, "the function is missing" and "the function is broken" are clearly not distinguishable from the client, and this story's framing assumes they are.
