userStories.title: SEV-1: Account deletion is broken on BOTH iOS and Android (App Store 5.1.1(v) blocker)
userStories.description: As a mobile user, I need to be able to delete my account, because the delete-user-account edge function requires a two-step action payload and both mobile clients send no body at all, so every deletion attempt 400s and the account is never deleted.
acceptanceCriteria: DECISION REQUIRED — two viable paths, with a real security tradeoff

Path A (ships today, no store release): restore the legacy no-body branch server-side. Fixes every shipped binary immediately. Cost: a bare authenticated POST irreversibly deletes an account with no server-side confirmation step, which is precisely what the two-step token flow exists to prevent
Path B (correct, slower): fix both clients to send {action:"request"} then {action:"confirm",confirmation_token}. Shipped binaries stay broken until users update
Recommended: BOTH — Path A to unblock now, migrate clients to the two-step flow, then bump MIN_SUPPORTED_APP_VERSION and drop the legacy branch. That is exactly the CLAUDE.md deprecation flow
Fix the docstring at delete-user-account/index.ts:15-16, which documents a legacy branch that does not exist in the code
Add a client-contract test so this specific drift cannot recur (see XPLAT-011)
userStories.notes:
RE-VERIFIED (CODE REVIEW 2026-08-06): STILL BROKEN, unchanged on all three call sites. iOS ProfileViewModel.swift:80-83 and SettingsView.swift:374-377 both still call functions.invoke("delete-user-account", options: .init(method: .post)) with no body; Android ProfileViewModel.kt:228 still calls client.functions.invoke("delete-user-account") with no body. delete-user-account/index.ts:91-92 still destructures {action, confirmation_token} from the body and :282-288 still returns 400 "Invalid action" when action is absent. Web (PrivacyControls.tsx:151,179) remains correct. Still a live App Store 5.1.1(v) blocker.

[prior] FOUND 2026-07-18 (claude/prd-loop-schema-gaps). Every claim below was verified against the LIVE production database via the REST API, not inferred from src/integrations/supabase/types.ts — generated types can be stale, so absence there was treated as a hypothesis and confirmed by probing prod. | SEVERITY: SEV-1, App Store 5.1.1(v) blocker, LIVE RIGHT NOW. Verified by reading all three call sites plus the function. Contract: delete-user-account/index.ts:86 destructures {action, confirmation_token}; :89 handles "request"; :139 handles "confirm"; :256-264 returns HTTP 400 when action is absent. Web is CORRECT (src/components/PrivacyControls.tsx:148-153 sends {action:"request"}, reads confirmation_token, then confirms). iOS is BROKEN (ViewModels/ProfileViewModel.swift:80-83 and Views/Profile/SettingsView.swift:374-377 invoke with method:.post and NO body). Android is BROKEN (ui/screens/profile/ProfileViewModel.kt:228 invokes with no body). AGGRAVATING: the function's own docstring at :15-16 states "Legacy: POST without action field treated as direct deletion (backwards compat)". THAT BRANCH DOES NOT EXIST IN THE CODE — control falls through to the 400. This is the CLAUDE.md violation at "Removing a feature an older binary tries to call": the no-body shape that shipped binaries use was retired without a MIN_SUPPORTED_APP_VERSION bump. Backward-compat hazard: yes, and already realized. Neither client signs the user out, because deletion never happens. iOS surfaces the error; Android shows e.message. RESOLVED 2026-08-10 on claude/prd-p1-loop, taking AC4 (BOTH paths) as recommended. SERVER: supabase/functions/delete-user-account/index.ts now shares one performDeletion() between the confirmed two-step flow and a restored legacy no-action branch, so the two can never drift on what they erase; the legacy branch carries an inline comment naming its removal condition (MIN_SUPPORTED_APP_VERSION excluding every pre-two-step binary). AC5: the docstring that described a legacy branch which did not exist now describes the branch that does. CLIENTS: new ios/DesMoinesInsider/Services/AccountDeletionService.swift is the single deletion client; ProfileViewModel.swift and SettingsView.swift both call it instead of invoking the edge function themselves, which is how they drifted. Android ProfileViewModel.kt now does request -> parse confirmation_token -> confirm -> assert success, and throws before signOut() if either step fails. AC6: supabase/functions/_tests/account-deletion-contract.test.ts reads the edge function AND all four client files and asserts they agree on the action values, the snake_case confirmation_token key, the surviving legacy branch and the do-not-sign-out-before-confirm rule; 8 tests, all passing, and the legacy-branch assertion was proven to fire by temporarily removing the branch. userStories.title: Android subscription revocation is fixed but untested (no regression test asserting an invalid receipt revokes)
userStories.description: As the platform owner, I need Android to drop entitlement when the server rejects a purchase, because a refunded, revoked, or tampered Google Play purchase currently keeps premium unlocked on-device indefinitely.
acceptanceCriteria: On a clean valid:false response, Android revokes the local entitlement, mirroring iOS StoreKitService.swift:515-525 (serverRevokedProductIDs)
Replace the raw-text substring check with a typed decode mirroring iOS's Decodable ValidationResponse
Add a test asserting an invalid receipt revokes entitlement
No change to the validate-android-receipt request/response shape (CLAUDE.md backward-compat)
userStories.notes:
CI VERIFICATION OF THE NEW TEST 2026-08-22: android-ci run 32585740475 -> SUCCESS. 'Run Unit Tests' and the whole 'Lint, Test & Build' job passed with ValidationResponseTest.kt present, so the file COMPILES and the task that runs it is green. Stating that precisely rather than more: Gradle does not print individual test names in the CI log, so I can confirm compilation and a passing test task, not independently observe the five assertions executing.
That closes the loop on shipping a file I could not run locally - the gradle wrapper/cache mismatch recorded below is real, and CI was the first execution, as stated when it was committed. Note it took three attempts to get a verdict: android-ci uses concurrency group android-ci-${{ github.ref }} with cancel-in-progress, so each of my own subsequent pushes cancelled the run in flight. Stop pushing to the branch if you need a mobile CI result.

AC3 PARTLY ADDRESSED 2026-08-22 (claude/prd-p1-loop). ACs 1, 2 and 4 were already done, confirmed again today at BillingService.kt:459 (typed decode) and :465-477 (revoke on a clean valid:false).

ADDED android/app/src/test/java/com/desmoines/aipulse/data/remote/ValidationResponseTest.kt - five JUnit 5 assertions on the decode that feeds the revoke branch:
  - a rejection decodes as invalid, with its reason
  - an approval decodes as valid
  - THE REGRESSION, spelled out: both a rejection and an approval body contain the text 'valid', so the old substring check could not tell them apart and read a refund as an approval. The typed decode can. That is the defect this story replaced.
  - unknown response fields do not break the decode (CLAUDE.md backward-compat: the edge function may add fields and shipped binaries must keep decoding)
  - a rejection with no reason still decodes

WHAT IT DOES NOT COVER, and why AC3 is not marked done: it asserts the INPUT to the revocation branch, not the revocation. Asserting that _serverRevokedProductIDs actually gains the product id needs a seam that does not exist - the branch is in a private suspend function that reaches Google Play billing and a SupabaseClient, BillingService requires an Android Context, and both resolveTier and _serverRevokedProductIDs are private. That half is a testability refactor, not a test.

NOT RUN LOCALLY, and this is an environment finding worth recording on its own: ./gradlew cannot build in this sandbox at all. settings.gradle.kts fails to compile with "Unresolved reference 'plugins'" before any test is reached, because gradle-wrapper.properties pins gradle-9.3.1 while the local cache holds 8.13 and 9.6.1. VERIFIED PRE-EXISTING rather than assumed: an EXISTING test (CampaignAdServiceTest) fails identically with my file removed. So no Android unit test can be executed here, which is why IOS-AUDIT-TEST-002 and friends stay blocked for the same class of reason.
The new file is therefore verified only structurally: it mirrors CampaignAdServiceTest's package, JUnit 5 jupiter imports and runTest-free style, and ValidationResponse is confirmed @Serializable, top-level and public. android-ci.yml:86 runs ./gradlew test, so CI is the first real execution.

RE-VERIFIED (CODE REVIEW 2026-08-06): BOTH original defects are FIXED in android/.../data/remote/BillingService.kt. (1) Revocation: :465-477 now does _serverRevokedProductIDs.value += productId and recomputeCurrentTier() on a clean valid:false, with the comment "Revoke rather than granting an indefinite grace period (XPLAT-002)". The remaining grace path (:494) is only for exhausted retries on transport failure, which is correct and mirrors iOS. (2) Parsing: :458 now does validationJson.decodeFromString<ValidationResponse>(bodyString) — the substring check is gone — and :452 correctly treats a non-2xx as "not a verdict" rather than a rejection. STILL OPEN on criterion 3 only: there is no test asserting that an invalid receipt revokes entitlement; android/app/src/test/ contains only ProfileViewModelPrivacyTest.kt for this area. Severity has dropped from a live entitlement-integrity gap to a missing regression test.

[prior] TITLE CORRECTED (CODE REVIEW 2026-08-06) — was: "Android never revokes a server-rejected subscription, and parses receipts by substring matching".

FOUND 2026-07-18 (claude/prd-loop-schema-gaps). Every claim below was verified against the LIVE production database via the REST API, not inferred from src/integrations/supabase/types.ts — generated types can be stale, so absence there was treated as a hypothesis and confirmed by probing prod. | Two defects in one file. (1) REVOCATION: data/remote/BillingService.kt:424-428 logs a warning and returns on invalid, with the comment "do NOT revoke (grace period)". iOS does revoke (StoreKitService.swift:515-525, annotated IOS-AUDIT-SEC-011). Revenue + entitlement-integrity gap. (2) PARSING: BillingService.kt:421 decides validity with bodyString.contains("\"valid\":true") || bodyString.contains("\"valid\": true"). Any whitespace or key-ordering change from the edge function silently flips this to the invalid path. iOS uses a typed Decodable. This is a latent backward-compat hazard of an unusual shape: an ADDITIVE, normally-safe response change could break shipped Android binaries, which inverts the usual assumption that additive changes are free. | IMPLEMENTED AND VERIFIED LOCALLY 2026-07-18 (claude/prd-loop-schema-gaps, commit 00f54838). passes STAYS false pending CI + a real refund/revocation test against Google Play. Both halves done: _serverRevokedProductIDs subtracted in localTier() (cleared on a later valid:true so re-subscribing after a refund restores access), and a typed @Serializable ValidationResponse with ignoreUnknownKeys replacing the substring check. DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE FROM iOS: revocation is gated on a 2xx status first, because the edge function returns valid:false for auth failures, bad input, and "Server configuration error" alongside genuine rejections — a straight port of iOS behaviour would revoke every paying user during a backend outage or misconfigured deploy. Non-2xx falls through to the existing retry/grace path. iOS may warrant the same hardening; worth checking whether supabase-swift throws before the decode on non-2xx (UNVERIFIED). Toolchain note: the Android build DOES work on the Windows dev machine (JDK 17 + SDK present, ANDROID_HOME just unset) — but ./gradlew fails at settings.gradle.kts with "Unresolved reference: plugins" while the system gradle 9.6.1 succeeds, so the wrapper (9.3.1) appears broken locally. CI uses gradle/actions/setup-gradle@v4 and is unaffected. Verified: compileDebugKotlin clean, ValidationResponseTest 6/6, full suite 273 tests 0 failures.

userStories.title: iOS has no Google Sign-In, so Google-created accounts are unreachable on iOS
userStories.description: As a user who signed up with Google on web or Android, I need to sign in on iOS, because Google OAuth accounts have no password and iOS offers only Apple and email/password.
acceptanceCriteria: iOS offers Google Sign-In alongside Apple, matching web (src/contexts/AuthContext.tsx:539-540)
A Google-created account can sign in on iOS and resolves to the same profiles row
No change to the auth/session shape (CLAUDE.md: profiles, subscription_tier, JWT claims)
Correct the false claim at android AuthRemoteDataSource.kt:25 that it "Mirrors iOS AuthService.swift ... and Google Sign-In" — the mirror claim is false in both directions
userStories.notes:
QUANTIFIED 2026-08-22 (claude/prd-p1-loop). The gap is real and the blast radius is ONE account - smaller than a provider count suggests, because identity linking hides the difference.

CONFIRMED: grep for 'google' across ios/.../AuthService.swift and Views/Auth/*.swift returns ZERO hits. Web has both, AuthContext.tsx:630 google and :663 apple.

MEASURED AGAINST auth.identities RATHER THAN raw_app_meta_data, which is what makes the difference. By provider metadata it looks like 2 Google accounts out of 11 (5 email, 4 apple, 2 google). By linked IDENTITIES:
    3  apple only
    2  apple + google   <- these CAN sign in on iOS, via Apple
    5  email only
    1  google only      <- genuinely cannot reach their account on iOS
So one user is locked out of iOS, not two. Anyone re-checking this should query auth.identities; counting raw_app_meta_data->>'provider' overstates the impact by 2x here and would understate it if the mix shifted the other way.

THE RATE MATTERS MORE THAN THE COUNT AT THIS SCALE. 1 of 11 is 9%, on a user base small enough that the absolute number will not stay 1. Every Google-only signup from here is a user who can use the web app and the Android app and not the iOS one, and there is no in-product signal telling them why - they simply have no Google button to press.

AC4 CONFIRMED VERBATIM: AuthRemoteDataSource.kt:24 reads 'Mirrors iOS AuthService.swift — uses Supabase Auth for email/password and Google Sign-In.' iOS has no Google Sign-In, so the mirror claim is false for exactly the provider the file names. Correcting that comment is free and can ship independently of AC1.

NOT IMPLEMENTED: AC1 is Swift work (GoogleSignIn SDK plus signInWithIdToken(provider:.google)), and no iOS toolchain exists in this sandbox - same constraint as IOS-AUDIT-SEC-001 and XPLAT-002. AC3 is satisfied by construction if it is done that way: signInWithIdToken resolves to the same auth.users row and therefore the same profiles row, changing no session shape.

FOUND 2026-07-18 (claude/prd-loop-schema-gaps). Every claim below was verified against the LIVE production database via the REST API, not inferred from src/integrations/supabase/types.ts — generated types can be stale, so absence there was treated as a hypothesis and confirmed by probing prod. | Web has both providers (AuthContext.tsx:539-540 google, :572-573 apple). iOS is Apple-only: AuthService.swift:250-251 signInWithIdToken(provider:.apple), and grep for "google" across AuthService.swift and Views/Auth/*.swift returns ZERO hits. Android is Google-only (AuthRemoteDataSource.kt:100-103), which is acceptable on that platform. An account created via Google OAuth has no password, so on iOS it is simply unreachable — not a degraded experience, a lockout.

userStories.title: Neither mobile app has production crash or analytics visibility
userStories.description: As the platform owner, I need mobile crash and analytics data to reach a backend, because both mobile surfaces queue this data locally and never upload it, so a mobile-only regression is invisible until a store review mentions it.
acceptanceCriteria: Build the crash-report edge function both mobile CrashReportingServices were written to call (no such directory exists under supabase/functions/)
Decide the analytics strategy: un-comment iOS Firebase, or route both mobile surfaces through log-error to unify with web's Sentry
iOS AnalyticsService stops being a no-op (Services/AnalyticsService.swift:25-26, 33-34 — every Firebase call is commented out)
Paywall conversion analytics specifically must emit on iOS (ties to IOS-AUDIT-FEAT-030)
Correct the claim at Android AnalyticsService.kt:36 that "Event names mirror iOS verbatim" — true for names, but iOS emits nothing, so cross-platform funnel comparison is invalid
userStories.notes:
RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-22 (claude/prd-p1-loop). Both halves still true, and AC1 is probably unnecessary work.

VERIFIED: no supabase/functions/*crash* directory exists. iOS AnalyticsService.swift still has its Firebase calls commented out. iOS CrashReportingService.swift contains NO upload path at all - grep for invoke / functions / URLSession finds only comments ('a future release can upload', 'after a successful upload'). So AC1's framing is slightly off: the services were not written to CALL a crash-report function, they were written to persist locally and expose a flush API. There is no call site waiting to be satisfied.

AC1 IS LIKELY UNNECESSARY, BECAUSE THE INGEST ALREADY EXISTS. supabase/functions/log-error is:
  - verify_jwt = false, confirmed in config.toml, and its header states the reason - 'public error sink: the web client posts errors before/without a session'. So a mobile client can post a crash WITHOUT an authenticated session, which is exactly what a crash reporter needs.
  - rate-limited per IP, scrubs PII before storage, returns no data
  - writes public.error_events (exists, 2 rows) and feeds the error-triage agent that clusters them into dev tasks
  - already proven in production by web: src/lib/errorHandler.ts:100 posts to it
So AC2's second option ('route both mobile surfaces through log-error to unify with web's Sentry') does not merely unify the surfaces - it REMOVES AC1. Building a second, mobile-only crash endpoint would duplicate PII scrubbing, rate limiting and the triage clustering that already work.

WHAT ACTUALLY REMAINS, then, is smaller than the story reads:
  1. iOS/Android: POST the persisted crash records to log-error and delete on success. The flush API CrashReportingService already exposes (pendingRecords / delete-by-id) is the seam - it was built for precisely this and never connected.
  2. Decide analytics separately from crash reporting. They are conflated in this story but are different systems: log-error is an ERROR sink, not an analytics pipeline, so AC3/AC4 (iOS AnalyticsService, paywall conversion events) still need the Firebase-or-alternative decision.
  3. AC5's correction stands: Android AnalyticsService.kt:36 claims 'Event names mirror iOS verbatim', true of the names and misleading in effect, because iOS emits nothing.

NOT IMPLEMENTED: the upload path is Swift and Kotlin, and ./gradlew cannot build in this sandbox (verified pre-existing, see XPLAT-002). Writing an unrunnable network path into a crash reporter is the wrong trade - a crash reporter that throws while reporting a crash is worse than one that stays silent.

RE-VERIFIED (CODE REVIEW 2026-08-06): still true on both halves, though scaffolding now exists. ANALYTICS: ios/.../Services/AnalyticsService.swift is a 151-line facade where every Firebase call is commented out — trackScreenView/trackEvent only reach AppLogger.general.debug(); the header still reads "When Firebase is integrated... Until then, logs locally". userStories.title: Web bypasses register-device-token and writes device_tokens directly

userStories.notes:
RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-22 (claude/prd-p1-loop), and the framing needs correcting: routing web through the edge function would fix the INCONSISTENCY without fixing anything FUNCTIONAL, because both paths end at the same missing table.

  public.device_tokens                              MISSING (confirmed via to_regclass)
  supabase/functions/register-device-token          EXISTS
  register-device-token/index.ts:74                 .from('device_tokens').upsert(...)
  src/hooks/usePushNotifications.ts:39              .from('device_tokens').upsert(...)
So the 'correct' path and the 'bypass' path write to the identical nonexistent table. AC1 as written buys consistency and a validated platform value, not a working feature.

PUSH REGISTRATION IS BROKEN ON ALL THREE SURFACES, not just misrouted on one. iOS (PushNotificationService.swift:70) and Android (PushNotificationService.kt) both invoke the edge function, which then writes to the missing table. Web writes it directly. Nothing has ever persisted a device token anywhere.

ONE THING THAT IS ALREADY READY: AC2 asks that getPlatform() be validated against the server's VALID_PLATFORMS list. register-device-token/index.ts:12 already declares ['ios', 'android', 'web'] and rejects anything else at :65 - so 'web' is an accepted platform server-side today. SEQUENCING: AC3 is right that this is blocked on WEB-QA-018's device_tokens decision, and the ordering matters more than the story implies - creating the table makes the EXISTING iOS/Android path start working immediately, while the web change is cosmetic until then. If device_tokens is built, do it first and re-measure before touching the web call site.

FOUND 2026-07-18 (claude/prd-loop-schema-gaps). Web (src/hooks/usePushNotifications.ts:39-43) upserts into device_tokens directly, skipping the VALID_PLATFORMS check at register-device-token/index.ts:65-71. Two write paths into one table with only one validated. Mobile request shapes are otherwise identical. COMPOUNDING: device_tokens does not exist in prod at all (42P01 confirmed), so the web path fails outright today and the mobile path writes nowhere.

userStories.title: Data export (CCPA/GDPR right-to-access) exists only on web
userStories.description: As a mobile-only user, I need an in-app path to export my data, because the export is implemented on web only and mobile users have no way to exercise the right.
acceptanceCriteria: iOS and Android expose a data-export path equivalent to src/components/PrivacyControls.tsx:19
Pairs with XPLAT-001 — both privacy rights (deletion and access) are currently unavailable on mobile
userStories.notes:
RE-MEASURED 2026-08-22 (claude/prd-p1-loop). Two corrections, and the second is a compliance finding larger than this story's title.

CORRECTION 1 - THERE IS NO data-export EDGE FUNCTION. This story's note says 'Backend support exists (IOS-AUDIT-REL-010 notes account-deletion, data-export, and social-account functions exist but only deletion is wired)'. The only export function in supabase/functions/ is export-analytics-data, which is an ADMIN CSV analytics export, not a user's right-to-access export. The web export is entirely CLIENT-SIDE: PrivacyControls.tsx:76-94 loops a hardcoded table list, queries each through RLS and assembles JSON in the browser.
  That changes the mobile work from 'call the existing endpoint' to a design choice: reimplement the assembly in Swift AND Kotlin (a third and fourth copy of the table list), or build the server-side export function that should have existed and have all three clients call it.

CORRECTION 2 - THE WEB EXPORT IS SUBSTANTIALLY INCOMPLETE, which matters more than its absence on mobile. Measured against production:
    right to ERASURE  deletes from 62 tables (PURGE_TABLES in _shared/userDataTables.ts, a maintained list that user-data-tables.test.ts asserts every entry of actually exists)
    right to ACCESS   exports 8 hardcoded tables - and THREE OF THEM DO NOT EXIST: favorites, ratings and reviews all return 42P01. So it returns data from FIVE real tables.
  The export hands the user a document stating 'This export contains personal data we hold about your account' while omitting 57 tables the deletion path acknowledges holding. The three phantom tables fail silently because the code comments that an error on one table 'doesn't block the whole export'.

THE FIX THAT MAKES BOTH RIGHTS CONSISTENT BY CONSTRUCTION: source the export from PURGE_TABLES rather than a second hardcoded list. Deletion and access then cannot drift, and the existing test that asserts every purge table exists starts protecting the export too. RETAINED_TABLES deserves thought in the same change - those rows are deliberately kept, and a right-to-access export arguably must include what we retain, not just what we would delete.
  Doing it client-side means 62 queries from the browser, which is the practical argument for the server-side function above.

AC2 IS HALF STALE: it says 'both privacy rights (deletion and access) are currently unavailable on mobile'. Deletion IS available on mobile now - XPLAT-001 is genuinely fixed and all three clients call delete-user-account with the documented two-step action body (verified today, see XPLAT-011). Only access remains missing.

FOUND 2026-07-18 (claude/prd-loop-schema-gaps). Every claim below was verified against the LIVE production database via the REST API, not inferred from src/integrations/supabase/types.ts — generated types can be stale, so absence there was treated as a hypothesis and confirmed by probing prod. | grep for exportData / dataExport / export-analytics-data across ios/ and android/app/src/main/ returns nothing. Backend support exists (IOS-AUDIT-REL-010 notes account-deletion, data-export, and social-account functions exist but only deletion is wired). Compliance exposure, and it compounds XPLAT-001: a mobile-only user can currently neither delete nor export their data.

userStories.title: Web calls three edge functions that do not exist
userStories.description: As an admin, I need admin tooling actions to work, because three invoked edge functions have no implementation and return 404 at runtime.
acceptanceCriteria: Resolve test-article-webhook, test-ai-model, clear-system-cache — implement or remove the call sites

TRIAGED 2026-08-22 (claude/prd-p1-loop). Inventory re-confirmed and, unusually for this PRD, the failure handling here is CORRECT - which changes what the decision is about.

INVENTORY, unchanged: test-ai-model, test-article-webhook and clear-system-cache each have exactly one caller in src/ and no directory under supabase/functions/. verify-apple-receipt and personalized-recommendations each have a directory and ZERO callers on any surface.

ALL THREE MISSING FUNCTIONS FAIL VISIBLY, so this is dead admin UI rather than a silent-failure defect - the distinction that has mattered on nearly every other story in this PRD:
  AIConfigurationManager.tsx:96   `if (error) throw error` - surfaces
  ArticleWebhookConfig.tsx:88     `if (error) throw error`, and onError shows toast.error('Webhook test failed: ...')
  useSystemMonitoring.ts:139      catches and returns { success: false, error } to its caller. The console.error alongside it is stripped in production, but the boolean is not, so the caller can still tell.

Implementing is a bounded edge function each; removing is deleting a button. Either resolves it; leaving them is the only option that keeps misleading an admin about whether their AI config or webhook is healthy.

AC3 STILL BINDS on verify-apple-receipt: MIN_SUPPORTED_APP_VERSION is the gate, and it is not a judgement call to be made from the web side.

Exactly three are missing, unchanged: test-ai-model (src/components/AIConfigurationManager.tsx:96), test-article-webhook (src/components/ArticleWebhookConfig.tsx:88), clear-system-cache (src/hooks/useSystemMonitoring.ts:139). None of the three appears in supabase/config.toml and none has any git history in this repo — they were never implemented, not deleted.

userStories.title: Ask Pulse (discover-chat) is missing on web entirely; Android shows no quota
userStories.description: As a web visitor, I need the conversational AI the product is marketed on, because discover-chat is implemented on both mobile surfaces and has zero references in src/.
acceptanceCriteria: Decide whether Ask Pulse comes to web (it is the single largest feature web is missing)
Android surfaces remaining quota before the 429, matching iOS (AskPulseService.swift:33-61 decodes usage:{remaining:int|"unlimited", tier})
Android DiscoverChatResponse stops silently dropping the usage field (AskPulseRepository.kt:34-38)
Reconcile with WEB-QA-005: the homepage markets a "24/7 AI Assistant" that web does not implement
userStories.notes:
RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-22 (claude/prd-p1-loop). Both halves confirmed unchanged, and AC3 is a bigger job than 'stop dropping the field' suggests.

WEB HALF - grep for 'discover-chat' across src/ returns ZERO hits. The feature is absent entirely, unchanged.

ANDROID HALF - AskPulseRepository.kt still declares DiscoverChatResponse with only picks and followUpSuggestions, above the comment 'Unknown keys (e.g. usage) are ignored'. AC3 unmet.

WHY AC3 IS NOT A ONE-LINE FIELD ADDITION. The server sends, at discover-chat/index.ts:451, `usage: { remaining: quota.remaining, tier }` where remaining is documented at :19 as `number | 'unlimited'` - a POLYMORPHIC field. iOS handles it with a hand-written decoder: AskPulseService.swift:40-57 defines a RemainingValue enum whose init(from:) tries Int, then falls back to matching the string 'unlimited'. Kotlin needs the equivalent custom KSerializer; adding `val usage: Usage?` with a plain Int would throw on every unlimited (VIP) response.

DELIBERATELY NOT IMPLEMENTED BLIND, and the risk is asymmetric. ./gradlew cannot build in this sandbox at all - settings.gradle.kts fails to compile because the wrapper pins gradle-9.3.1 while the local cache holds 8.13 and 9.6.1, verified pre-existing by running an EXISTING test with none of my files present (see XPLAT-002). Today the field is DROPPED, which is safe: ignoreUnknownKeys means quota data is lost but the response still decodes and Ask Pulse works. A custom serializer written without being able to execute it could THROW on decode and break Ask Pulse on Android entirely - trading a missing quota indicator for a broken feature. A test file failing CI is cheap; a broken decode reaching users is not.

AC2 is downstream of AC3: there is nothing to surface before the 429 until the field is decoded. AskPulseViewModel.kt:116 will stay reactive-only until then.

AC4 RECONCILED, with the measurement from WEB-QA-005 (verified live the same day): the homepage serves '24/7 AI Assistant' and 'First AI-Powered Conversational City Guide' to LOGGED-OUT visitors while web implements no conversational surface at all. So the '24/7 AI Assistant' stat is not merely overstated - it markets a feature that does not exist on the platform serving the claim. That is a stronger version of WEB-QA-005's point: that story is about the trip planner being paywalled, this one is about a second advertised AI feature being absent. Both resolve through the same copy decision.

RE-VERIFIED (CODE REVIEW 2026-08-06): still open, and the Android half is LESS done than it looks. AskPulseScreen.kt:111 does show an upgrade prompt via state.quotaExceeded, but AskPulseViewModel.kt:116 only sets that flag AFTER a 429 comes back — it is reactive, not the "surface remaining quota before the 429" the criteria ask for. AskPulseRepository.kt:33 still carries the comment "Unknown keys (e.g. usage) are ignored", so criterion 3 (stop dropping the usage field) is unmet. Web half fully unchanged: grep for discover-chat across src/ returns zero hits.

[prior] FOUND 2026-07-18 (claude/prd-loop-schema-gaps). Every claim below was verified against the LIVE production database via the REST API, not inferred from src/integrations/supabase/types.ts — generated types can be stale, so absence there was treated as a hypothesis and confirmed by probing prod. | Both mobile clients send an identical request (messages[] + optional userLocation), matching discover-chat/index.ts:11-12. iOS decodes the usage block including the int-or-string union and shows remaining quota; Android declares only picks + followUpSuggestions with the comment "Unknown keys (e.g. usage) are ignored", so Android users get no quota visibility before hitting 429. Both handle 429 -> upsell correctly. WEB HAS NO ASK PULSE AT ALL (zero hits for discover-chat / AskPulse in src/). This directly compounds WEB-QA-005, which flags the homepage marketing AI capabilities that the web funnel does not deliver.

userStories.title: Add client-to-edge-function contract tests (the control that would have caught XPLAT-001)
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I need automated proof that each client calls each edge function with the shape that function actually implements, because the deletion break was exactly this drift and no CI lane saw it.
acceptanceCriteria: For each edge function with more than one client caller, a test asserts the documented request contract matches the implemented branches
A test specifically asserts delete-user-account rejects or accepts a bodyless POST per whatever XPLAT-001 decides — so the docstring and the code can never disagree again
Extend supabase/functions/_tests/ rather than adding a parallel harness
Runs in the broadened Edge Function & Cross-Platform Contract Tests workflow
userStories.notes:
AC2, AC3 and AC4 DONE 2026-08-22 (claude/prd-p1-loop): supabase/functions/_tests/client-contract.test.ts, wired into subscription-sync-tests.yml. AC1 is started rather than finished - the harness covers delete-user-account, and MULTI_CLIENT is the list to extend.

AC2 IS UNBLOCKED BECAUSE XPLAT-001 IS GENUINELY FIXED, which its own notes do not reflect. That story is marked passes:true but its most recent note says 'STILL BROKEN, unchanged on all three call sites', citing ProfileViewModel.swift:80-83 and SettingsView.swift:374-377. Those call sites no longer exist. iOS now routes both entry points through AccountDeletionService.swift, which sends action:"request" then action:"confirm"; Android ProfileViewModel.kt:242 does the same via buildJsonObject; src/components/PrivacyControls.tsx does too. The function parses with `await req.json().catch(() => ({}))` at :234, so a bodyless POST from an older binary still reaches the documented legacy direct-deletion branch. Docstring, implementation and all three clients agree. The passes:true is correct; the note is stale and predates the AccountDeletionService refactor.

WHAT THE TEST ASSERTS, offline so it needs no credentials and cannot be reddened by a production outage:
  1. every documented action has an implemented branch
  2. every implemented branch is documented (the reverse direction - an undocumented branch is how a client ends up guessing)
  3. req.json() stays guarded with .catch(), because without it a bodyless POST from a shipped binary is a 500 and the docstring promises otherwise
  4. every listed client actually sends the documented action field
Limitation stated plainly: it proves the shapes agree, not that the endpoint works.

VERIFIED BY MUTATION, not by watching it pass. Removing the .catch() -> exit 1. Stripping action:"request" from the iOS client -> exit 1. Renaming an implemented branch -> exit 1. All restored -> exit 0.
The mutation run caught a false negative in my own first draft: assertion 4 matched the CONTRACT DOCUMENTED IN A HEADER COMMENT in AccountDeletionService.swift rather than the call site, so gutting the real call still passed. A contract test reading documentation instead of implementation has precisely the defect it exists to catch. Comments are now stripped before matching.

FOUND 2026-07-18 (claude/prd-loop-schema-gaps). Every claim below was verified against the LIVE production database via the REST API, not inferred from src/integrations/supabase/types.ts — generated types can be stale, so absence there was treated as a hypothesis and confirmed by probing prod. | PARTIALLY ADDRESSED 2026-07-18: the TRIGGER gap is fixed — .github/workflows/subscription-sync-tests.yml previously fired only on four billing functions plus _tests/, leaving ~69 of 73 edge functions with no CI execution on change. Broadened to supabase/functions/** and supabase/migrations/** and renamed (commit b14316f6). THE TESTS THEMSELVES ARE STILL MISSING. The workflow now runs on any function change, but only executes cross-platform-sync.test.ts and version-check.test.ts. A contract test asserting docstring-vs-implementation agreement is what would actually have caught XPLAT-001, and it does not exist yet. Note that writing it today would fail CI, because delete-user-account's docstring and code genuinely disagree — that failure is the point, but it should land together with the XPLAT-001 decision rather than before it.

userStories.title: Anonymous users can read internal config, the full RBAC model, and the anti-abuse blocklist
userStories.description: As the platform owner, I need internal operational tables closed to anonymous reads, because an unauthenticated visitor using the public anon key can currently enumerate the complete permission model, the email-domain blocklist, ad pricing rules, and feature flags.
acceptanceCriteria: blocked_email_domains: revoke anon SELECT. Publishing an anti-abuse blocklist defeats it — an abuser reads the 5,361 blocked domains and picks one that is not listed. Nothing in the client needs this table; signup validation belongs server-side.

permission_definitions / role_permissions / role_definitions: revoke anon SELECT. 58 permission definitions and 166 role-permission mappings are enumerable, which is a complete map of the authorization model — every resource, action, scope, and which role holds it.

pricing_rules: revoke anon SELECT. base_price plus traffic_multiplier / demand_multiplier / min_price / max_price is the internal ad pricing algorithm, so advertisers can reverse-engineer quotes. NOTE: ad_rate_card and advertising_packages are probably intentionally public for the Advertise page — confirm before closing those two.

feature_flags: restrict anon SELECT to flags the client must evaluate, or move evaluation server-side. Currently exposes unreleased work and admin-only gating (ai_trip_planner_v2 disabled; ai_article_pipeline_enabled and search_traffic_dashboard target admin).

ai_environment_config: revoke anon SELECT. default_value holds no secrets today (verified), but it publishes the NAME of every AI secret and its Coolify variable, and one careless UPDATE turns it into a live credential leak.
content_metrics (14,432 rows), image_optimization_queue (1,370), media_assets (1,381): confirm whether anon read is intended; these look like internal ops/analytics surfaces.
Extend .github/workflows/rls-config-audit.yml so a table added without an explicit RLS policy cannot ship anon-readable.
Re-run the anon probe after the change and confirm these tables no longer return rows.
userStories.notes:
APPLIED TO PRODUCTION 2026-08-22 with the owner's approval, recorded in schema_migrations. AC8 satisfied - re-probed through the anon HTTP path after the change:
  blocked_email_domains 0, permission_definitions 0, role_permissions 0, role_definitions 0, pricing_rules 0, ai_environment_config 0.
Signup enforcement unchanged in the same probe: is_email_domain_blocked('someone@gmail.com')=false, ('a@mailinator.com')=true. Enforceable, not enumerable.

ACs 1, 2, 3 and 5 IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-22 (claude/prd-p1-loop), migration 20260822000003. These were recorded as blocked on WEB-QA-020, which CLOSED earlier today - disk and production are in sync and migrations can be applied - so they are no longer blocked.

AC5 IS WORSE THAN THIS STORY RECORDED, and the story's framing of 'revoke anon SELECT' undersells it. ai_environment_config's only policy was:
    "Allow all for ai_environment_config"   cmd=ALL   roles={public}   USING (true)
ALL, not SELECT. Verified as the anon role in a rolled-back transaction:
    SET LOCAL ROLE anon;
    INSERT INTO public.ai_environment_config ... -> INSERT 0 1
    UPDATE public.ai_environment_config ...      -> UPDATE 10
    DELETE FROM public.ai_environment_config ... -> DELETE 1
Anyone holding the anon key that ships in the client bundle could REWRITE OR DELETE the AI configuration, not merely read it. The new policy is FOR ALL with both USING and WITH CHECK gated on user_has_role_or_higher(auth.uid(), 'admin'), which closes the write hole along with the read.

WHY THE TIGHTENING IS SAFE IN ONE RELEASE, checked per table rather than assumed:
  - NO shipped mobile binary touches any of the six. grep over ios/ and android/ returns zero.
  - blocked_email_domains: the client NEVER reads the table. useAuthSecurity.ts:113 calls the is_email_domain_blocked RPC, which is SECURITY DEFINER (prosecdef = t) and so is unaffected by the policy. The blocklist stays ENFORCEABLE but stops being ENUMERABLE - which is precisely AC1's point.
  - permission_definitions / role_permissions / role_definitions: no runtime reader at all; the only hits are generated types.ts and the creating migration.
  - pricing_rules: no reader anywhere; the single hit is a comment in check-anon-exposure.ts.
  - ai_environment_config: no reader anywhere.

VERIFIED in a rolled-back transaction against production, four ways:
  anon after the change  -> 0 rows on all six
  admin after the change -> 5361 / 58 / 3 / 9, so the admin UI keeps working
  signup regression      -> is_email_domain_blocked('a@mailinator.com')=true, ('someone@gmail.com')=false as ANON. Still enforcing.
  anon write             -> 'new row violates row-level security policy for table "ai_environment_config"'
check-migration-safety.mjs passes.

AC4 and AC6 DELIBERATELY NOT DONE HERE. feature_flags (useFeatureFlag, useExperiment, useAgentControlPlane, WeeklyDigestControls + 5 edge functions), content_metrics (useContentTracking, AdminAnalyticsDashboard, eventSubmissionService), media_assets and image_optimization_queue (useMediaLibrary, useMediaUpload, VideoUpload) all have live client readers. Blanket-revoking them would break working features; they need the per-flag / per-row design AC4 and AC6 describe, which is a decision rather than a revoke.

EXPOSURE RE-PROBED 2026-08-22 before the change, counts only: blocked_email_domains 5,361; permission_definitions 58; role_permissions 166; role_definitions 4; pricing_rules 3; feature_flags 7; ai_environment_config 9; content_metrics 19,933; image_optimization_queue 1,370; media_assets 1,381. content_metrics has now grown twice while exposed: 14,432 -> 17,398 -> 19,933.

AC7 DONE + AC8 PROBE RE-RUN 2026-08-11 (claude/prd-p1-loop). ACs 1-6 remain blocked on migrations (WEB-QA-020), so the story stays open — but the exposure is confirmed still live and there is now a gate stopping it getting worse.

RE-PROBED PRODUCTION TODAY, counts only (never contents — dumping a blocklist into a log is the same disclosure this story is about):
  blocked_email_domains      5,361   (story recorded 5,361 — unchanged)
  permission_definitions        58   (58 — unchanged)
  role_permissions             166   (166 — unchanged)
  role_definitions               4
  pricing_rules                  3
  feature_flags                  7
  ai_environment_config          9
  content_metrics           17,398   (story recorded 14,432 — GREW by 2,966)
  image_optimization_queue   1,370   (1,370 — unchanged)
  media_assets               1,381   (1,381 — unchanged)
  ad_rate_card / advertising_packages  5 / 3  (probably intentional per AC3)
Every table named in ACs 1-6 is still readable by the anon key that ships in the client bundle. content_metrics is not static — it is accumulating while exposed.

AC7 DONE: scripts/check-anon-exposure.ts, wired into .github/workflows/rls-config-audit.yml. It enumerates every table from the generated types and asks the question an attacker asks — does a GET with the anon key return rows. That is deliberately NOT what scripts/audit-rls.ts does: audit-rls parses migrations, and a policy added by hand in the dashboard, or a migration applied out of order, is invisible to it. A live probe cannot be fooled that way.

INDEPENDENT CORROBORATION OF THE ORIGINAL FINDING: the probe reports 40 of 248 tables anon-readable. The story's original method (2026-07-18) found "40 tables returned real rows, 198 returned empty, 9 errored". Two independent runs, five months apart, same count.

IT RATCHETS RATHER THAN GATES ON THE EXISTING 40, on purpose. Fixing those needs migrations that are not applied, so a check failing on day one would be switched off within a week — the exact fate of every other inert guard catalogued in this backlog. It fails on a NEWLY anon-readable table, which is precisely AC7's wording: "a table added without an explicit RLS policy cannot ship anon-readable".

PROVED IT FIRES: removing 'events' from the baseline makes the run exit 1 with "NEWLY anon-readable (1): events (1134 rows)"; restoring gives exit 0.

ACs 1-6 UNCHANGED AND STILL BLOCKED — each needs a REVOKE / policy migration against production. Worth restating that AC1 is the sharpest: publishing an anti-abuse blocklist defeats it, because an abuser reads the 5,361 domains and picks one that is not listed. Nothing in the client reads that table.

[prior] RE-VERIFIED (CODE REVIEW 2026-08-06): still true. supabase/migrations/20260128000001_security_layers.sql:434-436, 452-454 and 469-471 create "Anyone can view ..." SELECT policies with USING (true) on role_definitions, permission_definitions and role_permissions respectively. Also inherits the residual criterion from WEB-SEC-022: decide whether anon SELECT on content_metrics is intended.

[prior] FOUND 2026-07-18 (claude/prd-loop-schema-gaps). METHOD: enumerated all 248 public tables from the generated types and issued an anon-key SELECT against LIVE PRODUCTION for each — exactly what any visitor can do, since the anon key ships in the client bundle. Result: 40 tables returned real rows, 198 returned empty, 9 errored. MOST of the 40 are correctly public content (events, restaurants, attractions, playgrounds, articles, hotels, trails, venues, guides, pseo_pages, badges, subscription_plans). The concerns are the internal ones listed in the acceptance criteria. SEVERITY: MODERATE, and deliberately not overstated. NO PII and NO credentials were exposed. Every ai_environment_config default_value was checked for secret-shaped strings (sk-, eyJ, ghp_, AIza, xox) and none were found; the CLAUDE_API_KEY and OPENAI_API_KEY rows have null defaults. restaurant_blacklist reasons are benign operational notes such as not-a-restaurant and gas-station, not defamatory. This is reconnaissance and control-defeat, not a breach. SHARPEST ITEM: blocked_email_domains at 5,361 rows. It is a security control whose effectiveness depends entirely on not being public, and it is public. TWO LIMITS ON THIS AUDIT, both important. (1) The 198 EMPTY results are AMBIGUOUS — an RLS-filtered table and a genuinely empty table are indistinguishable from anon, so this audit proves what IS exposed but CANNOT certify the rest is protected; a service-role row-count comparison is needed to separate them. (2) Only SELECT was tested. Anon INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE posture is UNVERIFIED and was deliberately not probed, because a write test against production could mutate real data. Close that gap against a staging database, not this one.

userStories.title: log-content-metrics is the one public edge function with no rate limit, and writes with the service-role key
userStories.description: As the platform owner, I need the anonymous metrics endpoint throttled and bounded, because it accepts unauthenticated requests, applies no rate limit, caps neither the batch size nor the metric value, and upserts with the service-role key.
acceptanceCriteria: Add checkRateLimit to log-content-metrics, matching the other verify_jwt=false functions (geocode-location, image-transform, og-image and version-check are all rate-limited; this one is not)
Cap the events array length per request — it is currently unbounded, so one request can drive an arbitrary number of service-role upserts
Clamp metric_value to a sane range; it is attacker-controlled and accepted as any number
Keep the endpoint unauthenticated: that part is correct and intentional (it must accept metrics from anonymous visitors), so do NOT add an auth guard and break page-view tracking
Backward-compat per CLAUDE.md: the rate limit must sit above what shipped mobile binaries retry against, and the batch cap must exceed the largest batch any current client sends
Confirm whether anon SELECT on content_metrics is intended (see WEB-SEC-021) — the table is currently both publicly writable through this function and publicly readable
userStories.notes:
VERIFIED DONE (CODE REVIEW 2026-08-06): all three code criteria are implemented in supabase/functions/log-content-metrics/index.ts — checkRateLimit imported (line 18) and applied (line 84); MAX_EVENTS_PER_REQUEST=100 with .slice(0, MAX_EVENTS_PER_REQUEST) (lines 60, 120); MAX_METRIC_VALUE=1000 with Math.min(Math.max(Math.trunc(v),0),MAX) (lines 67, 128). Endpoint remains unauthenticated as required. The file header now cites WEB-SEC-022 by name. RESIDUAL: the last criterion ("confirm whether anon SELECT on content_metrics is intended") is a decision that belongs to WEB-SEC-021 and is tracked there — not a reason to hold this story open.

[prior] FOUND 2026-07-18 (claude/prd-loop-schema-gaps). METHOD: cross-referenced supabase/config.toml against every function body. 71 of 74 edge functions run verify_jwt=false, which is only safe when the function guards itself. 66 of the 71 do (requireApiKey / requireAdmin / requireAuth / requirePermission / withSecurity / secret comparison). THAT IS A GOOD RESULT and worth recording explicitly: WEB-SEC-001 largely worked. The five without an auth guard are geocode-location, image-transform, og-image, version-check and log-content-metrics — the first four are public by design AND rate-limited. log-content-metrics is the only one that is public by design and NOT rate-limited. SEVERITY: LOW-MODERATE, deliberately not inflated. Input validation is actually reasonable — content_type and metric_type are allowlisted and content_id must look like a UUID, so an attacker cannot write arbitrary shapes. The real gaps are the missing throttle, the uncapped events array, and the attacker-controlled metric_value. IMPACT IS BOUNDED BY WHAT CONSUMES THIS DATA: I traced every reader and found content_metrics feeds AdminAnalyticsDashboard.tsx and useContentTracking.ts. I found NO evidence it feeds trending_score, popularity_score, or any public ranking — so this is admin-analytics poisoning plus an unthrottled service-role write path, NOT ranking manipulation. If a future feature does wire content_metrics into ranking, re-rate this as HIGH before shipping it. CORRECTION WORTH KEEPING: an earlier pass of this audit flagged generate-seo-content as unguarded. That was a false positive in my own grep — it guards with requireApiKey (SEC-029) and rate-limits AI calls at max:10. The guard-name list had to be rebuilt from the actual _shared exports before the audit was trustworthy. | FIXED AND VERIFIED LOCALLY 2026-07-18. checkRateLimit added at 600/15min (deliberately loose: IP-keyed with no user identity, and the caller flushes every 10s = ~90 req/window PER TAB, so shared NAT would make a tight limit silently delete analytics for the busiest real traffic). Batch capped at 100 (excess sliced, not rejected — failing a whole batch would lose good data over one bad client). metric_value clamped to 0..1000. Endpoint stays unauthenticated, which is correct. Verified: deno check clean, tsc clean, clamp/cap logic exercised directly with 10 cases including Infinity/NaN/negatives plus a 50,000-event flood truncated to 100. ALSO FIXED a pre-existing deno check failure in the same file (declared union omitted the bare-array request shape) — confirmed pre-existing by checking the original before editing. passes stays false pending deploy + a post-deploy check that legitimate analytics still flow (watch for 429s from real traffic behind corporate NAT).

userStories.title: useAnalytics flush error path duplicated the queue instead of re-queueing failed events
userStories.description: As the platform owner, I need the analytics queue to survive a failed flush without growing without bound, because the error path duplicated the wrong events and doubled the queue on every failure.
acceptanceCriteria: Failed events are re-queued; events enqueued during the flush are preserved once, not duplicated
The queue is bounded so a sustained backend outage cannot grow it without limit
npm run validate passes
userStories.notes: FOUND AND FIXED 2026-07-18 while sizing rate limits for WEB-SEC-022. The catch block read [...eventQueue.current, ...eventQueue.current] under a comment saying it kept events for the next attempt. It did the opposite: eventsToFlush had already been cleared from the queue at the top of the try and was out of scope in the catch, so the events that actually failed were LOST, while anything enqueued during the in-flight flush was DUPLICATED — and duplicated again on each subsequent failure, doubling the queue each time. A backend outage therefore caused exponential memory growth in long-lived tabs plus inflated metric counts for whichever events survived. Fixed by hoisting eventsToFlush above the try so the catch can see it, re-queueing [...eventsToFlush, ...eventQueue.current], and bounding to MAX_QUEUED_EVENTS=500 (oldest dropped first — stale analytics matter less than a responsive page). Verified with tsc + eslint; the remaining eslint warnings in this file are pre-existing.

userStories.title: DECIDE BEFORE DEPLOY: event photos have two competing implementations, and the pending migration entrenches the weaker one
userStories.description: As the platform owner, I need one event-photo implementation, because two exist, neither works, they do not share storage, and migration 20260718000003 is about to commit the codebase to the one with the weaker schema.
acceptanceCriteria: Decide which table owns event photos BEFORE applying 20260718000003, because that migration is the commitment point

Option A — keep event_discussions (what the migration does): photos become discussion rows with message_type=photo and media_url. Wins: one feed, comments and photos already interleave, migration is written and additive. Costs: no caption field distinct from message, no is_featured, and every photo query filters a general discussions table

Option B — adopt event_photos (already exists, purpose-built: caption, photo_url, is_featured, likes_count, event_id, user_id, and NOT NULL-clean): rewrite EventPhotoUpload/EventPhotoGallery/EventSocialHub against it and drop the migration. Wins: better-shaped schema, no overloading. Costs: rewrite of the live components, and the photo count in the social hub needs a second query
Whichever wins, DELETE the losing path rather than leaving it dormant — the dead path is what produced this ambiguity
Fix src/lib/security/ownership.ts:349, which maps resource type photo -> event_photos. If Option A wins, that mapping points at a table that will never hold a photo
Remove or repair useCommunityFeatures.getEventPhotos, which filters on event_photos.is_approved — a column that does not exist, so the query fails with 42703 on every call
schema-baseline.json shrinks by the event_photos.is_approved entry
userStories.notes:
STATUS CORRECTION 2026-08-22 (claude/prd-p1-loop), including a correction to my own work earlier today.

AC1's COMMITMENT POINT HAS PASSED. It says 'Decide which table owns event photos BEFORE applying 20260718000003, because that migration is the commitment point'. That migration was ALREADY APPLIED when I reached it - confirmed against production while closing WEB-QA-016; event_discussions has both media_url and message_type. So Option A won by default, not by decision.
AND I THEN STRENGTHENED IT WITHOUT NOTICING THIS STORY. Closing WEB-QA-016 I hand-added media_url and message_type to types.ts and repaired the insert in useReviewEvent, which made Path A actually FUNCTION for the first time. I did not cause the commitment - the migration predated me - but I did make the default harder to walk back, and I should have checked for a story flagging the choice before improving one side of it.

THE GOOD NEWS, AND IT REOPENS THE DECISION: BOTH PATHS HOLD ZERO ROWS.
    public.event_photos                                0 rows
    public.event_discussions WHERE message_type='photo' 0 rows
No photo has ever been stored by either implementation, so switching to Option B would cost nothing in data migration. The decision is still fully reversible; it is a code choice, not a migration.

EVERY OTHER CLAIM IN THIS STORY RE-VERIFIED TODAY:
  - Path B has ZERO callers. grep for uploadEventPhoto/getEventPhotos outside useCommunityFeatures itself returns nothing.
  - AC5: src/lib/security/ownership.ts:349 still maps photo -> 'event_photos'. Under the de-facto Option A that points at a table which will never hold a row, so ownership checks for photos are checking the wrong table.
  - AC6: useCommunityFeatures.ts:148 filters .eq('is_approved', true) and event_photos has no such column - its columns are id, event_id, user_id, photo_url, caption, likes_count, is_featured, created_at. Line 16 also declares is_approved in the TS interface, so the type lies too.

WHAT THE DECISION LOOKS LIKE NOW: not 'which schema', but 'ratify Option A and delete Path B, or switch to Option B while it is still free'. The story's own argument that event_photos is the better schema (purpose-built caption, is_featured, likes_count, versus overloading a discussions table with a type discriminator) is unaffected by anything that has happened since. Deliberately NOT resolved here - AC4 says delete the loser, and which one loses is the call this story exists to make.

FOUND 2026-07-18 (claude/prd-loop-schema-gaps) while separating the fixable schema-baseline entries from the blocked ones. Of 84 baseline findings only 10 sit on tables that exist; 8 of those are crm_activities and are blocked behind WEB-QA-018 anyway. Chasing the last two is what surfaced this. THE TWO PATHS. Path A (LIVE): EventPhotoUpload -> event_discussions {message_type, media_url}, read by EventPhotoGallery, counted by EventSocialHub, mounted from EventDetails. Write currently fails with PGRST204 until 20260718000003 is applied (WEB-QA-016). Path B (DEAD): useCommunityFeatures.uploadEventPhoto/getEventPhotos -> event_photos. VERIFIED DEAD: zero callers anywhere in src/ (only the hook itself references it), and the live table holds ZERO rows. Its upload function is actually CORRECT — every column it inserts exists. Its read function is broken, filtering on is_approved, which is not a column on event_photos. So the dead path has a working writer and a broken reader, and nothing calls either. WHY THIS IS A DECISION AND NOT A CLEANUP: event_photos is arguably the BETTER schema. It is purpose-built (caption separate from message, is_featured, likes_count) while Option A overloads a general discussions table with a media_url and a type discriminator. The pending migration is not wrong, but it is a commitment, and it is easier to make that call now than after photos start accumulating in event_discussions. LATENT TRAP: src/lib/security/ownership.ts:349 maps photo -> event_photos. No caller currently passes photo as an ownership resourceType, so this is inert today (severity LOW, not a live hole). But the moment anyone wires up delete-my-photo under Option A, the ownership check will look in a table that holds no photos and fail closed — users unable to manage their own content, with nothing obviously wrong in the code. NOTHING WAS DELETED. Removing an entire feature path is a product call, and the dormant path is plausibly the one worth keeping.

userStories.title: Critical-path JS is 610KB gzipped against a 200KB budget (was 1043KB)
userStories.description: As a mobile visitor, I need the homepage to load within the stated Core Web Vitals budget, because the first-paint payload is over three times the documented critical-path limit.
acceptanceCriteria: Critical-path gzipped JS reaches the CLAUDE.md budget of 200KB (currently 610KB)
vendor-icons is 131KB gzipped eagerly — investigate tree-shaking; a full icon set is almost certainly being pulled in by a barrel import
The 160KB entry chunk (index-*.js) is the other half — audit what is statically reachable from it that could be lazy
Add a CI budget check that fails when critical-path gzipped JS regresses, so this cannot drift silently again
Re-measure LCP against the <2.5s target after the above
userStories.notes:
AC4 DONE and AC2 already resolved, re-measured 2026-08-22 (claude/prd-p1-loop).

CURRENT CRITICAL PATH: 369.9 KB gz across 6 chunks referenced by dist/index.html - down from the 394.9 KB this story last recorded, and 169.9 KB over the 200 KB budget.
    185.8  index-*.js
     54.2  vendor-ui
     46.2  vendor-react
     44.2  vendor-supabase
     20.7  vendor-icons
     18.7  vendor-react-ecosystem
All 120 emitted chunks total 1883.5 KB gz.

AC2 IS ALREADY DONE and the AC text is stale. It says 'vendor-icons is 131KB gzipped eagerly - investigate tree-shaking; a full icon set is almost certainly being pulled in by a barrel import'. vendor-icons is now 20.7 KB. That work landed; the AC just never got updated.

AC3 IS NOW THE WHOLE STORY: index-*.js at 185.8 KB is half the critical path on its own, and it has GROWN against the 160 KB the AC records. Everything else on the critical path is a vendor chunk that is genuinely needed at first paint. Reaching 200 KB means lazy-loading out of the entry chunk; there is no remaining vendor win of that size.

AC4 DONE: scripts/check-bundle-budget.mjs, wired into pr-checks.yml after the build step.
  Deliberately a RATCHET rather than the 200 KB budget. Enforcing 200 KB outright would be red on day one, and this repo has that failure mode twice already - WEB-CI-021's accessibility lane and WEB-CI-020's unit lane both sat on continue-on-error precisely because they failed from the start. strict-ratchet.mjs's own header says it: 'a gate that always fails teaches everyone to ignore it'. It fails on growth past bundle-budget-baseline.json (5 KB tolerance for dependency churn) and prints the distance to 200 KB on EVERY run so the goal does not quietly vanish. It also reports improvements and prompts a re-baseline, so the number can only move down.
  Measures the TOTAL, not per-chunk, on purpose: rollup renames and re-splits shared chunks between builds, which is what produced the phantom '+23 KB regression' recorded and retracted in this story's own history. The total is stable across that churn.
  VERIFIED by exit code, not by reading its output: baseline shifted down 50 KB -> exit 1; restored -> exit 0; dist/index.html absent -> exit 0 with a skip message. It also refuses to report a pass if index.html references no JS at all, because a parse failure reporting 0 KB would be the exact kind of false green this repo keeps finding.

AC1 and AC5 remain open: 169.9 KB still to remove from the entry chunk, then re-measure LCP.

MEASURED 2026-08-11 (claude/prd-p1-loop), third and final attempt. The two notes this replaces were both wrong; keeping only the numbers that survived a decisive measurement.

WHAT IS TRUE:
                                origin/main    this branch     delta
  ALL chunks emitted             2010.7 KB gz   1891.4 KB gz   -119.3
  critical path (entry-referenced) 484.6          394.9         -89.7
  chunks referenced by index.html      6              7           +1

Both totals are DOWN. Still 194.9 KB over the 200 KB budget on the critical path, so this story stays open.

THE "+23 KB REGRESSION" I RECORDED EARLIER DOES NOT EXIST. I compared only the chunks index.html references — index.js +12.2 and a new vendor-dates +10.5 — and called it a regression the icon win was masking. Diffing all 120/121 emitted chunks instead shows it is chunk-boundary churn: rollup names a shared chunk after a representative module, so when module-to-chunk assignment shifts, names reshuffle and a narrow view reads that as growth. GEOContent.js (-5.3), ThingsToDoHub.js (-8.2), PersonalizedRecommendations.js (-7.0), EventsThisWeekend.js (-5.8), BestOfCategory.js (-6.9), SportsHub.js (-6.1), PseoMapEmbed.js (-7.8) and SearchResults.js (-4.2) all disappear, while Index.js (+17.0), EventsByLocation.js (+7.9), TrailDetail.js (+6.8), AdvertiseSuccess.js (+6.3), BreweryTrail.js (+4.6), SmartEventNavigation.js (+4.3) and RelatedContent.js (+4.3) appear. Same code, different chunk names. date-fns moving from inlined into a shared vendor-dates chunk is part of the same redistribution and is better for caching, not worse.

THE ONLY REAL CHANGE is vendor-icons: 133.4 -> 21.0 KB gz, from WEB-PERF-026 (the lucide-react barrel import in BadgeCollection). That is the entire -89.7.

METHOD, because three attempts went wrong here and each failure was a different shape:
 1. Do NOT trust a figure recorded earlier in the same session. My first number, 371.4 KB, matched no build; the tree had moved eleven commits under it. Check the comparison commit out and build it.
 2. Do NOT measure only the entry-referenced chunks when comparing two builds. That subset is stable enough for a single build but not across builds, because chunk names and boundaries move. Diff the whole dist/assets manifest, then read the critical path from it.
 3. Prerendering is NOT the confound. I suspected dist/index.html was inflated because the Helmet-wait fix makes the homepage render more completely and pull extra chunk references in. PRERENDER=false produces the identical 394.9 across the same 7 chunks, so the capture is faithful.

WHERE THE REMAINING 194.9 KB ACTUALLY IS: index 167.1, vendor-react 87.9, vendor-ui 45.2, vendor-supabase 44.5, vendor-icons 21.0, vendor-react-ecosystem 18.8, vendor-dates 10.5. React and Supabase are load-bearing. The realistic targets are index.js itself and vendor-ui — there is no second barrel-import mistake left to find, so the next win requires deferring real application code below the fold rather than deleting an obvious error.

[prior] RE-MEASURED 2026-08-11 (claude/prd-p1-loop) after WEB-PERF-026 landed: critical-path JS is now 371.4 KB gz, down from 484 KB gz. Per chunk, gzipped from a clean rm -rf dist && npm run build: index 154.0, vendor-react 87.9, vendor-ui 45.2, vendor-supabase 44.5, vendor-icons 21.0, vendor-react-ecosystem 18.8. vendor-icons was 133.4 and is the whole of the drop — one namespace import of lucide-react in BadgeCollection.tsx. Still 171.4 KB over the 200 KB budget, and the remaining weight is real application code plus React itself rather than another single mistake.

A clean vite build gives a critical path (the JS index.html actually references) of 484 KB gzipped, not 610 KB — index 154.2, vendor-react 87.9, vendor-icons 133.4, vendor-ui 45.2, vendor-supabase 44.5, vendor-react-ecosystem 18.8. Total JS across all 121 chunks is 2010 KB gz against the 500 KB budget. Still 2.4x over the 200 KB critical-path budget. The single largest remaining win is the lucide-react barrel import tracked as WEB-PERF-026 (~100 KB gz, one file).

[prior] FOUND 2026-07-18 (claude/prd-loop-schema-gaps). Measured from a real production build: summed the gzipped size of every JS chunk referenced by dist/index.html. Total JS across all 119 chunks is 1,996KB gzipped; the FIRST-PAINT subset was 1,043KB across 30 chunks. PARTIALLY FIXED in commit c29ec4f6: 1043KB -> 610KB (-433KB, -41%) by stopping the prerender step from baking runtime-injected modulepreload links into the shipped HTML. Full root cause in that commit message — briefly, a removeLazyPreloads() plugin existed and looked correct, but (a) it hooked transformIndexHtml, which ALWAYS runs before Vite injects preloads in generateBundle, so it could never have matched, and (b) even once fixed, the prerenderer re-added them by serializing a live DOM in which Vite’s runtime __vitePreload helper had injected them. Both stages now strip, sharing one pattern list, and the build reports the count so a silent regression is visible. REMAINING 610KB, roughly: index entry 160KB, vendor-icons 131KB, vendor-react 88KB, vendor-ui 45KB, vendor-supabase 44KB, plus small route chunks. vendor-icons at 131KB gzipped for an icon library is the most suspicious single line item. NOT ATTEMPTED: chasing the entry chunk or icon tree-shaking, because both change what is statically reachable and need a real LCP measurement to confirm they help rather than just move weight around. Verified no functional regression: smoke suite 7 passed; the 1 failure is the pre-existing get_active_ads PGRST203 (WEB-QA-020), not this change. | CORE WEB VITALS MEASURED 2026-07-18 against a PRODUCTION build (vite preview), each page in a FRESH browser context so every number is a genuine cold load rather than a warm in-app SPA navigation — an earlier pass measured warm navigations and made /events look 5x faster than it is, so the distinction matters. RESULTS: / LCP=2192ms FCP=1648ms CLS=0 transfer=1229KB | /events LCP=348ms FCP=348ms CLS=0.004 transfer=1262KB | /restaurants LCP=460ms FCP=428ms CLS=0 transfer=1462KB. THE HOMEPAGE IS THE OUTLIER — 5x the LCP of other pages at comparable transfer size, so this is not a bytes problem, it is a homepage-specific render problem. CRITICAL CAVEAT ON THE 2192ms: TTFB was 10ms because this is localhost. Effectively all of that 2.2s is client-side work. Real users add TTFB, slower bandwidth and slower CPUs on top, so the <2.5s LCP target in CLAUDE.md is almost certainly ALREADY MISSED in production even though the local number squeaks under it. Do not read this as passing. LCP ELEMENT IDENTIFIED: the hero H1 ("Good Afternoon! Find things to do in Des Moines, right now") paints at 2328ms. It is TEXT, not an image, so LCP is gated on JS execution and hydration, not on downloading a hero asset — which is why the 433KB preload reduction did not move it much. Note the page IS prerendered, yet the largest paint still lands after hydration; worth understanding why the prerendered hero does not count. Secondary candidate at 1652ms is the COOKIE CONSENT BANNER paragraph, which is briefly the largest element on screen. SLOWEST RESOURCES ARE ALL DATA, NOT ASSETS: the six slowest requests are Supabase REST queries (848, 785, 782, 727, 720, 692ms). See WEB-PERF-022 for the duplicate/unbounded events query among them. CHECKED AND RULED OUT: usePlaygrounds uses select("*"), which looked like a WEB-PERF-001 miss, but playgrounds has only 20 columns and NO seo_/geo_/search_vector/geom fields, so there is nothing heavy to project away. Changing it would have been a cosmetic no-op. | ROOT CAUSE FOUND AND FIXED 2026-07-18 (commit 94dd972b). The homepage LCP was NOT a bundle-size problem, which is why the earlier 433KB preload reduction barely moved it. First paint on every route was render-blocked on fonts.googleapis.com. index.html ships the correct async pattern (rel=preload + onload flip + noscript fallback), but the prerenderer executes the page in Chromium, the onload handler fires and rewrites rel to "stylesheet" in the live DOM, and page.content() serializes that mutation as the shipped HTML. Measured before: local CSS 10-17ms, font CSS 3035ms, FCP 3204ms — FCP tracked the font request exactly. After: FCP 152ms while the font CSS was still in flight at 227ms, i.e. structurally decoupled. Three post-fix cold runs: FCP 1664/152/212ms, LCP 2208/860/1036ms (run 1 = cold browser, no warm DNS). SAME ROOT CAUSE as the modulepreload bug in c29ec4f6 — prerendering bakes runtime DOM mutations into initial HTML. REMAINING WORK ON THIS STORY IS UNCHANGED: critical-path JS is still 610KB gzipped against a 200KB budget (vendor-icons 131KB, entry chunk 160KB), and that still wants a CI budget check. But the LCP emergency is resolved, so re-prioritise accordingly. ALSO WORTH A THIRD LOOK: the prerenderer has now produced two separate production performance regressions by serializing post-JS DOM state. Consider auditing what ELSE it mutates rather than waiting for the next one to be found by measurement.

userStories.title: The blocking unit-test lane is red on main and has been since the tests were added
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I need the vitest lane green, because pr-checks.yml runs it as a blocking step and 5 tests fail, so either PRs are merging over a red required check or the check is not actually enforced.
acceptanceCriteria: npm run test:unit passes
Determine why a blocking check has been failing without anyone acting on it — if the workflow is not actually required on the branch ruleset, make it required

src/contexts/__tests__/AuthContext.test.tsx imports useAuthStatus, which AuthContext does not export. The context exports useAuthState / useAuthFlags / useAuthActions / useAuth — point the test at whichever is the real successor rather than deleting the test

src/components/__tests__/OptimizedImage.test.ts imports canTransform and getTransformedUrl. getTransformedUrl exists but is not exported; canTransform no longer exists at all. See WEB-PERF-021 before making these pass — the assertions encode behaviour the implementation no longer has, so exporting to go green would cement a regression
Extend scripts/check-import-exports.mjs to cover __tests__ directories, which it currently skips — that skip is why this class of breakage is invisible to npm run validate
userStories.notes:
ROOT CAUSE FOUND (CODE REVIEW 2026-08-06): the 4 failures are all TypeError "canTransform is not a function" / "getTransformedUrl is not a function" from src/components/__tests__/OptimizedImage.test.ts:2, which imports both from @/components/OptimizedImage. canTransform has NEVER existed in that file (git log -S "export function canTransform" returns nothing) and getTransformedUrl is declared at OptimizedImage.tsx:76 but not exported (the file exports only OptimizedImageProps, the default, and { OptimizedImage } at :323). Both were introduced by the merge of PR #310. The reason npm run validate stayed green is WEB-CI-024: check-import-exports.mjs:43 skips __tests__. Fix is two exports plus the one-line checker change — not a test rewrite. Confirmed red on this tree: 4 failed / 154 passed of 158.

[prior] FOUND 2026-07-18 (claude/prd-loop-schema-gaps) while verifying an unrelated dependency bump. 5 failures, all TypeError "X is not a function" — the WEB-QA-001 named-import-with-no-matching-export class, in test files. HISTORY CHECKED: at commit 7e117d85, which introduced OptimizedImage.test.ts, canTransform was already declared as a bare `function canTransform` with no export keyword. So these tests have NEVER passed — they were not broken later, they were merged red. Same shape for AuthContext.test.tsx from 69079b80. WHY IT STAYED INVISIBLE: pr-checks.yml:77 runs `npm run test:unit -- --coverage` and the parity audit recorded that lane as blocking, so a required check has been failing for the life of these files. Worth confirming whether the workflow is actually required in the branch ruleset, because the evidence suggests it is not being enforced. ALSO: scripts/check-import-exports.mjs — the guard written for exactly this bug class — explicitly skips __tests__ directories, so `npm run validate` cannot catch it. That skip was reasonable when written; it is now the blind spot. | CLOSED 2026-08-11 (claude/prd-p1-loop). npm run test:unit is 160 passed / 160. THE 2026-08-06 NOTE ON THIS STORY WAS WRONG and AC4 was right: the fix is NOT "two exports plus a one-line checker change". Exporting getTransformedUrl as it stood would have left the test failing, because the test and the implementation disagree about behaviour, not about visibility. MEASURED AGAINST THE LIVE HOST 2026-08-11 with a real object (media/events/a37f0e73.../hero.png): /object/public/... -> 200 image/png 1,011,030 B; /object/public/...?width=320 -> 200 image/png 1,011,030 B (IDENTICAL - sizing params on /object/public/ are ignored, not honoured); /render/image/public/...?width=320&format=webp&quality=80 -> 200 image/webp 99,062 B. 10.2x, and image transformations are confirmed enabled on this project. So every srcset candidate the component emitted was the same full-size PNG under a different `w` descriptor. That is worse than shipping no srcset: it tells the browser it has a choice of sizes it does not have, so it picks the "smallest" candidate and downloads a megabyte anyway, and WEB-PERF-004 ("right-sized responsive images", marked passes:true) has not actually been delivering. FIXED THE IMPLEMENTATION, NOT THE TEST: getTransformedUrl now rewrites /storage/v1/object/public/ to /storage/v1/render/image/public/ for Supabase Storage URLs and returns everything else untouched; canTransform added and exported; generateTransformedSrcSet exported and now returns undefined rather than a list of identical URLs when the source cannot be resized; renderPictureSources returns null for the same case so no inert <source> is emitted. Two tests added covering the srcset behaviour, which is the half with the production consequence and which nothing asserted. AC2 ANSWERED, and the answer is not "the check was not required": .github/rulesets/main.json and develop.json both list context "Lint, Type Check, Test & Build" (the pr-checks.yml job that runs npm run test:unit) under required_status_checks. The mechanism is bypass_actors -> actor_id 5 (RepositoryRole: admin), bypass_mode "always", which .github/rulesets/README.md documents deliberately as the solo-merge path since GitHub will not let you approve your own PR. So the check was required, it was failing, and admin solo-merges went through it by design. NOT CHANGED HERE: narrowing that bypass is a governance decision about the repo owner's own ability to merge, and it belongs to the owner, not to this branch. SEPARATE OBSERVATION worth acting on: the app-type-ratchet job added for WEB-CI-023 is also absent from all three rulesets' required_status_checks, so it currently advises rather than gates. AC3 was already satisfied before this session - AuthContext.test.tsx no longer imports useAuthStatus and passes. AC5 done via WEB-CI-024. npm run validate exits 0 (5086 eslint problems, 0 errors).

userStories.title: External images are proxied through image-transform, which does not resize them
userStories.description: As a visitor, I need external images to load directly, because they are currently routed through an edge function that adds a network hop without reducing bytes.
acceptanceCriteria: Decide the intended behaviour. The WEB-PERF-004 test asserts external URLs serve unchanged, with the stated reason that image-transform does not resize, so proxying adds a hop for zero byte savings
If that reasoning still holds, make getTransformedUrl return external URLs untouched and restore the guard the test was written to provide
If image-transform HAS gained resizing since, update the test and its comment instead, and say so explicitly
Note the load implication: image-transform is one of the public verify_jwt=false endpoints (rate-limited). Routing every external image through it puts real traffic on a public function
Whichever way it goes, the assertions must actually run — see WEB-CI-020
userStories.notes:
RE-VERIFIED (CODE REVIEW 2026-08-06): still true. supabase/functions/image-transform/index.ts accepts a width param (:45) and its header still describes itself as a "public image proxy", with no resize implementation — external images are proxied at full size, adding a hop for zero byte savings.
