This is also why src/components/OptimizedImage.tsx deliberately refuses to route external URLs through it (the behaviour the broken WEB-CI-020 test was trying to assert).

[prior] FOUND 2026-07-18. src/components/OptimizedImage.tsx getTransformedUrl sends any non-Supabase-Storage URL to /functions/v1/image-transform with width/format/quality params. The test at src/components/__tests__/OptimizedImage.test.ts asserts the opposite ("returns external URLs unchanged (no transform applied)") and documents the reason inline as WEB-PERF-004. This is NOT simply a stale test. The test encodes a deliberate performance decision; the implementation does the thing that decision rejected. Because the test never ran green (see WEB-CI-020), nothing ever flagged the divergence. SEVERITY kept at 3 deliberately: I did not measure how many external images a real page actually loads, so the impact is unquantified. Measure before prioritising — if most images are Supabase Storage URLs, the proxy path is rarely taken and this is minor. NOT FIXED HERE: changing image routing alters what every page requests, and the right answer depends on whether image-transform has gained resizing since WEB-PERF-004. That is a product/infra fact I could not establish from the code alone. | CLOSED 2026-08-11 (claude/prd-p1-loop) as part of WEB-CI-020. AC1 decided: the WEB-PERF-004 reasoning still holds. Re-checked the function rather than trusting the story - image-transform/index.ts:219-222 is still a commented-out sharp resize block, so it remains a pass-through proxy. AC3 therefore does not apply. AC2 done: getTransformedUrl returns non-Supabase-Storage URLs unchanged, and generateTransformedSrcSet now emits no srcset at all for them instead of seven proxy URLs that all resolve to the same full-size bytes. AC4 satisfied as a side effect: the web app no longer sends any traffic to /functions/v1/image-transform - it is now unreferenced from src/. DELIBERATELY NOT DELETING THE EDGE FUNCTION: iOS prd POLISH-002 documents the image-transform contract (verify_jwt=false, ?url=&width=&quality=), so shipped mobile binaries may still call it, and retiring it is a MIN_SUPPORTED_APP_VERSION-gated decision per CLAUDE.md, not a cleanup. AC5 done: the assertions run and pass.

userStories.title: Color contrast fails WCAG AA across the site (71 nodes on /events alone)
userStories.description: As a low-vision visitor, I need text to meet the 4.5:1 contrast ratio CLAUDE.md commits to, because axe reports serious color-contrast violations on every measured public page except /auth.
acceptanceCriteria: Identify the offending token(s) in the Tailwind theme — the volume (71 nodes on one page) points at a small number of shared colours, most likely muted-foreground on a light surface, not 71 separate mistakes
Raise the failing token(s) to 4.5:1 for body text and 3:1 for large text, and re-run the axe probe on / /events /restaurants /pricing
Fix at the token level, not per-component — a per-instance fix will drift straight back
Verify in dark mode as well; the probe only covered the default theme
Once clean, remove continue-on-error from the accessibility job in e2e.yml so this cannot regress silently (see WEB-CI-021)
userStories.notes:
SCOPE FOLLOW-UP 2026-08-22 (claude/prd-p1-loop). This story is CORRECTLY closed - AC2 named '/ /events /restaurants /pricing' and all four measure clean, confirmed independently by a full axe run today. But the token work did not reach the rest of the site, and a wider run found contrast still failing on NINE other pages: free-events, open-now-restaurants, attractions, playgrounds, articles, contact, privacy-policy, terms, accessibility-statement.

The dominant offender was ONE pair, and it is now fixed: #9ca3af (gray-400) on #f9fafb (gray-50) at 2.43:1 against a 4.5:1 requirement, 198 of ~212 failing nodes. Interestingly this vindicates the ORIGINAL hypothesis in AC1 that these failures come from 'a small number of shared colours' - true here, just with a different token than the muted-foreground it guessed, and on pages this story never probed.

FIXED at the token level per AC3: all 30 `text-gray-400` usages in src/ moved to `text-gray-500`, the first shade clearing 4.5:1 on BOTH light backgrounds (4.63:1 on gray-50, 4.83:1 on white; gray-400 was 2.43 and 2.54). Checked first that none of the 30 sat on a dark background where the change would make contrast worse - none did. Same methodology this story used to pick -700 for the category hues.
VERIFIED by re-running the axe block: occurrences of #9ca3af went 297 -> 0.

NOT FIXED, deliberately: #16a34a (green-600) on white at 3.30:1, 4 nodes. green-700 would clear it at 5.02:1, but `text-green-600` has 141 usages of which 15 ARE on dark backgrounds, where the change would make things worse. A blanket swap risks 15 regressions to fix 4 nodes; it needs per-instance judgement and is not worth doing blind.

FIXED 2026-08-11 (claude/prd-p1-loop). Both themes now measure CLEAN on / /events /restaurants /pricing.

AC1 — THE STORY'S HYPOTHESIS WAS WRONG, and measuring is what showed it. It predicted 'a small number of shared tokens, most likely muted-foreground'. Every core token in src/index.css already passed: muted-foreground is 6.62:1 on background, 6.02:1 on muted, and 7-9:1 in dark. The light-theme failures were raw Tailwind -500 shades used as badge backgrounds under white text, spread across components.

MEASURED, LIGHT THEME: 126 color-contrast nodes + 1 button-name -> 0. Worst offenders by count: white on violet-500 (50 nodes, 4.23:1), neutral-500 on neutral-900 (24, 3.78:1), white on amber-500 (22, 2.15:1), orange-600 on orange-50 (12, 3.35:1), white on emerald-500 (4, 2.54:1).

AC2+AC3 — FIXED AT THE TOKEN LEVEL. src/lib/categoryStyles.ts moved all seven category hues to -700, the first shade where white clears 4.5:1 on ALL of them (-600 clears violet, pink and slate but not orange, emerald, sky or green, so a per-hue mix would have been unreasonable). Added a STATUS_BADGE export for featured/open/free/closing-soon, which had been pasted as literals into SocialEventCard, RestaurantCard, HotelCard and AttractionDetails — all four wrong the same way, which is exactly the drift AC3 warns about. Also fixed at source: Footer (neutral-500 -> -400, 7.11:1), RestaurantOpenings' status map, RestaurantCard's Popular chip and dietary chips, two Index tile accents, the Newsletter subscribe button.

AC4 — DARK THEME, WHICH HAD NEVER BEEN MEASURED: 70 nodes -> 0. Unlike light mode these WERE the theme tokens. --primary at L=60% failed both ways it is used: 4.23:1 for --primary-foreground on a primary button (21 nodes, every primary CTA in the app) and 4.26:1 for text-primary on the dark card (5 more). Now L=68% -> 5.87:1 and 5.92:1. --secondary at L=55% was 4.10:1 under white across 21 nodes; now L=45% -> 5.23:1. Its old comment read 'slightly brighter for dark mode', which is what broke it — brightening a mid-red UNDER white text moves it toward the text. Hover now darkens (40%, 6.33:1) to match the light theme's 41%->36% instead of contradicting it.

THE BUG CLASS WORTH REMEMBERING: a token whose lightness FLIPS between themes cannot be paired with a fixed text colour. DEFAULT_CATEGORY_STYLE.bg was 'bg-primary' and every consumer appends literal text-white — fine on the light theme's deep navy (15.23:1), 3.23:1 on the dark theme's lightened blue. Now a fixed blue-900 (10.36:1 in both). Seven more 'bg-primary text-white' sites moved to text-primary-foreground, which tracks.

ALSO FIXED, each measured first: three dark-mode patterns that were silently inert. RestaurantCard's dietary chips carried 'dark:bg-opacity-20 dark:text-opacity-90' — opacity modifiers with no colour utility to act on, so in dark mode the chips kept their LIGHT background (3.02:1); they now carry real dark pairs. Restaurants.tsx wrapped the page in bg-gray-50 with no dark counterpart, so dark:text-gray-100 headings landed on near-white (3.00:1). Two hardcoded text-[#2D1B69] / text-[#DC143C] values that bypass the theme entirely.

ONE FALSE POSITIVE, HANDLED WITHOUT SUPPRESSING ANYTHING: the gold QuickActions button reported 4.5:1 against the PAGE background, because a gradient sets background-image and leaves background-color transparent, so axe resolves against the nearest solid ancestor. Real ratio is 10.17:1 at the gradient's start. Added a solid bg-[#FFC107] under the gradient (8.75:1) so the computed colour is honest for any tool that reads it, and so the button degrades sanely if the gradient never paints.

RATCHET: src/lib/__tests__/categoryStyles.test.ts, 29 tests that compute the real WCAG ratio for every value the map can return rather than pinning class strings, so a future bg-teal-500 fails without anyone remembering the rule. Proved it fires by reverting violet to -500 and watching 'Music: white on the solid badge clears 4.5:1' fail. It has no exemption for the default entry — that exemption is precisely how 8 dark-mode nodes shipped.

METHOD: scripts/.axe-probe.mjs (throwaway, not committed) serves dist/ and runs @axe-core/playwright with wcag2a+2aa+21a+21aa. The dark pass seeds localStorage 'dmi-theme' before first paint and ASSERTS the .dark class actually applied, so a failed toggle cannot be reported as a clean light-theme run.

AC5 STAYS OPEN and belongs to WEB-CI-021: contrast is clean, but the a11y suite also covers keyboard nav, focus visibility, skip links, heading order, touch targets and document titles, and the last full run was 66 passed / 24 failed. Removing continue-on-error needs those too. It is further blocked by WEB-CI-025 — the PR pipeline is switched off.

[prior] MEASURED 2026-07-18 (claude/prd-loop-schema-gaps) with @axe-core/playwright against a running app, tags wcag2a+wcag2aa+wcag21a+wcag21aa. Per-page violation counts: / = critical/button-name(1) + serious/color-contrast(10); /events = serious/color-contrast(71); /restaurants = critical/button-name(1) + serious/color-contrast(30); /pricing = serious/color-contrast(6); /auth = CLEAN (0). The button-name half is FIXED in commit 6ad76efd (NLPSearchBar icon buttons). Everything remaining is colour contrast. NOT ATTEMPTED, deliberately: contrast is fixed by changing theme tokens, which is a brand/design decision with site-wide visual consequences. Guessing at replacement colours would be worse than reporting the measurement. The concentration (71 nodes on one page) strongly suggests one or two shared tokens rather than scattered one-offs, so the real fix is probably small once someone picks the values. CONTEXT: CLAUDE.md Quality Standards claims "A11y: WCAG 2.1 AA, keyboard nav, ARIA labels, 4.5:1 contrast". The full suite result was 66 passed / 24 failed, so that claim is currently aspirational rather than met.

userStories.title: The accessibility suite runs in CI but cannot fail the build
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I need a11y regressions to block, because e2e.yml runs the accessibility suite with continue-on-error: true, so 24 failing tests have never surfaced as a red build.
acceptanceCriteria: Once WEB-UX-030 is fixed, remove continue-on-error from the "Run critical E2E suites" step in .github/workflows/e2e.yml, or split accessibility into its own blocking job
If the suite is too flaky to block on wholesale, gate on the axe checks only (they are deterministic) and leave the keyboard/focus tests advisory — partial enforcement beats none
Record the current failure list as a baseline if a ratchet is preferred, matching the strict-baseline and schema-baseline convention already used here
userStories.notes:
THE AXE BLOCK IS FULLY GREEN 2026-08-22: 48 passed, 0 failed, in 1.1 minutes. It started this session at 20 failed / 28 passed with 18 real failures across nine pages.

THE LAST TWO 'FAILURES' WERE NOT DEFECTS, and finding that out is the useful part:
  1. /articles reported color-contrast #757d95 on white at 4.09:1. Solved rather than guessed: --muted-foreground is HSL(225 20% 40%) = #525c7a, which is 6.62:1 on white and passes comfortably. #757d95 is EXACTLY #525c7a composited over white at 80% opacity - a byte match, checked against 50/60/70/75/80/90%. Cause: `animate-fade-in` animates opacity 0->1 over 0.3s with a staggered animationDelay (Articles.tsx uses index * 50ms across 18 published articles, so the last card is still fading at ~1200ms). Axe was scanning mid-fade and measuring contrast against partially transparent text. Fixed by waiting for non-infinite animations to reach playState 'finished' before scanning.
  2. Both HOMEPAGE scans were goto timeouts, not findings - so the highest-traffic page on the site was never actually being scanned. Measured: DOMContentLoaded at 22.4s in dev, #main-content at 22.5s, and networkidle NEVER arrives - goto still times out at 60s. Raising the timeout does not help because requests stay in flight indefinitely. Replaced with domcontentloaded + the #main-content landmark + animations settled, which is both reachable and a better 'rendered and stable' signal than networkidle ever was.

A CHANGE I MADE AND REVERTED, recorded so nobody repeats it: I converted the OTHER describe blocks (Keyboard, ARIA, Semantic, Focus, Skip, Heading Hierarchy) to the same wait. It looked like a win - the full suite went 21 failed / 114 passed to 10 failed / 125 passed and 7.5min to 2.3min, with the 18 timeouts gone. But it turned them into EIGHT 'exactly one h1' failures reporting Received: 0, and #main-content mounts before those pages render their heading. I could not establish whether those were real, because by then the dev server had degraded under ~15 consecutive suite runs to the point that a bare goto to / timed out at 60s. Reverted rather than ship failures I could not verify. The non-axe blocks are unchanged and still carry their pre-existing ~18 networkidle timeouts.
  If someone picks this up: the conversion is probably right, but gotoSettled needs a content-rendered signal stronger than #main-content, and it must be measured on a FRESH dev server.

AC1 STATUS: available for the axe checks specifically, which is AC2's proposal and now a much better deal than when it was written - the deterministic half is 48/48 green rather than where all the failures lived. The full suite is not ready; its remaining failures are dominated by the timeouts above, not by site defects.

DOWN TO ONE REAL PAGE 2026-08-22. The axe block is now 4 failed / 44 passed - and TWO of the four are goto timeouts on the HOMEPAGE, which is harness flake, not the site. Started this session at 20 failed / 28 passed with 18 real failures across nine pages.
  Remaining real: /articles only, both its axe tests, one rule.

THE LAST DEFECT, measured precisely: color-contrast, #757d95 on #ffffff at 4.09:1 against a 4.5:1 requirement. A 0.41 miss. Solved for its origin rather than guessing: --muted-foreground is HSL(225 20% 40%) = #525c7a, and compositing that over white at exactly 80% opacity yields #757d95 - an exact byte match, checked against 50/60/70/75/80/90%. So something renders muted-foreground at 80% opacity on an article card.
  It is NOT a literal class: grep for 'muted-foreground/80' across src/ returns nothing, and Articles.tsx has no opacity- utility. So it comes from a shared card component's CSS or a computed style. That is where the next person should look; the colour and the exact opacity are the search key.

FIXED THIS ROUND: FreeEvents text-green-600 -> green-700 (3.30:1 -> 5.02:1), 2 usages, scoped to that page for the same reason as OpenNowRestaurants - the global change stays declined because 15 of green-600's 141 usages sit on dark backgrounds.

A CORRECTION TO MY OWN EARLIER NOTE: I attributed the two timeouts to free-events. They are on the HOMEPAGE. I had grouped failures by page without checking which were timeouts, and the counts happened to line up. Classify by error type, not by count.
  Also worth knowing: a standalone probe of /articles and /free-events with the SAME networkidle wait reported both CLEAN while the suite reported both failing. Page content varies between runs (which articles and free events happen to render), so a green probe is not proof - re-run the suite itself.

AC1 IS NOW WITHIN REACH: one page, one rule, one 0.41 ratio miss. Fix that and remove continue-on-error. The homepage timeouts should be addressed in the same change or the gate inherits them - switching those goto calls off waitUntil:'networkidle' is the usual remedy.

MOST OF THE BACKLOG IS GONE 2026-08-22 (claude/prd-p1-loop). The axe block went from 20 failed / 28 passed to 5 failed / 43 passed, and REAL failures from 18 across nine pages to THREE across two.
Remaining: free-events x2, articles x1 (one color-contrast), plus 2 goto timeouts which are harness flake, not the site.

This changes the AC1/AC2/AC3 answer recorded earlier. A ratchet is no longer worth building for three failures; finish them and AC1 becomes available - remove continue-on-error and get a real gate rather than a fourth baseline file codifying the debt.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY WRONG, all of it mundane and none of it needing a design decision:
  link-in-text-block (serious) - in-text links distinguished by COLOUR ALONE. `text-primary hover:underline` underlines only on hover, which fails WCAG 1.4.1. Fixed on PrivacyPolicy (14), AccessibilityStatement (7), Terms (3) by underlining at rest; Contact's 8 mailto links used `text-muted-foreground hover:text-primary` with no underline at all and got the same treatment.
  button-name (critical) - Radix <SelectTrigger> renders <button role="combobox"> with NO accessible name. Each had a visible <label> above it carrying no htmlFor, so it named nothing. Fixed on Articles (2), Attractions (3), Playgrounds (3) with aria-label DERIVED FROM THAT VISIBLE LABEL - 'Attraction Type', 'Minimum Rating', 'Age Range' and so on - so the accessible name matches what a sighted user reads. This is a shadcn/ui pattern issue and will recur on every new Select; the durable fix is a wrapper that requires a label.
  color-contrast - OpenNowRestaurants used text-green-600 (3.30:1) and text-muted-foreground/70. Scoped to that page, which is why it was safe here: doing text-green-600 globally was declined earlier because 15 of its 141 usages sit on dark backgrounds where -700 is worse.

MEASUREMENT NOTE worth keeping: a probe using domcontentloaded + a fixed wait reported /free-events CLEAN while the suite's networkidle wait reports it failing. Different wait strategies see different render states, so verify against the suite's own strategy before believing a page is fixed.

Quality: npm run validate exit 0, strict ratchet no regressions.

PARTIAL PROGRESS 2026-08-22, and an honest negative result: fixing the dominant contrast offender did NOT reduce the failure count.

All 30 `text-gray-400` usages moved to `text-gray-500` (see WEB-UX-030). Verified: #9ca3af occurrences in the axe output went 297 -> 0. But the axe block still reports 18 real failures across the SAME nine pages, because each page carries several distinct violation types and the test asserts ZERO violations - so one remaining rule keeps a page red regardless of how many nodes were cleared.
Rule mix after the fix: link-in-text-block 7, color-contrast 5 (other colours), button-name 5, link-in-text-block-style 4, implicit-label 3, aria-label 3.

That is the useful lesson for whoever picks this up: node-count reduction and page-level pass/fail are different measures, and only the second one moves this gate. The remaining work is a per-page sweep of 9 pages across ~5 rule types, not another token change.

MEASURED 2026-08-22 (claude/prd-p1-loop) so the AC1/AC2/AC3 choice can be made on numbers. AC1's precondition is met - WEB-UX-030 is closed - but AC1 is NOT available, because closing it did not clear axe.

Ran tests/accessibility.spec.ts on chromium-desktop alone (the story's 66/24 figure predates the page list growing; it is 135 tests now, not 90):
    94 passed, 41 failed, 9.1 minutes
Splitting the 41 by cause, which is the part that decides the story:
    18  REAL axe violations
     3  real behavioural failures (heading hierarchy, keyboard, ARIA)
    20  page.goto TIMEOUTS on waitUntil:'networkidle' against the dev server - infrastructure flake, not accessibility
Nearly half the red is the harness, not the site. Note playwright.config.ts starts `npm run dev` and the spec waits for networkidle; a dev server with HMR may never go idle, so this flake is structural and will occur in CI too.

AC1 IS OUT: 18 real axe violations remain, so removing continue-on-error wholesale turns the lane red on day one - the exact failure mode WEB-CI-025's AC5 warns about and the reason strict-ratchet.mjs's own header says 'a gate that always fails teaches everyone to ignore it'.

AC2 IS WEAKER THAN IT SOUNDS: it proposes gating on the axe checks 'because they are deterministic'. They are deterministic, but they are also where ALL 18 real failures live. Gating on axe only is gating on the failing half.

AC3 IS THE RIGHT ANSWER, and here is the baseline it asks for. Exactly NINE pages fail, each failing both axe tests (violations + critical violations) = 18:
    free-events, open-now-restaurants, attractions, playgrounds, articles, contact, privacy-policy, terms, accessibility-statement
Rules cited, by frequency: label 30, aria-labelledby 25, aria-label 21, color-contrast 15, link-in-text-block 15, button-name 9, button-has-visible-text 6, non-empty-title 6, implicit-label 6.

TWO THINGS WORTH NOTICING. The homepage and /events PASS - the highest-traffic pages are clean, so this is a long-tail problem, which makes a ratchet more attractive than a freeze. And color-contrast still appears 15 times even though WEB-UX-030 is closed, so that work did not reach these nine pages; worth re-checking before WEB-UX-030 is trusted as done.

THE CHEAPER OPTION THAN A RATCHET: 9 pages, dominated by missing form labels and accessible names on buttons/links. That is a bounded fix, not a programme - plausibly smaller than building and maintaining a fourth baseline file alongside strict-baseline.json, schema-baseline.json and app-type-baseline.json. Fixing the nine and THEN removing continue-on-error gets a real gate instead of a ratchet that codifies the debt.

SEPARATELY, AND FIRST: the 20 networkidle timeouts should be addressed whichever route is chosen, or any gate built on this suite inherits a ~15% flake rate. Switching those goto calls to waitUntil:'domcontentloaded' plus an explicit wait for the assertion target is the usual fix.

FOUND 2026-07-18. .github/workflows/e2e.yml runs tests/accessibility.spec.ts (plus links-and-buttons, forms, mobile-responsive) under `continue-on-error: true`. The suite is genuinely strict — it asserts zero axe violations against wcag2a/2aa/21a/21aa — but nothing acts on the result. Ran it locally: 66 passed, 24 failed, 11.5 minutes. Failures span axe violations, keyboard navigation, focus visibility, skip links, heading hierarchy (h1 count and level skips), icon-button labels, touch targets, and document titles. This is the same shape as WEB-CI-020 (the unit lane failing under a supposedly blocking check): a quality gate that exists, runs, and cannot fail. Worth treating the two together — the pattern is guards that are present but inert.

userStories.title: Homepage fires two overlapping events queries, one of them unbounded
userStories.description: As a visitor, I need the homepage to fetch events once and with a bound, because it currently issues two near-identical queries and one has no limit, making it the slowest request on the page.
acceptanceCriteria: SmartEventNavigation calls useEvents() with no arguments, so no limit is applied and the query returns every future event (260 today) with the full 24-column projection. Give it the limit it actually renders

Reconcile with AllInclusiveDashboard, which issues its own useEvents call with different filters — different filters mean different react-query keys, so both fetch independently rather than sharing a cache entry
Confirm whether both components need distinct result sets at all, or whether one query can serve both via a shared key
Re-measure: the unbounded query took 848ms and the limited one 785ms, together the two slowest requests on the homepage
No change to the events response shape that shipped mobile binaries read (CLAUDE.md)
userStories.notes:
FIXED 2026-08-11 (claude/prd-p1-loop). One line, but the reasoning behind the specific value matters more than the change.

AC1 DONE. src/components/SmartEventNavigation.tsx called useEvents() with no arguments, so no limit reached PostgREST and the homepage pulled every future event with the full EVENT_LIST_COLUMNS projection — to render at most 30 items across six slices, none larger than 6. It now passes { limit: 100 }.

AC2 + AC3 DONE, and they are the same fix. eventsQueryKey() is built from the normalised filter object, so an identical filter object is an identical react-query key. AllInclusiveDashboard already asks for exactly { limit: 100 } and is mounted on the same page, so matching it collapses the two components onto ONE cache entry and one request. Any other number here — including a more "tuned" 40 — silently reintroduces the second fetch. That coupling is stated in the code, because it is the kind of thing someone tidies up later without knowing.

MEASURED on a clean production build served locally against the real backend, counting every /rest/v1/ request:
  homepage total   24 -> 22 REST requests
  events table      6 ->  5 requests
  full-projection list queries  2 -> 1
The surviving events requests are: [1] the shared limit=100 list, [2] and [3] the two head:true counts from useHomepageStats (WEB-QA-024), [4] a featured rail at limit=6, [5] an upcoming rail at limit=6. Everything left is bounded and distinct — there is no remaining pair fetching the same rows under different keys.

AC4 PARTIALLY. Request COUNTS re-measured as above. Per-request timings were not: the original 848ms/785ms figures came from a production trace, and re-timing against a live backend from a local box produces numbers that vary more than the effect being measured. The durable result is structural — one fewer unbounded full-projection query — rather than a millisecond delta I cannot reproduce reliably.

AC5 SATISFIED TRIVIALLY: only a client-side limit changed. No request or response shape moved, so nothing a shipped mobile binary reads is affected.

NOT THE TARGET, checked and left alone: useFeaturedEvents in src/hooks/useSupabase.ts issues two events queries, but that is a deliberate two-pass design — sponsored first, then organic fill for the remaining slots — and both passes are bounded. Consolidating them would change what the rail shows.

VERIFIED: npm run lint 0 errors, npx vitest run 193/193, check-imports clean, build green at 35/35.

[prior] RE-VERIFIED (CODE REVIEW 2026-08-06): src/pages/Index.tsx no longer calls useQuery directly (grep count is 0) and takes its counters from useHomepageStats. The unbounded second query described here now lives in that hook — src/hooks/useHomepageStats.ts issues three head:true count queries in a Promise.all (:37-55), two of them against events. Overlapping-events work is therefore partly relocated rather than removed; useEvents is still consumed by src/components/AllInclusiveDashboard.tsx:150. Re-scope alongside the new WEB-QA-024, which rewrites that hook.

[prior] FOUND 2026-07-18 while measuring Core Web Vitals on a production build (see WEB-PERF-020). Resource timing on a cold homepage load shows two events requests with the same EVENT_LIST_COLUMNS projection and the same date/is_merged/is_hidden filters, differing only in that one carries limit=100 and the other carries no limit at all. Both AllInclusiveDashboard and SmartEventNavigation are mounted on the homepage and each calls useEvents with different filter objects, which produces different query keys, so react-query cannot dedupe them. SEVERITY 3 deliberately: these are parallel XHRs after first paint, so they do not block LCP directly (LCP is the hero H1 at 2328ms, gated on hydration). The cost is server load, bandwidth, and interaction latency once the lists populate — not the headline metric. NOT FIXED HERE: adding a limit changes what SmartEventNavigation renders, and I could not establish from the code how many events it is meant to show. A wrong limit silently truncates a homepage module, which is worse than a slow query. | RAISED 3 -> 2 ON MEASUREMENT (2026-07-18). Captured actual response sizes on the homepage against production: the unbounded query returns 238,593 BYTES, making it by far the largest single request the homepage issues — bigger than the entire critical-path JS payload after compression, and roughly 7x the next event query. The limited companion returns 90,871B. Total events payload on one homepage load is ~341KB uncompressed. This was filed at severity 3 when the only evidence was "two overlapping queries, one unbounded"; the size changes the picture. It is now the single biggest data-transfer item on the homepage and should be treated as the next performance task after WEB-PERF-020. The fix is still blocked on the same question as before: SmartEventNavigation calls useEvents() with no arguments, and I could not establish from the code how many events it is meant to render, so a guessed limit risks silently truncating a homepage module. Someone who knows the intended design can close this in minutes.

userStories.title: 12 prerendered routes render no SEOHead, so they ship with no canonical and the site-wide default description
userStories.description: As the platform owner, I need every indexable route to declare its own SEO metadata, because a dozen routes ship with no canonical of their own and all 31 share a single meta description.
acceptanceCriteria: Add SEOHead (with an explicit url prop) to: /advertise, /business, /calendar, /deals, /itineraries, /map, /pricing, and the five /events/<city> pages
/business and /map additionally render no h1 at all — add one

Give the five /events/<city> pages distinct titles. They currently all share the same "Events by Location" title, which reads as duplicate content across Altoona, Ankeny, Clive, Johnston and Urbandale
/calendar duplicates the homepage title verbatim
All 31 routes currently share ONE meta description (the static default in index.html). Give at least the top landing routes their own
Re-run the audit and expect: 31 routes, 0 missing canonical, 0 duplicate title groups, 0 duplicate canonical groups
userStories.notes:
FIXED 2026-08-11 (claude/prd-p1-loop). AC6 met in full, measured against dist/**/index.html on a clean build: 35 routes, 0 missing canonical, 0 missing h1, 0 duplicate title groups, 0 duplicate canonical groups, 0 duplicate description groups, and every canonical self-references its own URL.

THE DIAGNOSIS IN THIS STORY WAS WRONG, and that matters more than the numbers. AC1 says to add SEOHead to twelve routes including the five /events/<city> pages. There was nothing to add: FreeEvents, DateNightEvents, KidsEvents, EventsByLocation, EventsToday and EventsThisWeekend all already render EnhancedLocalSEO with a canonical prop, verified by grep across all six. ACs 2, 3 and 4 (missing h1, shared "Events by Location" title, /calendar duplicating the homepage title) were already satisfied by earlier work and measured clean before I changed anything.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY BROKEN was the prerenderer, not the pages. Audit of the build before this fix:
  /events/free         data-rh= 9  canonical=NO   jsonld=1
  /events/date-night   data-rh= 9  canonical=NO   jsonld=1
  /events/ankeny       data-rh= 9  canonical=NO   jsonld=1
  /events/johnston     data-rh= 9  canonical=NO   jsonld=1
  /events/kids         data-rh=31  canonical=yes  jsonld=6
  /events/urbandale    data-rh=30  canonical=yes  jsonld=5
  /events/altoona      data-rh=30  canonical=yes  jsonld=5
  /events/clive        data-rh=30  canonical=yes  jsonld=5
/events/ankeny and /events/urbandale are the SAME component with the SAME props in the SAME build, and one shipped a canonical while the other did not. 9 is exactly the number of data-rh tags index.html authors itself, so on the failing routes Helmet never committed at all and the page shipped with only the shell fallback tags. A race, not a missing component — which is why the count of affected routes kept moving between audits and read as "12 routes render no SEOHead".

ROOT CAUSE. scripts/prerender.mjs waited for Helmet with the predicate !!document.head.querySelector('[data-rh]') and a 5s timeout. That had silently become a no-op: index.html now authors 9 data-rh tags of its own, because WEB-SEO-002/012 deliberately hands the fallback title/description/og tags to Helmet so per-page values REPLACE rather than duplicate them. The selector therefore matched before React had even mounted, every route fell through to a fixed 250ms sleep, and the heaviest pages lost. This is the second heuristic in that file broken by the same index.html change — the "ALREADY PRERENDERED" guard was the first, fixed earlier in this session under WEB-OPS-020.

FIX. The wait now requires the live head's data-rh count to EXCEED the shell's baseline, computed from buildHtml at runtime rather than hardcoded, with the timeout raised 5s -> 8s. A route that genuinely renders no SEO component still times out exactly as before, so nothing is masked.

VERIFIED under load (the app-project tsc was running concurrently, which makes the race MORE likely, not less): 35/35 routes prerendered, data-rh range 11-52 across all routes — every one above the baseline of 9, which is direct evidence Helmet committed everywhere rather than an inference from the canonical being present.

AC5 is met as a consequence: the four routes sharing the site-wide default description were the same four that lost Helmet. With Helmet committing, each carries its own.

NOT CLOSED BY THIS: /events/date-night ships 756 KB of HTML with 734 inline SVGs, 8x the /events hub that lists more items. It is the page that lost the race most reliably, which fits the prerenderer's own browser-per-worker note that the heaviest page loses first. Filed as WEB-PERF-027.

CAVEAT: verified locally only. There is no CI run to confirm against — see WEB-CI-025, the PR Checks workflow is switched off.

[prior] FOUND 2026-07-18 (claude/prd-loop-schema-gaps) by auditing the actual prerendered output rather than the source, across all 31 dist/**/index.html files with HTML comments stripped. EXPOSED BY, NOT CAUSED BY, commit 6d1bf574. These 12 routes never rendered SEOHead; they were silently inheriting the hardcoded homepage canonical from index.html. That inherited tag was actively harmful — it told crawlers each route was a duplicate of the homepage — so removing it is a net improvement, since Google self-canonicalizes to the page URL when no tag is present. The underlying gap is that these pages have no SEO identity of their own. STATE AFTER THE FIX: 31 routes, 0 missing title, 0 missing description, 12 missing canonical, 5 missing h1, 0 duplicate canonical groups, 2 duplicate title groups, and all 31 sharing one description. CONTEXT WORTH KEEPING: the prerender step exists specifically to fix soft-404 and "discovered, not indexed" (PROD-SEO-001). Before this fix it emitted 31 pages that each declared the homepage as their canonical — it was actively instructing Google not to index the very routes it was built to get indexed. That is a plausible cause of the original symptom, so re-check Search Console once this deploys. | RELATED FINDINGS 2026-07-30 (claude/des-moines-seo-strategy-n54bjj), surfaced by WEB-SEO-012. Two things this story should absorb. FIRST, the homepage renders two competing head managers: SEOEnhancedHead (Index.tsx ~379) and SEOStructure (~409) both emit title and meta description into Helmet, and last-mount-wins means SEOStructure's defaults silently beat anything set on SEOEnhancedHead. Any page rendering both has the same trap, and it is invisible in review — an edit to the losing component compiles, reads correctly, and changes nothing in the shipped HTML. Worth auditing every page for multiple head managers and collapsing to one per page. SECOND, this story's claim that all 31 routes share ONE meta description is now half-addressed: the static description in index.html has been rewritten from a product pitch to a query-focused site-wide fallback, so routes with no description of their own at least inherit something sensible. But Helmet APPENDS rather than replacing it, so every prerendered route now ships TWO description tags with the static one first. Giving each route its own description is still needed, and deduplicating the tag is new work this story should own. | MAJOR PRERENDER BUG FOUND AND FIXED 2026-07-30 (claude/des-moines-seo-strategy-n54bjj) while auditing this story. THE PRERENDERER WAS SILENTLY DISCARDING THE <head> OF THE HEAVIEST PAGES. scripts/prerender.mjs opened N concurrent pages in ONE Chromium. Only one page is ever the active tab, and the rest never get rAF callbacks serviced; react-helmet-async commits <head> from a rAF, so on backgrounded tabs it never runs at all. The failure is silent and asymmetric — the body renders completely, correct content and correct h1, while title, canonical and every JSON-LD block stay at the build shell's values, and the run reports success. Measured on a pristine dist/ varying only concurrency: 1 and 2 gave the homepage its real title and canonical; 3, 4 and 6 gave data-rh=0, no canonical, shell title. The heaviest page loses first, which here was the homepage — so the single most valuable URL on the site was shipping no canonical, no JSON-LD, and a title nobody wrote. FIX: one browser process per worker, each with its own foreground page. Verified data-rh=35 and correct canonical at concurrency 3 and 6. Two hypotheses were tested and REJECTED with clean A/Bs before landing this — --disable-renderer-backgrounding and friends make no difference, and the flat 600ms settle was a symptom not the cause (it is now a precise wait for Helmet's data-rh marker, 5s cap). NOTE THIS WAS PARTLY SELF-INFLICTED: the concurrency pool was added in this same branch for WEB-SEO-006, so the shared-browser bug shipped and was caught within the same session. ALSO FIXED: prerender re-run against an already-prerendered dist/ served the rendered homepage as the SPA fallback, corrupting heads via hydration mismatch — 9 of 35 routes failed the canonical guard in that state. It now detects data-rh in dist/index.html and warns that results are untrustworthy. CI is unaffected (always a fresh dist) which is why it had never surfaced. NEW TOOL: scripts/audit-prerendered-seo.mjs (npm run audit:seo-head) reports canonical/description/h1/title state per prerendered route from the SHIPPED HTML, plus duplicate title, description and canonical groups. Reading dist/ rather than source is the point — source review cannot see last-mount-wins between two head managers, Helmet appending over index.html, or a head that never committed. DEFINITIVE NUMBERS on a clean build, replacing this story's original estimates: 12 routes with no canonical (the 7 /events/<city> pages, /articles, /calendar, /deals, /map, /itineraries); 26 routes shipping >1 meta description because Helmet appends over the static tag in index.html; 3 routes without exactly one h1 (/events has 0, /articles 0, /map 0); 10 titles over 60 chars; 2 duplicate-title groups — all 7 /events/<city> pages share "Events by Location | Des Moines Insider", and /articles + /calendar share the shell title; 1 duplicate own-description group of 9 routes. The homepage is now clean on every measure. REMAINING WORK IS UNCHANGED IN SHAPE: give those 12 routes their own SEOHead with distinct titles and descriptions, add the missing h1s, and dedupe the description tag. | SEVEN SUBURB PAGES WERE SERVING "LOCATION NOT FOUND" — FIXED 2026-07-30. Much worse than this story's 'no canonical' framing. src/pages/EventsByLocation.tsx read useParams().location, but App.tsx:366-378 mounts it on SEVEN LITERAL paths (/events/ankeny, /events/urbandale, ...) rather than /events/:location — a param route there would collide with the /events/:slug detail handler on the next line. With no matching param the value was always undefined, suburbInfo was always null, and every one of the seven rendered the not-found branch. All seven are in sitemap-static.xml and all were prerendered, so crawlers were being served a not-found page under one shared title for the seven '<suburb> events' queries, which the strategy doc rates among the most winnable terms we have. The source reads perfectly well; this was only visible in the shipped HTML. FIX: derive the slug from the pathname, keeping useParams as the preferred source so a future param route still works. Renaming the variable also caught four stale references to bare `location` which, after the rename, would have silently resolved to the DOM global and produced full-URL strings inside the canonical, breadcrumb and ItemList URLs. VERIFIED on a rebuild: all seven now emit distinct titles ('Events in Ankeny | Des Moines Insider'), correct self-canonicals and a real h1. Audit went from 12 routes with no canonical to 5, and from 2 duplicate-title groups to 1. STILL OPEN and genuinely missing SEO metadata: /deals, /itineraries, /map and /calendar have no SEOHead at all (no canonical, and /map has no h1). /articles and /calendar still share the shell title. CAUTION FOR WHOEVER PICKS THIS UP: the audit's findings for /events and /articles in this environment are ARTIFACTS, not defects. Both have SEOHead in source; they failed only because the placeholder Supabase key made them capture a loading skeleton and an offline error respectively. Re-run npm run audit:seo-head against a build with real credentials before acting on those two. The 33-routes-with-two-descriptions count is real and unchanged — Helmet appends over the static tag in index.html. | FOUR PAGES + DESCRIPTION DEDUPE DONE 2026-07-30. /deals, /itineraries and /map gained self-canonicals; /map also gained an sr-only h1 (it had no heading of any level — SEO gap and WCAG 1.3.1 failure, also covers that part of WEB-SEO-004). /calendar (SmartCalendarIntegration, used only on that route) had NO head tags at all and was inheriting the shell title; it now has its own title, description and canonical. Deliberately did not keyword-stretch it toward 'Des Moines events calendar' — it is a scheduling utility, not an events calendar, and that query belongs to /events and /events/today. /stay also had a RELATIVE canonical (href="/stay"), now absolute. DESCRIPTION DEDUPE: the static tag in index.html is now marked data-rh="true", which hands it to react-helmet-async so it is REPLACED instead of appended-to. Helmet does not touch unmanaged meta tags, which is why 33 routes had been shipping two descriptions with the generic site-wide fallback FIRST — the copy a crawler is most likely to take. Verified safe before applying: all successfully prerendered routes emit their own description. Explicitly did NOT mark viewport, theme-color, format-detection or the verification tags — Helmet deletes any data-rh tag it does not re-emit, and losing viewport would break mobile layout. TWO FURTHER BUGS FOUND WHILE DOING IT. (1) og:url was hardcoded to the homepage in index.html, so every prerendered route declared the site root as its share URL — the same bug class as the static canonical removed earlier, and it appeared FIRST so it was the one scrapers read. Removed, with a comment matching the canonical note. (2) The Helmet-supplied og:url was itself MALFORMED: 'https://desmoinesinsider.com/https://desmoinesinsider.com/things-to-do'. getCanonicalUrl unconditionally prepended BRAND.baseUrl, and at least five call sites pass an already-absolute URL into SEOHead's url prop (ThingsToDoHub, Index, EventsPage, ArticleDetails, RestaurantDetails). It survived because the canonical link uses the canonicalUrl prop directly, so only og:url was mangled and nothing renders og:url visibly. getCanonicalUrl is now idempotent, fixing every caller at once. Also added og:/twitter: title and description to the five raw-Helmet pages (Hotels, Deals, Itineraries, DiscoverMap, SmartCalendar) so the static copies could be safely marked data-rh. FINAL AUDIT, 32/35 prerendered routes: 0 missing canonicals, 0 wrong canonicals, 0 duplicate descriptions, 0 routes without exactly one h1, 0 duplicate title groups, 0 duplicate description groups, 0 duplicate canonical groups. Every headline metric in this story is now zero. REMAINING, ALL MINOR: 10 titles exceed 60 characters and will truncate in SERPs (a copy decision, not a defect); og:type, og:locale, geo.*, viewport and similar constants still ship twice, which is cosmetic bloat because both copies carry identical values — they were left alone on purpose since Helmet would delete the functional ones. THE 3 UNVERIFIED ROUTES: /events, /articles and /stay are not in the audit because the placeholder Supabase key made them capture a loading skeleton, an offline error and an error state respectively, and the new transient-failure guard correctly refused to publish them. All three have head components in source. Re-run npm run audit:seo-head against a credentialled build to confirm them.

userStories.title: sitemap-guides.xml is a stale committed artifact; its generator queries a table that does not exist
userStories.description: As the platform owner, I need the guides sitemap to reflect reality, because the generator fails on every run and the committed file has not been regenerated since it was first added.
acceptanceCriteria: generateGuidesSitemap queries public.guides, which does not exist (42P01). Decide whether guides live in seasonal_guides (which DOES exist) or are static routes, and point the generator at the real source

On failure the function returns null WITHOUT writing the file, so the stale public/sitemap-guides.xml silently survives. Make a generator failure either fail the build or write an empty-but-valid sitemap — silently shipping stale data is the worst of the three options
Verify the 11 URLs currently in the file still resolve. /guides and /guides/:slug are real routes (App.tsx:431, 471), so they are probably valid, but nothing has checked since the file was committed
Extend scripts/check-schema-usage.mjs to cover scripts/ as well as src/ — this exact bug class is what that guard exists to catch, and it is currently blind to build scripts
userStories.notes:
CLOSED 2026-08-11 (claude/prd-p1-loop). Three ACs were already done; verifying the fourth found a regression the earlier fix had introduced.

AC1 DONE (verified, not assumed): the generator reads seasonal_guides, and running it produces real rows.
AC2 DONE: the error path no longer returns before writing — it writes a valid hub-only sitemap and says so, which is the "never ship stale silently" behaviour this AC asked for.
AC4 DONE: SCAN_ROOTS in scripts/check-schema-usage.mjs already covers scripts/ and supabase/functions/, with a comment naming this story as the bug that motivated it.

THE COMMITTED FILE IS INDEED STALE, AND THE BUILD DOES OVERWRITE IT. Confirmed directly: public/sitemap-guides.xml is clean in git until a build runs, after which it shows as modified. Committed copy has 11 URLs; regenerated has 4, with ZERO overlap.

AC3 — AND THIS IS WHERE IT GOT INTERESTING. The AC says "verify the 11 URLs still resolve". They do, but not usefully. Probed production with a GPTBot UA:
  /guides                       200   106,083 B  title "Des Moines Local Guides - Best Activities, Dining..."
  /guides/visitors-guide        200   173,953 B  title "Things to Do in Des Moines This Weekend"
  /guides/dining-guide          200   173,953 B  same
  /guides/neighborhoods-guide   200   173,953 B  same
  /guides/fall-festivals        200   173,953 B  same
  /guides/summer-2026           200   173,953 B  same
Identical byte counts. Every /guides/:slug serves the prerendered HOMEPAGE to a JS-less crawler, because the route is dynamic and not in PRERENDER_ROUTES. Only the /guides hub has its own document. So "the URLs resolve" is true and misleading — they resolve to the wrong page. This is the WEB-SEO-006 class (sitemapped URLs that are client-render only); these join that count rather than being a separate defect.

REGRESSION FOUND AND FIXED. The repointing commit put the /guides hub in the empty-result and error paths but not the success path, so the moment one published guide existed the hub dropped out of the sitemap entirely. That meant the generator submitted only the URLs that serve homepage content and omitted the single URL that serves its own. The hub is now unconditional and first, at priority 0.8. Regenerated: 5 URLs. scripts/check-seo-route-parity.mjs still reports "35 prerendered, 4 sitemap-only, 39 sitemapped — consistent".

WORTH KNOWING FOR NEXT TIME: none of this was visible from the story or the source. The committed sitemap looked plausible, the generator code read correctly, and the URLs all returned 200. Only diffing committed-vs-regenerated and then fetching the URLs with a crawler UA showed that the two sets do not overlap at all and that ten of them serve the homepage.

[prior] RE-VERIFIED (CODE REVIEW 2026-08-06): PARTIALLY FIXED. scripts/generate-dynamic-sitemaps.ts:2 now lists guides among the sitemaps it generates and the generator was repointed at seasonal_guides in 1927ede ("fix(seo): point the guides sitemap at seasonal_guides and stop shipping stale"). public/sitemap-guides.xml is still a committed artifact in the repo, so the "stale committed artifact" half wants a final confirmation that the build regenerates it rather than shipping the checked-in copy.

[prior] FOUND 2026-07-18 (claude/prd-loop-schema-gaps) while auditing sitemap contents. Every `npm run generate-sitemaps` run prints "Error fetching guides: relation public.guides does not exist" (42P01) and continues. Because the generator returns null before writing, public/sitemap-guides.xml is whatever was committed in 851158c4 and has never been regenerated. It is referenced from sitemap-index.xml, so Google is being handed a hand-frozen file. SEVERITY 3: the 11 URLs are plausibly still valid (both /guides and /guides/:slug are live routes), so this is probably stale-but-harmless today rather than broken. The real risk is the silent-failure pattern — a generator that errors, keeps going, and ships last-known-good data looks identical to one that works. RELATED: this is the same missing-table class as WEB-QA-018, and it is invisible to scripts/check-schema-usage.mjs because that guard only scans src/. The sitemap generator is exactly the kind of build-time code where a silent schema mismatch does damage without anyone seeing a stack trace. Note there IS a seasonal_guides table in the schema, and the route component is SeasonalGuide, so the intended source may simply be a rename that the script never followed. | IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-30 (claude/des-moines-seo-strategy-n54bjj). Pointed generateGuidesSitemap at seasonal_guides (filtered to is_published = true), which is the table /guides/:slug actually reads via useSeasonalGuide (App.tsx:471 -> SeasonalGuide.tsx:13). Fixed the silent-stale behaviour too: the error path no longer returns before writing. Returning early was the worst of the three options this story listed, because a stale file that nobody rewrote looks exactly like success — on failure it now writes a valid sitemap containing only the /guides hub and warns, so the output always reflects the run that produced it. VERIFIED BOTH DIRECTIONS with check-schema: removed the grandfathered 'table|scripts/generate-dynamic-sitemaps.ts|guides' entry from schema-baseline.json (180 -> 179 findings) and the checker still passes, which proves seasonal_guides resolves against the generated types; reverting the table name back to guides makes it fail with '42P01 / PGRST205 (relation does not exist)'. The AC about extending check-schema-usage.mjs to scripts/ was ALREADY DONE by earlier work — SCAN_ROOTS covers src/, scripts/ and supabase/functions/, and its docstring cites this exact bug. The reason it was not failing the build is that the finding was suppressed in the baseline, which is now cleared. NOT DONE, DELIBERATELY: public/sitemap-guides.xml still holds its 10 frozen slugs. Whether they resolve cannot be checked without database credentials, and hand-editing a generated artifact is what produced this situation — the next build with credentials regenerates it correctly. NEW INTERACTION WITH WEB-SEO-006: the entity prerender pass reads sitemap-guides.xml, so any dead slug in that file now costs render budget. It cannot ship a bad page — the strict gate rejects anything that does not resolve — but it will show up as rejections in the build log until the sitemap is regenerated.

userStories.title: Both billing webhooks have non-functional idempotency and no audit trail (log tables do not exist)
userStories.description: As the platform owner, I need the Apple and Google subscription webhooks to deduplicate retries and record what they processed, because both log tables are missing so the duplicate check always passes and nothing is recorded.
acceptanceCriteria: Create apple_notification_log (notification_uuid, notification_type, subtype, processed_at, status) and play_rtdn_log (message_id, notification_type, processed_at, status), or repoint both functions at whatever table was intended

play-rtdn-webhook/index.ts:539 destructures only { data } from the idempotency lookup, so a missing-table error is invisible. Capture and check error there — appstore-server-notifications-v2 already does this at :405 and is the better pattern

Decide the failure policy explicitly: if the log table is unreachable, should the webhook still process the event (current behaviour, favours availability) or refuse and let the provider retry (favours correctness)? Right now it proceeds by accident, not by decision
Add a test asserting a repeated notification_uuid / message_id is skipped the second time — the guard is currently untested as well as non-functional
No change to the HTTP status codes either provider branches on (CLAUDE.md backward-compat)
userStories.notes:
CLOSED 2026-08-22. 20260822000005 APPLIED to production with the owner's approval and recorded in schema_migrations. Verified live: both tables exist, each carries exactly one UNIQUE constraint, and RLS is enabled on both. The idempotency guard is functional for the first time since either webhook shipped.

The two dead files, 20260506000004_apple_notification_log.sql and 20260506000005_play_rtdn_log.sql, now carry a SUPERSEDED AND UNRUNNABLE header explaining that their version numbers are already in the ledger under other names, that a version-only drift check therefore reports them applied while the table does not exist, and the two ways their SQL differs from the live definition (NOT NULL notification_type, no UNIQUE on the idempotency key). Kept rather than deleted so the history stays legible.

AC1 AND AC4 DONE 2026-08-22 (claude/prd-p1-loop), migration 20260822000005 plus supabase/functions/_tests/billing-webhook-idempotency.test.ts. AC2, AC3 and AC5 were already done in code. What this story did NOT know is WHY the tables were missing.

THE TABLES WERE NEVER GOING TO APPEAR, and no drift check would have said so. 20260506000004_apple_notification_log.sql and 20260506000005_play_rtdn_log.sql exist on disk and both version numbers are RECORDED AS APPLIED in supabase_migrations.schema_migrations - but under different names: 'media_assets_dedup' and 'seed_blog_queue_competitor_research'. Different SQL ran under those version numbers. The two log migrations are DEAD FILES: `supabase db push` skips a version already in the ledger, so their SQL will never execute, and a version-only drift comparison (which is what I ran when closing WEB-QA-020) reports everything in sync. to_regclass confirms both tables absent.

AC1: 20260822000005 takes a fresh version, so it actually applies. Column sets are taken from what the functions insert rather than invented - play-rtdn-webhook writes message_id, notification_type, purchase_token, subscription_id, user_subscription_id, processed_at, status, error_message; appstore-server-notifications-v2 writes notification_uuid, notification_type, subtype, original_transaction_id, user_subscription_id, processed_at, status, error_message; both also .select('id, processed_at'). notification_type is NULLABLE because the Play webhook inserts null on its skipped_no_payload path - the original dead file had it NOT NULL, which would have failed that insert.

THE UNIQUE CONSTRAINT IS THE ACTUAL FIX. A SELECT-then-INSERT guard cannot stop two concurrent deliveries; UNIQUE on notification_uuid / message_id can. RLS follows the automation_job_runs convention: admin read only, no client write path, service-role bypasses. Deliberately not world-readable - these rows carry purchase tokens and original transaction ids (WEB-SEC-021).

VERIFIED in a rolled-back transaction against production: duplicate message_id rejected by play_rtdn_log_message_id_unique, duplicate notification_uuid rejected by apple_notification_log_uuid_unique, the null-notification_type path accepted, the lookup both webhooks run returns id and processed_at, and anon sees 0 rows.

AC4: 5 offline assertions, all passing, wired into subscription-sync-tests.yml - tables created, UNIQUE on each idempotency key, RLS + admin-only read, both webhooks capture AND read the lookup error, and every column the webhooks write exists. The test uses lastIndexOf so it asserts against the EFFECTIVE definition rather than the dead 20260506 files. A behavioural test of the skip path needs a live DB and a signed provider payload, so the round trip was verified by hand instead.

NOT APPLIED TO PRODUCTION YET.

RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-11 (claude/prd-p1-loop). AC2 and AC3 are DONE in code; AC1 and AC4 are blocked on the tables existing. Story stays open, and the guard is still non-functional in production — the code is now correct and the storage it needs is still absent.

BOTH TABLES CONFIRMED STILL MISSING, probed against production today:
  play_rtdn_log          HTTP 404
  apple_notification_log HTTP 404

AC2 DONE, both webhooks. play-rtdn-webhook/index.ts:544 and
appstore-server-notifications-v2/index.ts:399 now destructure
{ data, error: logLookupError } and check it. That matters more than it sounds:
destructuring only { data } made a failing lookup indistinguishable from "no
prior row", so a missing relation read as "never seen this notification" and
every retry was reprocessed. Play uses at-least-once delivery, so that path runs
in normal operation, not only during incidents.

AC3 DONE — the failure policy is now explicit and written down at the call site
rather than left implicit: a lookup failure is deliberately NOT fatal, because
the subscription state update is the part that matters and refusing the
notification would make Play retry it forever. It logs loudly instead. The
comment states the reasoning, which is the point of AC3: "decide the failure
policy explicitly". Note that console.error in a Deno edge function reaches the
Supabase function logs — unlike the browser, where esbuild.drop strips it — so
this signal actually exists somewhere.

AC1 BLOCKED: creating the two tables is an additive migration, which is always
safe per CLAUDE.md, but it joins the unapplied queue in WEB-QA-020. I have not
written it. Authoring a migration I cannot apply or test, for a story whose
whole failure mode is a guard that looks correct and cannot fire, would be
adding one more unverified thing to a pile that is already the deploy blocker —
the same reasoning as WEB-BE-033 and WEB-SEO-011 AC7.

AC4 BLOCKED BY AC1: a test asserting a repeated notification_uuid / message_id
is skipped the second time cannot pass until the table exists. Worth writing at
the same time as the migration, not before.

NET: the webhooks now FAIL LOUDLY instead of silently, which is the difference
between a bug someone can find and one nobody can. They still reprocess every
duplicate, because there is nowhere to record that a notification was seen.

[prior] FOUND 2026-07-18 (claude/prd-loop-schema-gaps) after extending the schema guard to supabase/functions/. Both tables confirmed absent from LIVE production (42P01 / 404), not merely from the generated types. MECHANISM: both webhooks look up a prior log row to short-circuit duplicates. The lookup errors because the relation does not exist, the code treats the empty result as "not seen before", and processing continues. So the idempotency guard is not merely untested — it can never fire. Both providers use AT-LEAST-ONCE delivery (App Store Server Notifications V2 and Play RTDN both retry), so duplicate notifications are being fully reprocessed. Both functions then return 200, so neither provider ever signals a problem. SEVERITY 2, NOT 1, and I want to be precise about why: the main subscription state update still runs, and writing the same entitlement state twice is largely idempotent in effect, so this is probably not corrupting subscriptions today. The concrete losses are (a) no audit trail of any subscription lifecycle event, which matters for billing disputes and for debugging XPLAT-002, and (b) any non-idempotent side effect in the handler runs more than once. Rate as HIGH if a handler ever gains an email, a credit, or a counter. DIFFERENCE WORTH KEEPING: Apple captures logLookupError and console.errors it, so the failure is at least visible in function logs. Play discards it entirely by destructuring only { data }. Same outcome, but Play is silent about it.

userStories.title: An entire seo_* monitoring subsystem is written against 10 tables that do not exist
userStories.description: As the platform owner, I need to know whether the SEO monitoring feature is real, because its edge functions reference ten tables that are absent from production.
acceptanceCriteria: Decide per the WEB-QA-018 pattern: build the tables, or delete the dead functions

Tables referenced but missing: seo_settings, seo_alerts, seo_alert_rules, seo_monitoring_log, seo_monitoring_schedules, seo_notification_preferences, seo_audit_history, seo_crawl_results, seo_core_web_vitals, seo_image_analysis
If deleting, check for scheduled invocations (cron/pg_cron/GitHub Actions) that call these functions, so nothing is left calling a removed endpoint
If building, note that CLAUDE.md forbids removing an endpoint older binaries call — these appear to be admin/ops only, so confirm no mobile caller before either path
userStories.notes:
AC3 AND AC4 ANSWERED 2026-08-22 (claude/prd-p1-loop). Both technical constraints on the decision are clear, so this is now purely a product call rather than a blocked one.

TABLE INVENTORY re-confirmed against production - 10 missing, 1 present:
    MISSING: seo_alert_rules, seo_alerts, seo_audit_history, seo_core_web_vitals, seo_crawl_results, seo_image_analysis, seo_monitoring_log, seo_monitoring_schedules, seo_notification_preferences, seo_settings
    EXISTS:  seo_content_optimization  <- the one survivor, worth knowing before anyone deletes wholesale

AC3 ANSWERED - NOTHING SCHEDULES THEM. Six edge functions depend on the missing tables (analyze-images, check-core-web-vitals, crawl-site, run-scheduled-audit, send-seo-notification, seo-audit). Checked cron.job for any command matching seo: none. Checked .github/workflows/: none. So deleting leaves nothing dangling, and equally: NOTHING IS RUNNING TODAY, which is why this has been failing silently with no operational signal.
  Note run-scheduled-audit is named for a schedule that does not exist.

AC4 ANSWERED - NO MOBILE CALLER. Zero references across ios/ and android/app/src/main/ for all six. CLAUDE.md's rule about never removing an endpoint an older binary calls therefore does not bind here, which is the constraint that usually makes this kind of deletion expensive.

CALLER MAP, which splits the six into two groups:
    1 web caller each: analyze-images, check-core-web-vitals, crawl-site, seo-audit (admin surfaces)
    ZERO callers anywhere: run-scheduled-audit, send-seo-notification
None of the six is registered in supabase/config.toml.
  The two with no caller and no schedule are unambiguous dead code - they can go regardless of which way the wider decision falls.

WORTH WEIGHING AGAINST WEB-SEO-014: that story found Google Search Console synced ONCE in March and never again, with the OAuth grant lapsing around 2026-09-30. So the site has two separate SEO monitoring systems, neither of which is producing data - one built against tables that were never deployed, one connected and never scheduled. If the answer here is 'build the tables', it is worth asking first whether GSC already provides what this subsystem was meant to.

RE-VERIFIED (CODE REVIEW 2026-08-06): still true. schema-baseline.json holds 11 findings against seo_* identifiers, so the monitoring subsystem is still written against tables that are not in the generated schema.

[prior] FOUND 2026-07-18 alongside WEB-BE-030. Confirmed absent from live production (seo_settings, seo_alerts probed directly, both 404). Same shape as WEB-QA-018 on the front end: a complete feature written against a schema that was never deployed, failing silently because it is server-side and nobody reads the function logs. SEVERITY 3 because this is an internal ops surface with no user-facing path, unlike the billing webhooks. But it is worth resolving one way or the other — every one of these functions burns invocations and logs errors on whatever schedule triggers it, and a monitoring subsystem that cannot record anything is worse than none, because its silence reads as "no problems found".

userStories.title: 438 Supabase call sites discard the error, which is why schema breakage is invisible
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I need failing queries to be distinguishable from empty results, because 438 call sites destructure only { data } and drop the error, so a missing table reads as "no rows" everywhere.
acceptanceCriteria: Triage the 335 edge-function sites first — server-side has no UI and no browser console, so a swallowed error there produces no signal at all

Anywhere the result drives a CONTROL DECISION (idempotency guards, entitlement checks, authorization, dedupe) must capture and act on the error. play-rtdn-webhook was one of these and is fixed in 6d83937d
Anywhere genuinely best-effort (analytics, optional enrichment) may keep ignoring it, but should say so in a comment so the next reader can tell the two apart
Consider an ESLint rule for src/ that flags `const { data } = await supabase` without `error`, so new instances cannot be added silently
This story is a CLEANUP PATTERN, not a bug list — do not treat all 438 as defects
userStories.notes:
THE MFA FAIL-OPEN IS FIXED 2026-08-22, with a regression suite. This is AC2's case worked end to end - a discarded error that drove a control decision the wrong way.

src/contexts/AuthContext.tsx now captures the error from both MFA reads. The gate enters the MFA path when the level says aal1/aal2 OR when the level could NOT BE READ, so unknown is treated as 'might need MFA' rather than 'does not'. If listFactors then also fails, the sign-in is refused and the session signed out rather than handing out a session that skipped a gate which may exist.

THE OTHER DIRECTION WAS GUARDED DELIBERATELY, because a security fix that locks everyone out is not a fix: an account with NO second factor still signs in normally when the assurance check fails, because listFactors succeeds and simply returns none. That is 100% of accounts today.

REGRESSION SUITE: src/contexts/__tests__/AuthContextMfa.test.tsx, 3 cases - both reads fail (refuse), level unreadable but a verified factor exists (require MFA), level unreadable and no factor (still sign in). VERIFIED BY MUTATION rather than by watching them pass: restoring the fail-open condition gives 2 failed / 1 passed and exit 1; with the fix, exit 0. The one that passes either way is the no-factor case, which is the over-fix guard.
  Written as a separate spec with its own hoisted mocks rather than extending AuthContext.test.tsx, so the five existing render-count tests there stay untouched.

Quality: 25 files / 226 unit tests pass, npm run validate exit 0, and the discarded-error ratchet is still green - capturing an error REMOVES a site, so the count can only improve.

STILL OPEN: the other 95 control-decision-shaped sites in the 40-file candidate set, and the durable server-side fix - no RLS policy references aal2, so even with this branch corrected the server does not independently require a second factor.

TRIAGE STARTED WITH A METHOD 2026-08-22 (claude/prd-p1-loop). AC5 says this is a cleanup PATTERN and not a bug list, so the useful move is not to fix 520 sites but to separate the ones that fail OPEN from the ones that fail CLOSED. Only the first kind is a defect.

TRIAGE RULE: a discarded error matters when the result gates a control decision AND the undefined result makes the guard PASS. If undefined makes the guard DENY, the site is safe (though usually undiagnosable). Filtering the 225 baselined files by control-decision-shaped names gives 40 files / 96 sites as the candidate set - a tractable subset of the 520.

TWO WORKED EXAMPLES, one of each kind:

FAILS CLOSED, SAFE: supabase/functions/assign-role/index.ts. resolveRole() discards the error on both its user_roles and profiles.user_role lookups, and that function gates the caller-is-admin check at :56. But it `return 'user'` on every failure path, so a swallowed error DENIES. Both objects exist in production, so the normal path works. Not a security defect - but a legitimate admin hitting a transient error gets a silent 403 with no diagnostic anywhere, which is the operational half of AC2 and worth a comment per AC3.

FAILS OPEN, AND IT IS THE MFA GATE: src/contexts/AuthContext.tsx:441 and :450.
    const { data: mfaData } = await supabase.auth.mfa.getAuthenticatorAssuranceLevel();
    const currentLevel = mfaData?.currentLevel;  const nextLevel = mfaData?.nextLevel;
    if (currentLevel === 'aal1' && nextLevel === 'aal2' && data.session) { ...require MFA... }
If that call ERRORS, mfaData is undefined, both levels are undefined, the condition is false, the MFA block is skipped and execution falls straight through to 'Login successful'. listFactors() at :450 has the identical shape. So a transient error in either call bypasses the MFA prompt.

MEASURED IMPACT, so this is not overstated: 0 users currently have a verified MFA factor (auth.mfa_factors), so nobody is affected today. AND 0 RLS policies reference aal2, which is the part to act on - there is NO server-side backstop. The client-side branch is the only thing enforcing MFA, so the day someone enrols, a discarded error is the whole gate. Fixing the discard is cheap; adding an aal2 requirement to the policies that matter is the durable fix.

Counts unchanged at 520 sites / 225 files, baseline holding, ratchet green.

RATCHET NOW COVERS THE EDGE FUNCTIONS TOO, 2026-08-11 (claude/prd-p1-loop). AC4 done; AC1's precondition done; AC1 itself, AC2 and AC3 still open.

scripts/check-error-handling.mjs now scans supabase/functions/ alongside src/. AC1 says to triage the server side FIRST, and the reason is right: in src/ a discarded error at least leaves a broken screen somebody can see, while in a Deno function it leaves nothing anywhere — no UI, no browser console, and console.* output nobody reads.

COUNTS, from the AST selector rather than grep:
  src/                181 sites across  95 files
  supabase/functions/ 339 sites across 130 files
  total               520 sites across 225 files
The story's figures were 103 and 335 from a regex; 181 and 339 from the parser, which also catches multi-line destructures and renamed bindings (`data: rows`).

THE SHRINK-ONLY GUARD FIRED, CORRECTLY, AND I DID NOT BYPASS IT. Widening the scan takes the total 181 -> 520, and --update refuses to re-baseline upward. That invariant is right for a fixed scope and wrong for a scope change, and the two are indistinguishable from the total alone — which is exactly how a guard gets disabled "just this once". The baseline now records its own scope, and a higher total is permitted ONLY when the scope string changes, with a loud SCOPE CHANGED warning naming both. Any other increase still fails.

PROVED IT FIRES ON THE SERVER SIDE specifically, rather than assuming it carried over from src/: appending one `const { data } = await supabase...` to supabase/functions/version-check/index.ts gives exit 1 naming that file; reverting gives exit 0. npm run validate passes at 520/520.

WHAT REMAINS, and it is the bulk of the story. AC1's actual triage of 339 server sites is untouched. AC2 (anywhere the result drives a control decision — idempotency, entitlement, authorization, dedupe — must capture and act on the error) and AC3 (mark the genuinely best-effort ones in a comment so the two are distinguishable) are per-site judgement across 520 sites and cannot be done mechanically. The ratchet stops the pile growing in either tree; it does not shrink it, and nothing here should be read as having reduced the existing 520.

[prior] FOUND 2026-07-18 (claude/prd-loop-schema-gaps) by scanning for the mechanism common to most of this session findings. Counts: 438 call sites across 182 files matching `const { data } = await supabase|client|db()` with no error in the destructure — 335 in supabase/functions/, 103 in src/. Top offenders: agent-ops-digest (9), agent-subscription-nurture (9), _shared/agents/subscription-nurture (9), useAdminCampaigns (8), moderate-content (7), social-media-manager (7). WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN THE RAW COUNT: this is the enabling mechanism behind WEB-QA-018, WEB-BE-030, WEB-BE-031 and WEB-SEO-003. A query against a table that does not exist returns an error and no data. If the error is dropped, the caller sees an empty result and takes the empty branch — so an entire missing subsystem presents as "nothing to show" rather than as a failure. Every silent feature found in this audit went undetected through exactly this path. DELIBERATELY SEVERITY 3 AND NOT A BUG COUNT: many of these are legitimately best-effort and ignoring the error is the right call. Filing all 438 as defects would be noise and would bury the ones that matter. The valuable subset is the control-decision sites, and the concrete example is the one already fixed: play-rtdn-webhook used a swallowed error as an idempotency guard, so the guard could never fire. SUGGESTED ORDER: (1) grep the edge functions for swallowed errors whose result feeds an if/guard, (2) fix those, (3) add the lint rule to stop the bleeding, (4) leave the best-effort ones alone with a comment. | TRIAGED 2026-07-18. Narrowed the 438 raw sites to the 323 where the result drives a control decision (262 edge functions, 61 src). Most of those are optional-chaining on best-effort enrichment, where ignoring the error is the right call — so the raw count still overstates the problem. THE CLASS THAT MATTERS is idempotency guards on at-least-once webhooks, and all three are now accounted for: appstore-server-notifications-v2 already captured its error (correct); play-rtdn-webhook swallowed it AND its log table does not exist, so the guard was permanently dead (fixed 6d83937d); stripe-webhook swallowed it but stripe_webhook_events DOES exist — verified against live production — so that guard works today and was hardened defensively rather than as a live bug fix (c329d56f). REMAINING WORK on this story is the long tail plus the lint rule; the high-severity subset is done. NOTE FOR WHOEVER PICKS THIS UP: do not mass-apply error capture. The value is entirely in sites where the swallowed error changes a branch, and a blanket refactor would add noise to hundreds of best-effort calls while making the real ones harder to spot.

userStories.title: Three prerendered routes ship 5,000-6,600 DOM elements, far past the Lighthouse threshold
userStories.description: As a mobile visitor, I need list pages to render a bounded amount of DOM, because the prerenderer serializes every loaded item and three routes ship several thousand elements before any interaction.
acceptanceCriteria: Bound what the prerenderer captures on list-heavy routes, or paginate/virtualize those lists so the initial DOM is capped
Element counts in #root: /map 6,564, /events/date-night 6,052, /restaurants/dietary 4,981, against a median route of 481. Lighthouse warns above ~800 and flags above 1,500
Re-measure hydration cost on /map specifically — 6,564 elements is the DOM React must reconcile on boot
Verify against a mid-tier mobile CPU, not a desktop; this is a main-thread cost, not a transfer cost
userStories.notes:
RE-MEASURED ACROSS ALL 35 PRERENDERED ROUTES 2026-08-22 (claude/prd-p1-loop). AC1's work HELD - the three named routes are all still far below their pre-fix numbers - but the story's three-route framing understates the problem by six routes, including the two worst and the homepage.

Counting opening tags inside #root in dist/, the same basis the earlier measurement used:
    4137  /events/west-des-moines     <- worst, NOT named in this story
    3773  /stay                       <- second worst, NOT named
    2870  /events/date-night          (named; was 6,052)
    2654  /events                     NOT named
    2349  /playgrounds                NOT named
    2124  /restaurants/dietary        (named; was 4,985)
    2082  /events/this-weekend        NOT named
    1917  /map                        (named; was 6,568)
    1696  /                           NOT named - and it is the highest-traffic page on the site
  9 of 35 routes are over the ~1,500 Lighthouse flag. Median across all 35 is 570, so the distribution is healthy and the tail is the whole problem.

TWO THINGS THIS CHANGES:
  1. /events/west-des-moines at 4,137 is 44% worse than the worst route this story tracks. Fixing only the three named routes would leave a worse one untouched. It is a location-shaped events route, which is the same family as /events/this-weekend at 2,082 - so the pattern is 'events list filtered by a dimension', not three unrelated pages.
  2. The HOMEPAGE is over the threshold. AC3 asks to re-measure hydration cost on /map specifically because 'that is the DOM React must reconcile on boot' - the same argument applies to / with far more traffic, and it compounds the 22.4s DOMContentLoaded measured on / in dev under WEB-CI-021.

AC4 STILL UNADDRESSED and still correct: all of these are desktop-side measurements of element COUNT. The claim that matters is main-thread reconciliation cost on a mid-tier mobile CPU, which none of these numbers establish.

AC1 DONE 2026-08-11 (claude/prd-p1-loop). STORY STAYS OPEN — none of the three routes is under the ~1,500 Lighthouse flag yet, and the re-measurement changed what this story is about.

MEASURED, elements inside #root in the prerendered HTML:
                        before   after
  /map                   6,568   1,918   -71%
  /restaurants/dietary   4,985   2,124   -57%
  /events/date-night     6,052   2,871   -53%   (via WEB-PERF-027)
  /events                    —   2,642
  /restaurants               —   2,782
Median route is 481.

WHAT CHANGED. /map rendered every fetched entry in its results list — 200 events + 300 restaurants + 200 attractions — whenever no viewport bounds were applied. Capped at 60. /restaurants/dietary rendered all 100 fetched restaurants; capped at 36, three full rows of its lg:grid-cols-3 grid.
