ONLY THE RENDERED LIST IS CAPPED, NEVER A COUNT. /map's markers still plot everything and its two "N in view" counters still report the true total; /restaurants/dietary's heading and body copy still read restaurants.length. Both pages state what is not shown — "Showing the first 60 of N results", "Showing 36 of N". A list that stops without saying so is how a truncation becomes a fact, which is the same failure this codebase already had in the prerenderer's route counts and in the guides sitemap.

THE STORY'S PREMISE IS NOW OUT OF DATE, and that is worth more than the numbers. "Three prerendered routes" no longer describes it: /restaurants (2,782) and /events (2,642) were never named here and are now among the heaviest, above the two routes this story is about. The three originally listed were the extreme tail; capping them exposed that the whole list-page family sits at 2,000-2,900 against a 481 median. Whoever picks this up should treat it as a shared list-rendering problem — every one of these is a card grid with no virtualization — rather than continuing to fix named routes one at a time.

AC2 NOT MET: nothing is under 1,500 yet. AC3 (re-measure hydration cost on /map) and AC4 (verify on a mid-tier mobile CPU) NOT DONE — both need CPU profiling against a throttled device, which this environment cannot do. Element counts are not hydration timings and I am not treating them as a proxy.

VERIFIED: npm run lint 0 errors, npx vitest run 193/193, build green at 35/35.

[prior] RE-MEASURED 2026-08-11 (claude/prd-p1-loop). One of the three routes is fixed; two are unchanged.

Elements inside #root, live in a browser / in the prerendered HTML:
  /map                  7,166 / 6,568   (story recorded 6,564 — unchanged)
  /restaurants/dietary  4,983 / 4,985   (story recorded 4,981 — unchanged)
  /events/date-night    2,870 / 2,872   (story recorded 6,052 — HALVED)

date-night improved as a side effect of WEB-PERF-027, which capped its rendered list at 40 because the page was shipping 756 KB of HTML. Same root cause the AC1 here names — an uncapped list — so the remedy transfers directly: /map and /restaurants/dietary need the same treatment.

Still above the ~1,500 Lighthouse flag on all three, so this stays open. Median route for comparison is 481.

AC4 (verify against a mid-tier mobile CPU) NOT DONE and not doable here — that needs a throttled device profile, and the numbers above are element counts, not hydration timings.

[prior] MEASURED 2026-07-18 (claude/prd-loop-schema-gaps) from the production build. Raw HTML: /map 984KB, /restaurants/dietary 842KB, /events/date-night 772KB, against a 94KB median. DELIBERATELY NOT FRAMED AS A BANDWIDTH PROBLEM. Gzipped those same documents are 56KB, 39KB and 37KB — repetitive DOM compresses extremely well, so transfer is fine and reporting "984KB page" would be misleading. The real costs are HTML parse time, DOM memory, and React hydration over several thousand nodes, all of which land on the main thread of whatever device the user has. ROOT CAUSE is the same prerender behaviour behind three earlier fixes: the prerenderer captures the DOM after the app has fetched and rendered its data, so every loaded list item is baked into the shipped HTML. On /map that is 517 map entities with their popups (300+ h3 elements). This is arguably WORKING AS INTENDED for SEO — the content is crawlable — so the fix is a bound, not a removal. SEVERITY 3: no measurement here shows a user-visible regression, and prerendered content is genuinely good for indexing. Raising this above 3 requires an actual hydration measurement on a real device, which I could not do from this machine.

userStories.title: /business is prerendered as a sign-in wall, so that is what crawlers index
userStories.description: As the platform owner, I need /business to present indexable content, because the prerendered page contains only a sign-in prompt rather than the Business Hub marketing copy.
acceptanceCriteria: Decide the intent: if /business is a dashboard, it probably should not be in the prerender route list or the sitemap at all
If it is meant to attract businesses, render the marketing content to signed-out visitors and gate only the dashboard widgets
Either way /business currently has NO h1 in the shipped HTML — the h1 "Business Hub" exists only in the signed-in branch
/map also has no h1; it needs one (an sr-only heading is acceptable for a map-first UI)
Both are WCAG 1.3.1 heading-hierarchy failures as well as SEO gaps
userStories.notes: FOUND 2026-07-18 while auditing heading structure across prerendered routes. 29 of 31 routes have exactly one h1, which is correct; the two exceptions are /business and /map, and they fail for different reasons. /business: the prerendered visible text is "Business Hub — Sign in to access your business dashboard — Join Des Moines Insider to grow your business with powerful tools". The h1 at BusinessHub.tsx:128 sits in the authenticated branch, so an unauthenticated crawler never reaches it. Google is indexing a login wall on a route that is in the sitemap. /map: genuinely has no h1 anywhere — 300+ h3 elements for map markers and no top-level heading. SEVERITY 3 for both: neither is a broken feature, and a gated dashboard being gated is defensible. The decision worth making is whether /business belongs in the prerender/sitemap set at all. | CLOSED 2026-07-30. Resolved across two changes in this branch. THE INTENT DECISION: /business is a dashboard, so it was removed from both scripts/prerender-routes.mjs and public/sitemap-static.xml under WEB-SEO-005 and recorded in DELIBERATELY_EXCLUDED_ROUTES. Google is no longer being handed a login wall. The 'render marketing content to signed-out visitors instead' option was NOT taken, deliberately: /advertise and /business-partnership already exist as the business-facing marketing pages and both remain in the sitemap, so duplicating that pitch onto a dashboard route would create the same competing-page problem WEB-SEO-007 documents. THE ACCESSIBILITY HALF still needed doing, because a missing h1 is a WCAG 1.3.1 failure whether or not the page is indexed: BusinessHub.tsx had its only h1 inside the AUTHENTICATED branch, so signed-out visitors got a page with no h1 at all. Added one to the sign-in card. Used a plain h1 with CardTitle's classes copied across rather than <CardTitle> — that component renders an h3 and has no asChild escape hatch, so it could not have carried the h1 role. /map's missing h1 was fixed under WEB-SEO-002 with an sr-only heading, appropriate for a map-first layout. Both routes now have exactly one h1; the prerendered audit reports 0 routes without exactly one h1.

userStories.title: /attractions scrolls horizontally by 1px at 320px width
userStories.description: As a visitor on a small phone, I should not be able to scroll the attractions page sideways, because a 1px overflow makes the page feel loose and can shift tap targets.
acceptanceCriteria: documentElement.scrollWidth equals clientWidth on /attractions at 320x568
The mobile-responsive suite goes fully green — this is the last remaining failure

Check the view-mode toggle group in the attractions header. The probe surfaced a rounded bg-white/20 flex container holding two 44px buttons, but they sit inside a clipped ancestor, so the true culprit needs devtools rather than a guess
userStories.notes:
FIXED 2026-08-11 (claude/prd-p1-loop).

AC1 VERIFIED at 320x568: /attractions now reports scrollWidth=320 against clientWidth=320. Re-measured /events, /restaurants, /playgrounds and /stay in the same run — all 320/320.

THE 1px WAS ROUNDING. THE REAL OVERFLOW WAS 17px, and that is why this story went unsolved. AC3 recorded elements with right edges of 328-374 sitting inside clipped ancestors, concluded they were not the cause, and said the true culprit needed devtools. Correct on both counts, but searching for a 1px-wide cause was searching for something that never existed.

WHAT IT ACTUALLY IS. The results header at src/pages/Attractions.tsx:559 was a non-wrapping "flex items-center justify-between" row. Measured at 320px:
  row (parent)        x=16   w=288   -> right edge 304
  h2                         w=124.97  (already at its min-content, text wrapped)
  SortDropdown        x=140.97 w=180   -> right edge 320.97
SortDropdown hardcodes w-[180px] (src/components/SortDropdown.tsx:26) and cannot shrink below its own min-content, so 124.97 + 180 = 304.97 against 288 available. The 16.97px escapes the row, reaches the document, and documentElement.scrollWidth ceils 320.97 to 321. Hence "exactly 1px" on every probe.

FIX: flex-wrap + gap-2 on that row. The dropdown drops to its own line at 320px and nothing changes at any wider viewport, because a row that fits never wraps. Chose this over capping SortDropdown's width because the component is shared with EventsPage, which measures clean, and because the row genuinely cannot fit on one line at 320px — wrapping is the honest layout rather than a suppression.

WHAT MADE IT FINDABLE, since the earlier attempt had the same information and could not: (1) skip any element with a clipping ancestor, which removes exactly the 328-374px red herrings the first probe surfaced; (2) print x and width at EVERY ancestor level, so a child ending 16.97px past its own parent is a visible number rather than something inferred from reading JSX.

AC2 (mobile-responsive suite fully green) NOT VERIFIED HERE. The suite needs a dev server and a full Playwright run; I verified the specific assertion this story is about — documentElement.scrollWidth === clientWidth — directly against the production build at 320x568, on five routes. If another failure remains in that suite it is a different defect.

VERIFIED: npm run lint 0 errors, npx vitest run 193/193, build green at 35/35.

[prior] MEASURED 2026-07-18 (claude/prd-loop-schema-gaps) on the production build. /attractions at 320x568 reports scrollWidth=321 against clientWidth=320 — exactly 1px. Every other audited route and viewport is clean. SEVERITY 3 and deliberately NOT fixed: 1px is not user-visible, and the elements the probe surfaced report right edges of 328-374 while the document overflows by only 1px. That means they sit inside a clipped or scrollable ancestor and are not necessarily the cause. Guessing at a 1px fix from that evidence is how a working layout gets broken. Needs a devtools session at a 320px viewport. CONTEXT: this was the ONLY genuine failure among 105 mobile-responsive tests. The other three were false positives in the content-fits-viewport test, which counted horizontal-carousel children as overflow — at 375px it reported 24 overflowing elements on /, 64 on /events and 67 on /restaurants, while documentElement.scrollWidth was exactly 375 on all three. That test was rewritten in ca03f45d and the suite now sits at 104 passed / 1 failed.

userStories.title: Shared Checkbox renders a 20x20px hit area, below every touch-target guideline
userStories.description: As a touch user, I need checkboxes big enough to tap reliably, because the shared component renders a 20x20px target and 46% of buttons on /advertise fall below the 44x44 recommendation as a result.
acceptanceCriteria: Decide the target: WCAG 2.2 AA (2.5.8) requires 24x24 minimum; 44x44 is the Apple/Android and WCAG AAA recommendation this suite checks against
Enlarge the hit area in src/components/ui/checkbox.tsx — padding or a wrapper can expand the target WITHOUT changing the visual box size, which avoids a site-wide visual change
Audit other small controls at the same time (radio, switch, icon-only buttons) rather than fixing checkbox alone
links-and-buttons touch-target test on /advertise goes green — it is the last remaining failure in that suite
userStories.notes:
FIXED 2026-08-11 (claude/prd-p1-loop), measured in a browser rather than read from source.

MEASURED ON /advertise AT 1280px, before and after:
  checkbox hit area   20x20 -> 60x60
  visible box         20x20 -> 20x20   (unchanged)
  sibling content x     167 -> 167     (nothing reflowed)
  buttons under 44x44   6 of 13 (46%) -> 1 of 13 (8%)
The suite fails above 20%, so AC4 is satisfied.

AC1 DECIDED: 44px minimum, the threshold tests/links-and-buttons.spec.ts actually asserts. Implemented as h-12 (3rem), which is 48/54/60px across the breakpoints.

THE REM BASE IS THE BURIED FACT, and it explains why this story carried two contradictory measurements. src/index.css:761-778 sets html { font-size } to 16px mobile / 18px tablet / 20px desktop, so EVERY Tailwind size class is 12.5-25% larger than its name implies above the mobile breakpoint. h-4 is 16px on a phone and 20px on a desktop. The story title said 20x20; the 2026-08-06 re-verification called that "optimistic" and corrected it to 16x16 from reading h-4 w-4 in the source. Both were right, at different viewports, and neither said which. Worth knowing generally: reasoning about px from Tailwind class names is wrong in this codebase.

That also caught a real hazard in my own first attempt. I used h-11 (2.75rem), which is EXACTLY 44px at the mobile base, and the test asserts `width < 44` — passing by zero margin, where sub-pixel rounding fails intermittently and gets written off as flake. h-12 clears it at every breakpoint.

AC2 SATISFIED, THOUGH NOT THE WAY IT SUGGESTED. It proposed padding or a wrapper "WITHOUT changing the visual box size". The visual box is indeed unchanged, but the element's OWN box had to grow: the test reads getBoundingClientRect() on the element (spec:143-152), which a pseudo-element does not affect. So the button is 3rem and -m-4 pulls its layout footprint back to exactly the 1rem the old h-4 occupied — at any rem base, since both scale together. That is why sibling-x did not move, which matters because 28 files render this primitive.

AC3 AUDITED, AND IT FOUND SOMETHING. radio-group had the identical defect and got the identical fix. switch (h-6 w-11) is still under 44 on height — but it, and 5 other sites, already carry a `tap-area-44` utility (src/index.css:257-280). That utility does NOT do what its name promises for this test: it expands an ::after pseudo-element, so getBoundingClientRect is unchanged and the suite can never see it. It is also deliberately disabled under @media (pointer: fine), so on desktop there is no expansion at all. The one remaining sub-44 button on /advertise is exactly such an element, measuring 30x30 with tap-area-44 applied.

A TENSION I AM LEAVING IN PLACE RATHER THAN SILENTLY OVERRIDING: tap-area-44's authors chose not to expand on fine pointers, because the overlay could overlap adjacent controls. My checkbox/radio fix expands at all pointer types. I think that is right — WCAG 2.5.8 is pointer-agnostic, 20x20 is under the 24px AA floor for a mouse too, and -m-4 means nothing moves — but it is a different convention from the one already here, and somebody should decide whether tap-area-44 should follow or whether these two should. Not resolved here.

VERIFIED: npm run lint 0 errors, npx vitest run 193/193, build green at 35/35.

[prior] RE-VERIFIED (CODE REVIEW 2026-08-06): still true, and the number in the title is optimistic. src/components/ui/checkbox.tsx:14 applies "peer h-4 w-4 ..." — Tailwind h-4/w-4 is 1rem = 16x16px, not the 20x20px this story reports, and the inner <Check> at :22 is also h-4 w-4. Against a 44x44 (Apple) / 48x48 (Material) minimum this is worse than recorded. No wrapping label or padding enlarges the hit area at the primitive level.

[prior] MEASURED 2026-07-18 (claude/prd-loop-schema-gaps). The five ad-placement checkboxes on /advertise render at 20x20px (Tailwind h-4 w-4 plus border). The links-and-buttons touch-target test allows 20% of buttons under 44x44 and measured 46%. NOT FIXED HERE, deliberately: these are instances of the shared shadcn ui/checkbox, so resizing changes every checkbox in the product. That is a design-system decision with visual consequences across admin forms, filters and settings — not something to change from a test failure. The low-risk path is expanding the HIT AREA via padding while keeping the drawn box at 16px, which satisfies the guideline without a visual redesign. RELATED AND ALREADY FIXED (e4b65fcc): the same five checkboxes had no accessible name at all — no id, aria-label, aria-labelledby or associated label — so a screen reader announced them as bare "checkbox". They are now associated with their visible h3 via aria-labelledby. Size is the remaining half of the problem. | SCOPE WIDER THAN CHECKBOX (2026-07-18): the forms suite independently measures 76.9% of form controls on /auth below the 44px touch-target height, against a 30% threshold. So this is not one component — inputs, selects and buttons in the shared ui/ set are all built at default shadcn sizing (h-9/h-10 = 36-40px), which is under 44 and, for the 20x20 checkbox, under even the WCAG 2.2 AA minimum of 24x24. Treat this as a single design-system pass over ui/input, ui/select, ui/button, ui/checkbox, ui/radio and ui/switch rather than per-page patches, and re-run both tests/forms.spec.ts and tests/links-and-buttons.spec.ts as the check. It is now the ONLY remaining failure in each of those suites.

userStories.title: A failed prerender exits 0, so a deploy can silently ship zero prerendered routes
userStories.description: As the platform owner, I need a prerender failure to be visible, because the step catches every error and exits 0 — a build that prerenders none of its 31 routes reports success and deploys.
acceptanceCriteria: Decide the failure policy. The current never-fail behaviour is documented and deliberate ("worst case is same as before"), but it means the entire SEO mechanism can vanish without a signal
At minimum: if fewer than N routes are written, exit non-zero or fail the deploy. Shipping 1 of 31 should not look identical to shipping 31 of 31
The internal static server binds a fixed port (4178). Bind port 0 and read back the assigned port, so a leftover process cannot take the build down
Have the build assert the expected route count against the ROUTES list rather than trusting the log line
Consider surfacing the count in CI output so a drop is visible in the deploy log
userStories.notes:
AMENDED 2026-08-11, same session, after the new gate fired on a real build.

THE GATE CAUGHT A GENUINE DEFECT IN THE PRERENDERER, not a flake. /articles failed on 2 of 4 consecutive clean builds with "captured a transient failure/loading state (Loading articles... (only 1300 chars rendered))". I first blamed resource contention from a concurrent vitest run, and I was wrong — it failed again on a completely idle box.

ROOT CAUSE was the capture WAIT, not the gate. renderRoute waited for "#main-content textContent > 40 characters", which "Loading articles..." plus a heading satisfies instantly, so the wait resolved mid-fetch and the publish gate then correctly refused to write a skeleton. The timing was visible in numbers I already had and misread: 11s render passes on the failures against 20s on the successes. The wait now holds until the page stops reporting a loading state, using the SAME predicate as the publish gate (a "Loading <thing>..." marker only counts while #main-content is under 2000 chars, so a below-the-fold spinner on an otherwise complete page does not block the capture). Timeout raised 15s -> 20s.

VERIFIED BY REPETITION, not by one green run — one green run is what let me draw the wrong conclusion the first time. Three consecutive npm run build invocations: 35/35, 35/35, 35/35, 0 of 3 failed, render passes 67s / 73s / 37s. The pass now takes as long as actually waiting for content takes.

CI IMPLICATION, MEASURED. I checked whether the fatal gate would turn pr-checks red, because that job builds with no VITE_SUPABASE_* env. It cannot, for a reason worse than the original worry: PR Checks is disabled_manually on GitHub and has not run since 2026-02-12. Filed as WEB-CI-025. Separately, clearing VITE_SUPABASE_URL locally shows "vite build" dying in 4ms at the assert-html-env-placeholders plugin, long before prerender — so whenever that workflow is re-enabled its Build step fails on the missing env first, and WEB-CI-025 AC2 covers it. This story is NOT verified against a real CI run, because there is no real CI run to verify against.

[prior] FIXED 2026-08-11 (claude/prd-p1-loop). scripts/prerender.mjs no longer exits 0 unconditionally.

AC1 FAILURE POLICY DECIDED, and recorded in the file header: a hub-route shortfall fails the build; the entity pass stays non-fatal because it is opt-in, budgeted and already fail-closed. Fatal now: puppeteer unimportable, Chromium unlaunchable, dist/index.html absent, or fewer hub routes on disk than PRERENDER_ROUTES contains. Each throws a PrerenderFailure carrying the likely cause rather than a bare stack.

EVIDENCE THE POLICY IS SAFE, measured against production 2026-08-11 with a GPTBot UA and no JS: / returns 39 data-rh tags with its own canonical, /restaurants/ 46, /events/today/ 32. So Chromium does launch on the Cloudflare Pages build image and a shortfall there means something actually broke, not that the host is incapable. Without that check I would have been guessing.

AC2+AC4 (one mechanism): after the hub pass, ROUTES is checked against the ARTIFACT — fs.existsSync on dist/<route>/index.html for every route — not against the in-process ok counter, and the missing routes are named in the failure message. 1 of 35 can no longer look like 35 of 35.

AC3: the static server binds port 0 and reads server.address().port back; the fixed 4178 is gone. The listen error is also wired to reject now, so EADDRINUSE (which is how this bug was originally found) propagates instead of surfacing as an unhandled event.

AC5: the counts go to GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY on success, and a failure emits ::error title=Prerender failed:: so the reason lands on the run's front page instead of in build-log scrollback.

ALSO FIXED, same signal-quality problem: the 'dist/index.html is ALREADY PRERENDERED' guard tested for data-rh anywhere in the file, and index.html now authors data-rh onto its own fallback tags on purpose (WEB-SEO-002/012) — so that warning fired on EVERY clean build. It now checks whether the shell noscript block survives inside #root, which React necessarily replaces when it renders. A warning that is always wrong is how the real one gets scrolled past.

VERIFIED: rm -rf dist && npm run build exits 0, prints 'hubs: 35 prerendered, 0 skipped, of 35 routes', 'hub coverage verified on disk: 35/35', and no longer prints the false ALREADY PRERENDERED warning.

NOT DONE: no negative test forces the failure path in CI. The failure modes need a broken Chromium or a deleted dist route to exercise, and faking either in the build job would mean shipping a switch that turns prerendering off — the thing this story exists to prevent.

[prior] RE-VERIFIED (CODE REVIEW 2026-08-06): still true, verbatim. scripts/prerender.mjs:501-502 is main().catch((e) => warn(...)).finally(() => process.exit(0)) — the exit code is 0 unconditionally, so a browser-launch or server-bind failure warns and the build ships an SPA-only bundle with zero prerendered routes.

[prior] FOUND 2026-07-18 (claude/prd-loop-schema-gaps) by accident, which is the point. A leftover process from an earlier run still held port 4178, so the prerenderer failed with EADDRINUSE. It logged, exited 0, and `npm run build` reported success — while writing ONE index.html instead of 31. Every prerendered landing page, all the JSON-LD, and the SEO fixes from WEB-SEO-002/003 were simply absent from the output, and nothing said so. I only noticed because a test failure did not match a probe, and chasing that discrepancy led to dist/events/index.html not existing. Had I not been comparing two measurements, I would have drawn conclusions from a silently broken build — and in fact briefly did. THE FAILURE MODE IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL IN CI: Chromium unavailable on the runner, a port already bound, an OOM on a large route, or a route timing out all take the same path. scripts/prerender.mjs:11-14 states plainly "SAFETY: this NEVER fails the build. Any error is logged and we exit 0". That was a reasonable choice when prerendering was a bonus; it is the wrong default now that PROD-SEO-001 depends on it and canonical/JSON-LD correctness lives there. SAME PATTERN as the rest of this audit: a step that errors, continues, and reports success. See WEB-SEO-003 (sitemap generator ships stale data on failure), WEB-CI-020 (red unit lane), WEB-CI-021 (a11y suite under continue-on-error), WEB-BE-030 (idempotency guard that cannot fire). This one is arguably the most consequential because it silently removes an entire subsystem from the deploy artifact.

userStories.title: Events list made 113 REST requests for 40 cards; batch query was defeated by a first-render race
userStories.description: As a visitor, I need the events list to fetch social data once rather than per card, because a race between the batch query and first render made every card issue its own three requests.
acceptanceCriteria: FIXED in commit 917e7861: forward the batch query isPending into SocialEventCard so it can distinguish batch-not-yet-arrived from batch-has-nothing, and skip the individual fetch while pending
Verify on a production build: /events should issue ~14 REST requests for 40 cards, not 113
Audit the same shape elsewhere — any list that pairs a batch hook with a per-item fallback keyed only on data presence has this race
Consider whether event_attendees / event_discussions should be queried at all while both tables are empty in production
userStories.notes:
VERIFIED 2026-08-11 (claude/prd-p1-loop). The fix was already in (commit 917e7861); what was missing was AC2's verification, which is now measured.

AC2 MEASURED on a production build served locally against the real backend, counting every /rest/v1/ request on first load with no interaction:
  /events       9 REST requests for 40 card links
                  1 events, 1 event_attendees, 1 event_discussions, 1 event_live_stats,
                  3 rpc, 1 subscription_plans, 1 user_analytics
  /restaurants  7 REST requests for 42 card links
Against 113 originally, and better than the ~14 this AC predicted. The three social tables are now exactly one batched request each rather than 34 apiece, which is the batch working.

AC3 AUDITED. Searched for the same shape — a batch hook paired with a per-item fallback keyed only on data presence. useBatchEventSocial is the only batch hook in the tree, and SocialEventCard is its only consumer. Four other components call a per-item hook from inside a mapped list: EventCard (useViewTracking), RestaurantCard (useSponsoredImpression), VotingBooth (useUserVote) and SocialEventCard (useSponsoredImpression). Only useViewTracking issues a query, and it did NOT fire on the homepage — zero event_analytics requests in the measurement above — so none of them reproduces this defect. Nothing else to fix.

AC4 ANSWERED. event_attendees and event_discussions are still queried, and that is now fine: one request each rather than 34, which is not worth a conditional that would have to know whether a table is empty. Note for anyone revisiting — a production probe on 2026-08-11 confirms both tables EXIST (they are not in the 45 confirmed-missing set from WEB-QA-017), so the queries are valid; they are simply empty, and will stop being empty when the social features are used.

THE ORIGINAL DIAGNOSIS IS WORTH KEEPING because every piece looked correct: EventsPage called useBatchEventSocial, SocialEventCard disabled its per-event fetch, useEventSocial early-returned on a falsy id. The defect was purely timing — batchSocialData is undefined until the query resolves, so on first render every card took the fallback and 100+ requests were already in flight by the time the batch landed. Forwarding isPending is what distinguishes "batch not arrived" from "batch has nothing".

[prior] MEASURED 2026-07-18 (claude/prd-loop-schema-gaps) on the production build with no user interaction. /events: 40 cards, 113 REST requests — event_attendees=34, event_discussions=34, event_live_stats=34, i.e. three per card. /restaurants for comparison: 42 cards, 11 requests total. EVERY PIECE LOOKED CORRECT, which is why this survived. EventsPage already called useBatchEventSocial(eventIds); SocialEventCard already disabled its per-event fetch with useEventSocial(socialData ? "" : event.id); useEventSocial already early-returns on a falsy id. The batching was implemented and wired. The defect is purely timing: batchSocialData comes from useQuery and is undefined until it resolves, so on FIRST RENDER every card sees no batch data and takes the fallback. By the time the batch lands, 100+ requests are already in flight. AFTER THE FIX: 14 requests for the same 40 cards, one each to the three social tables. WORTH KNOWING: event_attendees and event_discussions are both EMPTY in production (0 rows), so those 102 extra round trips were retrieving nothing. That made the fix risk-free — no social affordance could render either way — but it also means the events list has been paying a per-card network cost for a feature with no data behind it. See WEB-QA-022 for the related question of which event-social implementation is real. HOW IT WAS FOUND: chasing a failing debounce test. The test was a false positive (it counted event card IMAGES as search requests), but classifying the real traffic to disprove it is what exposed the fan-out. passes stays false pending a production re-measure after deploy.

userStories.title: get_active_ads fails on every page load and is retried 3x per placement
userStories.description: As the platform owner, I need ad serving to make one working call per placement, because every page issues six get_active_ads requests and all six currently return HTTP 300.
acceptanceCriteria: Apply migration 20260718000001 so the RPC stops returning PGRST203 (see WEB-QA-020). That alone takes the homepage from 6 failing calls to 2 succeeding ones

Consider treating 3xx as non-retryable in shouldRetry (src/lib/queryConfig.ts). A PostgREST 300 means "could not choose the best candidate function" — a permanent schema condition that will never resolve by waiting, yet the current policy retries it because the guard only excludes 4xx
Re-measure after the migration: expect 2 calls returning 200 on the homepage, not 6 returning 300
userStories.notes:
CLOSED 2026-08-22 (claude/prd-p1-loop). All three ACs satisfied, and AC1's premise turned out to be only half the story.

AC1 - migration 20260718000001 IS applied. Confirmed by diffing schema_migrations against disk. But the AC says applying it 'alone takes the homepage from 6 failing calls to 2', implying the calls then SUCCEED. They did not. Dropping the stray TEXT overload stopped PostgREST returning PGRST203 before it reached the function body - and revealed a SECOND defect underneath: 42702, 'column reference \"campaign_id\" is ambiguous', because RETURNS TABLE(campaign_id uuid, ...) makes campaign_id an OUT parameter in scope for the whole PL/pgSQL body while both frequency-cap subqueries referenced it unqualified against ad_impressions. Fixed by 20260822000001, applied to production earlier today. See WEB-CI-026, where the same defect was the single failing assertion in the required smoke gate.

AC2 - already done and unchanged: shouldRetry in src/lib/queryConfig.ts treats any sub-400 status as terminal, with the reasoning inline.

AC3 - RE-MEASURED TODAY AND NOW SATISFIED. Called the RPC through PostgREST with the anon key for all four placements:
    top_banner HTTP 200, below_fold HTTP 200, featured_spot HTTP 200, sponsored_listing HTTP 200
The AC asked for 200 rather than 300. The call count half (2 per page, no retries) was already verified on 2026-08-11 by the AC2 work; the status was the outstanding piece.
Note the RPC returns [] rather than rows, which is CORRECT and not a regression: campaign_creatives holds 0 rows, so there is no approved creative to serve (see WEB-LEGAL-011). An accurate empty result, where before it was an error on every page load.

THE GENERAL LESSON, which recurs across this PRD: 'apply the migration and it works' was true of the symptom and not of the cause. Fixing one error revealed the next, and only calling the endpoint with a real caller's arguments showed it.

AC2 DONE AND VERIFIED 2026-08-11 (claude/prd-p1-loop). shouldRetry in src/lib/queryConfig.ts now treats any sub-400 error status as terminal, not just 4xx, with the reasoning recorded inline. A PostgREST 300 (PGRST203, ambiguous overload) is a permanent schema condition that cannot resolve by waiting.

MEASURED on a production build, counting RPC calls by function name:
  BEFORE (2026-07-18): 6 get_active_ads calls per page, every one status 300
  AFTER  (2026-08-11): 2 get_active_ads calls per page, still status 300
Two placements, one call each, no retries. The wasted two-thirds is gone.

AC1 and AC3 REMAIN BLOCKED on migration 20260718000001 (WEB-QA-020). The calls still fail — the overload ambiguity is unchanged — they just fail once instead of three times. Story stays open because the RPC is still broken for every visitor.

FOUND WHILE MEASURING THIS: get_trending_events returns 400/42804 twice per homepage load. Filed as WEB-BE-033. My earlier probes counted all /rest/v1/rpc/* together and hid it; counting by function name is what surfaced it.

[prior] MEASURED 2026-07-18 (claude/prd-loop-schema-gaps) on a production build. Every list page and the homepage issue exactly 6 get_active_ads calls, and every response status was 300 (PGRST203, the ambiguous overload). Confirmed on /events, /restaurants, /attractions and /. So this is two problems stacked: the RPC is broken for everyone (WEB-QA-020, one command to fix), AND it is being called twice as many times as there are placements. The second is worth fixing regardless — once the migration lands, six working calls per page view is six round trips where three would do, on every page, for every visitor. Severity 3 because the failing calls degrade gracefully to the house-ad fallback and cost only latency today. It becomes a real revenue-path concern the moment ads work again. | DIAGNOSIS CORRECTED 2026-07-19. I originally wrote that six calls meant each placement was being requested twice and recommended deduplication. THAT WAS WRONG, and inspecting the request payloads disproved it. There are only TWO distinct placements on the homepage (top_banner, below_fold) and each is requested exactly THREE times. React-query deduplicates by queryKey, so identical keys cannot produce parallel requests — three attempts per key is RETRY behaviour. Root cause: src/lib/queryConfig.ts shouldRetry() declines to retry 4xx (except 408/429) but PGRST203 surfaces as HTTP 300, which is not >= 400, so it falls through to the retryable branch and burns MAX_RETRIES on a permanent condition. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE FIX: there is no dedup work to do. Applying 20260718000001 takes this from 6 failing calls to 2 succeeding ones by itself. The only optional hardening is excluding 3xx from retry, which matters mainly for how loudly the next such failure fails. I am recording the error rather than quietly editing it because the original wording would have sent someone hunting for a duplicate-render bug that does not exist. | RETRY HALF FIXED 2026-07-19 (commit 8ae1a8ab), MEASURED. Root cause was NOT the 3xx status range — that was my second wrong guess. Supabase Postgrest errors carry NO http status at all; they arrive as { code, message, details, hint }, so a status-based guard could never match them however the ranges were tuned. I only found this because widening the guard to 3xx passed its unit tests and then changed nothing in a real page load. Added isPermanentDataError (PGRST* codes and Postgres class-42 SQLSTATEs), checked before status, deliberately excluding connection classes 08xxx/53xxx which do resolve by waiting. Measured before -> after: / 6->2 ad calls and 31->25 total REST, /events 6->2 and 14->10, /restaurants 6->2 and 11->7. The extra drop beyond ads is other schema-error retries disappearing for the same reason. REMAINING: the calls still FAIL (2 per page instead of 6) until migration 20260718000001 is applied — this change only stops multiplying the failure. passes stays false until then.

userStories.title: The two highest-intent landing pages are excluded from prerendering while /pricing, /advertise and /search are included
userStories.description: As the platform owner, I need the pages that match our money queries to ship as static HTML, because /events/this-weekend and /things-to-do are advertised in the sitemap but prerendered for nobody, while four commercial and utility routes consume the prerender budget instead.
acceptanceCriteria: Add to the ROUTES array in scripts/prerender.mjs: /events/this-weekend, /things-to-do, /events/west-des-moines, /events/windsor-heights, /neighborhoods/downtown, /neighborhoods/east-village, /neighborhoods/beaverdale, /neighborhoods/highland-park. All eight are already in public/sitemap-static.xml, so we are advertising URLs we render for no non-JS client

Remove /search from ROUTES and add <meta name="robots" content="noindex, follow"> to src/pages/SearchResults.tsx. Internal search result pages are thin-content by construction and Google explicitly discourages indexing them; today the page has no robots directive at all
Remove /pricing, /advertise and /business from ROUTES. They are conversion pages with no organic query to win, and /business additionally prerenders as a sign-in wall (see WEB-SEO-004)
Do not remove /contact from consideration — it is in sitemap-static.xml but not in ROUTES. Either prerender it or drop it from the sitemap; the two must agree

Add a build-time guard: every <loc> in public/sitemap-static.xml must have a matching entry in prerender.mjs ROUTES, and vice versa. This drift is the actual bug class — the two lists were maintained independently and diverged
Verify after build: dist/events/this-weekend/index.html and dist/things-to-do/index.html exist and contain event/category text in the served HTML, not just the SPA shell
userStories.notes: FOUND 2026-07-29 (claude/des-moines-seo-strategy-n54bjj) while auditing organic and AI-search position against catchdesmoines.com. scripts/prerender.mjs:31-62 lists 31 curated routes. Cross-referencing that list against public/sitemap-static.xml (36 URLs) shows eight sitemap'd routes are absent from ROUTES, and the two most commercially important are /events/this-weekend and /things-to-do — precisely the pages that map to "what events are happening this weekend" and "things to do in Des Moines". Meanwhile /pricing, /advertise, /business, /map and /search ARE prerendered. SEVERITY 1 BECAUSE OF WHO CANNOT READ THEM: Googlebot renders our SPA fine (brand searches surface /events/steve-martin-martin-short-2026-10-11, so the JS path demonstrably works), but public/robots.txt explicitly Allows GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, Applebot-Extended, YouBot and meta-externalagent — none of which execute JavaScript. We invite every AI search crawler and hand it an empty shell on our best pages. That is worse than blocking them: it teaches them the site has no content. This story is the cheapest half of that fix; WEB-SEO-006 is the expensive half. | IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-30 (same branch). Route list extracted to scripts/prerender-routes.mjs as the single source of truth; prerender.mjs imports it. Added: /events/this-weekend, /things-to-do, /events/west-des-moines, /events/windsor-heights, the four /neighborhoods/* pages, /contact. Removed: /search, /pricing, /business, /weekend. /search now renders NoIndexMeta (the component already existed, unused for this). public/sitemap-static.xml gained /calendar, /deals, /map and /itineraries, which were already being prerendered but never submitted. NEW GUARD: scripts/check-seo-route-parity.mjs enforces PRERENDER_ROUTES subset-of sitemap in both directions, with declared exceptions in SITEMAP_ONLY_ROUTES for /advertise, /business-partnership, /privacy-policy and /terms; wired into npm run validate as check-seo-routes and negative-tested in both directions. Current state: 35 prerendered, 4 sitemap-only, 39 sitemapped, consistent. PASSES STAYS FALSE pending the last AC — confirming dist/events/this-weekend/index.html and dist/things-to-do/index.html actually contain listing text after a real build. That needs a build host with Chromium and Supabase credentials for the sitemap step, which this session did not have. | VERIFIED 2026-07-30 by a real build. Note first: `npx vite build` fails on a CLEAN checkout with "[vite:build-html] URI malformed" when VITE_SUPABASE_URL is unset — index.html contains href="%VITE_SUPABASE_URL%" and vite calls decodeURI() on the unsubstituted literal, so "%VI" throws. Not a Node-version issue and not caused by this change (reproduced on a stashed tree); worth its own story since it makes the build unrunnable for anyone without env vars. With env set the build succeeds. RESULTS: prerender reports "35 prerendered, 0 skipped, of 35 routes". All nine newly added routes emit dist/<route>/index.html; dist/search, dist/pricing, dist/business and dist/weekend are all absent as intended. dist/events/this-weekend/index.html is 79KB with title "Events This Weekend | Des Moines Insider", the correct self-canonical, BreadcrumbList/FAQPage/WebSite JSON-LD and 1,636 chars of rendered #main-content text including the "Weekend of July 30, 2026" header. dist/things-to-do/index.html is 114KB with 3,647 chars of category copy. PASSES=TRUE: route coverage, the noindex, and the parity guard are all confirmed against real build output. RESIDUAL, NOT PART OF THIS STORY: the build ran with a placeholder anon key (no key is committed — client.ts deliberately has no fallback), so the prerendered listing pages contain page chrome, headings and FAQ but no live event rows. Whether a production build bakes in current listings is the question WEB-SEO-011 owns.

userStories.title: 884 sitemapped entity URLs are client-render only, so no AI crawler can read any event, restaurant or venue page
userStories.description: As the platform owner, I need entity detail pages to be readable without JavaScript, because the 884 event, restaurant, attraction, playground, article and guide URLs we submit to search engines are exactly the pages AI assistants cite, and none of them render for a crawler that does not run JS.
acceptanceCriteria: Count of record: 284 events + 480 restaurants + 22 attractions + 69 playgrounds + 18 articles + 11 guides = 884 URLs across public/sitemap-*.xml. scripts/prerender.mjs:18-20 states detail pages are "data-driven and intentionally out of scope"

Pick an approach and record the decision in the story notes before building. Option A: enumerate entity URLs from Supabase in prerender.mjs and render them at build time. Option B: a Cloudflare Pages Function that serves a cached server-rendered snapshot to non-JS user agents — functions/_middleware.ts already exists as the hook point. Option A is simpler and cacheable; Option B keeps build time flat and stays fresh between deploys

If Option A: batch the renders, cap concurrency, and preserve the existing never-fail-the-build guarantee (prerender.mjs:11-14 and the exit-0 finally block). 884 sequential Chromium page loads at the current ~600ms settle will not fit a Pages build; measure before committing to it

Whichever approach: the shipped HTML for an event must contain title, date, start time, venue name, street address and price as readable text. Verify by fetching with curl and no JS, then grepping for the event title and venue
Regression test: extend tests/ with a check that a sample of entity URLs returns HTML containing the entity name to a plain HTTP GET
Re-verify the AI-crawler path specifically: request an event URL with a GPTBot user agent and confirm real content comes back
userStories.notes:
SCOPE IS LARGER THAN THIS STORY STATES: the same defect is already shipped on the pSEO surface. 244 published pSEO pages are live in sitemap-pseo.xml (verified in production 2026-08-22) and every one serves the homepage with canonical=/ exactly like the entity URLs. sitemap-pseo.xml is already in ENTITY_SITEMAPS (prerender.mjs:109), so PRERENDER_ENTITIES covers those 244 as well as the 884 counted here - roughly 1,128 URLs ride on that one flag. See WEB-SEO-013.

PRODUCTION RE-MEASURED 2026-08-22 (claude/prd-p1-loop). The blocker is unchanged - PRERENDER_ENTITIES is still not set in the Cloudflare Pages build - but the framing of this story UNDERSTATES the damage, and the correction matters for how it gets prioritised.

'Client-render only' implies an empty shell. It is not. Fetched with a GPTBot user agent and no JS on 2026-08-22, every entity URL returns HTTP 200 with 174,557 bytes and 10,603 characters of readable text - and all of it is THE HOMEPAGE. Verified across an event (/events/harry-potter-and-the-deathly-hallows-part-2-live-in-concert-2027-02-26), a restaurant (/restaurants/4-brothers-bar-grill) and an attraction (/attractions/515-brewing-company): identical <title> 'Things to Do in Des Moines This Weekend | Des Moines Insider', identical 10,603 characters, byte-identical to the homepage itself. '4 Brothers' appears ZERO times on its own restaurant page.

WORSE, AND THIS IS THE PART TO ACT ON. The served HTML carries the homepage's OWN canonical:
    <link rel="canonical" href="https://desmoinesinsider.com/" data-rh="true">
    <meta property="og:url" content="https://desmoinesinsider.com/">
So the sitemap submits 884+ URLs whose non-JS response explicitly instructs crawlers to treat each one as the homepage. That is not invisibility, it is a consolidation directive at scale. This story's prior note says 'Google IS indexing these pages today, so this is not a Google-traffic emergency' - that claim now needs re-checking in Search Console, because a canonical pointing at / is precisely the signal that would deindex them. Googlebot does execute JS and would see the corrected canonical after hydration, so this may be recoverable for Google; for GPTBot and every non-rendering AI crawler it is not.

STRUCTURED DATA IS WRONG ON EVERY ENTITY URL: the 7 ld+json blocks served on that event URL are SoftwareApplication, WebSite, Organization, LocalBusiness, WebPage, LocalBusiness, FAQPage - the homepage set. No Event. No Restaurant. An assistant asking 'when is X playing' gets FAQPage about Des Moines Insider.

SOFT-404 AT UNBOUNDED SCALE, not previously recorded and arguably its own story: /events/this-event-does-not-exist-9999 and /restaurants/nonexistent-place-xyz both return HTTP 200 with the same 174,557-byte homepage. There is no 404 for entity routes at all, so every stale link, typo and expired slug is a live duplicate of the homepage. By contrast /events/today returns 308, so prerendered hub routes are handled differently and are not affected.

WHAT THIS CHANGES: turning PRERENDER_ENTITIES on fixes the 884 real URLs but NOT the soft-404 surface, because an unknown slug will still fall through to the SPA shell. The fallback itself needs to stop serving homepage meta on unmatched routes - that is a separate fix and it is cheap next to the prerender work.

AC6 is therefore ANSWERED IN THE NEGATIVE with evidence, rather than blocked: the AI-crawler path was verified against production and it returns the homepage. Re-run the same check after the flag is on.

MEASURED 2026-08-11 (claude/prd-p1-loop). Still blocked on the env var, but AC3's question — "measure before committing to it" — now has an answer, and AC4 is verified. Nobody has to guess at viability again.

RAN THE ENTITY PASS FOR REAL: PRERENDER_ENTITIES=true with a 150s budget on a 12-core box at concurrency 6.
  1,115 entity URLs enumerated from the sitemaps (the story's count of record was 884 — it has grown)
  328 prerendered, 0 FAILED, 787 left over budget
Zero failures is the headline. The prior assessment measured all 877 producing the same ~1,370 characters of promo boilerplate, but that was against an UNREACHABLE database. With real data, and with the two prerenderer fixes made earlier in this session (wait until the page stops reporting a loading state; wait for Helmet's data-rh count to exceed the shell baseline), every single page cleared the strict quality gate.

AC4 VERIFIED on six sampled event pages — all six carry date, time, venue, address and price as readable text inside #main-content. A representative page: title "2026 Central States Insurance Auditor Association Convention at Hilton Garden Inn West Des Moines - Sunday, October 4 at 4:00 PM", its own canonical, 5 ld+json blocks, and 4,270 characters of readable text including "Sunday October 4, 2026 4:00 PM CT" and the venue name. This is exactly what AC4 asked for and it is already true of the output — no further work needed on the rendering side.

AC3 ANSWERED, AND THE ANSWER IS CONDITIONAL. Throughput measured at 328 routes / 150s = 2.19 routes/sec at concurrency 6. Extrapolated:
  concurrency 6  ->  1,115 routes in ~510s  (~8.5 min) + vite 50s + hub 21s = ~9.7 min total
  concurrency 3  ->  ~17 min total
  concurrency 2  ->  ~25 min total
Cloudflare Pages kills a build at 20 minutes. prerender.mjs sets CONCURRENCY = min(6, max(2, cores-1)), so the outcome depends entirely on the CPU count of the Pages build container — which I cannot determine from here. It FITS at 6 cores-ish, is TIGHT at 4, and FAILS at 2. That is the number the story asked for and the reason Option A cannot simply be switched on without checking.

RECOMMENDATION, recorded per AC2 which asks for a decision before building: Option A (build-time prerender) is viable and needs no new code — the implementation is done, verified, and produces correct output. The single risk is build duration on the host. So: set PRERENDER_ENTITIES=true in the Cloudflare Pages environment and read the build log. If the entity pass reports a large "left unrendered (budget)" figure or the build nears 20 minutes, that is the signal to move to Option B (the functions/_middleware.ts snapshot path) rather than to raise the budget. The existing budget mechanism already fails safe: it stops at the deadline and reports the shortfall loudly rather than timing out the build.

ALSO WORTH KNOWING: the pass wrote 308 event pages plus others in a 150s sample and stripped 6,893 runtime-injected modulepreload links doing it, so the lazy-chunk hygiene applies to entity pages too.

STILL BLOCKED, unchanged: PRERENDER_ENTITIES is not set in the Cloudflare Pages build, and setting it is a host configuration change this environment cannot make. AC5 (a regression test asserting entity URLs return entity content to a plain GET) and AC6 (verify with a GPTBot UA against production) both require the flag to be on in a real deploy first.

[prior] RE-VERIFIED (CODE REVIEW 2026-08-06): correctly open. The entity prerender pass IS implemented — scripts/prerender.mjs:63-120 (ENTITY_SITEMAPS, collectEntityRoutes, PRERENDER_ENTITY_BUDGET_SECONDS default 420) and :458-486 (renderPool with a strict quality gate). But it is OFF BY DEFAULT: the header at :102 spells out why, and PRERENDER_ENTITIES must be set for any of the 884 URLs to render. Until that flag is on in the Cloudflare Pages build, the outcome this story asks for is not shipping.

[prior] FOUND 2026-07-29 (claude/des-moines-seo-strategy-n54bjj). This is the single largest structural gap between our stated GEO ambition and reality, and it is the precondition for every other AI-search item — llms.txt, FAQ markup, Speakable, the openapi.yaml surface and the whole GEO field set on events/restaurants are all inert while the pages they describe are invisible to non-JS clients. Entity pages matter disproportionately for AI citation because assistants answer entity questions by name ("is X open", "when is Y", "where is Z playing") and cite the page that states the fact. Note the asymmetry with WEB-SEO-005: Google IS indexing these pages today, so this is not a Google-traffic emergency — it is an AI-visibility emergency, plus a resilience improvement for Google (rendered indexing is slower and less reliable at 884 URLs than static HTML). SEVERITY 1 for scope and blocking-ness, but sequence it AFTER WEB-SEO-005 and the Phase 0 correctness fixes, because those are hours of work and this is days. | PROTOTYPED, MEASURED AND LANDED BEHIND A FLAG 2026-07-30 (claude/des-moines-seo-strategy-n54bjj). DECISION: build-time prerendering, not edge-side snapshots. Rationale — Cloudflare Workers cannot run Chromium, so the edge route would mean the Browser Rendering API or a render-on-first-bot-hit cache: materially more moving parts, a cold-start penalty on the first crawler request, and a new runtime dependency in front of pages we need crawlers to trust. The measurements below show build-time fits, so the simpler option wins. IMPLEMENTATION: scripts/prerender.mjs now runs two passes. Hubs first, unbudgeted. Then entity URLs enumerated from the sitemaps already sitting in dist/ — chosen over querying Supabase because the sitemaps are generated immediately beforehand by generate-sitemaps, it keeps prerendered as a subset of sitemapped by construction, and the prerender step needs no credentials. Added a concurrency pool (PRERENDER_CONCURRENCY, default cores-1 capped at 6), a time budget (PRERENDER_ENTITY_BUDGET_SECONDS, default 420) and priority ordering by sitemap so events render before evergreen guides if the budget bites. MEASURED on a 4-core box: 2.26 s/route sequential, ~0.94 s/route at concurrency 3 (2.5x), so 877 entity URLs is about 13.7 minutes on top of the ~70s vite build. Cloudflare Pages kills a build at 20 minutes, so it fits but without much margin, and the measurement used a placeholder Supabase key so pages never waited on real queries — production will be slower. THE MOST IMPORTANT FINDING IS A NEAR-MISS: with an unreachable database, the first working version happily wrote 127 event pages that were all the same 1,370 characters of promo boilerplate, no title of their own, no canonical. An earlier version was worse still — it captured the prerendered HOMEPAGE, canonical and all, under event URLs. Shipping either is strictly worse than doing nothing, because today those URLs serve a shell that Googlebot renders into real content, whereas static thin duplicates give Google a reason not to re-render and hand it hundreds of near-identical pages. So the entity pass now FAILS CLOSED: a page is only written if it carries a canonical matching its own route and a title different from the build shell's. Verified both directions — with the database unreachable, 0 written and 67 rejected with a clear reason; positive control with two known-good routes forced through the strict path, 2 written with correct canonicals, 0 failed. Budget overrun is reported loudly rather than silently truncating. DEFAULT IS OFF (PRERENDER_ENTITIES unset). Not timidity: entity rendering cannot be validated against real data from this session, and the honest sequence is one deliberate run on the real build host to confirm pages resolve and to get a true timing, then flip it on. The strict gate is what makes that first run safe — worst case is zero pages written and a log saying why. REMAINING: enable on the build host and tune the budget; confirm shipped entity HTML carries date/time/venue/price as text; add the regression test asserting a plain HTTP GET returns the entity name; re-check with a GPTBot user agent. NOTE THE INTERACTION WITH WEB-SEO-011: the daily rebuild that story adds would now carry the entity pass too, so enabling both means a ~15 min daily build. Tune the budget with that in mind. | NEW SAFEGUARD 2026-07-30, from a risk observed while fixing WEB-SEO-002. The prerenderer captures whatever state a page happens to be in, and it was happily writing transient failures to disk: with unreachable credentials /events captured 'Loading events page…' and /articles captured "You're offline — Check your internet connection", both reported as successful prerenders. In production a brief Supabase hiccup mid-build would therefore publish an offline error as the static, crawler-facing HTML for a hub route, and it would stay that way until the next deploy. renderRoute now rejects any capture containing a known loading/failure marker. Throwing leaves no file, so Cloudflare serves the SPA shell and Googlebot renders it client-side — exactly the pre-prerender behaviour, and strictly better than publishing an error page. This complements the entity-pass strict gate: that one proves a page rendered as ITSELF, this one proves it did not render a FAILURE, and it applies to hub routes too. Verified: both routes now rejected with a clear reason instead of shipping.

UPDATE 2026-08-18 (claude/desmoines-jsonld-price-fix-slyku1). Two things, neither of which unblocks the story.

PRIORITY ORDER REVERSED in scripts/prerender.mjs: restaurants now run before events. The old order put 312 event URLs ahead of 480 restaurant pages on the stated assumption that events are highest-intent. The 2026-08-17 Search Console pull does not support that assumption -- restaurant URLs drew 6,794 impressions and event URLs drew far fewer, converting zero clicks -- and with the budget truncating roughly seven URLs in ten (328 of 1,115 rendered), the order decides most of the coverage. This is inert until the flag below is set. It is also a single pull rather than a trend, so re-check it before treating it as settled.

STILL THE ONE BLOCKER, unchanged since 2026-08-11: PRERENDER_ENTITIES=true is not set in the production build environment. It is host-side (Cloudflare Pages build settings), not in the repo or CI, so no commit can turn it on. 883 entity pages currently ship the prerendered homepage shell, which means each one carries the homepage title and a canonical pointing at https://desmoinesinsider.com/ -- every entity page declares itself a duplicate of the homepage. Setting the flag alone will not finish the job either: 883 pages do not fit one build at the current budget, so PRERENDER_ENTITY_BUDGET_SECONDS and PRERENDER_CONCURRENCY need raising with it, minding the Cloudflare Pages build timeout.

userStories.title: /weekend and /events/this-weekend compete for the same query, and the page with no canonical or schema is the prerendered one
userStories.description: As the platform owner, I need one canonical weekend page, because two routes target the same intent with the same title concept and the crawlable one is the weaker of the two.
acceptanceCriteria: Compare the two: src/pages/WeekendPage.tsx sets title "This Weekend in Des Moines - AI-Curated Event Guide" with no canonical prop, no faqData and no EventListJsonLd. src/pages/EventsThisWeekend.tsx sets an explicit canonical via getCanonicalUrl('/events/this-weekend'), passes faqData and breadcrumbs to EnhancedLocalSEO with isTimeSensitive, and emits EventListJsonLd
Keep /events/this-weekend as canonical. Add `/weekend  /events/this-weekend  301` to public/_redirects, following the existing WEB-UX-016 entry as the pattern
Per the Backward Compatibility rules in CLAUDE.md, /weekend is a public route referenced by the sitemap, so the 301 must stay in place for at least one release cycle before the route is removed
Remove /weekend from public/sitemap-static.xml and from prerender.mjs ROUTES in the same change, so we stop prerendering a page that now redirects

Decide the fate of src/components/WeekendGuide.tsx — it is the only thing WeekendPage renders. If it has content EventsThisWeekend lacks, port it across before deleting the route rather than losing it
Verify: curl -I https://desmoinesinsider.com/weekend returns 301 to /events/this-weekend, and only one URL in the sitemap targets weekend intent
userStories.notes:
VERIFIED COMPLETE 2026-08-11 (claude/prd-p1-loop). No code change needed — the work had landed and the story was never closed. All six ACs checked against the repo and against production rather than against the previous note.

AC2 + AC6, MEASURED LIVE with a GPTBot user agent:
  curl https://desmoinesinsider.com/weekend             -> 301 -> https://desmoinesinsider.com/events/this-weekend
  curl https://desmoinesinsider.com/events/this-weekend -> 308 -> .../events/this-weekend/  (trailing-slash normalisation, then 200)
public/_redirects:13 carries the rule with the reasoning above it.

AC4 DONE, and I initially misread it. grep put "/weekend" at scripts/prerender-routes.mjs:107 and I took that for PRERENDER_ROUTES. Importing the arrays instead of trusting the line number: PRERENDER_ROUTES.includes("/weekend") is FALSE — line 107 is inside DELIBERATELY_EXCLUDED_ROUTES, which is the right place for it and records why. public/sitemap-static.xml:186 has the removal plus a comment. scripts/check-seo-route-parity.mjs passes: "35 prerendered, 4 sitemap-only, 39 sitemapped — consistent", and its check 3 specifically catches a route that is both excluded and used, so a half-finished revert here would fail the build.

That is now inverted: /events/this-weekend is prerendered and, per the WEB-SEO-002 work in this same session, ships its own canonical and 5-6 ld+json blocks.

[prior] FOUND 2026-07-29 (claude/des-moines-seo-strategy-n54bjj). The cannibalization itself is ordinary; what makes it severity 1 is the direction of it. /weekend is in prerender.mjs ROUTES and /events/this-weekend is not, so the version a crawler can read is the one with no canonical tag of its own, no FAQ content and no ItemList/Event schema, while the fully-marked-up version is JS-only. Cheap fix, and it compounds with WEB-SEO-005 — doing 005 without 007 would leave two prerendered pages fighting each other, which is worse than today. | IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-30 (same branch), PARTIAL. AC5 IS THE PART THAT WAS OPEN, and the answer is delete, not port. src/components/WeekendGuide.tsx had nothing EventsThisWeekend lacks: fetchWeekendGuide() never queried anything, it built a literal object ("This weekend in Des Moines! Check out these featured events.", events_count: 5) and the page presented it to the public as "AI-generated guide featuring 5 local events" and "Generated by AI on <today>".
