userStories.title: The FAQPage duplication GSC is reporting was fixed in June and never revalidated
userStories.description: As the platform owner, I need the stale duplicate-FAQPage error cleared and the regression guarded, because the defect was fixed on 2026-06-26 but our only GSC export predates the fix by four months, so nobody knows it is resolved.
acceptanceCriteria: No code change is required for the duplication itself. Verified emitter by emitter: EnhancedAttractionSEO.tsx:127 and EnhancedPlaygroundSEO.tsx:140 now contain only a comment recording that FAQPage was removed; FreeEvents.tsx and KidsEvents.tsx pass showSchema={false}; EnhancedLocalSEO emits only when faqData is supplied and no page supplies it alongside FAQSection; EnhancedEventSEO emits unconditionally but no page renders it with FAQSection; PseoFaq is presentational and PseoPage owns the pSEO FAQPage
Request validation for `Duplicate field "FAQPage"` in Google Search Console and confirm the 34 items clear. This is the whole remaining task and it is a console action, not a commit
Re-export GSC/ once validation passes so the committed snapshot stops describing a fixed defect. Depends on WEB-SEO-014

DONE: scripts/check-duplicate-schema.mjs statically resolves which FAQPage-emitting components each page renders and whether each is active, and fails npm run validate on any page with more than one. Verified against a deliberately reintroduced duplicate

The guard models emitters from the implementation, not from src/pseo/componentSpecs.ts — that file describes PseoFaq as carrying FAQPage markup, which is the design spec and not what the component does. Keep that distinction if the emitter list is extended

Separate follow-up, not a blocker here: EnhancedEventSEO.tsx:176-210 generates mad-lib FAQ answers that restate the page title ("When is {title}?" -> "{title} takes place {date} at {venue}"). They add nothing extractable. Worth replacing with substantive answers, tracked on its own
userStories.notes:
REOPENED ON EVIDENCE 2026-08-22 (claude/prd-p1-loop). THIS IS NOT A STALE REPORT. The FAQPage duplication GSC flagged is LIVE IN PRODUCTION RIGHT NOW on at least four URLs.

Fetched with a GPTBot UA and no JS, counting ld+json blocks whose @type is FAQPage:
    /events/today          FAQPage x2   <- duplicate
    /events/this-weekend   FAQPage x2   <- duplicate
    /events/date-night     FAQPage x2   <- duplicate
    /events/altoona        FAQPage x2   <- duplicate
    /events, /restaurants, /restaurants/open-now, /attractions, /playgrounds, /articles, /guides, /events/ankeny, /events/clive   all x1, correct
On /events/today the two blocks are IDENTICAL, both asking 'What's happening today in Des Moines?' and 'How current is this information?'. That is exactly the `Duplicate field "FAQPage"` GSC reported.

WHY THE STORY CONCLUDED OTHERWISE, and it was a reasonable conclusion from the evidence it had: AC1 checked each React EMITTER against its render path and found no page rendering two. That is TRUE - EventsToday.tsx renders exactly one FAQPage source, EnhancedLocalSEO. The duplication does not come from a second component.

IT COMES FROM THE pSEO OVERLAY, which is WEB-SEO-013's collision list materialising. public.pseo_pages holds PUBLISHED rows for the exact colliding slugs - /events/today, /events/this-weekend, /events/date-night, /events/ankeny are all is_published = true, and there are 25 published pSEO rows under /events/ alone. WEB-SEO-013's audit predicted precisely these ten collisions with real prerendered routes; four of the ones I sampled now emit schema twice. The React route emits its FAQPage and the pSEO page for the same slug emits another.

WHY THE GUARD CANNOT CATCH IT: scripts/check-duplicate-schema.mjs reports '549 components scanned, 25 emit FAQPage, 0 duplicates' and is CORRECT about components. It models React emitters and their render paths; the pSEO overlay is data in a database table, invisible to a static scan. A guard that models the implementation cannot see a duplicate introduced by content.

ONE MORE THING THAT MISLEADS: a LOCAL npm run build of the same source produces FAQPage x1 for /events/today, while production serves x2. Source is identical to main for both EventsToday.tsx and EnhancedLocalSEO.tsx, and the June fix 2c28084 is on main. So this cannot be reproduced by building and inspecting dist/ - only by fetching production, where the pSEO rows exist.

AC2 SHOULD NOT BE ACTIONED YET. Requesting GSC validation now would fail on these URLs and burn the revalidation. Resolve the collision first - decide whether the React route or the pSEO page owns each colliding slug, per WEB-SEO-013 AC7 - then revalidate.

FOUND 2026-07-29 (claude/des-moines-seo-strategy-n54bjj), CORRECTED 2026-07-30. I originally filed this as a live P1 defect duplicating FAQPage across 8 page types, and that was WRONG. The claim came from counting `grep -c FAQPage` hits per file without checking whether the matches were code or comments — in EnhancedAttractionSEO and EnhancedPlaygroundSEO the sole remaining match is a comment reading "FAQ schema is output by FAQSection ... avoid duplicate FAQPage". Checking each emitter against its actual render path shows zero duplicates in the tree today. git log -S dates the fix to 2c28084, merged 2026-06-26 (PR #306); the GSC export committed under GSC/ is dated 2026-03-13, four and a half months earlier. So the critical error is a stale report, not an open bug, and the reason nobody noticed is exactly WEB-SEO-014 — GSC has not been synced since March. DROPPED FROM P1 TO P3: the remaining work is one console action plus the regression guard, which is already written and wired into npm run validate. The guard is the durable value here — the bug is genuinely hard to catch in review because every component is correct in isolation and the duplication only exists in the composition, which is presumably how it shipped in the first place. | VERIFIED IN BUILD OUTPUT 2026-07-30. Grepped '"@type":"FAQPage"' across all 35 dist/**/index.html files: maximum 1 per page, zero duplicates. That is empirical confirmation on shipped HTML, not just the static analysis — the code-side conclusion holds. PASSES STAYS FALSE because the one remaining AC is a console action nobody in this session can perform: requesting validation in Google Search Console so the stale 34-item error clears. Flip this to true once that validation passes.

userStories.title: Concluded events are marked EventPostponed and stay index,follow forever
userStories.description: As the platform owner, I need past events to describe themselves accurately, because every concluded event asserts schema.org/EventPostponed — which means "moved to an unannounced future date" — and none are ever de-indexed.
acceptanceCriteria: src/components/EnhancedEventSEO.tsx:129 reads `"eventStatus": isUpcoming ? "https://schema.org/EventScheduled" : "https://schema.org/EventPostponed"`. A finished concert is not postponed. Past events should stay EventScheduled with a past endDate, which is how schema.org expresses "this happened"

Reserve EventPostponed for events actually flagged as postponed in the data, and EventCancelled for cancelled ones. If the events table has no status column to drive this, do not invent one for this story — just stop asserting the false value

EnhancedEventSEO.tsx:267 emits `index, follow` unconditionally. Add `noindex, follow` for events more than ~30 days past, so concluded listings drop out of the index instead of accumulating. Keep follow so the internal links still pass

Coordinate the threshold with scripts/generate-dynamic-sitemaps.ts:122, which uses GRACE_DAYS = 7 for sitemap inclusion. The sitemap window and the noindex window should be deliberate about the gap, not accidentally different

Check src/components/schema/EventSchema.tsx:53 as well — it fabricates an endDate of startDate + 3 hours when none is supplied. Fabricating a duration is defensible for a rich-result requirement, but it should be a documented decision, not a silent default
Verify: pick a concluded event URL, confirm eventStatus is EventScheduled with a past endDate and that robots is noindex,follow past the threshold
userStories.notes:
VERIFIED DONE (CODE REVIEW 2026-08-06): both halves are fixed in src/components/EnhancedEventSEO.tsx. The isUpcoming prop that drove the EventScheduled/EventPostponed switch was removed and the header now states the reasoning ("a concluded event is not postponed"); :152 documents that EventPostponed means "moved to a date not yet announced". The robots half is fixed too: :139-140 compute robotsDirective = isStaleEvent ? "noindex, follow" : "index, follow", derived from the event's own start date rather than a caller-supplied flag, and both the robots (:307) and googlebot (:308) meta tags use it. :126 records the old behaviour ("index, follow", so concluded listings never aged out) as the bug this replaced.

[prior] FOUND 2026-07-29 (claude/des-moines-seo-strategy-n54bjj) while auditing Event markup quality. Two problems compound here. The false EventPostponed is the sharper one: it is a factual misstatement on what is likely hundreds of URLs, and Event markup accuracy is exactly what Google's structured-data spam guidance targets. Because the same component also keeps every past event index,follow, those false assertions accumulate in the index rather than aging out. It is plausible that this contributes to the invalid-item count in GSC/Chart.csv alongside the FAQPage duplication in WEB-SEO-008, though the GSC export we have only names the FAQPage issue explicitly, so treat that as a hypothesis to confirm after 008 clears rather than an established second cause. SEVERITY 2 not 1: it degrades trust in our Event markup and bloats the index, but unlike 005/007 it is not costing us a page we could otherwise rank. | IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-30 (same branch). EnhancedEventSEO.tsx no longer emits EventPostponed for past events — eventStatus is now unconditionally EventScheduled, with the past endDate carrying the "this is over" meaning, which is how schema.org expresses it. Real postponements would need a status column on events; none exists, so we no longer guess. Also added STALE_EVENT_NOINDEX_DAYS = 30: robots/googlebot/bingbot flip to noindex,follow once an event is more than 30 days past, replacing the previously unconditional index,follow. The 30-day threshold is intentionally later than the 7-day GRACE_DAYS in scripts/generate-dynamic-sitemaps.ts, so between day 7 and day 30 an event stays indexable but unsubmitted. PASSES STAYS FALSE on the remaining AC: EventSchema.tsx still fabricates endDate as startDate + 3h when none is supplied, and that is still an undocumented silent default rather than a recorded decision. | FOLLOW-UP 2026-07-30: removed the now-dead `isUpcoming` prop from EnhancedEventSEOProps and from its only call site (EventDetails.tsx). It existed solely to drive the EventScheduled/EventPostponed switch this story deleted, and eslint flagged it unused. Staleness for the robots directive is derived internally from the event start date instead, so the component no longer depends on the caller computing it correctly. tsc and eslint clean on both files.

userStories.title: We name ourselves as organizer and performer on events we neither organize nor perform
userStories.description: As the platform owner, I need organizer and performer omitted when unknown, because EventSchema defaults both to "Des Moines Insider", which asserts that we organize touring Broadway shows and perform at symphony concerts.
acceptanceCriteria: src/components/schema/EventSchema.tsx:79-95 falls back to `{"@type": "Organization", name: "Des Moines Insider", url: "https://desmoinesinsider.com"}` for organizer when none is passed, and to the same value for performer when neither performer nor organizer is passed
Omit both fields when the underlying data is unknown. Neither is required by Google's Event structured data guidance, and an absent field is strictly better than a false one
Audit EnhancedEventSEO.tsx for the same pattern before closing — it builds its own Event object and shows 3 Organization nodes, so check whether it repeats this fallback
If a real organizer exists on the event record but is not being passed through, wire it up in the same change — that is the actual win here, not just removing the false value
Verify: an event with no known organizer emits no organizer and no performer key at all
userStories.notes:
FIXED 2026-08-11 (claude/prd-p1-loop). AC3 was the whole story and the earlier pass got it wrong.

THE BUILDER THAT MATTERED WAS NEVER TOUCHED. src/components/schema/EventListJsonLd.tsx:85-92 hardcoded BRAND.name as organizer of every event in the list and named the VENUE as performer — so Iowa Cubs vs St. Paul Saints shipped as organized by Des Moines Insider and performed by Field of Dreams. It renders on the PRERENDERED hub pages (/events/today, /events/this-weekend, /events/free, /events/kids, /events/date-night, the monthly pages), which is precisely the HTML that JS-less crawlers read. EventSchema.tsx and EnhancedEventSEO.tsx — the two the earlier pass fixed — do not appear in that output at all.

MEASURED, not assumed. Parsed every ld+json block in all 35 dist/**/index.html files from a clean build. BEFORE: 6 pages carrying 119 organizer keys. AFTER: 1 page, 1 organizer key, 0 performer keys — and that one is /iowa-state-fair naming 'Iowa State Fair' with its own url, which is true and stays.

TWO MORE SITES FOUND IN THE SAME SWEEP, both hardcoded: src/components/LocalSEO.tsx:180 (organizer = BRAND.name on whatever event the neighbourhood pages pass in) and src/components/SEOTools.tsx:378 (organizer = 'Des Moines Insider' in schema markup this admin tool generates for an operator to paste ELSEWHERE, so a false value propagates off-site where we cannot correct it). Both removed. src/components/EnhancedLocalSEO.tsx:216 was already correct — spread conditionally on real organizer data.

AC4 is N/A and now documented in the code: the events table carries no organizer, performer or artist column, so there is nothing true to wire through. If ingestion ever captures one, add it back conditionally — never as a fallback.

AC5 VERIFIED as above: 0 organizer and 0 performer keys on every event with no known organizer, across all 35 prerendered pages.

[prior] FOUND 2026-07-29 (claude/des-moines-seo-strategy-n54bjj). This is a small diff with a disproportionate risk profile. An aggregator that inserts its own name as the organizer and performer of third-party events is a recognisable spam pattern — it is how scraped-event doorway sites present themselves — and we do it by default on every event lacking organizer data, which given crawled sources is most of them. There is no upside being captured: neither field drives a rich result for us. SEVERITY 2 rather than 1 only because the blast radius is reputational/algorithmic rather than a measurable ranking loss we can point at today. Fix it alongside WEB-SEO-009; they are the same file family and the same review. | IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-30 (same branch). Two components were affected and the worse one was not the one this story originally named. EventSchema.tsx: organizer and performer are now spread conditionally and omitted entirely when unknown, instead of falling back to "Des Moines Insider". EnhancedEventSEO.tsx — the component actually rendered on live event detail pages — was worse than described: it hardcoded Des Moines Insider as organizer UNCONDITIONALLY (no fallback logic at all), and named the VENUE as performer when one was known, so a touring show was published as organized by us and performed by the building it played in. Both fields are now removed with the reasoning recorded inline. CONFIRMED there is no truthful value available: neither src/lib/types.ts Event nor the events table in the generated Supabase types has an organizer, performer, artist, presenter or promoter column, so the "wire up the real organizer" AC has nothing to wire — noted inline so a future change adds them conditionally rather than reinstating a fallback. PASSES STAYS FALSE only pending a Rich Results Test on a deployed event URL confirming neither key is present.

userStories.title: The daily event crawl never reaches a sitemap, the prerendered HTML, or any indexing endpoint
userStories.description: As the platform owner, I need freshness to actually ship, because the crawler ingests events every day and nothing downstream regenerates sitemaps, rebuilds prerendered pages, or notifies a search engine until a human happens to deploy.
acceptanceCriteria: .github/workflows/event-crawler.yml runs on `cron: 0 12 * * *`. After it writes to the database, no step regenerates sitemaps, triggers a rebuild, or pings any indexing endpoint

Sitemaps are only produced by `npm run generate-sitemaps`, which package.json wires into `npm run build`, which Cloudflare Pages only runs on push to main. A week with no deploy is a week of stale sitemaps on an events site

The prerendered hub HTML has the same problem and it is worse: dist/events/today/index.html is frozen at last deploy, so a crawler fetching /events/today gets whatever "today" meant when we last shipped
Add post-crawl steps to event-crawler.yml: invoke the existing regenerate-sitemaps edge function, then trigger a Cloudflare Pages deploy hook so prerendered output is rebuilt with the day's data

Schedule submission of new and changed URLs. Note the constraint: the Google Indexing API officially supports only JobPosting and BroadcastEvent, so do not build the whole plan on the existing google-indexing-api function. Implement IndexNow for Bing/Yandex, and rely on accurate sitemap lastmod plus a fast rebuild for Google
Both regenerate-sitemaps and google-indexing-api exist as edge functions and are on no schedule at all — check supabase/migrations for seo_monitoring_schedules rows before adding a parallel mechanism
Measure the outcome: median days from event ingest to indexed URL. Target under 3. This is the number the whole story exists to move
userStories.notes: FOUND 2026-07-29 (claude/des-moines-seo-strategy-n54bjj). Strategically this is the most damaging finding in the set, because freshness and coverage are the ONLY structural advantages we have over catchdesmoines.com. They are a DMO with the backlink profile of every hotel and chamber in Polk County; we will not out-authority them. What we can beat them on is that their calendar is submission-based and curated while ours is crawled daily — and we currently throw that advantage away between the database write and anything a crawler can see. The infrastructure to fix it already exists (regenerate-sitemaps, google-indexing-api, seo_monitoring_schedules); nothing is scheduled to call it. SEVERITY 1. Sequence note: this compounds with WEB-SEO-006 — if entity prerendering moves to build time, a daily rebuild becomes a daily 884-page render, so decide 006's approach before wiring the daily trigger here. | SCOPE CORRECTED 2026-07-30 after reading the implementation. The sitemap half of this story was written as "nothing regenerates sitemaps", which is wrong and understates how much already exists. supabase/functions/regenerate-sitemaps drains a sitemap_change_queue populated by DB triggers, regenerates per-table XML, uploads to a public `sitemaps` storage bucket and pings search engines — and migration 20260623000001_sitemap_change_queue.sql DOES schedule it on pg_cron every 6h (jobname regenerate-sitemaps-event-driven). So regeneration runs. THE ACTUAL BUG IS SHARPER AND WORSE: nothing serves those files. robots.txt points crawlers at https://desmoinesinsider.com/sitemap-events.xml, which Cloudflare Pages serves from the static build output — the copy frozen at last deploy. public/_redirects has no sitemap rule, public/_headers only sets Cache-Control on /sitemap*.xml, and functions/_middleware.ts:157 explicitly early-returns for any .xml path, so it never proxies them either. The freshly regenerated sitemaps sit in a storage bucket that no crawler is ever pointed at. FIX IS NOW SMALLER THAN THE ORIGINAL STORY IMPLIED: route /sitemap-*.xml to the bucket (a _redirects 200-rewrite or a middleware branch that stops skipping .xml), or have the function commit/deploy instead of uploading. The prerendered-HTML staleness and the indexing-submission ACs are unaffected and still stand. | PARTIALLY IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-30. Added a publish-freshness job to .github/workflows/event-crawler.yml, gated on success and skipped for dry runs. It calls regenerate-sitemaps (continue-on-error, best effort) and then POSTs a Cloudflare Pages deploy hook. CHOSE THE DEPLOY HOOK OVER ROUTING THE STORAGE BUCKET DELIBERATELY: a rebuild regenerates sitemap-*.xml AND re-runs the prerenderer, so it fixes the stale-prerendered-HTML half of this story too, which routing the bucket does nothing for. It also avoids putting a runtime dependency in front of every sitemap URL — if a bucket-proxy function failed Google would lose all sitemaps at once, whereas a failed rebuild just leaves the previous working static files in place. Both steps no-op with a GitHub warning when their secret is absent, so merging this cannot break the existing crawl. BLOCKED ON A HUMAN: CLOUDFLARE_DEPLOY_HOOK_URL must be created in the Cloudflare Pages project and added as a repository secret, and SUPABASE_URL likewise — only SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, SUPABASE_ANON_KEY and EDGE_FUNCTION_API_KEY are configured today. Until then the job runs and warns rather than failing. STILL OPEN: IndexNow submission, and the median-days-from-ingest-to-indexed measurement this story exists to move. | INDEXNOW SHIPPED 2026-08-11 (claude/prd-p1-loop). AC5 done. THE FINDING THAT MADE IT URGENT: regenerate-sitemaps' "ping search engines" step was calling two dead endpoints. Probed live 2026-08-11 — GET https://www.google.com/ping?sitemap=... returns 404 "Sitemaps ping is deprecated" (Google retired it June 2023) and the Bing equivalent returns 410 Gone. The job had been running every 6h and writing {google: 404, bing: 410} into its own job metadata as though that were the notification step. So the story's premise ("nothing pings any indexing endpoint") was true in a worse way than written: something DID run, reported numbers, and notified nobody. IMPLEMENTATION: supabase/functions/_shared/indexNow.ts (buildIndexNowPayload + submitToIndexNow + describeIndexNowStatus), wired into regenerate-sitemaps step 5 in place of pingSearchEngines. It submits the SPECIFIC changed URLs already resolved from sitemap_change_queue in step 4, so it inherits the existing pg_cron 6h schedule AND the daily post-crawl invocation added earlier in this story — no parallel mechanism, per AC6. Covers Bing/Yandex/Naver/Seznam. Google is deliberately NOT covered here: they never replaced the ping and ask publishers to rely on sitemap lastmod, which step 3 of the same job already regenerates, plus the existing Indexing API path where a service account is configured. KEY HANDLING, DELIBERATE: public/c2d7b3a0ed753ae68b306e25422227ff.txt is committed, containing exactly the key and nothing else (32 bytes, no trailing newline). An IndexNow key is public by protocol — the whole authorization model is that the key must be fetchable at https://<host>/<key>.txt — so knowing it grants exactly one capability, asking Bing to recrawl a URL on our own host, which any reader of that file can already do. It is NOT in a secret store on purpose: the edge function and the static file must agree, and splitting one public value across two config surfaces is how they drift into 403s nobody sees. functions/_middleware.ts:157 already passes .txt through to the asset handler, so Cloudflare Pages serves it. FILTERING IS THE PART THAT MATTERS: IndexNow rejects the ENTIRE batch with 422 if one URL is off-host, so buildIndexNowPayload drops off-host/unparseable/non-HTTP URLs, dedupes, caps at the 10,000 protocol limit, and reports what it dropped instead of losing the run silently. TESTS: supabase/functions/_tests/indexnow.test.ts, 9 Deno tests, all passing. One of them asserts the key file still contains exactly INDEXNOW_KEY — proved it fires by appending a single newline (FAILED as intended, then restored), because a formatter adding a newline is the realistic way this breaks. Wired into subscription-sync-tests.yml, and public/*.txt added to that workflow's path filter so a PR touching only public/ still runs it. deno check on regenerate-sitemaps shows 1 error, confirmed pre-existing on main by stash-and-recheck (the supabase-js SupabaseClient generic mismatch on buildSitemaps, untouched by this change). STILL OPEN, and it is now the only thing left besides the secrets: AC7, median days from event ingest to indexed URL. Design if picking this up with database access — gsc_page_performance (migration 20260331000002) holds per-page GSC rows, so median(first row date for a URL minus events.created_at) is computable as a view plus an RPC. Note it is a PROXY: first impression is not the same as first indexed, and it undercounts URLs that are indexed but never surfaced. NOT WRITTEN HERE on purpose — there is no Postgres in this environment (no docker, no local instance, hub DISARMED), and shipping an unverified view in a migration is worse than leaving the AC honestly open. STILL BLOCKED ON A HUMAN, unchanged: CLOUDFLARE_DEPLOY_HOOK_URL and SUPABASE_URL repository secrets.

userStories.title: The homepage targets our own architecture instead of any query a person searches for
userStories.description: As the platform owner, I need the homepage to answer "what is there to do in Des Moines", because our highest-authority page currently sells the product to itself and its on-page FAQ explains our AI stack.
acceptanceCriteria: src/pages/Index.tsx title is `${BRAND.name} - Conversational City Guide | AI-Powered Event & Restaurant Discovery`. "Conversational City Guide" and "AI-Powered Discovery" have no search volume; nobody searches for how we are built

The on-page FAQ is titled "Frequently Asked Questions About Des Moines AI Pulse" with description "Learn how our conversational AI technology transforms the way you discover and experience Des Moines." Replace with questions real visitors ask: what is there to do in Des Moines this weekend, what is free, where should I eat, what is on tonight
Rewrite the title around the actual head term. Keep the brand suffix — getPageTitle in src/lib/brandConfig.ts already handles that convention

BRAND.description in src/lib/brandConfig.ts:32 is the site-wide default meta description and leads with "Discover events, restaurants, and attractions in Des Moines, Iowa. AI-powered local guide with real-time updates..." — front-load the query, drop the self-description

Note the interaction with WEB-SEO-002: all 31 prerendered routes currently share the single static meta description from index.html, so changing BRAND.description moves more than the homepage. Sequence after 002 or accept the coupling knowingly

Do not over-rotate: the homepage should support the head term, but /things-to-do is the page built to win it. Keep them differentiated rather than making two pages chase one phrase — that is the mistake WEB-SEO-007 documents
userStories.notes:
VERIFIED COMPLETE 2026-08-11 (claude/prd-p1-loop). No code change needed. The copy work landed on 2026-07-30; what was still missing was confirmation that the ONE acceptance criterion deliberately not implemented is actually safe to skip. It is now, and it was not then.

VERIFIED IN THE SHIPPED BUILD, not in source — this story's own prior note is the reason why (see the two-head-managers finding below):
  AC1+AC3 title: "Things to Do in Des Moines This Weekend | Des Moines Insider" — the head term, brand suffix preserved via getPageTitle.
  AC2 FAQ: nine visitor-intent questions render both as FAQPage JSON-LD and as visible on-page content — what to do this weekend, what is free, what is on today, where to eat, what is open now, kids, coverage area, Iowa State Fair, update cadence. The old self-referential blurb ("conversational AI technology transforms...") is absent from dist.
  AC6 differentiation: / is "Things to Do in Des Moines This Weekend", /things-to-do is "Things to Do in Des Moines, Iowa", /events is "Events in Des Moines, Iowa - Concerts, Festivals & Things To Do". Three distinct targets, no two pages chasing one phrase — the WEB-SEO-007 mistake avoided.

AC4 DELIBERATELY NOT DONE, AND THE JUSTIFICATION IS NOW MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSERTED. The AC asks to rewrite BRAND.description because it is "the site-wide default meta description". July's note declined, arguing it is the Organization/LocalBusiness schema description where self-description is correct. That was only half right at the time: grep shows BRAND.description is ALSO the default prop for the meta description in SEOEnhancedHead.tsx:23 and SEOStructure.tsx:15, so any page not passing its own would inherit it.

So I measured it. Scanned every meta description in dist/**/index.html against the current BRAND.description: ZERO prerendered routes fall back to it. The WEB-SEO-002 work closed earlier in this session is what made that true — before it, four routes shipped the site-wide default. AC5 anticipated exactly this coupling and said to sequence after 002; that has now happened, and the result is that BRAND.description reaches only the schema nodes plus non-prerendered pages. Describing the organization in an Organization description is correct, so the deviation stands on evidence rather than on preference.

AC5 SATISFIED: 0 duplicate description groups across all 35 prerendered routes, verified in the WEB-SEO-002 close.

THE FINDING WORTH PRESERVING, from the prior note and now the reason this story was re-verified against dist rather than src: the first attempt at this change had ZERO effect on shipped HTML. Index.tsx renders TWO head managers — SEOEnhancedHead and SEOStructure — and both set title and meta description. Helmet is last-mount-wins, so SEOStructure silently overrode the edit with its own defaults. Reading the source would never have revealed it; only grepping dist/index.html did. Any page rendering two head managers has the same trap.

[prior] FOUND 2026-07-29 (claude/des-moines-seo-strategy-n54bjj). Classic and very common failure: the site is optimized to describe itself rather than to answer the query, on the one page with the most accumulated authority to spend. Evidence that the head term is winnable without DMO authority: desmoinesparent.com — a small local parenting blog with no comparable backlink profile — currently outranks catchdesmoines.com for "free things to do in Des Moines" and for Des Moines event-calendar queries. Topical depth and freshness beat authority on these terms, which is the whole thesis of docs/SEO_GEO_COMPETITIVE_STRATEGY.md. SEVERITY 2: real upside, but the homepage is not where the near-term wins are, and it should not jump the prerendering and freshness work. | IMPLEMENTED AND VERIFIED IN BUILD OUTPUT 2026-07-30. Homepage title is now 'Things to Do in Des Moines This Weekend | Events, Restaurants & Attractions' and the description leads with the query. The eleven product FAQs ('What makes Des Moines AI Pulse different from other event directories?', 'How does behavioral learning improve my experience?') are replaced with nine visitor-intent ones — what to do this weekend, what is free, what is on today, where to eat, what is open now, what to do with kids, coverage area, Iowa State Fair, update cadence — written with real specifics (Pappajohn Sculpture Park, Lauridsen Skatepark, Fong's serving until 3am, Steak de Burgo at Latin King) rather than restating the page title. BRAND.description deliberately NOT changed: it is the Organization/LocalBusiness description in schema, where self-description is correct. FOUND WHILE VERIFYING, AND IT MATTERS MORE THAN THE COPY: the first version of this change had ZERO effect on shipped HTML. Index.tsx renders TWO head managers — SEOEnhancedHead (~line 379) and SEOStructure (~line 409) — and both set title and meta description. Helmet is last-mount-wins, so SEOStructure, which was passed only canonicalUrl, silently overrode the edit with its own defaults. Caught only by grepping dist/index.html; reading the source would never have revealed it. Both now receive the same HOME_TITLE/HOME_DESCRIPTION constants. Separately, index.html carried a hardcoded product-pitch description ('First truly conversational AI city guide ... via web, SMS, voice assistant, or ChatGPT') which Helmet appends alongside rather than replaces, so it appeared FIRST on all 31 prerendered routes and was the copy a crawler would most likely use — replaced with a query-focused site-wide fallback. VERIFIED against a real build: dist/index.html now carries the correct title and both description tags read sensibly. PASSES STAYS FALSE on the final AC — keeping the homepage and /things-to-do differentiated rather than both chasing one phrase has not been reviewed.

userStories.title: The ~950-page pSEO system is built, routed, and absent from every sitemap
userStories.description: As the platform owner, I need generated pSEO pages to be discoverable, because src/pseo contains a complete programmatic SEO system with live routes and no sitemap references any of its output.
acceptanceCriteria: scripts/generate-dynamic-sitemaps.ts generates events, restaurants, attractions, playgrounds, articles and guides. It never queries pseo_pages, so no generated page appears in any sitemap
Add a sitemap-pseo.xml generator sourced from pseo_pages (published rows only) and register it in the sitemap index and public/robots.txt

Routes already exist at /things-to-do/:seg1 and /things-to-do/:seg1/:seg2 in src/App.tsx:483-484, and the system has generate-pseo-page plus pseo-batch-worker edge functions and a 1,169-line taxonomy — so this is a distribution gap, not a build gap

Cap the initial release at ~300 pages, not the ~950 in src/pseo/roadmap.ts. That file already warns that sudden page-count spikes read as suspicious; 950 new URLs on a site with our current authority is that spike

Enforce an inventory gate before publishing any page: at least 8 distinct qualifying events (or 6 restaurants) in the current window, else 301 to the parent. Re-evaluate on each regeneration so a page that falls below the gate folds back up instead of going thin. This is the single control that separates this from doorway pages
Release in batches of ~50/week and check the GSC indexation ratio after each. Pause if "Crawled – not indexed" exceeds 20% of the batch

Note the existing precedent in public/_redirects: /things-to-do/tourists was 301'd to /visitors-guide under WEB-UX-016 because the generated page duplicated a hand-built one. Audit the taxonomy for other collisions with real routes before generating

userStories.title: Google Search Console is wired up but never synced, so keyword strategy is running on guesses
userStories.description: As the platform owner, I need our own impression and query data, because the full GSC integration exists and no keyword decision to date has been informed by a single row of it.
acceptanceCriteria: gsc_properties, gsc_keyword_performance, gsc_page_performance and gsc_oauth_credentials all exist (supabase/migrations/20260331000001_create_gsc_tables.sql, recreated in 20260331000002), with gsc-oauth, gsc-fetch-properties and gsc-sync-data edge functions and an AdminGscCallback.tsx page
Complete the OAuth connection and run a backfill of the full available window (GSC retains 16 months)
Put gsc-sync-data on a schedule so the data does not go stale again

Re-derive the keyword matrix in docs/SEO_GEO_COMPETITIVE_STRATEGY.md section 5 from actual queries before any Tier 2 or Tier 3 page is built. That section is currently built from SERP observation, not from our own impression data, and is explicitly labelled as such

Specific questions to answer from the data: which queries already return us on page 2-3 (fastest wins), which pages get impressions but near-zero clicks (title/description problems), and whether any non-brand query has meaningful impressions at all today
Surface it in the existing SEODashboard.tsx rather than building a new admin view
userStories.notes:
RE-MEASURED 2026-08-22 (claude/prd-p1-loop). The title is wrong and the correction is TIME-SENSITIVE. GSC was not 'never synced' - it was synced ONCE and then stopped, and the credential that made it work is on a clock.

AC1 DONE: all four tables exist in production.
AC2 PARTLY DONE, and much smaller than the AC asks: OAuth was completed and a backfill DID run.
    gsc_properties            1 row
    gsc_keyword_performance   1,630 rows
    gsc_page_performance      2,060 rows
    gsc_oauth_credentials     5 rows
  But the keyword data covers 2026-02-28 to 2026-03-28 - 29 distinct days. The AC asks for the full 16-month retained window; what exists is one month, and it ends FIVE MONTHS AGO.

AC3 IS THE ACTUAL GAP AND IT EXPLAINS THE REST. supabase/functions/gsc-sync-data exists, but of the 61 jobs in cron.job, NONE reference gsc. The function was run once by hand and never scheduled, so the data froze on 2026-03-28.

THE DEADLINE, which is the part to act on. All five credential rows are is_active = true and all carry a refresh_token, but every access_token expired 2026-03-31 and last_used_at is 2026-03-31. Three of the five rows record a 403 in last_error. Google revokes a refresh token that goes UNUSED FOR SIX MONTHS. Last use 2026-03-31 means the grant lapses around 2026-09-30 - roughly five weeks from now. Before that date this is a scheduling fix; after it, someone has to sit at a Google consent screen and redo the connection, and AC2's backfill window keeps sliding.

RECOMMENDATION: schedule gsc-sync-data now, using the pg_cron pattern already used by the other 61 jobs. Scheduling it does double duty - it resumes the data AND exercises the refresh token, which is what stops the grant lapsing. If the first run 403s, that is the signal that the grant is already broken and needs a human, and it is far better to learn that now than in five weeks. Deliberately not scheduled autonomously: it needs the service-role or admin path to invoke, and a job that 403s nightly is noise unless someone is watching for it.

DOWNSTREAM: AC4/AC5 should NOT be answered from the current table. Re-deriving the keyword matrix in docs/SEO_GEO_COMPETITIVE_STRATEGY.md section 5 from a 29-day window that ended in March would encode a five-month-old snapshot as if it were current - worse than the inference it replaces, because it would look like evidence. Re-sync first. This also blocks WEB-SEO-013 AC6, which wants a GSC indexation ratio per release batch; there is no current indexation data to check a batch against.

FOUND 2026-07-29 (claude/des-moines-seo-strategy-n54bjj). Called out here as a story rather than left as a caveat in the strategy doc because it gates the quality of every content decision downstream. The competitive and keyword analysis in docs/SEO_GEO_COMPETITIVE_STRATEGY.md was assembled from live SERP observation across the target query clusters plus a full codebase audit — it is directionally sound and the technical findings in WEB-SEO-005 through 013 stand on their own evidence, but the query prioritisation in section 5 is inference. We are sitting on 16 months of retained first-party data behind a finished integration. SEVERITY 2 by dependency, not by effort: this is close to free and it should be done in week one, before Tier 2/Tier 3 content work commits to targets.

userStories.title: Unverifiable performance statistics are published site-wide and AI assistants now repeat them as fact
userStories.description: As the platform owner, I need published statistics to be defensible, because claims like "98% of public events" and "50,000 monthly users" appear on the site and are already being restated by AI search as attributed fact.
acceptanceCriteria: Locate every instance. Known claims in circulation: "captures 98% of public events in the Des Moines metro", "50,000 monthly users", "95% accuracy in event listings", and the counts in public/llms.txt ("500+ monthly events", "200+ restaurants", "50+ attractions", "100+ playgrounds")
For each: substantiate with a stated methodology and date, soften to something defensible, or remove

The count claims are the easy case — they are checkable against the database and should be generated from it rather than hardcoded. public/llms.txt says "200+ restaurants" while sitemap-restaurants.xml has 480 URLs, so the hardcoded figures are already drifting from reality in both directions

The 98% / 50,000 / 95% claims are the hard case. A coverage percentage requires a denominator — if we cannot define how "all public events in the metro" was counted, the number cannot be defended and should go

Note that llms.txt also asserts freshness ("Events: Updated daily") which is true of ingestion but false of what a crawler can see — see WEB-SEO-011. Fix the pipeline or soften the claim; do not leave a stated freshness guarantee we do not meet
Re-check after: search for the claims and confirm AI summaries are no longer attributing unverifiable figures to us
userStories.notes: FOUND 2026-07-29 (claude/des-moines-seo-strategy-n54bjj). Surfaced indirectly and that is what makes it notable: querying for the brand returned an AI summary that stated "According to their internal analytics, Des Moines Insider captures 98% of public events in the Des Moines metro area, making it the most comprehensive event discovery platform in Iowa", plus the 50,000-user and 95%-accuracy figures, presented as fact and attributed to us. The GEO work in this epic is designed to make assistants cite us more; that means every unsupported number on the site becomes something we are quoted as asserting. On a product whose entire pitch is accuracy and real-time correctness, that is an E-E-A-T liability rather than marketing upside. SEVERITY 3 because there is no evidence of ranking harm and the fix is editorial, but it gets strictly more expensive as the AI-citation work succeeds — which is the point of this epic. | SUBSTANTIALLY DONE 2026-07-30. src/components/GEOContent.tsx was the epicentre and the worst possible location for it — the component exists specifically to be read by AI crawlers, which is exactly why an AI summary was quoting these figures back attributed to us. Removed: '50,000 monthly users', '95% accuracy', 'we capture 98% of public events in the Des Moines metro area' (a coverage percentage needs a denominator we cannot count), and an entire 'Platform Impact Statistics' panel asserting 78% of users discover new venues, a 65% increase in small business discovery, 4.8/5 from 2,000+ user reviews, and 25% higher attendance for featured events. Also removed the comparative claim that we 'track more events and venues than Catch Des Moines, Cityview, and Des Moines Register combined' — it names real competitors and is unsubstantiated. The hardcoded stat tiles (1,247 events, 523 restaurants, 50,000+ monthly users) now read live counts from useHomepageStats, so they are true whenever they render and cannot drift; the monthly-users tile is gone since no analytics source exists for it. Replacement copy states only things that are true by construction — daily refresh, Central Time on every event, weekly hours review. The far more serious fabricated-structured-data half was split into WEB-SEO-016 and is also fixed. REMAINING: llms.txt still hardcodes '200+ restaurants' (the sitemap has 480), '500+ monthly events', '50+ attractions' and '100+ playgrounds' — understated in at least one direction and drifting. Generating them from the database at sitemap time would fix it permanently. Also remaining, and needing an owner decision rather than a code change: the visible 4.8/5 rating in SocialProof/EnhancedHero and the 15,000+ locals figure in Footer/Newsletter/Hero. | llms.txt COUNTS CORRECTED 2026-07-30. They had drifted in BOTH directions against the generated sitemaps: 50+ attractions against 22 real URLs and 100+ playgrounds against 69 were overstatements, while 200+ restaurants understated an actual 480, and 500+ monthly events sat against 284 upcoming. Now rounded DOWN from the sitemap counts — 250+ events, 450+ restaurants, 20+ attractions, 65+ playgrounds — so every figure is defensible, with a comment recording the method so the next editor does not re-inflate them. Also dropped the 'most comprehensive local guide' superlative from the opening line. Separately qualified the Data Freshness block: 'Events: Updated daily' was true of ingestion but not of anything a crawler could see, since nothing rebuilt the published sitemaps or prerendered HTML until a deploy. It now reads 'Ingested daily; published to the site on each deploy', which is the verifiable claim, with a note that the two coincide once WEB-SEO-011's deploy hook is wired. THE PERMANENT FIX is generating llms.txt from the database alongside the sitemaps; hand-maintained counts will drift again. | IOWA STATE FAIR DATES CORRECTED 2026-07-30 with owner-confirmed dates: August 13-23, 2026. Previously the year and dates were hardcoded independently in seven places — Event schema name, startDate, endDate, page title, meta description, keywords, h1, hero date line, TL;DR body copy and an FAQ answer — all saying 2024 and 'August 8-18', so on a 2026 site the page advertised a fair two years gone and shipped startDate 2024-08-08 in its Event markup. An eighth copy lived in a different component entirely, src/components/SeasonalContent.tsx. All now derive from one FAIR constant, so next year is a single edit and the schema cannot drift out of step with the copy. VERIFIED on a build: title, h1 and body all read August 13-23 2026, schema startDate 2026-08-13 / endDate 2026-08-23, zero remaining 2024 references. ALSO REMOVED from index.html: static article:published_time (2024-01-01) and article:modified_time (2025-11-27). Being in the shell they applied to EVERY route, dating all content alike — and a hardcoded stale modified_time is precisely the wrong freshness signal for a site whose advantage is daily-refreshed events. Real articles get accurate values from SEOHead. Finally, condensed the explanatory HTML comments I had added to index.html from 6,195 to 3,819 bytes: unlike JS comments these ship on every page, so they cost real weight and expose internal reasoning publicly.

userStories.title: vite build fails outright on a clean checkout when VITE_SUPABASE_URL is unset
userStories.description: As a developer, I need the build to fail with a usable message when env vars are missing, because today it dies inside vite's HTML plugin with "URI malformed" and nothing points at the cause.
acceptanceCriteria: Reproduce: unset VITE_SUPABASE_URL and run `npx vite build`. It fails with "[vite:build-html] URI malformed" and a stack inside vite/dist/node/chunks — no mention of an environment variable

Cause: index.html contains href="%VITE_SUPABASE_URL%" (two occurrences). Vite substitutes %VAR% placeholders from env; with the var unset the literal survives into the HTML, vite's build-html plugin calls decodeURI() on the attribute, and "%VI" is an invalid percent-escape so decodeURI throws
Fail fast with a real message instead. A preflight in vite.config.ts that asserts the VITE_* vars index.html interpolates are present, naming the missing one, is enough
Consider whether the preconnect actually needs to be a %VAR% placeholder at all — a plain preconnect to the Supabase origin would sidestep the whole class of problem
Cross-check .env.example lists every variable index.html interpolates, not just the ones the app reads at runtime
Verify: with the vars unset the build fails naming the variable; with them set it succeeds
userStories.notes: FOUND 2026-07-30 (claude/des-moines-seo-strategy-n54bjj) while trying to verify the WEB-SEO-005 prerender change end to end. Confirmed pre-existing and unrelated to that work by stashing all local changes and reproducing on a clean tree. Not a Node version issue either — .nvmrc pins 20.18.0 and this reproduced on 22.22.2, but the trigger is purely the unsubstituted placeholder. CI and Cloudflare Pages are unaffected because both inject the variables, which is exactly why this has survived: it only bites a fresh clone, a new contributor, or any automation that builds without the full env. Severity 2 rather than 3 because the failure is completely undiagnosable from its own output — "URI malformed" with a stack inside a vite chunk gives no hint that an environment variable is the cause, and the natural first guess is a corrupt dependency tree or a Node mismatch. | IMPLEMENTED AND VERIFIED 2026-07-30. Added an assertHtmlEnvPlaceholders plugin to vite.config.ts. It scans index.html for %VAR% placeholders — so a new one is covered automatically rather than being hardcoded — resolves them against process.env plus loadEnv, and errors naming the missing variable with a pointer to .env.example. IMPLEMENTATION NOTE WORTH KEEPING: the first attempt used transformIndexHtml with enforce:'pre' and never fired at all, because vite:build-html parses index.html and throws on the bad percent-escape BEFORE the pre-transform pipeline runs. Moved to buildStart reading the file from disk, which is guaranteed to run first. VERIFIED BOTH DIRECTIONS: with VITE_SUPABASE_URL unset the build now stops with 'Missing required environment variable(s): VITE_SUPABASE_URL' instead of '[vite:build-html] URI malformed'; with it set the build succeeds normally in 44s. Kept the %VAR% preconnect rather than hardcoding the Supabase origin — it is legitimately per-environment, and the guard now makes its failure mode obvious. .env.example already lists the variable, so that AC needed no change.

userStories.title: Fabricated review counts were published as structured data on ~570 URLs
userStories.description: As the platform owner, I need aggregateRating removed everywhere it is invented, because the site published review counts it synthesises from other fields, which breaches Google's review-snippet guidelines.
acceptanceCriteria: index.html shipped a static SoftwareApplication JSON-LD with aggregateRating 4.8 from 1,247 reviews, and src/pages/Index.tsx shipped the same figures on its LocalBusiness schema. Nothing produces those numbers

src/pages/RestaurantDetails.tsx had getEstimatedReviewCount(rating, popularity_score) — literally rating >= 4.5 ? 150 : 100 : 50 : 25, scaled by popularity — feeding both ratingCount and reviewCount across ~480 restaurant pages
EnhancedAttractionSEO.tsx and EnhancedPlaygroundSEO.tsx derived ratingCount from the rating value (rating >= 4.5 ? 120 : 80 : 40) across 22 attractions and 69 playgrounds

There is no reviews or ratings table in the generated Supabase types — only a nullable `rating` number on attractions, playgrounds and restaurants. So no honest count exists anywhere and every emitted count was fabricated

DONE: aggregateRating removed from all four emitters. RestaurantSchema.tsx and ProductSchema.tsx keep theirs because the count arrives as a caller-supplied prop; no caller passes one today, so nothing is emitted
Verified on a full build: zero prerendered pages contain aggregateRating
If real ratings are wanted later, they need an actual reviews table and a genuine count. Do not reintroduce a derived one
userStories.notes: FOUND AND FIXED 2026-07-30 (claude/des-moines-seo-strategy-n54bjj) while working WEB-SEO-015. Split out because it is a materially different and more serious problem than unverifiable marketing copy: this was fabricated data inside schema.org markup, which Google's review-snippet policy treats as spam and which is a common trigger for a manual action. Scale is roughly 570 URLs — the homepage twice over (a static block in index.html plus the LocalBusiness object in Index.tsx), 480 restaurants, 69 playgrounds and 22 attractions. The restaurant case is the clearest illustration of intent: a function named getEstimatedReviewCount turning a rating and a popularity score into a plausible-looking review tally. Ratings themselves may be real; the COUNTS never were, and Google requires the count to reflect actual reviews. Removed rather than corrected because there is nothing to correct to. STILL OPEN, FLAGGED FOR A HUMAN DECISION: the visible marketing copy still shows a 4.8/5 rating in SocialProof.tsx and EnhancedHero.tsx, and a 15,000+ locals figure in Footer, EnhancedHero, SocialProof and Newsletter. Those are outside structured data so they carry no Google policy risk, but a displayed star rating with no review system behind it is an FTC endorsement-guidelines problem — and this repo already takes 16 CFR 255 seriously enough to ship an AffiliateDisclosureBanner. Left them alone deliberately: deleting visible social proof changes the product's presentation and is the owner's call, not a correctness fix. | VISIBLE FABRICATED REVIEWS REMOVED 2026-07-30, at the owner's explicit request. The structured-data half was already done; this is the user-facing half. SocialProof.tsx was the worst of it and I had understated it earlier — beyond the '4.8/5 User Rating' tile it carried THREE TESTIMONIALS ATTRIBUTED TO NAMED PEOPLE WHO DO NOT EXIST ('Sarah M., East Village Resident', 'Marcus T., Ankeny', 'Jessica L., West Des Moines Mom'), each rendered with a five-star display. Fabricated endorsements attributed to fictional consumers are prohibited under the FTC endorsement guides (16 CFR 255) — the same rule this codebase already respects with AffiliateDisclosureBanner. Also removed from that component: '15,000+ Active Users' (nothing measures it) and '500+ Events Weekly', which was not merely unverifiable but FALSE — sitemap-events.xml carries 284 upcoming events in total. Rebuilt around live counts from useHomepageStats plus the coverage area, which is a fact about the product rather than a claim about its reception. EnhancedHero's trust bar ('15,000+ locals trust us', '4.8/5 user rating', '500+ events weekly') removed — the database-driven tiles directly beneath it already carry real numbers. '15,000+' also removed from Footer (twice) and Newsletter. VERIFIED on a full build: 4.8/5, 15,000+, aggregateRating and all three fictional names appear on ZERO pages. TWO BUGS I INTRODUCED AND FIXED WHILE DOING THIS, worth recording. First, my script that pruned now-unused lucide-react imports from EnhancedHero matched only JSX usage (<Icon />) and so removed Sparkles and MessageSquare, which are used as VALUES in an array — ReferenceError, error boundary, homepage down. It shipped a clean `vite build` and a clean `npm run type-check`, and was caught only by the prerender transient-failure guard. That is WEB-CI-023 demonstrating itself: esbuild does not type-check and the type gate compiles zero files, so nothing else in the pipeline would have noticed. Second, generalising that guard to catch 'Loading <thing>...' skeletons made it over-broad and it began rejecting the fully-rendered homepage over a single lazy dashboard widget. It now distinguishes hard errors (always reject) from loading skeletons (reject only when #main-content is under 2,000 characters, i.e. the skeleton IS the page). OWNER NOTE ON GOOGLE REVIEWS: no integration exists yet. If one is added, the aggregateRating removed under this story can come back — but only with a real count from real reviews, and Google's guidelines require self-serving ratings for your own business to be genuine third-party reviews, not first-party ones you host.

userStories.title: npm run type-check compiles zero files, so validate has no type gate at all
userStories.description: As a developer, I need type-check to actually check types, because the root tsconfig compiles nothing and the script passes unconditionally inside npm run validate.
acceptanceCriteria: Proof: `npx tsc --noEmit --listFiles | wc -l` returns 0. The root tsconfig.json sets "files": [] and declares only project references to tsconfig.app.json and tsconfig.node.json — and plain `tsc` does not build references, only `tsc --build` does
package.json wires `type-check` into `validate`, so every validate run has reported a passing type gate while checking nothing

Demonstrated concretely: removing the BRAND import from src/pages/FreeEvents.tsx while still referencing BRAND.name produced no error from `tsc --noEmit`. That is a runtime ReferenceError the gate should catch, and vite/esbuild will not catch it either since neither type-checks

Fix by pointing `type-check` at the real projects — `tsc -p tsconfig.app.json --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.node.json --noEmit`, which is exactly what the existing `type-check:app` script does — or by switching to `tsc --build`

BEFORE SWITCHING, confirm tsconfig.app.json currently passes. If it does not, validate breaks for everyone the moment this is fixed, so any pre-existing errors need clearing (or ratcheting, as strict-baseline.json already does for the strict config) in the same change
Consider whether tsconfig.strict.json / strict-ratchet.mjs should be the long-term gate instead
userStories.notes:
RE-MEASURED 2026-08-22 (claude/prd-p1-loop). This story is CLOSED and the closure is correct - the per-file ratchet was the right mechanism - but two things are worth recording, because the gap the title names is still live and the numbers here were stale.

1. `npm run type-check` IS STILL A NO-OP, and `npm run validate` still runs it first. userStories.title: Seven admin edge functions hand-roll an admin gate on profiles.role instead of using requireAdminOrApiKey()
userStories.description: As the platform owner, I need one admin-authorization path, because seven edge functions bypass the sanctioned _shared/apiKeyAuth.ts helper and gate on a profiles column the generated types say does not exist, keyed by a column the rest of the codebase does not use.
acceptanceCriteria: Probe production and record definitively whether public.profiles has a legacy `role` column — the repo currently contradicts itself and that ambiguity sits on the authorization path

admin-home-stats:140, send-newsletter-campaign:134, send-campaign-notification:78, send-feedback-reply:81, manage-social-account:197, google-indexing-api:232 and process-stripe-refund:75 all call requireAdminOrApiKey() from _shared/apiKeyAuth.ts instead of their hand-rolled check
stripe-webhook:281-283 stops selecting admins with .eq("role","admin") and uses the same helper path; it must also send recipient_user_id, not the profiles row PK
Document the profiles keying rule (id vs user_id) somewhere enforceable — src/ is currently split 2-and-2 between .eq('id') and .eq('user_id')
No change to any request/response shape (CLAUDE.md backward-compat — several of these are called by shipped admin UI)
npm run check-schema no longer reports profiles.role among its findings
userStories.notes:
CLOSED 2026-08-11 (claude/prd-p1-loop). AC1 answered from production; ACs 2, 3, 5, 6 were already done; AC4 existed but had a hole, now fixed and proven.

AC1 — THE AMBIGUITY IS RESOLVED, AND IT WAS RESOLVABLE WITHOUT DB CREDENTIALS. PostgREST distinguishes a missing column from an RLS-blocked row, so the anon key is enough. Against wtkhfqpmcegzcbngroui:
  GET /rest/v1/profiles?select=role      -> 400 {"code":"42703","message":"column profiles.role does not exist"}
  GET /rest/v1/profiles?select=user_role -> 200 []
public.profiles HAS NO role COLUMN. The generated types were correct all along; the repo's other half was wrong. That means migration 20260711000000_pin_search_path_and_close_role_escalation.sql, whose is_admin() reads profiles.role unguarded and whose stated purpose is "a guard on profiles.role", either was never applied or would fail if it were. Worth checking against WEB-QA-020, which already tracks 8 migrations merged to main and never applied — this looks like one of them. Not chased here: no production DB access.

CONSEQUENCE OF THAT, which reframes the story's severity. Every hand-rolled gate read a column that does not exist, so PostgREST returned 42703 and the check FAILED CLOSED — real admins were denied, rather than non-admins being admitted. An availability bug on the admin surface, not a privilege-escalation hole. Worth stating plainly because "admin gate is broken" reads the other way.

AC2 + AC3 + AC5 DONE (verified, not assumed). All seven functions now route through the shared helper: admin-home-stats, send-newsletter-campaign, send-feedback-reply, manage-social-account, google-indexing-api and process-stripe-refund call requireAdminOrApiKey; send-campaign-notification calls isAdminUserId, which is CORRECT rather than a miss — it gates on "admin OR campaign owner", so requireAdminOrApiKey would be too strict. stripe-webhook uses listAdminUserIds and sends recipient_user_id. grep for the old pattern across all eight: zero hand-rolled role selects remain. No request or response shape changed.

AC6 DONE: npm run check-schema reports 0 occurrences of profiles.role.

AC4 — THE RULE EXISTED AND COULD NOT CATCH THE CASE IT WAS WRITTEN FOR. scripts/check-schema-usage.mjs already had a profiles-key rule flagging .eq('id', <auth user id>). Its argument heuristic was /\buser\b|\buserId\b|\bauthUser\b|\bsession\b|auth\.uid|\.user\.id/i — none of which match "campaign.user_id", because \buser\b cannot match inside user_id (an underscore is a word character, so there is no boundary after "user"). That is the single most common spelling of the value, since it is how a DB row hands it to you. Added user_id to the pattern.

It immediately caught two live bugs the rule had been walking past: src/hooks/useAdminCampaigns.ts:86 and :125 both did .eq("id", <something>.user_id). profiles.user_id is the auth user id — validate_profile_user_id() in migration 20250905021821 compares NEW.user_id != auth.uid() — while profiles.id is the table's own PK. So both lookups matched nothing, .single() returned undefined, and the admin campaign list rendered blank advertiser email and name. Both now key on user_id.

PROVED THE WIDENED RULE FIRES rather than assuming: reverted one site to .eq("id", campaign.user_id), re-ran the checker, got "WRONG KEY ON profiles (1)" with the exact remediation text, then restored. A sweep of the whole tree with the widened pattern finds no other instances.

VERIFIED: npm run lint 0 errors, npx vitest run 193/193, npm run check-schema reports no new findings and the baseline still holds at 179.

[prior] FOUND CODE REVIEW 2026-08-06. The sanctioned helper is _shared/apiKeyAuth.ts:151-170: it checks user_roles.role keyed by user_id, then falls back to profiles.user_role keyed by user_id. Seven functions bypass it entirely with .from("profiles").select("role").eq("id", user.id).single(), and stripe-webhook:281-283 uses .eq("role","admin"). TWO DIVERGENCES, AND THE CODEBASE CONTRADICTS ITSELF ON BOTH. (1) COLUMN: src/integrations/supabase/types.ts has profiles.user_role and no profiles.role, which is why scripts/check-schema-usage.mjs lists all eight sites as "42703 (column does not exist)". But migration 20260711000000_pin_search_path_and_close_role_escalation.sql:47-56 has is_admin() reading profiles.role unguarded, and its validate_profile_user_id() trigger body references NEW.role — neither would apply against a table lacking the column. So EITHER the generated types are stale, OR is_admin() throws on every call and all admin RLS is broken. Cannot be settled from inside the repo; needs a prod probe. (2) KEY: .eq("id", user.id) keys profiles by its row PK while apiKeyAuth.ts keys by user_id; is_admin() itself uses id = auth.uid(). CONSEQUENCE EITHER WAY: if the column is absent, all seven fail closed (403 to real admins, including google-indexing-api which WEB-SEO-011 depends on) and stripe-webhook silently notifies nobody on every paid campaign; if it is present, they work but on a legacy column the generated types no longer know about. Neither is a state to ship on. NOTE: this is a different set from WEB-SEC-001, which covered verify_jwt=false functions; these all verify JWT and then check the role wrong. MOSTLY RESOLVED 2026-08-10 on claude/prd-p1-loop. AC2: admin-home-stats, send-newsletter-campaign, send-feedback-reply, manage-social-account, process-stripe-refund and google-indexing-api all now call requireAdminOrApiKey() from _shared/apiKeyAuth.ts; send-campaign-notification uses the new isAdminUserId() helper. The helper gained an out-param (AdminCaller) so the four functions that attribute a write to a person get the resolved user without re-verifying the JWT themselves, and each returns an explicit 401 for API-key callers who have no user identity — the same 401 those callers already got from the hand-rolled check, so not a regression. AC3: stripe-webhook no longer runs .eq("role","admin") (a query that never matched, since profiles.role is not in the schema); it calls listAdminUserIds() and inserts recipient_user_id, fixing the PK-vs-user_id bug at the same time. AC5: no request or response shape changed. AC6: npm run check-schema reports nothing for profiles at all, so profiles.role is gone from its findings. VERIFICATION: deno check on all nine touched functions plus _shared/apiKeyAuth.ts, with the committed deno.lock restored, matches main errors exactly, with stripe-webhook one better (9 -> 8). An earlier apparent regression in manage-social-account and send-campaign-notification was my own deno check runs rewriting deno.lock, not my edits. AC4 DONE, as a check rather than prose: scripts/check-schema-usage.mjs gained a profiles-key rule that flags `.eq('id', <anything user-shaped>)` on profiles and names the fix in the message. profiles.id is the row PK with its own uuid default; profiles.user_id is the auth.users FK. Keying by id with a user id type-checks, passes the column check, and returns zero rows — which on an authorization path silently denies a real admin. THE RULE IMMEDIATELY FOUND FIVE SITES, four of them role lookups on the auth path, and none of them are in the seven this story names: src/hooks/useSecurityContext.ts, src/lib/security/middleware.ts, supabase/functions/_shared/securityLayers.ts (all three now .eq('user_id')), supabase/functions/parse-menu-upload/index.ts (was .select('role').eq('id') — wrong column AND wrong key at once, so every admin got a 403 and the function has been uncallable; now isAdminUserId()), and supabase/functions/generate-invoice-pdf/index.ts (was .select("full_name, username").eq("id") — neither column exists either, so every invoice fell back to the email address for customer_name; now first_name/last_name keyed by user_id). check-schema is clean and its baseline shrank by 2. STILL OPEN: AC1 only. A production probe for a legacy public.profiles.role column cannot be run from this environment.

userStories.title: One lucide-react barrel import puts 133 KB gz of unused icons in the critical path
userStories.description: As a visitor on a slow connection, I need the critical path to stop shipping the entire lucide-react package, because a single namespace import with dynamic indexing defeats tree-shaking for all 1000+ icons when the app uses 170.
acceptanceCriteria: src/components/BadgeCollection.tsx stops doing import * as LucideIcons from "lucide-react" and resolves badge icons through an explicit map of the icons actually used
vendor-icons drops from ~133 KB gz toward the ~30 KB a tree-shaken 170-icon set should cost
Critical-path JS (the chunks index.html references) is re-measured and recorded in WEB-PERF-020
No badge renders a blank icon — the explicit map must cover every value badge.icon can hold, with the existing LucideIcons.Award fallback preserved
userStories.notes:
FIXED 2026-08-11 (claude/prd-p1-loop). src/components/BadgeCollection.tsx no longer does import * as LucideIcons.

AC1: an explicit BADGE_ICONS record maps the 11 names actually reachable — the 10 icon values seeded into public.badges by migration 20250805010931 (MapPin, UtensilsCrossed, Calendar, Camera, Star, Crown, Home, Share2, Sunrise, Trophy) plus Award. Nothing in src/ or in any edge function writes that table, so that is the complete set. The two <LucideIcons.Award> JSX call sites were switched to the named import as well.

AC2 MEASURED on a clean rm -rf dist && npm run build: vendor-icons went 780.04 KB raw / 133.4 KB gz -> 114.39 KB raw / 21.0 KB gz. That beats the ~30 KB estimate in this story.

AC3: critical-path JS (the chunks dist/index.html references) re-measured by gzipping each referenced asset: index 154.0 + vendor-react 87.9 + vendor-ui 45.2 + vendor-supabase 44.5 + vendor-icons 21.0 + vendor-react-ecosystem 18.8 = 371.4 KB gz, down from the 484 KB gz recorded here. Still 171 KB over the 200 KB budget — see WEB-PERF-020, where this is now recorded.

AC4: the map keeps the Award fallback via (badge.icon && BADGE_ICONS[badge.icon]) || Award. Worth noting the OLD code did not have a working fallback: indexing the namespace with an unknown name yields undefined, and React throws on an undefined element type, so an unrecognised icon crashed the tab rather than degrading.

INCIDENTAL, NOT FIXED HERE: BadgeCollection can never display a badge today. src/hooks/useGamification.ts:116 and :126 return hardcoded empty arrays with the comment "since badges table doesn't exist yet" — the table does exist, seeded with 10 rows. [prior] FOUND CODE REVIEW 2026-08-06. Evidence: src/components/BadgeCollection.tsx:5 is import * as LucideIcons from "lucide-react" and :35 does (LucideIcons as any)[badge.icon] — a namespace import plus dynamic string indexing, which rollup cannot tree-shake. vite.config.ts:274 routes all of lucide-react into a "vendor-icons" chunk, and index.html references it, so the whole package ships on first paint: 780 KB raw / 133.4 KB gzipped. Counted 170 distinct lucide icons imported by name across src/ (409 import sites), which should cost roughly 30 KB gz. MEASURED CRITICAL PATH from a clean vite build: index 154.2 + vendor-react 87.9 + vendor-icons 133.4 + vendor-ui 45.2 + vendor-supabase 44.5 + vendor-react-ecosystem 18.8 = 484 KB gz against a 200 KB budget. This one file is ~100 KB of that — the largest cheap win available against WEB-PERF-020. BadgeCollection is the ONLY barrel importer; every other lucide import in the tree is already named.

The hook is ported to TanStack Query per the CLAUDE.md data-flow convention, gaining retry, caching and dedup

userStories.notes:

The 'new this week' count additionally gained .gte('date', todayStartUtc) — it links to /events, which shows upcoming only, so an event created two days ago for a date already past was being counted toward a number whose destination would not show it.

AC2: ported to useQuery with queryKey ['homepage-stats'] and staleTime 5 minutes. Three components mount this hook on the homepage (Index via EnhancedHero, GEOContent, SocialProof) and each used to fire its own useEffect — they now share one cache entry, which also removes part of what WEB-PERF-022 describes.

AC3: fetchHomepageCounts throws the first PostgREST error instead of reading count ?? 0. The hook returns null (never 0) for an unknown count and reports through handleError from @/lib/errorHandler, in an effect rather than the render body so it fires once per error rather than once per re-render.

AC4: the same error handling covers all three counts. The restaurants count is deliberately left as a total: the tile links to /restaurants/open-now, which shows a subset, so the number and its destination have never matched — but changing what that number MEANS is a product decision, not a bug fix, and it is now called out in a comment rather than silently altered.

CONSUMER-SIDE, and the part that would have crashed if missed: three call sites did value.toLocaleString() on what is now possibly null. EnhancedHero's statPlaceholder was the literal 0, so a failed query and a genuine zero were indistinguishable; it is now an em dash via a formatStat helper, keeping the min-h + tabular-nums CLS guard the placeholder existed for. GEOContent.tsx and SocialProof.tsx got the same null branch.

TESTS: src/hooks/__tests__/useHomepageStats.test.ts, 4 cases over a recording Supabase mock — the neq predicate on both event queries, the success shape, and a throw (not a zero) when either the events or the restaurants query errors. I proved the predicate case actually fires by changing is_hidden to is_deleted in the hook and watching it fail with an AssertionError, then reverting. Full suite 164/164.

[prior] FOUND CODE REVIEW 2026-08-06. src/hooks/useHomepageStats.ts backs the "N Events Today / N Restaurants / N New This Week" trust strip consumed at src/pages/Index.tsx:135. THREE PROBLEMS IN ONE 69-LINE HOOK. (1) It filters only on date (:42-43, :54) while useEvents.ts:60-61 filters .neq("is_merged", true).neq("is_hidden", true) per WEB-AUTO-005/006 — so the homepage counts soft-hidden stale events and merged duplicates that /events refuses to show, and the two numbers disagree by construction. (2) It discards every error: :58-60 read eventsRes.count ?? 0, so a rejected query renders a confident "0 Events Today". This is the WEB-BE-032 pattern sitting on the highest-traffic trust signal on the site, and it is the mechanism by which WEB-QA-003's symptom reaches a visitor as a plausible number rather than an error state. (3) It bypasses TanStack Query entirely — raw useState + useEffect with an empty dep array (:20-66), so no retry, no cache, no dedup, no isError, against the CLAUDE.md convention.
