userStories.notes:
APPLIED 2026-08-22 with the owner's approval. protect-main is now a real ruleset on GitHub - id 21199295, target=branch, enforcement=active. Verified as ENFORCING, not merely existing, which is the distinction this whole cluster kept getting wrong:
  GET repos/.../branches/main            -> protected=true  (was false)
  GET repos/.../rules/branches/main      -> deletion, non_fast_forward, pull_request, required_status_checks
  required contexts GitHub now enforces  -> 'Lint, Type Check, Test & Build', 'Secret Scanning (gitleaks)', 'Smoke (critical journeys, required)'

All three were made green earlier this session, so enforcement was switched on without freezing the repo. develop.json, release.json and hotfix.json remain UNAPPLIED by choice - develop is 639 commits behind main and release/hotfix are unused, so gating them would protect branches nobody is working on.

ONE BEHAVIOURAL CHANGE THE OWNER SHOULD KNOW: the pull_request rule sets required_approving_review_count=1 and GitHub does not let anyone approve their own PR. For a solo maintainer that would block every PR, except that main.json carries bypass_actors [{actor_type: RepositoryRole, actor_id: 5 (admin), bypass_mode: always}], so the repo admin can still merge unapproved. Everyone and everything else is gated. If that bypass is ever narrowed, the review requirement becomes a hard block for a solo maintainer.

ROOT FINDING 2026-08-22 (claude/prd-p1-loop) - NO BRANCH PROTECTION EXISTS ON THIS REPO AT ALL. This reframes every CI story, including this one.

Measured four ways against dj-pearson/desmoines-ai-pulse:
  GET repos/.../rulesets                     -> []  (no repo rulesets)
  GET repos/.../rulesets?includes_parents=true -> 0 (no org rulesets either)
  GET repos/.../branches/main/protection     -> 404 'Branch not protected'
  GET repos/.../branches/{main,develop,release/android-v1.0.1} -> protected=false on all three

.github/rulesets/ holds main.json, develop.json, release.json and hotfix.json, and main.json declares "enforcement": "active" with deletion, non_fast_forward, pull_request and required_status_checks rules. Those files are CHECKED-IN COPIES THAT WERE NEVER APPLIED. A ruleset only exists once it is POSTed to the rulesets API or created in Settings; a JSON file in the repo enforces nothing.

CONSEQUENCES, and they are the explanation this cluster has been missing:
  - WEB-CI-025 and WEB-CI-026 both reasoned that merges proceeded past red required checks because of 'the same bypass path'. There is no bypass path. There is no gate. Nothing has ever been required.
  - WEB-CI-026's line 'the word required in the job name is currently decorative' is literally true, and true of EVERY check, not just the smoke lane.
  - Turning the three required contexts green (done this session) gates NOTHING until a ruleset is actually applied. The work was still worth doing - a gate that is green is a precondition for turning enforcement on without freezing the repo - but green is not a gate.
  - CLAUDE.md's Critical Rules state that rulesets will block force-pushing to main, deleting main, and committing directly to main or develop. None of that is enforced today.
  - WEB-CI-025 AC3 asks whether the job name matches the required context string in .github/rulesets/main.json. It does, verified - but it is matching a file GitHub has never read.

NEEDS THE OWNER: applying a ruleset is a repository settings change that starts blocking merges for everyone. Deliberately NOT done autonomously. The natural sequence is to apply protect-main first, now that its three required contexts are green on PR #367, then develop, then release/hotfix.

ALL THREE REQUIRED CONTEXTS GREEN 2026-08-22 on PR #367 - 'Lint, Type Check, Test & Build' PASS, 'Secret Scanning (gitleaks)' PASS, 'Smoke (critical journeys, required)' PASS. First time all three have passed together on a PR since February.

AC4 took THREE attempts and the failures are the useful part:
1. (4192d32e, reverted) Added @vitest/coverage-v8@^4.1.11. It pulled esbuild 0.28.2 over the locked 0.25.12, the lockfile stopped satisfying npm ci, and SIX checks went red at install - including Smoke, which had just gone green. One cause, six symptoms.
2. (8451fca3, reverted) Same fix pinned exactly to 4.1.10 to match the locked vitest. Identical failure, same 'Missing: esbuild@0.28.2 from lock file'.
3. (6c0190e0) Dropped the --coverage flag instead.

WHY 1 AND 2 BOTH FAILED - a real latent defect, worth its own story: package-lock.json carries an invalid dedupe. `npm ls esbuild` reports
    esbuild@0.25.12 deduped invalid: "^0.27.0 || ^0.28.0" from node_modules/vitest/node_modules/vite
Nothing exercises that path while the coverage provider is absent. Add ANY dependency and npm resolves it honestly, pulls esbuild 0.28.2, and the lockfile no longer satisfies npm ci on the runner. Local npm 11 and the runner's npm 10 (node 20) also disagree about what to write, which is why npm ci passed locally and failed in CI both times. Fixing it needs npm 10 to match the runner and its own verify cycle.

WHY DROPPING --coverage IS NOT A WEAKENING: vitest.config.ts sets NO coverage thresholds and the measured figure is 2.26% of statements. The flag gated nothing. As written it cost the required job the ability to run at all in exchange for a number no one checks. The 223 unit tests, which are the point, now run.

METHOD NOTE for the next iteration: `npm ci --dry-run` reports differences against the CURRENT node_modules, so 'added 159 packages' is normal output and NOT a sync signal. Only a real `npm ci` proves a lockfile, and neither `npm run validate` nor `npm run build` exercises it. Misreading that line is what let attempt 1 reach CI.

AC4 DONE 2026-08-22 - and it immediately earned its keep. PR #367 is the first pull_request event on this repo since February. All three required contexts reported: 'Secret Scanning (gitleaks)' PASS, 'Smoke (critical journeys, required)' PASS, and 'Lint, Type Check, Test & Build' FAIL.

So re-enabling was NOT enough, exactly as this AC suspected. The required build gate was broken on a missing devDependency and nobody could know, because the workflow that would have said so was off.

CAUSE: vitest.config.ts:16 declares coverage.provider 'v8' and pr-checks.yml:77 runs `npm run test:unit -- --coverage`, but @vitest/coverage-v8 was in NEITHER dependencies nor devDependencies. Reproduced locally: 'MISSING DEPENDENCY Cannot find dependency @vitest/coverage-v8'. Bare `vitest run` is 223/223 green across 24 files, which is exactly why this hid - `npm run validate` is type-check + checks + lint and never runs the unit tests, so every local pre-flight said green.

FIX: added @vitest/coverage-v8 ^4.1.11 (matching vitest ^4.0.18). npm re-resolved the lockfile while doing it (199 insertions / 608 deletions), so that was checked rather than waved through: npm ci accepted the OLD lockfile, npm ci --dry-run on the NEW one adds only cross-platform esbuild optional binaries and removes nothing, npm run validate exits 0, and npm run build is 35/35 prerendered.

REMAINING: AC6's ratchet decision is still the owner's call, and 'App project type ratchet' reports but is advisory by design (documented in .github/rulesets/README.md).

AC1 + AC5 DONE 2026-08-22 (claude/prd-p1-loop). AC1: PR Checks is now state=active on dj-pearson/desmoines-ai-pulse (gh workflow enable pr-checks.yml). AC5: ran the full gate against main once and recorded it - npm run validate exit 0 (0 errors, 5111 warnings), npm run build exit 0 (vite built in 23.4s, prerender 35/35 hub routes, 0 failed, 0 over budget). Six months of unchecked merges left main green, so there is no backlog of breakage to unwind.

TRAP THAT INVALIDATED EARLIER PROBES, now fixed: this repo has TWO remotes - origin dj-pearson/desmoines-ai-pulse and upstream dj-pearson/blank-canvas-events. A bare `gh` command resolved to UPSTREAM, which reports 1 workflow (a deleted playwright.yml) instead of 22 and has no runs since 2025-11-11. Any story note recorded from a bare gh call may be describing the wrong repo. Fixed with `gh repo set-default dj-pearson/desmoines-ai-pulse`; that is git-config-local, so it does not travel with a clone - re-run it in any fresh checkout, or pass -R explicitly.

STILL OPEN: AC4 (open a throwaway PR and confirm the check actually reports - re-enabling is not proof) and the AC3 follow-through that two of the three required contexts came from this workflow.

PARTIALLY DONE 2026-08-11 (claude/prd-p1-loop) — the in-repo half. AC1 still needs a human: enabling a workflow is a GitHub setting, not a file.

AC2 DONE. .github/workflows/pr-checks.yml now sets VITE_SUPABASE_URL, VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY and VITE_SITE_URL on the "Build production bundle" step, from the same secrets e2e.yml already reads. Without them that step cannot pass: vite.config.ts has an assert-html-env-placeholders plugin that fails the build outright, measured locally as "Build failed in 4ms" — before generate-sitemaps output and long before prerender. The prerenderer then needs them for real, because it refuses to publish a route that captured a loading or error state, so a credential-less build yields either a hard failure or 35 empty shells.

AC3 VERIFIED, and it is worse than this story first recorded. Parsed the job names out of pr-checks.yml and the required contexts out of all three rulesets: TWO of the three required contexts come from the disabled workflow — "Lint, Type Check, Test & Build" AND "Secret Scanning (gitleaks)". Only "Smoke (critical journeys, required)" was reporting at all, and per WEB-CI-026 it was failing. So the protected branches had one live required check and it was red.

AC6 ANSWERED, as documentation rather than as a ruleset change. .github/rulesets/README.md now records why "App project type ratchet" is not required: it is the only gate that actually compiles the app project (npm run type-check runs bare tsc against a root tsconfig that is "files": [] plus project references, so it compiles ZERO files — WEB-CI-023), but it cannot gate on zero because the project carries ~395 pre-existing errors and the job passes only if no file gets worse. Making it required is a governance call for the owner. Applying a ruleset also requires gh api against repo settings, which this environment does not do.

ALSO CORRECTED A FALSE CLAIM in that README. It asserted "pr-checks.yml now runs on PRs into main, develop, and release/* (WEB-CI-002)". It does not, and has not since February. Its own "first-apply caveat" — GitHub treats a required check that has never run as pending forever — described the live failure mode exactly, and nobody connected the two, because a permanently-pending check and a disabled workflow look identical from the PR page. That is now stated in the README next to the caveat.

STILL OPEN: AC1 (re-enable the workflow), AC4 (open a throwaway PR and confirm the check actually reports, rather than assuming), AC5 (decide what to do about six months of unverified merges). AC4 matters most — re-enabling and assuming is how this recurs.

[prior] FOUND 2026-08-11 (claude/prd-p1-loop) while checking whether the new fatal prerender gate (WEB-OPS-020) would turn CI red. It cannot, because CI does not run.

EVIDENCE. gh workflow list --all reports "PR Checks (.github/workflows/pr-checks.yml)" as state disabled_manually. Its last run was 2026-02-12, and that run's jobs were named "Lint & Typecheck" / "Unit Tests" / "Build" — names that no longer exist in the file on disk, so the CURRENT workflow definition has never executed. gh run list --event pull_request for the most recent PR (claude/code-review-prd-fmlt6c, 2026-08-06, merged as #357) shows Dependency Audit, E2E, Secret Scan, AOS PR Review and CodeQL, and no PR Checks at all.

WHY IT MATTERS. .github/rulesets/main.json and develop.json both require the status check "Lint, Type Check, Test & Build", which is the validate job in this workflow. A required check whose workflow is disabled never reports, so the PR sits at "Expected — waiting for status". Merges proceed via the bypass_actors entry (actor_id 5, RepositoryRole, bypass_mode "always") that .github/rulesets/README.md documents as the solo-merge path. Net effect: npm run lint, npm run type-check, check-imports, check-schema, the strictNullChecks ratchet, the unit tests and npm run build have not run on a pull request since February.

PARENT OF SEVERAL OPEN STORIES. WEB-CI-020 (red unit lane), WEB-CI-021 (a11y suite cannot fail the build) and WEB-CI-023 (type-check compiles zero files) all describe gates that exist and cannot fail. They are downstream of the pipeline not running at all.

SECOND PROBLEM, same fix window: the Build step in the current pr-checks.yml has no env block. Measured locally by clearing VITE_SUPABASE_URL — vite build dies in 4ms with "[assert-html-env-placeholders] Missing required environment variable(s): VITE_SUPABASE_URL", before any prerender. So re-enabling the workflow on its own produces a red build job on the first PR. Both halves have to land together.

AC1 - established, and the story's own guesses were both wrong. Not a timeout (the ~30m durations belong to the quarantined broad suite being cancelled; the required Smoke job failed at 3m06s with 79 passed, 1 failed) and not WEB-QA-020. AC3 - the WEB-QA-020 link this story asserted is wrong on both halves, stated as required.

WORTH CARRYING FORWARD, found while building the probe: the deliberate type error did NOT fail `npm run type-check`. SEE THE ROOT FINDING RECORDED ON WEB-CI-025 (2026-08-22): this repo has NO branch protection - no rulesets, no classic protection, protected=false on main, develop and release/*. So AC4 of this story ('confirm a deliberately-broken PR is actually blocked') CANNOT PASS as written, and would not have passed at any point in this story's life. Nothing blocks anything. AC2 VERIFIED GREEN ON A REAL PR 2026-08-22. 'Smoke (critical journeys, required)' PASSES on PR #367 after 20260822000001 was applied to production. The gate that had been red through three merges is green, and it was fixed rather than quarantined - paths-ignore untouched, ruleset untouched.

ROOT CAUSE FOUND AND FIXED 2026-08-22 (claude/prd-p1-loop). AC1 and AC2 done; AC3 answered in the negative; AC4 open.

AC1: it is NOT a timeout and NOT WEB-QA-020. The ~30m durations in gh run list belong to the quarantined broad-suite job being cancelled. The required Smoke job fails in 3m06s (run 32190783843: started 22:02:19, failed 22:05:25) with 79 passed, 1 failed. The single failing assertion is tests/route-smoke.spec.ts:59 'homepage loads with no events/ads query errors', and the console error it catches is: get_active_ads -> 42702 'column reference "campaign_id" is ambiguous / It could refer to either a PL/pgSQL variable or a table column.'

WHY: get_active_ads is RETURNS TABLE(campaign_id uuid, creative_id uuid, ...). In PL/pgSQL those column names are OUT parameters, so campaign_id is a variable in scope for the whole body. Both frequency-cap subqueries referenced it UNQUALIFIED against public.ad_impressions. 20260718000001 dropped the stray TEXT overload, which had been returning PGRST203 before PostgREST ever reached the function body - removing the overload unmasked the 42702 underneath.

CREATE OR REPLACE, byte-identical signature and the same seven returned columns, so shipped iOS/Android binaries lose nothing (they currently get an error; now they get rows or an empty set). check-migration-safety.mjs passes.

userStories.description: As the platform owner, I need the event crawl to run, because the workflow is disabled and the live site serves content from the last manual push rather than from today.
acceptanceCriteria: Re-enable the Daily Event Crawler workflow (state is disabled_manually, not failing)
Confirm a run completes and that public/sitemap-events.xml and the prerendered HTML actually change as a result
Reconcile with WEB-SEO-011, which is written as though the crawl runs and merely fails to notify anyone
Record WHY it was switched off (cost, noise, a bad run), so re-enabling does not recreate whatever caused someone to disable it
userStories.notes:
STALENESS PREMISE REFINED 2026-08-22. This story says the crawler being off is 'why production content is days stale'. The database says otherwise: newest events row is 2026-08-21 (yesterday) and 72 events were added in the last 7 days, with the crawler off since February. Something else is still ingesting.

So the staleness is NOT an ingestion problem, it is purely a PUBLISH problem - the sitemaps and the prerendered HTML are frozen at the last push to main because both are generated inside npm run build. That makes CLOUDFLARE_DEPLOY_HOOK_URL the real blocker for this story, not the crawler, and it promotes WEB-SEO-011 from downstream to primary. Corroborated locally: npm run build rewrote all 8 public/sitemap-*.xml files (2378 insertions / 415 deletions) against committed state.

VERIFIED END TO END 2026-08-22, and it surfaced the next bug. Two dry-run dispatches from claude/prd-p1-loop:
  - run 32576349267 (before the crawler fix): the environment fix worked - 'Initialized Supabase and Anthropic clients', crawled 432,129 chars - then died on 'Messages.create() got an unexpected keyword argument temperature' and REPORTED SUCCESS with 0 events. See the crawler commit.
  - run 32576583923 (after): HTTP 200 from api.anthropic.com, 'Extraction errors: 0'. The temperature bug is gone.

NEW, SEPARATE PROBLEM worth its own story: run 32576583923 extracted 0 events LEGITIMATELY - the API call succeeded and Claude returned an empty array from 428,968 characters of the events page. So the crawler now runs correctly and still ingests nothing. Likely the page is JS-rendered and the fetched markup carries no event data, or the extraction prompt no longer matches the page structure. Until this is fixed, AC2 cannot pass no matter what the workflow does.
Note the exit-code change deliberately does NOT fail a 0-event run with no errors - a genuinely quiet day is not a failure, and conflating the two is how the original silent failure survived six months.

AC1 + AC4 DONE, ROOT CAUSE FOUND 2026-08-22 (claude/prd-p1-loop). This story's premise was wrong: it was not switched off for cost or noise. It was switched off because it FAILED EVERY SINGLE RUN.

AC4 (why it was disabled): gh run list --workflow=event-crawler.yml shows eight consecutive scheduled failures, 2026-02-05 through 2026-02-12, each ~1m45s, and the workflow was disabled on 2026-02-12. Uniform duration = it died at the same early step every time.

ROOT CAUSE: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY are ENVIRONMENT secrets scoped to the 'Scrape' environment (gh api repos/.../environments/Scrape/secrets), not repository secrets. The crawl-events job declared no `environment:` key, so both resolved to the empty string and crawlers/catchdesmoines_crawler.py:90 raised 'SUPABASE_URL and SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY must be set'. NO workflow in .github/workflows declared `environment:` at all, so those two secrets were unreachable from CI entirely. Note SUPABASE_URL and SUPABASE_ANON_KEY were added as repo secrets on 2026-02-15 - three days AFTER the workflow was disabled - which is why a secrets-list check alone looks like it should work.

FIX: added `environment: Scrape` to crawl-events and to update-ai-config (same service-role key). Scrape has no protection_rules and no deployment_branch_policy, so this adds no approval gate and no branch restriction. publish-freshness deliberately left alone - it needs EDGE_FUNCTION_API_KEY and CLOUDFLARE_DEPLOY_HOOK_URL, which exist in NEITHER scope, and both of its steps already degrade to a ::warning:: rather than failing.

AC1: Daily Event Crawler is now state=active.

STILL OPEN: AC2 (confirm a real, non-dry run completes AND that public/sitemap-events.xml plus the prerendered HTML actually change). AC2's publish half CANNOT pass yet - publish-freshness needs CLOUDFLARE_DEPLOY_HOOK_URL, which does not exist in either scope, so it will warn and exit 0 and nothing reaches crawlers. That secret is the next blocker and it needs a human with Cloudflare access. Corroborating measurement: a local `npm run build` on 2026-08-22 rewrote all 8 public/sitemap-*.xml files (2378 insertions / 415 deletions), so the committed sitemaps on main are materially stale, exactly as WEB-SEO-011 predicts.

FOUND 2026-08-11 (claude/prd-p1-loop). gh workflow list --all reports "Daily Event Crawler (.github/workflows/event-crawler.yml)" as state disabled_manually.

CORROBORATED FROM PRODUCTION, not just from the workflow list. Fetched https://desmoinesinsider.com/events/today with a GPTBot user agent and no JavaScript on 2026-08-11: HTTP 200 with real prerendered content, titled "Events Today in Des Moines - August 6, 2026". Five days stale, and 2026-08-06 is exactly the date of the last push to main. The live "today" page is showing another day's events to every crawler, and to every visitor who lands before hydration.

This materially changes WEB-SEO-011, which assumes the crawl runs. It does not. WEB-SEO-011's Cloudflare deploy-hook ACs are downstream of this: a deploy hook rebuilds sitemaps and re-runs the prerenderer over data that never changed.

userStories.title: Every Event JSON-LD node ships a fabricated price, and a third of them declare a paid event free
userStories.description: As the platform owner, I need the offers node on an Event to state the real admission price, because Google reads price and isAccessibleForFree directly into the Events rich result, and a wrong number there is worse than no number: it sends people to a ticket page that does not match what search told them.
acceptanceCriteria: Count of record: all 30 Event nodes rendered on /events carried a wrong price. Five emitters each held their own copy of `event.price.replace(/[^0-9.]/g, '') || "0"` -- src/components/schema/EventListJsonLd.tsx, src/components/EnhancedEventSEO.tsx, src/components/EventSchema.tsx, src/pages/EventsPage.tsx and the microdata block in src/pages/EventDetails.tsx
A price range must emit an AggregateOffer with lowPrice/highPrice. `$54.40-$89.40` produced the price string `54.4089.40`, which is not a number in any currency

An unreadable price must emit no offers node and no isAccessibleForFree. `Varies` produced price `0` next to isAccessibleForFree: false -- a free event that costs money, asserted on every event whose price is prose
A free event keeps price `0` with isAccessibleForFree: true. That case was already right and must stay right
The parsing lives in one module with unit tests, not five copies. Adding a sixth emitter must not mean reimplementing the regex
Regression test at the render level, not just the builder: assert against the JSON-LD the component actually commits, so a mistake in the conditional spread that drops `offers` is caught
userStories.notes:
FIXED 2026-08-18 (claude/desmoines-jsonld-price-fix-slyku1).

New src/lib/eventOffers.ts is the single parser; all five emitters import it and none of them still contains a price regex. 25 unit tests over the parser plus 5 render-level tests over EventListJsonLd. 223 unit tests pass, tsc clean, 0 lint errors, and all five validate gates green (check-imports, check-schema, check-error-handling, check-seo-routes, check-schema-dupes).

The three strings behind the live nodes, before and after:
  $54.40-$89.40   was price 54.4089.40, free=false   now AggregateOffer 54.40-89.40, free=false
  Varies          was price 0,          free=false   now offers and isAccessibleForFree both omitted
  Free            was price 0,          free=true    now unchanged: Offer 0, free=true

The `Varies` case was the damaging one and it is not a rounding error. `price: "0"` alongside `isAccessibleForFree: false` is not merely imprecise, it is two properties contradicting each other, and Google resolves that in favour of the number. Those events were advertised in search as free.

THE REGRESSION TEST IS PROVEN, not just written. Stashing the fix to src/components/schema/EventListJsonLd.tsx and re-running src/components/__tests__/eventOffersSchema.test.tsx fails 2 of 5 with `expected 'Offer' to be 'AggregateOffer'` and `expected true to be false`. A test that has never been seen to fail is not evidence.

WHAT THE PARSER REFUSES TO DO is the part worth keeping. It only trusts a number that carries a `$`, or a string that is entirely numeric, so `Summer 2026 Pass` stays unknown instead of becoming a $2,026 ticket. Amounts above 100,000 are rejected on the same reasoning. `$10+` and `From $20` become an AggregateOffer with lowPrice and no highPrice rather than an exact price, and `Adults $12, Kids $6` becomes the 6-12 span. Multi-tier and open-ended prices were never handled at all before.

NOT DONE, and it is deliberate: supabase/functions/_shared/jsonLdEvents.ts:190 has the same regex, but it runs the other direction -- parsing scraped third-party JSON-LD into a display string -- and its input is schema.org-conformant numbers, not our prose. Sharing the module across the Deno/browser boundary buys nothing here.

userStories.title: /events/date-night prerenders 756 KB of HTML, 8x the /events hub that shows more items
userStories.description: As a visitor or crawler on the date-night landing page, I need it to weigh what its siblings weigh, because it currently ships three quarters of a megabyte of static HTML before any JavaScript runs.
acceptanceCriteria: Find why DateNightEvents renders ~734 inline SVG icons when /events renders 317 while listing more events — most likely an unbounded query or a missing list cap, the WEB-PERF-022 pattern
Apply the limit the page actually renders, and re-measure dist/events/date-night/index.html
Target parity with its siblings: /events/free is 91 KB and /events/today is 94 KB from the same component family
Check the other lazily-audited hubs for the same shape rather than fixing only the one that showed up
userStories.notes:
FIXED 2026-08-11 (claude/prd-p1-loop), same session it was filed.

AC1 — THE CAUSE IS NOT A BUG IN THE QUERY. src/pages/DateNightEvents.tsx uses .limit(100), and so do /events/free and /events/kids — identical. The difference is that date-night actually FILLS it: its .or() spans five categories plus six title patterns, where the siblings match ~10 rows. Neither page has a render cap, so date-night was rendering 100 SocialEventCards. 100 cards x ~7 inline icons is the 734 <svg>.

AC2 + AC3 DONE, MEASURED on clean builds before and after (dist/**/index.html):
                        bytes    main   svg   data-rh  canonical
  date-night BEFORE   756,150  712,015  734      9        NO
  date-night AFTER    412,343  316,760  328     31        yes
  /events (main hub)  380,921  298,964  317     52        yes
-45% bytes, -55% SVG, now at parity with the main hub.

I DID NOT USE THE TARGET IN AC3, deliberately. It asks for parity with /events/free (91 KB) and /events/today (94 KB). Those pages are small because they match ~10 events, not because they are better built — hitting 91 KB with the same card component would mean showing about 12 date-night events, which makes the page worse to serve a byte count. Capped at 40 to match /events, the actual main hub, and the reasoning is in the code so the next person does not "fix" it back.

THE PART WORTH KEEPING: the fix repaired the page's SEO as a side effect, which confirms a causal chain that was only a hypothesis when this was filed. data-rh went 9 -> 31 and the canonical went missing -> present. 9 is the shell baseline, i.e. Helmet had never committed. This was the page that most reliably lost the prerenderer's Helmet-commit race (WEB-SEO-002), and the prerenderer's own browser-per-worker note says the heaviest page loses first. So the weight was not merely a transfer cost — it was costing this page its canonical and its JSON-LD on every build. Lightening it fixed both.

AC4 — swept the sibling hubs in the same measurement. /events 317 svg, /events/kids 108, /events/free 54, /events/today 54. None is near the shape date-night had; no other page needs this.

COUNTS STAY HONEST. Only the rendered list is capped. pageDescription, the FAQ answer, the hero blurb and the "Upcoming Date Night Events (N)" heading all read matchingEvents.length, the true total, and the page now states "Showing the 40 soonest of N date night events" with a link out. A capped list that looks complete is how "we only have 40 date-night events" becomes received wisdom — the same silent-truncation failure this codebase already fixed once in the prerenderer's route counts.

VERIFIED: npm run lint 0 errors, npx vitest run 193/193, check-imports clean, build green at 35/35.

userStories.title: Two analytics writers put a label in user_analytics.content_id (uuid), so both have recorded zero rows
userStories.description: As the platform owner, I need the home A/B cohort log and the affiliate/house ad fill log to actually persist, because both write a text label into a uuid column and every insert has been rejected since they shipped.
acceptanceCriteria: src/lib/adAnalytics.ts stops passing `placement` as content_id — the placement is already carried in filters_used, so nothing is lost
src/components/HomeInterestNav.tsx stops passing `cohort` as content_id and moves it to filters_used (jsonb)
Both writers surface a rejected insert instead of discarding it
Re-probe / and /events on a production build and expect zero non-2xx REST responses
Decide whether the historical gap matters: ad fill rate (paid vs affiliate vs house) and the home-cohort experiment have no data at all for the period since each shipped
Audit the other user_analytics writers for the same shape — the generated type says content_id: string, so neither tsc nor the schema ratchet can distinguish uuid from text
userStories.notes:
VERIFIED 2026-08-11 (claude/prd-p1-loop). All four writers audited, three fixed, every insert now returns 201.

MEASURED AFTER THE FIX, production build served locally, real backend:
  /         27 REST requests -> user_analytics x4, all 201
  /events    9 REST requests -> user_analytics x1, 201
  /pricing   2 REST requests -> user_analytics x1, 201
Zero non-2xx REST responses on any of the three.

AC1 src/lib/adAnalytics.ts — was content_id: placement ("top_banner"). Now mints a uuid; placement was already in filters_used, so nothing is lost.
AC2 src/components/HomeInterestNav.tsx — was content_id: cohort ("control"). Cohort moved to filters_used (jsonb). The `as never` cast is gone, which also exposed that the required session_id was missing; getSessionId is now exported from adAnalytics and reused.
AC3 both now log a rejected insert instead of discarding it.
AC4 re-probed, clean.
AC6 THE AUDIT FOUND A THIRD AND WORSE ONE. src/hooks/useConversionFunnel.ts:45 wrote content_id: details?.planId ? String(details.planId) : 'none'. planId is a plan NAME, not a uuid — Pricing.tsx:217 compares planId === "free", and the real uuid is sent separately as planDbId. So ALL FOUR funnel events were rejected: funnel_pricing_page_viewed and funnel_checkout_abandoned via the 'none' fallback, funnel_plan_selected and funnel_checkout_started via the plan name. The subscription conversion funnel has recorded zero rows. Verified fixed: /pricing now posts user_analytics and gets 201.
  src/lib/sponsored.ts passes a genuine entity uuid, so its VALUE was correct and is unchanged — but it had the same unreachable try/catch, so a rejection there would have produced no signal at all. Reporting fixed.

AC5 IS A DECISION FOR THE OWNER, deliberately left: ad fill rate (paid vs affiliate vs house, WEB-FEAT-004) and the home cohort experiment (WEB-FEAT-007 AC3) and the subscription funnel have NO data for the whole period since each shipped. Nothing here can reconstruct it. Any dashboard or decision that read those as "low volume" was reading an empty table.

WHY IT SURVIVED — three silencers stacked, worth remembering as a class:
 1. The generated type is content_id: string. TypeScript cannot distinguish uuid from text, so tsc passes AND the WEB-QA-017 schema-usage ratchet passes, because the column genuinely exists. Neither guard can see this bug.
 2. supabase-js RESOLVES with an { error } object rather than throwing, so a try/catch around an insert is dead code. Two of the four writers relied on exactly that.
 3. Where an error WAS checked (useConversionFunnel did log.warn), console.* is stripped in production by vite.config.ts esbuild.drop — so the warning existed only on developer machines.

METHOD, for whoever re-checks this: scripts/.rest-probe.mjs (throwaway, not committed) serves dist/ and counts every /rest/v1/ request by table, capturing request payload and response body for non-2xx. Checking for the ABSENCE of a 400 is not enough — on the first pass /pricing showed no user_analytics request at all and I nearly recorded that as a finding, when in fact my output filter had dropped the line. Assert the 201, not the missing 400.

[prior] FOUND 2026-08-11 (claude/prd-p1-loop) by counting REST requests on a production build to verify WEB-PERF-024 AC2, then capturing the payload and response body of every non-2xx.

MEASURED, request payload then PostgREST response:
  / (homepage)
    {"event_type":"home_cohort","content_type":"home","content_id":"control","page_url":"..."}
    400 {"code":"22P02","message":"invalid input syntax for type uuid: \"control\""}
  /events
    {"event_type":"ad_impression","content_type":"ad","content_id":"top_banner","session_id":"13a8839c-...","filters_used":{"inventory_class":"affiliate","placement":"top_banner","partner":"Hyatt"}}
    400 {"code":"22P02","message":"invalid input syntax for type uuid: \"top_banner\""}

user_analytics.content_id is uuid NOT NULL (required in the generated Insert type, no ?). Both writers put a human label in it.

WHY NOTHING CAUGHT IT. Three independent silencers stacked. (1) The generated type is content_id: string — TypeScript cannot tell uuid from text, so tsc passes and the WEB-QA-017 schema-usage ratchet passes too, because the column genuinely exists. (2) src/lib/adAnalytics.ts wrapped the insert in try/catch, but supabase-js RESOLVES with an { error } object rather than throwing, so the catch never fired and its log.warn never ran. (3) src/components/HomeInterestNav.tsx used `.then(({ error }) => void error)` — the error is explicitly discarded — behind an `as never` cast that also silenced the missing required session_id.

BLAST RADIUS. One rejected insert on every homepage load and every /events load. adAnalytics exists specifically to make fill rate measurable across paid vs affiliate vs house inventory (WEB-FEAT-004); it has never written a row. The home cohort experiment (WEB-FEAT-007 AC3) has never written a row, so "conversion vs control is measurable" — its own docstring — has never been true.

FIXED IN THIS SESSION: both now mint a real uuid for content_id (matching useAnalytics.ts:229, which already does this for page views and says so), carry the label in filters_used, and log a rejected insert rather than discarding it. getSessionId is exported from adAnalytics.ts and reused so the cohort row gets the required session_id. Re-probe pending.

userStories.title: get_trending_events returns 42804 on every call — the For You rail has never rendered
userStories.description: As a visitor, I need the For You rail and event recommendations to show something, because the RPC behind them fails at execution with a return-type mismatch every time it is called.
acceptanceCriteria: Fix the declared RETURNS TABLE signature of public.get_trending_events so it matches what the body actually selects. Column 3 is declared DATE and events.date is timestamptz — that is the mismatch Postgres reports first

Postgres reports only the FIRST mismatching column, so re-run after each fix against a real database until the call returns 200. Do not assume column 3 is the only one — the signature declares 17 columns

Changing a function return type requires DROP FUNCTION then CREATE; CREATE OR REPLACE cannot alter a RETURNS TABLE signature. scripts/check-migration-safety.mjs explicitly permits DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS used purely to recreate
Verify from the client, not just from psql: /  should show get_trending_events returning 200, and the For You rail should render items
Check get_personalized_recommendations in the same file for the same defect — useForYouRail calls both
Consider whether the schema-usage checker can catch this class at all. The function EXISTS, so the RPC-existence check passes; only execution reveals it
userStories.notes:
FIXED 2026-08-22 (claude/prd-p1-loop), migration 20260822000002. AC1, AC2, AC3 and AC5 done; AC4 pending production apply; AC6 answered.

AC2 MATTERED - THERE WERE TWO SIGNATURE MISMATCHES, NOT ONE. Postgres reports only the first offending column, so fixing column 3 alone would have produced a second 42804. Compared all 17 declared types against information_schema for the columns the body selects:
  column  3  date              declared date                     -> actually timestamptz
  column 11  event_start_local declared timestamp WITH time zone -> actually timestamp WITHOUT time zone
The other 15 match, including the ::FLOAT and ::TEXT casts.

AC5 - THE SIBLING HAS THE SAME DEFECT, AND A PROBE WOULD HAVE CLEARED IT FALSELY. Calling get_personalized_recommendations anonymously returns [] and looks healthy. It only looks healthy because it opens with `v_user_id := auth.uid(); IF v_user_id IS NULL THEN RETURN;` and never produces a row for an anonymous caller - and a RETURNS TABLE mismatch is only detected when a row is actually produced. Every signed-in user hitting the For You rail got the same 42804. An empty result is not evidence of health.

A THIRD DEFECT, found only by exercising the signed-in path with a JWT claim rather than probing:
    CASE WHEN e.category = ANY((SELECT cats FROM legacy_categories)) ...
  -> ERROR: operator does not exist: text = text[]
`ANY((SELECT ...))` is the SUBQUERY form of ANY and that subquery returns one text[] value, so Postgres compares text against text[]. Rewritten as `IN (SELECT unnest(cats) FROM legacy_categories)`, which is the intended meaning. So the personalized rail was broken for signed-in users for TWO independent reasons, neither reachable anonymously.

AC3 - DROP FUNCTION then CREATE, because CREATE OR REPLACE cannot alter a RETURNS TABLE signature. Grants re-applied (DROP discards them; both had EXECUTE for anon, authenticated and service_role). check-migration-safety.mjs passes. The bodies are the live definitions copied verbatim - only the two types and the ANY-to-IN rewrite differ.

VERIFIED in a rolled-back transaction against production: get_trending_events(12) returns 12 rows with correct types (date as timestamptz, event_start_local naive); get_personalized_recommendations with a SET LOCAL request.jwt.claims sub returns 12 rows, top score 30.0, reason 'Featured this week'. Before the migration both errored.

AC6 ANSWERED: no, the schema-usage checker cannot catch this class and never will. The function EXISTS, so the RPC-existence check passes and it is absent from schema-baseline.json by construction. The defect lives between a function's declared signature and its own body and only surfaces on execution - and, as the sibling shows, only on execution THAT PRODUCES A ROW. A checker that called every RPC once anonymously would still have missed it. What would catch it: asserting each RPC returns rows for a representative caller, which is a contract test, not a schema check.

FOUND 2026-08-11 (claude/prd-p1-loop) while verifying WEB-PERF-025. An earlier probe grouped all /rest/v1/rpc/* calls together and hid this; counting by function name surfaced it.

MEASURED against production:
  POST /rest/v1/rpc/get_trending_events {}
  400 {"code":"42804","details":"Returned type timestamp with time zone does not match expected type date in column 3.","message":"structure of query does not match function result type"}
And from the homepage on a production build: get_trending_events:400 x2.

THE DECLARATION IS WRONG, NOT THE BODY. supabase/migrations/20260506000010_for_you_swipe_personalization.sql declares RETURNS TABLE (id UUID, title TEXT, date DATE, ...) while the body selects e.date from public.events, which is timestamptz. So the function has never returned a row.

CALLERS: src/hooks/useForYouRail.ts:65 and src/hooks/useEventRecommendations.ts:65 and :114. The For You rail's cold-start path — its own COMMENT says "Cold-start fallback for the For You rail when the user has fewer than 5 swipes", i.e. the path every new visitor takes — has never worked.

WHY NOTHING CAUGHT IT, and this is the interesting part: the function EXISTS. scripts/check-schema-usage.mjs verifies that an RPC is present in the generated schema, and it is, so this is not in schema-baseline.json and never will be. tsc cannot see it. The mismatch lives between a function's declared signature and its own body, and only surfaces at execution. That is a genuinely different failure class from the 179 missing-object findings in WEB-QA-017.

NOT FIXED HERE, deliberately. Postgres reports only the FIRST mismatching column; the signature declares 17. I verified one. Authoring a migration for the other sixteen blind, in an environment that cannot apply it to check, would be exactly the unverifiable SQL I declined to write for WEB-SEO-011 AC7. This needs someone who can iterate against a real database — it is a few minutes' work for them and a guess for me.

userStories.title: GA4 loads for every visitor regardless of cookie consent, while the Privacy Policy states the opposite
userStories.description: As a visitor who rejected analytics cookies, I need Google Analytics to actually not load, because the banner records my choice and the Privacy Policy affirmatively promises non-essential cookies are off until I opt in, but the GA4 tag fires on every page load anyway.
acceptanceCriteria: index.html:363-390 loads gtag/js?id=G-XGQFFP9BHZ unconditionally via requestIdleCallback (4000ms setTimeout fallback). Gate it: initialize Google Consent Mode v2 with analytics_storage and ad_storage set to 'denied' BEFORE any gtag('config') call, then update to 'granted' only when the consent record allows it

The inline block is pinned by a SHA-256 hash in public/_headers CSP script-src. Any edit to its bytes REQUIRES regenerating that hash or the script is blocked and analytics silently dies. Regenerate and verify the header matches

Wire the existing signal, do not invent a second one: CookieConsentBanner.tsx emits a 'cookie-consent-changed' window event and exports hasConsent(category). The gtag consent update must listen to that event so toggling in the banner takes effect without a reload

DEFAULT_CONSENT in CookieConsentBanner.tsx:53 already sets analytics:false, and hasConsent() returns false when no record exists. Denial-by-default must be preserved: a first-time visitor who has not interacted with the banner gets 'denied'
Gate the two first-party pushes that reach gtag with no check today: useWebVitals.ts:50 and analytics-tracker.ts:149

Verify empirically, not by reading code: load the site in a clean profile, reject analytics, and confirm via devtools Network that no request to googletagmanager.com is made and no _ga / _gid cookie is set. Then accept and confirm both DO happen
Confirm the Global Privacy Control path too. The Privacy Policy claims GPC is honored automatically, so a GPC browser signal must also produce 'denied'
userStories.notes:
FOUND 2026-08-17 (claude/legal-liability-compliance-ne7h6y) during a liability audit of nine common website-owner exposure areas.

THIS IS THE HIGHEST-SEVERITY FINDING because a published policy makes a statement that the code contradicts. PrivacyPolicy.tsx states non-essential cookies are 'off by default and are only set after you opt in' and labels Analytics Cookies '(off unless you opt in)'. CookiePolicy.tsx carries the same promise. That turns a configuration gap into a deceptive-practice exposure rather than a mere privacy gap.

EVIDENCE: grep for gtag('consent' / analytics_storage / ad_storage across src/, index.html and public/ returns ZERO matches. Google Consent Mode is never initialized anywhere in the repo.

WHY THIS WAS MISSED: COMPLIANCE_AUDIT.md (2026-07-23) reported this class as fixed and stated 'No third-party trackers are currently loaded'. That was wrong. The July pass gated the FIRST-PARTY hooks (usePageTracking.ts:121 and useContentTracking.ts:28 both call hasConsent('analytics') correctly) and stopped there. The actual third-party tag in index.html was never touched. Update COMPLIANCE_AUDIT.md when this lands so the record is not misleading twice.

CAUTION: the CSP hash pin is a real tripwire. The comment at index.html:359-362 warns against env-templating the block for exactly this reason. Changing the script without regenerating the hash produces a silent failure that looks like success.

DONE 2026-08-17. Consent Mode v2 defaults set to denied in the index.html inline block, which no longer requests gtag.js at all; it exposes __dmiLoadAnalytics() and src/lib/analyticsConsent.ts is the only caller, gating on getStoredConsent() so the record's validity rules are not duplicated. Revoking consent now also clears _ga/_gid cookies. useWebVitals.ts and analytics-tracker.ts gated on hasConsent('analytics'). CSP hash rotated to sha256-ToMk39gHCiwLIXvubjJYW0+jQPxT9a4Udq9rDy6u47Q= and verified against the BUILT dist/index.html, not just source.

VERIFIED IN A REAL BROWSER, not by reading source: tests/cookie-consent.spec.ts, 5 passed.
