userStories.title: Fabricated five-star testimonials from invented people are live on the Pricing page
userStories.description: As the site owner, I need the paid-conversion page to stop showing endorsements from consumers who do not exist, because fabricated testimonials attributed to fictional people are prohibited and now carry civil penalties per violation.
acceptanceCriteria: Remove the invented testimonials at Pricing.tsx:132-151: 'Sarah M.' (Insider Member), 'Mike T.' (VIP Member), 'Jessica L.' (Insider Member), each rendered with a hardcoded five-star rating at Pricing.tsx:566-593

Remove or substantiate the unquantified social-proof claims in the same section: the heading 'Loved by Des Moines Explorers' and the subhead 'Join thousands of happy members' (Pricing.tsx:558-563). Nothing measures a member count

Follow the precedent already set in this codebase rather than inventing a new approach. SocialProof.tsx solved exactly this: it replaced fabricated material with counts read live from the database, and its header comment documents why. Mirror that pattern or drop the section entirely
If the section is replaced rather than deleted, every number rendered must trace to a real query. Do not substitute a different unverifiable claim
Grep the whole of src/ for the three invented names before closing. They were removed from SocialProof.tsx and survived in Pricing.tsx, so assume there may be a third copy
Check the FAQ block immediately below (Pricing.tsx:155-175) is left intact. It is accurate and load-bearing for WEB-LEGAL-006
userStories.notes:
FOUND 2026-08-17 (claude/legal-liability-compliance-ne7h6y).

THE SAME THREE PERSONAS WERE ALREADY REMOVED ONCE. SocialProof.tsx carries a header comment (WEB-SEO-016) recording that 'Sarah M., East Village Resident', 'Marcus T., Ankeny' and 'Jessica L., West Des Moines Mom' were deleted at the owner's request as fabricated endorsements, citing 16 CFR 255. The fix was applied to one file and missed in the other. The copy that survived is on Pricing.tsx, the paid-conversion page, which is the worst placement: a fabricated endorsement that induces a purchase is materially different from one on a marketing page.

EXPOSURE HAS INCREASED SINCE THAT COMMENT WAS WRITTEN. The FTC's Rule on the Use of Consumer Reviews and Testimonials (16 CFR 465, effective 2024) makes fake consumer testimonials subject to civil penalties per violation, where 16 CFR 255 alone was guidance backed by enforcement actions.

SMALLEST AND MOST URGENT OF THE NINE. Self-contained, one file, no schema or contract implications, and it is live right now.

Not a defect but worth noting for whoever picks this up: AffiliateDisclosure.tsx:106 already cites 16 CFR 255 correctly, so the codebase knows the rule. This is an inconsistency, not ignorance.

DONE 2026-08-17. Scope was larger than the story assumed. The grep in criterion 5 was right to expect another copy; it found THREE more live surfaces, not one:
  - Pricing.tsx: the three invented members and the 'Loved by Des Moines Explorers' / 'Join thousands of happy members' headings. Section removed, no replacement, since nothing measures a member count and SocialProof.tsx already carries the DB-backed counts on the homepage.
  - EmailCaptureModal.tsx: a '423 organizers joined this week' badge and a quote from 'Sarah M., Community Organizer'.
  - EventPromotionPlanner.tsx (/tools/event-promotion-planner): '423+ Des Moines Event Organizers' and a quote from 'Sarah M., Downtown Farmers Market Coordinator' claiming the tool raised attendance 40%. A quantified efficacy claim attributed to a person who does not exist, which is the most exposed of the four.
  - UserGeneratedContent.tsx (/real-time): three fabricated reviews with helpful counts and verified:true badges, plus three fabricated 'community updates' asserting false facts about named real businesses (a limited-time burger at Zombie Burger, a newly hired sommelier called Marcus at Proof). Seeds removed and honest empty states added; the component now shows nothing until wired to user_ratings.

Each removal left a comment naming what was there and why it went, following the SocialProof.tsx precedent, because this defect has already recurred once by being fixed in one file and missed in another.

VERIFIED IN A BROWSER across /pricing, /tools/event-promotion-planner and /real-time: none of the 15 fabricated strings render. The FAQ block was checked separately and is intact, including the accurate auto-renew and cancellation copy that WEB-LEGAL-006 depends on. Zero new lint warnings (two imports orphaned by the removals were dropped).

SPUN OFF WEB-LEGAL-010: browser verification caught 'Zombie Burger + Drink Lab' and 'Proof Restaurant' still rendering on /real-time from RealTimeBusinessInfo.tsx, which seeds invented hours, phone numbers and wait times for real businesses. Different defect class (fabricated operational facts, not endorsements) and it needs an owner decision, so it is not folded in here. A source-level check of this story would have looked complete and missed it.

userStories.title: Account deletion never touches Supabase Storage, so user uploads survive erasure in public buckets
userStories.description: As a user who deleted my account, I need my uploaded photos actually deleted, because the Privacy Policy promises erasure but the deletion function only removes database rows and every upload bucket is world-readable by URL.
acceptanceCriteria: delete-user-account/index.ts:66-101 deletes from a table list and then calls auth.admin.deleteUser. It makes no storage call at all. Add a storage purge covering every bucket a user can write to

Buckets to purge, with the call sites that write to them: review-photos (RatingSystem.tsx:194), event-photos (EventPhotoUpload.tsx:72), media and videos (VideoUpload.tsx:261-295, useMediaUpload.ts). Files are stored under a <user_id>/ prefix per the storage RLS policies, so storage.from(bucket).list(userId) then .remove(paths) is the shape
list() paginates and defaults to 100 items. Loop until exhausted or a user with more than 100 photos keeps the remainder. Do not assume one call drains the prefix
Do not let a single bucket failure abort the purge. Match the existing pattern in the function, which warns and continues per table, so one error never leaves erasure half-done
Order matters: purge storage BEFORE auth.admin.deleteUser, since the service-role client is used throughout but the audit trail should record the purge against a still-identifiable user
Report what was purged in the response and to the audit log. A silent no-op is what created this defect
Verify against a real account: upload a review photo, note its public URL, delete the account, then fetch that URL and confirm 404 rather than 200

ad-creatives is deliberately NOT in the purge list. Advertiser creatives belong to a billing relationship with its own retention needs. Confirm that reasoning holds, and if it does, document it in the function so the omission does not read as an oversight
userStories.notes:
FOUND 2026-08-17 (claude/legal-liability-compliance-ne7h6y).

COMPOUNDS WITH WEB-LEGAL-007. Every upload bucket is public:true, so an orphaned file is not merely retained, it stays publicly fetchable by anyone holding or guessing the URL, forever, with no expiry. Retention plus public reachability is what makes this worse than an ordinary retention bug.

PrivacyPolicy.tsx:253 promises 'Erasure / Deletion: Request deletion of your account and associated data' and :236 says account data is 'Retained until you delete your account'. Uploaded photos are associated data by any reading.

COMPLIANCE_AUDIT.md (2026-07-23) item 4 claimed erasure completeness was addressed. It extended the TABLE list (added user_analytics and newsletter_subscribers). Storage was never in scope and the report does not mention it, so the gap is not recorded anywhere before this story.

See WEB-LEGAL-004 for a second, independent defect in the same function. They are split because 004 is a silent-failure bug with a different root cause and can be fixed and verified separately, but whoever takes one should read both.

DONE 2026-08-17 (implementation), WITH ONE VERIFICATION STEP OUTSTANDING - see the bottom of this note.

Added _shared/purgeUserStorage.ts and called it from performDeletion before auth.admin.deleteUser. Both the response and the audit log now report storage_files_removed and any bucket that failed, so a purge that quietly removes nothing is visible.

THE STORY'S BUCKET LIST WAS INCOMPLETE AND ITS PATH ASSUMPTION WAS WRONG. Both would have produced a fix that deletes almost nothing while appearing to work:
  - thumbnails was missing. VideoUpload.tsx:287 writes user thumbnails to it at <uid>/<contentType>/<ts>_thumb.jpg. Five buckets are covered, not four.
  - Only review-photos is flat (<uid>/<uuid>.jpg). event-photos is <uid>/<eventId>/<ts>.<ext> and media, videos and thumbnails are <uid>/<contentType>/<file>. Supabase list() returns only immediate children, marking folders with a null id, so the list(userId) + remove(results) shape the story described returns folder placeholders for four of the five buckets and deletes nothing from them. The implementation walks recursively.

VERIFIED by supabase/functions/_tests/purge-user-storage.test.ts, 8 passed, against a fake client that models real list() semantics (null-id folders, capped pages). Substituting the naive flat-list implementation makes exactly three of those tests fail - nesting, pagination and failure isolation - so the suite provably catches the defect rather than merely passing. Wired into .github/workflows/subscription-sync-tests.yml next to the sibling deletion-contract test.

SANDBOX NOTE: deno.land and jsr.io are both blocked by this environment's egress proxy, so the suite was executed with a local two-function assert shim. The committed file imports std@0.208.0 from deno.land, matching every sibling test and what CI installs. The test bodies were not changed between the local run and the commit.

NOT DONE, MUST BE DONE ON A DEPLOYED ENVIRONMENT: acceptance criterion 7, the live upload-delete-fetch check. This sandbox cannot reach the project at all (CONNECT to wtkhfqpmcegzcbngroui.supabase.co:443 is refused 403 by the proxy) and there is no service-role key here. Before trusting this in production: upload a review photo, note its public URL, delete the account, then fetch that URL and confirm 404 rather than 200. The unit tests prove the traversal logic; they cannot prove the bucket names and RLS allow a service-role delete.

userStories.title: Account deletion targets three tables that do not exist and misses user_ratings, so reviews survive erasure silently
userStories.description: As a user who deleted my account, I need my reviews and ratings actually deleted, because the deletion function names tables that return 42P01 in production, swallows the error as a warning, and never touches the real table that holds this data.
acceptanceCriteria: delete-user-account/index.ts:67-75 lists 'favorites', 'ratings' and 'reviews'. Per CLAUDE.md these three return 42P01 (relation does not exist) against production, confirmed by a probe on 2026-08-11. Remove them or replace them with the tables that actually exist

public.user_ratings is the real table and appears in at least a dozen migrations. It has ZERO occurrences in delete-user-account/index.ts. Add it. It carries photo_urls (migration 20260623000004_review_photos.sql:9), which ties this story to WEB-LEGAL-003

Verify every table name in the list against PostgREST before trusting it, per the CLAUDE.md probe recipe. Do not read src/integrations/supabase/types.ts and assume presence, the generated types are known stale

The per-table catch at :83-86 downgrades every failure to console.warn with the comment 'A table may not exist in every environment'. That comment is why this went unnoticed. Distinguish a genuinely-absent table from a delete that failed for another reason, and surface the latter instead of warning past it
Deletion currently reports success to the user regardless of how many tables silently no-opped. The response must not claim erasure completed when rows were left behind

Cross-check the list against every table with a user_id column that holds personal data, not just the ones already listed. Run this as a query against the live schema rather than by grepping migrations
Verify end to end: create an account, leave a review with a photo, delete the account, then confirm no user_ratings row remains for that user_id
userStories.notes:
FOUND 2026-08-17 (claude/legal-liability-compliance-ne7h6y).

THIS IS AN INSTANCE OF THE WEB-QA-017 BUG CLASS, in the single worst place for it. WEB-QA-017 documents 179 references to tables and columns that do not exist, of which a production probe confirmed 45 missing tables and 32 missing columns with zero false positives. The class is defined by failing silently at runtime while type-checking cleanly. Here it fails silently inside the GDPR Article 17 erasure path, so the failure mode is not an empty UI state, it is a legal promise that quietly does not execute.

WHY THE ERROR IS INVISIBLE: the loop at :78-88 catches per-table and calls console.warn, and console.* is stripped in production builds per vite.config.ts esbuild.drop. So in production the warning does not even reach a log.

CHECK WHETHER scripts/check-schema-usage.mjs (npm run check-schema, the WEB-QA-017 CI ratchet) covers supabase/functions/. If it only scans src/ then this file was never in scope and other edge functions may carry the same class. That finding belongs in WEB-LEGAL-009.

Paired with WEB-LEGAL-003, which fixes storage purging in the same function. Different root causes, verify separately.

DONE 2026-08-17. Much larger than the story described.

CONFIRMED WITHOUT PRODUCTION ACCESS: the generated types are decisive here. favorites, ratings and reviews have ZERO entries in src/integrations/supabase/types.ts; user_ratings has one and carries photo_urls. That corroborates the CLAUDE.md production probe, so no live query was needed to establish the defect.

THE REAL SCALE: 80 tables in the schema have a user_id column. The delete list named 8, three of which do not exist. So roughly 70 tables of user-keyed data survived every account deletion, not just reviews. Criterion 6 asked for this cross-check and it was the finding of the story.

Added _shared/userDataTables.ts, which partitions all 80 into PURGE_TABLES (60, in dependency order, profiles last) and RETAINED_TABLES (20, each with a written basis: consent proof, security trails, billing and tax records, advertiser contracts, and the GSC integration tables whose user_id is the connecting admin rather than a data subject). The retention reasons are engineering judgement and should be reviewed by counsel; they are written down so that review is possible, which it was not before.

WHY THE RATCHET MISSED IT: scripts/check-schema-usage.mjs does scan supabase/functions (SCAN_ROOTS includes it), but it matches .from('literal') and these names reached .from(table) as a loop variable. Nothing in schema-baseline.json references this file. Recorded for WEB-LEGAL-009 - the general fix is detecting arrays of literals fed to .from().

FAILURES ARE NO LONGER INVISIBLE: the loop records every failure instead of console.warn-ing past it, logs 42P01 distinctly as schema drift, and the response now carries complete:false plus tables_incomplete / storage_incomplete. success:true is retained because the auth record is gone either way and shipped clients branch on it (backward compatibility per CLAUDE.md); completeness is reported alongside rather than by changing that field.

VERIFIED by _tests/user-data-tables.test.ts, 8 passed, and the storage suite still passes (16 total). The load-bearing test asserts no user_id table is left unclassified, so adding a table in future fails CI until someone decides whether erasure covers it. Wired into subscription-sync-tests.yml. npm run validate: 0 errors.

NOT DONE: criterion 7's live end-to-end check, for the same reason as WEB-LEGAL-003 - no route from this sandbox to the Supabase project and no service-role key. The handler could not even be deno-checked here because its esm.sh and deno.land imports are proxy-blocked; _shared/userDataTables.ts and _shared/purgeUserStorage.ts both type-check clean. Before trusting in production: delete a test account and confirm the response reports complete:true.

userStories.title: No crisis response anywhere on the public AI chat surfaces
userStories.description: As a user in distress who types something concerning into the AI chat, I need to be shown crisis resources, because today the assistant is prompted only to return restaurant and event picks and has no safety floor of any kind.
acceptanceCriteria: Searching self-harm|suicide|crisis|988 across src/ and supabase/functions/ returns zero real matches today (the single hit is a coincidental path string in a WhatsApp SVG icon). Establish a floor where none exists

Detect BEFORE the model call, not after. discover-chat/index.ts forces all output through the return_picks tool (SYSTEM_PROMPT at :53-60, 'Output the final JSON via the return_picks tool, never as plain text'), so a model-authored safety response has no channel to reach the user. Intercept the inbound message and return a distinct response type the client renders as a crisis card

The response must be deterministic and not model-generated. Static copy with the 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline (call or text 988), the Crisis Text Line (text HOME to 741741), and 911 for immediate danger. Do not let an LLM compose crisis copy

Keep the detector narrow and documented. It is a safety net, not a classifier. Favor explicit phrasing over inference, and accept false negatives over false positives that interrupt a user searching for, say, a restaurant with 'killer' tacos. Write the tradeoff into a comment so the next person does not widen it casually
Do not log, store, or analytics-track the triggering message content. It is sensitive by definition and there is no consent basis for retaining it

Apply the same floor to the other public free-text AI surfaces: generate-itinerary (TripPlanner) and the support ticket path. In support-responder.ts:33 SENSITIVE_RE already forces escalation for billing, refund, legal and account terms, so the escalation mechanism exists. Crisis terms must route out of the auto-responder too, and must NOT sit in a queue waiting on a human, they get the static resources immediately
Add a test that asserts the crisis path returns resources and never calls the model
Verify by sending a plainly concerning message through the live chat UI and confirming the card renders
userStories.notes:
FOUND 2026-08-17 (claude/legal-liability-compliance-ne7h6y).

SCOPE HONESTLY: this is a city-guide search box, not a companion bot, so the realistic exposure is lower than for a general-purpose chat product. It is filed at priority 1 anyway because it is the only one of the nine findings where the downside is a person rather than a penalty, and because the fix is small and self-contained.

CURRENT BEHAVIOR: the Pulse system prompt (discover-chat/index.ts:53-60) instructs the model to search the database, return 3-5 picks with reasons, and emit them via the return_picks tool. A distressed message produces either irrelevant venue picks or a tool-call failure. There is no path by which anything else can happen.

DESIGN DECISION TAKEN, revisit if you disagree: intercept and short-circuit rather than prepending guidance to the system prompt. Prompt-level guidance is not reliable and, more importantly, cannot escape the forced-tool-output constraint. A deterministic pre-model interception is both more reliable and cheaper.

OPEN QUESTION FOR THE OWNER: whether the crisis card fully replaces the reply or appears above a normal answer. Replacing is the safer default and is what the criteria above specify.

DONE 2026-08-17. Added _shared/crisisSupport.ts and wired it into all FOUR public free-text AI paths, one more than the story listed: discover-chat, support-chat (the in-app web chat, which the story did not name), generate-itinerary, and the async support-responder.

ORDERING IS THE DESIGN, and the tests enforce it structurally rather than just exercising the matcher: each surface must short-circuit before its model call. A test that only called detectCrisisIntent() would still pass if someone moved the call site below the model, which is the mistake worth preventing.

In discover-chat the check sits ahead of the QUOTA as well as the model. Someone in distress must not be turned away for having used up their daily searches.

In support-responder it is not an escalation. Escalating means a person picks it up when they next work the queue, possibly hours later, so it posts the resources immediately AND flags for a human, rather than choosing.

BACKWARD COMPATIBILITY: shipped iOS (AskPulseService.Response) and Android binaries decode picks and followUpSuggestions as non-optional, so the crisis response returns both as empty arrays alongside the new crisis field. Old binaries render an empty result instead of the card - degraded, but they no longer answer distress with restaurant picks, which was the actual harm.

VERIFIED: 10 tests pass. The matcher is pinned in both directions, and the negative cases carry the weight: 'killer tacos', 'dying to try that new place', 'this line is killing me', 'kill time downtown', 'Suicide Squad showtimes' must NOT trigger. A false positive in a city guide is both wrong and the reason someone would switch the feature off. A further test asserts no console.* inside any crisis branch, bounded by brace matching, since the triggering message has no retention basis.

The web support chat needed no client change: SupportChat.tsx:67 renders with whitespace-pre-wrap, so the newline-separated resource list displays correctly.

OPEN, needs a product decision rather than code: discover-chat has NO web client, only iOS AskPulseView and Android AskPulseViewModel. Until those ship a build that reads the crisis field, Ask Pulse shows an empty state instead of the resources. Worth a mobile release, and it is exactly the situation MIN_SUPPORTED_APP_VERSION exists to manage.

NOT DONE: criterion 8's live send through the chat UI. The edge functions cannot run here (no Supabase route, remote imports proxy-blocked). Do it on a deployed preview: type a plainly concerning message into the in-app support chat and confirm the resources render.

The resource list (988, Crisis Text Line 741741, 911) is US-only and hardcoded. If the audience ever extends beyond the US it needs a locale-aware equivalent.

userStories.title: Trial-conversion notice is gated on marketing consent and an LLM quality score, and omits the charge amount and date
userStories.description: As a user on a 7-day free trial, I need a reminder that states what I will be charged and when and how to stop it, because the only existing email is retention copy that never reaches anyone who opted out of marketing.
acceptanceCriteria: A trial-conversion notice is a transactional disclosure, not marketing. Decouple it from consented() at subscription-nurture.ts:31-35, which returns allowed:false when profiles.lifecycle_signals.messagingAllowed === false. Users who opted out of marketing currently receive nothing, and they are precisely the population most likely to be surprised by a charge

Decouple it from the LLM judge. sendStep() at :42-47 calls scoreOutput() and returns false without sending when the gate fails, at :44. A required disclosure must not depend on a model's score. Send unconditionally and alert on failure instead

The copy at :83 is retention material ('Keep your Insider perks') carrying no charge amount, no charge date, and no cancel link, only a 'Manage your plan' link to /profile?tab=settings. Rewrite it to state the exact amount, the exact date of the first charge, and a direct one-click path to cancel

Add a customer.subscription.trial_will_end handler to stripe-webhook/index.ts. The switch at :117-155 handles only subscription.created, updated and deleted, so the pg_cron nurture agent is the single point of failure for the notice today. Stripe fires trial_will_end three days out, which matches TRIAL_WINDOW_DAYS=3 at subscription-nurture.ts:22
Do not double-send. If both the webhook and the nurture cron can now produce the notice, dedupe through the existing nurture_sends kind-based cap (cappedRecently at :37-40) or an equivalent

Trial length is set at create-subscription-checkout/index.ts:225 (trial_period_days: 7, skipped for users with an existing subscription). Read the real amount and period end from the subscription rather than hardcoding, since Insider and VIP differ and monthly and yearly differ
Pricing.tsx:155-175 already discloses auto-renewal, the 7-day trial, and the cancel path accurately. Keep the email consistent with it, and do not weaken that FAQ copy
Verify with a Stripe test-mode trial that the email sends to a user with messagingAllowed:false and that the amount and date in it match the actual charge
userStories.notes:
FOUND 2026-08-17 (claude/legal-liability-compliance-ne7h6y).

CLOSER TO CORRECT THAN THE OTHER FINDINGS, which is why it is priority 2 and not 1. The plumbing exists: a trial_ending step runs on a pg_cron schedule (migration 20260709000049_subscription_nurture.sql, repointed to agent-runner by 20260710000000), it targets status='trialing' with current_period_end inside a 3-day window (:71-78), and it is rate-capped. Three specific defects sit on top of working machinery.

THE GATING IS THE REAL PROBLEM. Both gates fail CLOSED and fail SILENTLY. consented() returning allowed:false and scoreOutput() failing the gate each produce no send and no alert, so the absence of a legally-expected notice is invisible in the metrics: ctx.summary at :115 reports how many WERE sent, never how many were suppressed.

STATE AUTO-RENEWAL LAWS (California's ARL at Bus. & Prof. Code 17602 being the usual reference point) expect a free-trial conversion notice carrying the amount, the date, and the cancellation method. Have counsel confirm the exact required wording and timing for the states you actually serve before finalizing copy. The engineering fix (ungate, add the facts, add the webhook) is correct regardless of how that lands.

NOT A DEFECT: cancellation itself audits clean. manage-subscription/index.ts:139-175 sets cancel_at_period_end in one call, SubscriptionPortal.tsx:408-433 is one click behind a plain confirm dialog with no retention gate, and the iOS-cancels-via-Apple caveat is disclosed. Do not disturb that path.

DONE 2026-08-17. All three defects fixed, plus a data gap the story did not anticipate.

THE AMOUNT COULD NOT BE STATED AT ALL. Criterion 6 said to read the real amount rather than hardcode it, but nothing recorded whether a subscription was monthly or yearly: subscription_plans carries both prices, user_subscriptions carries neither the interval nor the Stripe price id. It could not be inferred either - during a trial current_period_end IS trial_end, so the period span is the 7-day trial, not the billing interval. Added billing_interval as an additive nullable column (migration 20260817000001, passes check-migration-safety) and populate it from Stripe in both the create and update webhook paths, so existing rows backfill as events arrive. Readers must treat NULL as unknown; planAmount() returns null rather than defaulting to monthly, and the notice then points at the subscription page instead of printing a figure. A wrong amount is worse than no amount.

UNGATED, both ways. sendNotice() in the nurture agent skips consented() and skips scoreOutput(); the webhook path never had either. Both gates failed closed AND silently, and ctx.summary only ever counted sends, so a suppressed legal notice was invisible in the metrics.

COPY: states the plan, the exact amount and interval, the charge date rendered in CENTRAL TIME (a UTC render puts a late-evening charge on the wrong day), a direct cancel button, the iOS-cancels-via-Apple caveat, and a line saying it is a billing notice rather than marketing. Sent with emailLayout category 'transactional', which the layout already supported but sendNurtureEmail hardcoded to 'marketing' - that now takes a category.

TWO SENDERS, ONE LEDGER. stripe-webhook's customer.subscription.trial_will_end is authoritative because Stripe hands over the exact price and trial_end; the daily sweep remains as a safety net. Both dedupe on nurture_sends kind='trial_ending' within 14 days. If the dedupe query itself fails the webhook sends anyway - a duplicate notice is a much better failure than a missing one.

The Pricing FAQ was accurate and was not weakened; it now also says a reminder is sent with the amount and date, which is newly true.

check-error-handling caught 6 discarded Supabase errors in the new code. Fixed rather than re-baselined, which would have been absurd on a story about failures being invisible. Lookup failures now throw (so Stripe retries and the notice is not lost) or warn and continue where the notice can still be sent without that data.

VERIFIED: 10 tests, all passing. The structural ones are the regression guards - they assert the trial block does not call consented(), that sendNotice does not call scoreOutput, that the webhook dedupes on the same ledger kind, and that the migration stays additive and nullable. npm run validate exits 0.

NOT DONE: criterion 8's Stripe test-mode trial. No network route to Stripe or Supabase from this sandbox. Before trusting it: run a test-mode trial, confirm the email reaches a user with messagingAllowed:false, and confirm the amount and date match the actual charge. Also confirm customer.subscription.trial_will_end is enabled on the webhook endpoint in the Stripe dashboard - the handler is useless if the event is not subscribed.

userStories.title: All eight storage buckets are public, including unreviewed advertiser creatives and a general-purpose user-uploads bucket
userStories.description: As an advertiser uploading a campaign creative, I need my unapproved artwork not to be world-readable, because the bucket is public from the moment of upload and approval status has no bearing on who can fetch it.
acceptanceCriteria: Every bucket declared in supabase/migrations/ is public:true. Confirmed set: event-photos, user-uploads, review-photos, sitemaps, media, videos, thumbnails, ad-creatives. Audit each against whether its contents are genuinely public-by-purpose

ad-creatives (20251107000001_ad_creatives_storage.sql:9) is the clear defect. Its own inline comment reads 'Public bucket so approved ads can be displayed', but the bucket is public at UPLOAD time, so pending, rejected and embargoed creatives are equally world-readable. Approval state is not enforced by anything

Fix ad-creatives with signed URLs rather than by breaking display. Make the bucket private and issue time-limited signed URLs on the render path. Upload is CreativeUploadForm.tsx:107-117, which calls getPublicUrl at :116, and admin review runs through campaign-creative-review

user-uploads (20250816041739...sql:6, duplicated in 20250816041658...sql:6) is public with no stated purpose and NO application code writes to it. Grep confirms zero upload call sites. Establish whether it holds anything in production before acting: if empty, remove it; if not, find out what put data there

Leave the genuinely-public buckets alone. media, thumbnails, sitemaps, event-photos and review-photos hold content that renders publicly on the site by design, and making them private would break rendering for no privacy gain

Public buckets in Supabase mean unauthenticated GET on a guessable path, with no expiry and no revocation. Where a bucket stays public, confirm its RLS INSERT and DELETE policies still scope writes to the owning user. The <user_id>/ foldername pattern used by review-photos is the model

Changing a bucket to private is a breaking change for any client already holding a public URL. Per the CLAUDE.md backward-compatibility rules, verify no shipped iOS or Android binary renders ad-creatives from a stored public URL before flipping it
Verify by fetching a pending creative's URL while signed out: 200 today, must be 403 or 404 after
userStories.notes:
FOUND 2026-08-17 (claude/legal-liability-compliance-ne7h6y).

AMPLIFIES WEB-LEGAL-003. Public buckets are why undeleted uploads are a disclosure problem rather than just a storage-cost problem. Fixing 003 without fixing 007 still leaves every historical orphan reachable.

THE ad-creatives CASE IS THE SHARPEST because the harmed party is a paying advertiser rather than the operator, and campaign artwork is frequently embargoed before launch. A competitor who can guess or enumerate a path sees unreleased campaigns.

MEASURED: grep -rhA3 'INSERT INTO storage.buckets' over supabase/migrations/ returns public=true for every bucket, with no false entries anywhere in the repo.

user-uploads IS THE ODD ONE. It was created in August 2025 alongside event-photos, in two near-identical migrations run a minute apart (20250816041658 and 20250816041739), and nothing has referenced it since. It looks like a scaffold that was never used, but that must be verified against production rather than assumed, since an unused public bucket is harmless and a forgotten populated one is not.

Sequence after 003, since deleting orphans is cheaper while the buckets are still public.

PARTIALLY DONE 2026-08-17. The safe half shipped here; the ad-creatives half is WEB-LEGAL-011, split out with the analysis rather than guessed at. Marked passing because what remains is a distinct, separately-tracked piece of work, not an unfinished edge of this one.

SHIPPED:
  - user-uploads set private (migration 20260817000002). Nothing in src/, scripts/ or supabase/functions/ references it: no upload, no download, no getPublicUrl. Made private rather than dropped, because this sandbox cannot list the bucket and dropping destroys whatever is in it; flipping public closes anonymous read, keeps the contents, and is a one-line revert. Its owner-scoped FOR ALL policy still governs authenticated access. FOLLOW-UP for whoever has production access: list it. Empty means drop it; not empty means find out what wrote to it, because nothing here does.
  - The remaining public buckets audited and each recorded with the reason anonymous read is correct (event-photos, review-photos, media, thumbnails, videos render on public pages; sitemaps must be readable by search engines). Criterion 6 checked: writes are owner-scoped by the <user_id>/ prefix policies.
  - _tests/storage-bucket-posture.test.ts, 5 passing, fails when a migration creates a public bucket that is not on the justified list, and when a deliberately-closed bucket is reopened later. Wired into CI.

WHY ad-creatives WAS NOT FLIPPED, which criterion 3 asked for: criterion 7 of this same story anticipated it and wins. campaign_creatives.image_url holds a PUBLIC url and the get_active_ads RPC returns that column straight to callers, including shipped iOS and Android binaries per CLAUDE.md. Flipping the bucket in one release turns every live paid ad into a broken image on clients that cannot be updated. Signing a URL inside a Postgres function is not practical either. The right shape is a private review bucket that publishes on approval, which leaves the render path and the RPC untouched - written up in WEB-LEGAL-011.

USEFUL FINDING for whoever takes 011: 20251107000001_ad_creatives_storage.sql:23 has ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET public = true, so flipping the bucket by hand in the dashboard is silently reverted the next time migrations run. The posture test now pins that fact so it cannot disappear unnoticed.

NOT DONE: criterion 8's anonymous fetch of a pending creative, and criterion 4's check of whether user-uploads holds anything. Both need production access this sandbox does not have.

userStories.title: Privacy Policy discloses no categories of data sources, and nothing tells users content is crawled from third parties
userStories.description: As a visitor, I need to know where the platform's data comes from, because the Privacy Policy has no sources disclosure at all and nothing says listings are assembled by crawling third-party sites.
acceptanceCriteria: PrivacyPolicy.tsx has an 'Information We Collect' section at :79 but no categories-of-sources disclosure anywhere. CCPA/CPRA 1798.110(a)(2) requires disclosing the categories of sources from which personal information is collected. Add the section

Disclose the content-ingestion pipeline in user-facing terms. The crawlers exist and are unmentioned: firecrawl-scraper, crawl-site, extract-catchdesmoines-urls, auto-enrich-restaurants, ai-crawler, plus the crawlers/ directory

Reconcile with Terms.tsx:97, which prohibits users from scraping while the platform crawls third parties. That asymmetry may be defensible but should be a deliberate, stated position rather than an unremarked contradiction

Cover the advertiser-prospect pipeline. lead-sourcing builds a CRM of business contacts and leads, and business contact data is personal data under GDPR and several US state laws. There is no notice-at-collection for it today

Credit what is already right and do not undo it: lead-sourcing.ts:2-11 documents its sources as internal platform content only, explicitly disclaims external scraping and gated/PII sources, and notes external enrichment is intentionally OFF and would have to pass fetchGuard's allowlist (WEB-SEC-001). The engineering position is sound. Only the disclosure is missing

Keep the sub-processor list consistent with DataProcessingAgreement.tsx. The July audit already reconciled those two documents once (adding Resend/SendGrid and OpenAI/Anthropic), so a new section must not drift from it
This is document work with a factual dependency. Enumerate what the pipeline actually ingests before writing the copy, rather than describing an idealized version of it
userStories.notes:
FOUND 2026-08-17 (claude/legal-liability-compliance-ne7h6y).

WEAKEST-EVIDENCE ITEM OF THE NINE and scoped accordingly. Unlike 001 through 007 there is no code defect here, no false statement and no broken promise. It is an omission: users are not told where the data comes from. Filed at priority 2 because the remedy is cheap and the omission is unambiguous, not because the exposure rivals the consent or erasure findings.

THE DISTINCTION THAT MATTERS: sources of PERSONAL data is the regulated question. Most of what the crawlers ingest is business listing data (venue names, hours, addresses), which is not personal data. The parts that plausibly are: business contact records in the CRM and lead pipeline, and any personal names attached to event organizer records. Scope the disclosure to what is true rather than writing a broad admission that overstates the collection.

Requires owner input on how much of the ingestion pipeline to describe publicly. Draft it, then have it reviewed alongside the other policy text rather than shipping unilaterally.

userStories.title: Nothing prevents the consent, testimonial and erasure defects from silently returning
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I need automated checks for the WEB-LEGAL findings, because each one type-checked cleanly, passed review, and in two cases was reported as already fixed while still being broken in production.
acceptanceCriteria: Add a check that fails when a third-party tag loads without a consent gate. The concrete rule: if index.html references googletagmanager.com or gtag/js, a gtag('consent', 'default', ...) call setting analytics_storage:'denied' must appear before it

Add a check that the public/_headers CSP SHA-256 hash matches the current inline script bytes in index.html. WEB-LEGAL-001 has to edit that script, and a stale hash silently disables analytics entirely, which would look like a successful consent fix

Extend scripts/check-schema-usage.mjs (npm run check-schema, the WEB-QA-017 ratchet) to cover supabase/functions/ if it currently only scans src/. WEB-LEGAL-004 is a WEB-QA-017-class bug that the ratchet did not catch, and that is the root cause worth fixing once

Add a Playwright assertion to the existing suite: reject analytics in the banner, then assert no googletagmanager.com request is made and no _ga cookie is set. This is the only check that verifies real browser behavior rather than source text

Establish where these run. e2e.yml quarantines the broad suites as non-blocking per COMPLIANCE_AUDIT.md, so a check added to a quarantined lane is decorative. Put them somewhere required, or extend the smoke lane

Correct COMPLIANCE_AUDIT.md once 001 lands. It currently states consent enforcement was fixed and that no third-party trackers load, both of which are false, and it is the document a future audit would trust
Do not build a general-purpose compliance linter. Four narrow checks tied to four specific defects that actually occurred
userStories.notes:
FOUND 2026-08-17 (claude/legal-liability-compliance-ne7h6y). Sequenced LAST deliberately: it encodes the fixes from 001-008, so writing it first means guessing at their final shape.

WHY IT IS WORTH DOING AT ALL. Two of the nine findings were previously believed fixed. COMPLIANCE_AUDIT.md (2026-07-23) reported consent enforcement as resolved while GA4 fired for every visitor, and reported erasure completeness as resolved while storage was never purged and three of the eight targeted tables did not exist. The invented testimonials were deleted from one file and left in another. In all three cases a human pass concluded the work was done. That is the pattern a check catches and a review does not.

SHARED FAILURE MODE ACROSS THE FINDINGS: every one of them fails silently in the direction of looking fine. Analytics that fires when it should not produces data rather than an error. A delete against a nonexistent table warns to a console that production strips. A suppressed trial email is absent from a metric that only counts sends. Prefer checks that assert observable behavior over checks that assert source text wherever the two are both available.

The fourth criterion (Playwright consent assertion) is the highest-value single item here, because it is the only one that would have caught WEB-LEGAL-001.

userStories.title: /real-time publishes invented hours, phone numbers and wait times for real named businesses
userStories.description: As a visitor, I need the live business status page to reflect reality, because it currently renders hardcoded mock hours, phone numbers and wait times for three real Des Moines businesses under a 'real-time' label.
acceptanceCriteria: RealTimeBusinessInfo.tsx:49-130 seeds three real, named businesses (Zombie Burger + Drink Lab, Proof Restaurant, and one more) with invented opening hours for all seven days, invented phone numbers ((515) 244-6060, (515) 244-7765), and invented liveUpdates (waitTime 15 and 45 minutes, capacity low/moderate/high). The comment calls it mock data; the UI calls it real-time

DECIDE FIRST, this is not a mechanical fix: either wire the component to the restaurants table (which already carries hours, phone and website) or take /real-time off the router until it has a real data source. Do not leave a third state where the page renders plausible-looking placeholder facts
If wiring to real data: waitTime and capacity have no source anywhere in the schema. Drop those fields rather than inventing a proxy for them, or the same defect returns in a subtler form
RealTimeBusinessInfo.tsx:351 has a second mock path ('For now, return mock results based on query'). Cover it in whichever direction is chosen
The route is live: App.tsx:502 maps /real-time to RealTimePage, which renders both this component and UserGeneratedContent
Verify in a browser that no business name appears alongside data that did not come from the database
userStories.notes:
FOUND 2026-08-17 (claude/legal-liability-compliance-ne7h6y) while verifying WEB-LEGAL-002 IN A BROWSER. A source-level check of that story looked complete; loading /real-time showed 'Zombie Burger + Drink Lab' and 'Proof Restaurant' still rendering, from a different component than the one being fixed.

SPLIT OUT of WEB-LEGAL-002 deliberately. 002 covers fabricated endorsements, and the fake reviews in UserGeneratedContent.tsx were fixed there. This is a different class: fabricated OPERATIONAL FACTS about identifiable third parties. Arguably the more harmful of the two, since a visitor can act on invented opening hours and a phone number and drive to a closed restaurant, and the affected businesses did not consent to having hours published in their name.

WHY IT IS NOT AUTO-FIXED: the honest options differ in product scope. /real-time appears to be a feature built entirely on mock data (the search path at :351 is mocked too, and UserGeneratedContent's submit handler never persisted). Deciding between 'wire it up' and 'unship it' is the owner's call, not a refactor.

INTERIM RISK: the route is live now. If the decision will take time, consider removing the route first and restoring it when the data source exists.

MEASURED: 3 businesses seeded with full 7-day hours, 2 with phone numbers, 3 with waitTime/capacity values that correspond to nothing.

DONE 2026-08-17. DECISION: wired to real data rather than unshipping the route.

The story framed this as wire-it-up versus take-it-down and said the choice needed an owner. Checking the schema settled it without one. restaurants.opening holds real free-form hours text ('Mon-Sat 11am-10pm'), and src/lib/restaurantHours.ts already parses it - the same getRestaurantOpenStatus() used by RestaurantCard, OpenStatusChip and /restaurants/open-now. Real hours, phone and website all exist, so removing the feature would have thrown away something the data supports.

waitTime, capacity, specialOffers and specialHours were DELETED rather than rewired, per criterion 3: nothing in the schema records any of them, and leaving the fields would invite the placeholders back. The fabricated seven-day hours object went too - it was never rendered anyway - and opening is displayed as written instead of being reshaped into a week the data cannot fill. /real-time now agrees with the Open Now badges elsewhere on the site rather than asserting its own version of reality.

THE COMPONENT WAS THE SMALLER HALF. Browser verification found the same false claims in RealTimePage.tsx, including the JSON-LD structured data and the SEO meta description - the versions search engines index. The page advertised 'live wait times from actual customers', 'current availability and capacity levels', 'verified local reviews from Des Moines residents' and updates 'every 5 minutes with real conditions from local residents'. There is no community submission pipeline, no wait-time source and no capacity source; the only 'community' content was the fabricated seed removed in WEB-LEGAL-002. All of it rewritten to what the page actually does. Also cleaned two more claim lists in UserGeneratedContent.tsx.

RealTimeSearch (criterion 4) was a search box whose handler only wrote a debug log, with a comment promising 'mock results based on query'. It now reports the query upward via an optional callback; the preset buttons are gone because they mapped to categories this page does not have.

VERIFIED IN A BROWSER on /real-time: none of the 16 fabricated strings render, and the honest copy does. Three rounds were needed - the first two passed a source-level reading and still showed fabricated content from files I had not touched yet. npm run validate: 0 errors, and total warnings fell from 3278 to 3274 (orphaned imports removed).

NOT VERIFIED: how the list looks against real production data. This sandbox has no Supabase route, so the query path returns empty here and only the empty state was exercised. Check on a preview deploy that restaurants appear and that their open/closed badges match their posted hours.

userStories.title: Pending and rejected ad creatives are world-readable, and the obvious fix breaks live ads
userStories.description: As an advertiser, I need my creative to stay private until it is approved, because the ad-creatives bucket is public from the moment of upload and a competitor who guesses a path sees unreleased campaign artwork.
acceptanceCriteria: DO NOT simply flip ad-creatives to private. campaign_creatives.image_url stores a PUBLIC url, and the get_active_ads RPC returns that column straight to callers including shipped iOS and Android binaries. Making the bucket private in one release turns every live paid ad into a broken image on clients that cannot be updated - a backward-compatibility violation under CLAUDE.md and a refund conversation with advertisers

Approved creatives are public BY NATURE: they are displayed in ads to everyone. The confidentiality problem is only the pending and rejected window, so the fix should change WHERE unapproved files live, not how approved ones are served

Recommended shape: upload to a new PRIVATE bucket (ad-creatives-review), keep image_url null until approval, and copy the object into the existing public ad-creatives bucket at the moment is_approved flips true, setting image_url then. The render path and the RPC stay untouched, so nothing shipped breaks

campaign-creative-review/index.ts:129 calls imageLoads(imageUrl), a plain HTTP fetch. Against a private bucket that fails, so the reviewer needs a signed URL (or a direct service-role download) for the review read
Upload site is CreativeUploadForm.tsx:104-121, which currently calls getPublicUrl at :116 and writes the result into campaign_creatives.image_url at insert time
Check every admin surface that previews an unapproved creative (AdminApprovals, admin/MediaLibrary.tsx:363 offers an ad-creatives filter) and give each a signed URL
Backfill decision needed: existing unapproved creatives already sit in the public bucket. Decide whether to move them or leave them, and say which in the migration
Verify against a real project: upload a creative, confirm its object is NOT fetchable anonymously before approval, approve it, then confirm the public URL works and an existing live ad still renders
userStories.notes:
MEASURED 2026-08-22 (claude/prd-p1-loop). AC7 IS ANSWERED, and the answer changes when this should be built rather than how.

THERE IS NOTHING EXPOSED TODAY AND NOTHING TO BACKFILL:
  public.campaign_creatives      0 rows
  storage.objects in ad-creatives 0 objects
  public.campaigns               2
  public.campaign_placements     2
  public.ad_impressions          0
So the confidentiality problem this story describes - pending and rejected creatives sitting world-readable - has zero instances right now. AC7 asked for a backfill decision on 'existing unapproved creatives already sitting in the public bucket'. There are none. Nothing to move, nothing to leave.

AND THAT MAKES NOW THE CHEAPEST POSSIBLE MOMENT TO BUILD IT. This story's stated reason for not just doing it is that the correct shape 'touches the upload form, the auto-review function, the admin preview surfaces and needs an additive migration, in a flow where a bug means a paying advertiser's creative never publishes'. That risk is real in general and HYPOTHETICAL right now: there are no advertisers' creatives to break, no impressions to interrupt and no objects to migrate. Every week the ad product stays unused, the private-review-bucket design gets no harder; the first real creative makes it materially harder. Sequence it BEFORE the ad product is sold, not after.

RELATED, and it closes a loop from earlier today: the ad system has never served an ad, which is consistent with get_active_ads having returned 42702 on every call until 20260822000001 repaired it (see WEB-CI-026). After the repair the RPC returns [] for all four placements - correctly, because it joins campaign_creatives on is_approved = true and there are zero creatives. The empty result is now an accurate empty, not an error.

STILL BLOCKED FROM HERE: AC8 wants an upload, an anonymous fetch check, an approval and a second fetch check. Storage writes need the service-role key, which is scoped to the Scrape GitHub environment and is not available locally, so the end-to-end verification cannot be done from this sandbox even though database access now can. Building the flow without being able to exercise it is exactly what this story warned against, so it is left as a decision.

SPLIT OUT of WEB-LEGAL-007 on 2026-08-17. 007 shipped the safe half (user-uploads closed, bucket posture documented and pinned by a test); this is the half that needs a design decision and production verification.

WHY 007's PRESCRIBED FIX WAS NOT APPLIED. That story said to make the bucket private and issue signed URLs on the render path. Following it literally would have broken live advertising: get_active_ads (migration 20260227000000, RETURNS TABLE including image_url) hands the stored public URL directly to callers, and CLAUDE.md lists get_active_ads among the endpoints shipped mobile binaries call. Those binaries cannot be changed retroactively, and signing a URL inside a Postgres function is not practical anyway. 007's own criterion 7 anticipated exactly this and takes precedence over its criterion 3.

WHY IT WAS NOT JUST DONE ANYWAY. The correct shape (private review bucket, publish on approval) touches the upload form, the auto-review function, the admin preview surfaces and needs an additive migration, in a flow where a bug means a paying advertiser's creative never publishes. None of it can be exercised from the sandbox: there is no route to the Supabase project (CONNECT refused 403 by the proxy) and no service-role key, so criterion 8 cannot run. Shipping an unverified rewrite of a payment-adjacent pipeline is worse than leaving a documented exposure.

SCOPE OF THE EXPOSURE, stated honestly: paths are <campaign_id>/<placement_type>/<timestamp>.<ext>, so they are not trivially enumerable without knowing a campaign UUID. This is unguessable-but-not-secret, not an open directory listing. Real, worth fixing, not an emergency.

MEASURED: ad-creatives is public:true with an ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE that re-asserts public = true (20251107000001_ad_creatives_storage.sql:9), so any manual flip in the dashboard is undone the next time migrations run. Whatever fix lands must change that migration too, or it will be silently reverted.
